| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | No public pricing page. Official package comparison: https://www.getalma.com/alma-packages-for-prek-12-independent-charter-schools/ |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | G2 4.2/5 (63; viewed Nov. 24, 2026); Capterra 4.6/5 (455; updated Sept. 3, 2026; viewed Nov. 24, 2026); no verified Alma SIS/Alma Now App Store or Google Play listing/rating. Software Advice: 4.5/5 (448). [9] [10] [11] |

### Overview

Alma is a US K–12 SIS combining records, attendance, scheduling, gradebook, report cards, enrollment, portals, communications, payments, analytics and state reporting. It also positions itself as an SIS/LMS environment, synchronizing assignments and grades with Google Classroom, Canvas, Microsoft Teams, Schoology and other classroom systems. [1] [2] [9]

The founders are Andrew Herman, Elizabeth Long and Michael Oliver. Founding-year databases conflict; Alma has no separate product-launch announcement, so 2014 is only a launch proxy. PitchBook reports one round and $699,000 raised; Crunchbase’s seed amount is obscured and Alma publishes no official total. Alma acquired Always Prepped in 2015 (terms undisclosed) and ESP Solutions Group in August 2026, extending into statewide data management, interoperability and reporting. [7] [8] [14] [17] [18] [23]

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser and cloud:** School accounts use school-specific Alma web addresses, and Alma describes the SIS as cloud-native with 99.99% scheduled uptime, multi-factor authentication, NIST 800-53 alignment, and releases approximately every two weeks. Alma does not publicly identify its cloud provider or school-data hosting regions. [2] [3]
* **Desktop/on-premise:** No installed desktop client or school-level on-premise Alma SIS edition was found. State-agency infrastructure documentation does describe Alma-hosted, SEA-hosted, and hybrid models, which should not be confused with a normal district subscription. [5]
* **Mobile:** Alma Now is Alma’s responsive mobile SIS/parent-student experience. It exposes assignments, schedules, teacher notes, grades, communications, and fee information on mobile devices. The reviewed official and independent pages did not provide a verified Alma SIS native iOS or Android store listing; therefore “mobile interface” is supported, while “native iOS+Android apps” is unverified. [4] [15]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment
Alma Start provides mobile-ready registration, re-enrollment, applications and admissions, customizable digital forms, secure document upload, saved progress, applicant-by-applicant review/editing, notifications and alerts, and a workflow intended to eliminate duplicate entry. The official package comparison also lists file-cabinet submissions and student/parent portals. [2] [3] [15]

#### Student information and records
Core SIS stores biographical and program data, household and associated contacts, emergency contacts, calendars, flexible groups, activities, critical medical data, immunizations, critical flags, custom fields, and a virtual/student filing cabinet. Data administrators get spreadsheet-style editing, validated bulk imports, bulk editing, mailing labels, stock reports, and historical enrollment records. [2] [3] [13]

#### Attendance
Attendance supports positive and negative attendance, teacher and administrator entry, attendance reports, attendance notifications, truancy reports, seating charts, and attendance dashboards. BeaconAI adds chronic-absence and submission-consistency views. [2] [3] [4]

#### Timetable, master scheduling, and academic operations
Alma lists advanced scheduling, walk-in scheduling, course and class management, course requests, calendars, graduation tracking, and multi-school/district oversight. “Advanced Scheduling” is an upgrade in the independent-school packages and included in the district package; no separate published scheduling price was found. [2] [12] [13]

#### Gradebook, assessment, and examinations
The gradebook supports traditional, standards-based and competency/proficiency grading; assignment management; missing-assignment tracking; calculated class grades; configurable competencies and rubrics; mastery and roll-up calculations; weighted assignments; skills-based learning; standards tracking; assessment tracking; and GPA equivalencies. Public materials do not describe a separate exam-engine module with question banks or proctoring. [2] [9] [10]

#### Report cards and transcripts
Academic records include report cards, progress reports, transcripts, enrollment history, imported historical grades, flexible GPA calculations, class ranks, graduation tracking, standards-based report cards, and electronic distribution. Report Builder and custom reports support school-specific layouts, although reviewers report that complex reporting can require CSV manipulation. [2] [10] [11]

#### Learning management and homework
Alma presents SIS and LMS tools together and lists built-in LMS, assignment management, lesson planning and blended learning. Its strongest documented learning workflow is interoperability: assignments, grades and feedback sync with Google Classroom, Canvas, Microsoft Teams, Schoology and Seesaw. Public pages do not document a full native course- or examination-authoring suite. [1] [9] [10] [16]

#### Communication
Communication includes student, staff and household messaging; group messaging; teacher-to-student messaging; embedded messaging in incidents; email-style notifications; and text alerts. The official integrations catalog includes ParentSquare, Remind, SchoolMessenger, OneCall Now, Signal Vine and other communications vendors. I found no public evidence of a native WhatsApp channel; SMS/text support should not be interpreted as WhatsApp support. [2] [3]

#### Parent, student, teacher and administrator portals
Parent and student portals expose grades, assignments, attendance, schedules, teacher notes, report cards, communications and, where enabled, fee plans. Alma supports role-based views, district/school dashboards, custom roles and permissions, and English/Spanish portals. A distinct teacher app is not marketed; teacher workflows are in the web platform and gradebook. [1] [2] [15] [16]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting
Fee Management supports any fee type, one-time/recurring invoices, configurable invoice and tuition plans, full or parity payments, credit-card, ACH and cash tracking, parent/mobile access, processing and reporting. No general-ledger accounting or payroll module is established. Payment integrations include e~Funds and PushCoin. [2] [3] [13]

#### Staff and user administration
Alma supports staff/teacher accounts, directories, role-based permissions, SSO, custom roles, account provisioning and district-level administrative controls. It is not a full HRIS: no native recruiting, benefits, time-and-attendance payroll, or payroll tax functions were documented. [2] [3] [9]

#### Health and medical
The native package includes medical notes and contacts, critical medical data and immunizations. Alma’s App Center also connects to CareDox, Health Etools, Health Office Anywhere and SNAP. Public documentation did not verify a comprehensive clinical record, medication administration, or nurse-case-management module. [2] [3]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care
Incident Tracking supports customizable incident codes, minor/major categories, workflow tools, multiple students on one report, and embedded messaging. BeaconAI provides incident heat maps, location/time comparisons, coding-gap identification and trend views. The platform does not publicly present a separate counseling or pastoral-care case-management product. [2] [4]

#### Special education and safeguarding
BeaconAI lists IEP and 504 tracking, ESL/ELL trends and intervention-timing signals; the App Center lists IEP Anywhere, IEP Direct and IEP Writer integrations. This is meaningful student-support and compliance visibility, but the reviewed sources do not prove that Alma natively authors IEP documents or provides a complete safeguarding/child-protection case system. [3] [4]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting
Operational analytics include custom reporting, embedded visualizations, a BI connector, district/school dashboards and summary views. BeaconAI provides attendance/truancy, enrollment, grading, family-engagement and behavior dashboards, subgroup/equity views, data-quality flags, cross-school comparisons and board-ready snapshots. [2] [4]

#### AI features
BeaconAI is Alma’s production analytics package and is marketed as using the live SIS data to surface patterns early, including chronic-absence risk, D/F trends, family disengagement, behavior hot spots, assessment gaps and data-quality problems. Alma’s 2023 CEO interview also described predictive analysis and AI-assisted state-reporting opportunities. No conversational AI assistant, generative lesson planner, or autonomous decision-maker was verified. [4] [16]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance
The platform offers state-specific fields, push-button reports, validations, a data dictionary, dedicated state support, compliance reporting, Ed-Fi and CEDS-aligned APIs, and state-level collection/validation/certification infrastructure. New Hampshire selected Alma for iNHDEX in 2022; the state says Alma users can submit with one click, receive validation-error navigation back to the SIS, run SASID checks and synchronize calendars. [2] [5] [6]

#### Mobile access
Alma Now provides mobile family/student access to learning activity, schedules, teacher notes, assignments, grades, communications and fees. Alma Start is mobile optimized for enrollment. There is no verified public evidence of separate native staff, parent and student apps in the Apple App Store or Google Play; mobile browser access is the safer classification. [4] [15]

#### Integrations and APIs
The App Center advertises 125+ push-button integrations, a searchable vendor library, configurable data sharing, an integrations dashboard, secure file transfer, public APIs and OneRoster API/SFTP. Examples span Google Classroom, Canvas, Microsoft Teams, Schoology, Blackboard, ClassLink, Clever, Google Drive/Docs, ParentSquare, Finalsite, Apple School Manager, Destiny, Raptor, transportation, cafeteria, health and Kindful fundraising systems. [2] [3]

#### Security and privacy
Controls publicly described include MFA, roles/permissions, cloud-native architecture, scheduled uptime, NIST 800-53 guidance, password controls and FERPA/COPPA provisions. Alma displays a GDPR badge and discusses children’s data and school/district control. SOC 2, ISO 27001, India DPDP readiness, hosting regions and a current independent audit were not verified. [2] [9] [13]

**Not verified as native modules:** transport routing, library management, hostel/boarding, inventory/assets, alumni/fundraising, payroll/accounting, WhatsApp communications, and full special-education case management are either integration-only or not documented. This distinction prevents the App Center’s broad connector list from being mistaken for native functionality.

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **BeaconAI:** production dashboards connect attendance, grades, enrollment, family engagement, incidents, assessments and data quality to early-warning operational action. [4]
* **Navigator onboarding:** step-by-step migration/project management with tasks, GPA setup, schedules, LMS integrations and progress monitoring. [16]
* **Spreadsheet Data Editor:** a bulk-edit workspace with validation, often singled out by administrators as a practical differentiator. [1] [11]
* **App Center:** self-service vendor selection, templates, data-sharing controls, update frequency and integration monitoring rather than one-off custom projects. [3] [16]
* **State-to-school data exchange:** iNHDEX and the ESP acquisition extend validation, certification, data dictionary and reporting capabilities beyond a conventional school SIS. [5] [18]
* **Configurable forms and workflows:** custom forms, fields, roles, permissions, incident workflows and reports allow school-specific processes without a separate development project. [2] [3]

### Pricing Details

Alma has no public price list, per-student/monthly rate, free trial, setup fee, implementation fee or tier price. The official package page names Foundations, Core and Essentials plus a District Solutions Package, but shows feature checkmarks rather than prices; Fee Management, Parent Messaging, School Messaging, Compliance Reporting and Advanced Scheduling are listed as upgrades/components. [12] [13]

Alma’s terms say school and district subscription length, estimated enrollment, fees and payment schedule are agreed in a separate written Statement of Work. Student, parent and teacher accounts are free to those users only when their school or district pays the subscription. Capterra and Software Advice both report “contact vendor”/custom quote and no free trial; neither opened source provides a defensible third-party Alma price range. [9] [10] [11]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Alma advertises a public API, 125+ App Center integrations, OneRoster via API/SFTP and secure file transfer. State materials mention Ed-Fi and CEDS. SSO connectors include ClassLink, Clever, GG4L and Pearson EasyBridge. Google Classroom/Drive/Docs cover Google Workspace; Microsoft Teams uses SDS and Graph for provisioning, rosters, assignments, grades and feedback. Canvas, Schoology, Seesaw, Blackboard and iReady are also listed. Payment connectors include e~Funds and PushCoin. No public LTI/SIF or 1EdTech certification evidence, or developer marketplace beyond App Center, was found. [2] [3] [5] [16]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Alma describes cloud-native delivery, MFA, configurable roles and permissions, 99.99% scheduled uptime and NIST 800-53 guidance. Its terms explicitly address FERPA “school official” handling and COPPA consent responsibilities, while the privacy policy describes children’s information, school/district control and deletion requests. Alma’s site displays a GDPR badge. [2] [13] [20]

No public SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate is linked from reviewed official pages; no provider or hosting region is disclosed, and India’s DPDP Act is not addressed. No publicly reported Alma SIS breach with a confirmed date was found in the reviewed sources, which is not evidence that none occurred. The privacy policy still shows an effective date of May 15, 2015; buyers should request current security and data-processing documents. [20]

### Strengths

* Broad native K–12 core coverage across records, attendance, grading, report cards, enrollment, communications, portals, payments and state reporting.
* Strong usability signal: Capterra reports 4.5/5 ease of use, Software Advice 4.5/5, and reviewers repeatedly call the interface intuitive and modern. [9] [10] [11]
* Practical interoperability through an API, OneRoster, SSO, App Center, LMS synchronization and secure file transfer.
* BeaconAI and the state-data/ESP expansion make analytics and compliance more distinctive than a basic small-school SIS.
* Customer support and onboarding are a recurring positive in independent reviews and Alma’s customer evidence. [1] [10] [11]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* Pricing is quote-only, so schools cannot compare total cost, module cost, payment fees or implementation cost without a sales process. [9] [10] [11]
* Capterra and Software Advice reviewers report limited or difficult-to-customize reporting, CSV workarounds and trouble with complex higher-grade reporting. [9] [10]
* Users report occasional glitches or downtime; Software Advice includes a review describing a workday affected when Alma was unavailable, and Capterra flags occasional technical difficulties. [9] [11]
* Some reviewers describe standards-based grading and gradebook workflows as time-consuming or prone to sync/save/view issues, especially with Google Classroom or higher grade levels. [10]
* Support is generally praised, but reviews also mention slow response/follow-up during difficult issues and a need for trial-and-error. G2 includes a user who said it took time to get help; Capterra summarizes concerns about uneven response times and sensitive-data visibility. [9] [10]
* Native breadth has limits: transport, library, hostel, inventory, payroll, fundraising and full special-education workflows depend on integrations or are not publicly documented; native mobile app-store support is also unverified.

### Key Milestones

* **2012–2013:** PitchBook and Tracxn databases list earlier founding years; these conflict with the 2014 date supported by G2 and Tech.co. PitchBook reports one financing round and $699,000 raised; other database amounts are obscured. [7] [14] [17] [23]
* **February 2014:** Tech.co reports Alma was founded; this is the most specific public founding claim located. [8]
* **2015:** Alma acquired Washington-area school-data platform Always Prepped; terms were undisclosed. Tech.co said Alma then operated in 37 states and 24 countries. [8]
* **2021:** Alma introduced Spanish parent/student portals, its App Center and Navigator onboarding/migration tooling. [16]
* **2022:** New Hampshire awarded Alma the iNHDEX statewide student-information/data-exchange contract; NHED said Alma was already used by about 33% of the state’s districts. [6]
* **2022:** Alma announced BeaconAI as the replacement for Data Lab, adding real-time operational analytics and pattern surfacing. [1] [16]
* **2023:** Alma’s CEO described expansion to 46 states and 54 countries, continued infrastructure scaling, Navigator, Data Lab/BeaconAI and predictive-analysis ambitions. [16]
* **March 2024:** Alma released Microsoft Teams Assignments sync using SDS and Microsoft Graph for provisioning, rosters, assignments, grades and feedback. [16]
* **August 6, 2026:** Alma announced acquisition of ESP Solutions Group, extending the connected platform to state agencies and strengthening data management, interoperability and state reporting. [18]
* **November 24, 2026:** Latest official homepage claim reviewed: more than 6 million students, 44 states and 61 countries; current institution count and an official Alma funding total remain undisclosed. [1] [17] [23]

## #5. FACTS SIS (FACTS Management Company / Nelnet Business Solutions)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | FACTS Management Company, a Nelnet Business Solutions, Inc. (NBS) brand and Nelnet company |
| Headquarters | Lincoln, Nebraska, United States; the former RenWeb operation was headquartered in Burleson, Texas [7] |
| Company founded (year) | 1986 (FACTS, originally “Fast Automatic Cash Transfer System”) [6] [8] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | Not publicly disclosed. FACTS says SIS was launched “over 20 years ago”; RenWeb was acquired in 2014 and the product was renamed FACTS SIS in 2018 [3] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud SaaS and web-based; native iOS and Android family app; no current desktop client or on-premise deployment publicly documented |
| Primary segments | Private K–12, independent, Christian/faith-based, Catholic and diocesan schools; families, teachers, administrators and business offices |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | FACTS claims 12,000+ schools in the United States and 55+ other countries and 2M+ families (checked 24 Nov 2026). A SIS fact sheet claims 5,700 K–12 schools and 97% retention; the SIS page claims 4M+ staff, students and parents. These are vendor claims [1] [3] [6] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://factsmgt.com/ |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://factsmgt.com/features/student-information-system/ |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | https://www.nbshubhelp.com/ (Hubhelp portal; some content requires sign-in); support landing page: https://factsmgt.com/support/ |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | No public pricing page |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | Viewed 24 Nov 2026: G2 4.1/5 (120); Capterra 4.2/5 (57, updated 17 Nov 2026); Apple App Store FACTS Family App 3.4/5 (8.3K ratings); Google Play FACTS Family App 3.75/5 (933 ratings, independently captured by AppBrain). Software Advice lists 3.9/5 (78) [9] [10] [11] [13] [25] |

### Overview

FACTS SIS is a cloud student information system for private and faith-based K–12 schools. It combines a school record, academic operations, family communications, health and behavior records, scheduling, admissions/enrollment, and links to FACTS tuition, financial aid, billing, fundraising and application products. The strategic value is the shared FACTS IQ data layer: a school can keep applicant, student, family, academic and financial workflows connected instead of reconciling separate systems [1] [2].

FACTS began in 1986 as a tuition-payment service, added financial aid in 2002, and joined Nelnet in 2005. The SIS lineage is RenWeb, acquired in June 2014 and renamed FACTS SIS in 2018. FACTS also acquired Dynamic Internet Applications in 2016, adding website/CMS and fundraising capabilities [6] [7] [26].

The product suits schools wanting one vendor for admissions, tuition and academic records, but some breadth comes from separately branded products or integrations rather than one native SIS module.

### Platform Classification Explained

- **Browser/cloud:** FACTS describes SIS as its first cloud-based SIS and provides separate browser logins for the SIS administrator console at https://sis.factsmgt.com/admin and Family Portal at https://sis.factsmgt.com/family-portal. The vendor describes the current platform as cloud SaaS and says its data centres use restricted physical access, redundancy and disaster-recovery controls [3] [16].
- **Desktop/on-premise:** No current Windows/macOS client or on-premise option was found. Historical reviews describe RenWeb’s transition from desktop/client-server to web delivery [9].
- **Mobile:** The named native app is **FACTS Family App** for iPhone/iPad and Android. It exposes announcements, attendance, classes, calendar, billing/tuition, homework, lunch, medical information, report cards and student schedule. FACTS also offers school-branded family-app experiences. The public evidence identifies a strong parent/student app, but not separate native teacher and administrator apps [4] [12] [25].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

Application Builder supports no-code/custom online applications, branded inquiry/application pages, dynamic forms, automated touchpoints, task routing, status changes, document collection, review workflows and reports. Enrollment Management tracks inquiry-to-registration progression, digital contracts and packets, reenrollment campaigns, acceptance-to-payment-plan handoff, family accounts and data flowing into SIS. FACTS reports 6K+ schools using enrollment products and 1.3M+ enrollments processed in 2025, but those are product-family claims rather than SIS-only adoption [21] [22].

#### Student information and records

The SIS is a single system of record for student, family and staff records, demographic data, contact relationships, academic history, documents and historical transcripts. Records also feed health, behavior, attendance, communication, admissions and financial workflows. Role-based access and centralized data reduce duplicate entry, while the Family Portal exposes permitted student information [2] [3].

#### Attendance

Schools can configure day setups and attendance codes, capture attendance by class or day, monitor attendance in real time, generate attendance reports and automatically alert families. The Family App exposes attendance, and FACTS positions attendance alongside academic and compliance data [2] [4].

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Scheduling supports block schedules, complex schedules and multi-campus structures. The 2025 release added general-scheduling updates, templates/patterns and a person locator that finds students and staff by daily schedule. FACTS’s roadmap includes course requests, courses/classes/rooms, manual and automatic scheduling enhancements and schedule-conflict reporting; those later phases should not be treated as fully delivered without a current release note [5].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Teacher tools include configurable gradebooks, grading scales, standards-based grading, assignments, missing-work visibility, lesson plans and classroom planning. A dedicated high-stakes examination engine is not clearly documented; exam administration should be validated in a demonstration [2] [9] [24].

#### Report cards and transcripts

Schools can customize report-card layouts, generate parent-ready reports, calculate GPAs and store historical transcripts. Transcript generation is tied to recorded grades and report cards. Reviewers value report-card workflows, while some report and transcript customization limitations remain common complaints [2] [10] [24].

#### Learning management and homework

SIS includes homework visibility, lesson plans, assignment/grade access and a learning-platform connection in the wider FACTS ecosystem. The Family App lists homework. Independent listings do not consistently evidence a full built-in LMS, so schools should treat FACTS SIS as an academic-management hub rather than a full course-content or LTI LMS [4] [9] [24].

#### Communication

Communication includes email, SMS/text, push, voice/text-to-speech alerts, targeted recipients, preferences, templates, scheduling, newsletters and announcements. WhatsApp is not advertised. Reviewers ask for better two-way communication and message history [4] [10] [11].

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Family Portal gives parents/students access to grades, assignments, attendance, schedules, calendars, report cards, homework, announcements, medical-related information where authorized, tuition and school bills. Teachers and administrators use the browser SIS console for attendance, grades, lesson plans, records, reports, behavior and communications. Premier integration provides a single-login/SSO-style experience across Family Portal and FACTS financial services, though a standards-based enterprise SSO directory integration is not publicly specified [2] [3].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Connected FACTS financial modules cover tuition payment plans, enrollment fees, incidental billing, prepay accounts, lunch/field-trip/childcare charges, configurable schedules and due dates, automated reminders, ACH, checks and debit/credit cards. Advanced Accounting acts as an accounts-receivable subsidiary ledger, linking charges, credits, payments, bank/institution accounts and adjustment reasons; financial-aid awards can be applied to tuition plans. Payment Forms provide branded online forms and data exports. FACTS states PCI DSS Level 1 validation and SSAE 18 auditing for its payment/SIS materials [3] [23].

#### Cafeteria and after-school care

Cafeteria functions include online menus, lunch balances/prepay, POS barcode scanning and lunch activity. The wider product description also names after-school-care management and student pickup/time-clock workflows. These are distinctive operational extensions, although they may be sold or configured separately by school [2] [11].

#### HR, staff and payroll

Staff/faculty records, permissions, schedules and staff lookup are present, including the scheduling person locator. A complete U.S. HR/payroll module is not publicly evidenced for FACTS SIS. FACTS’s Australia-oriented pages mention payroll and asset management, so regional availability should not be assumed for the U.S. product.

#### Transport, library, hostel and boarding

No first-party public SIS page verified native bus-routing, library circulation, hostel/boarding or dormitory-management modules. Transportation and library tools appear in third-party catalogs/integrations, but not as verified native modules [9] [24].

#### Inventory and assets

Asset-management language appears in Australia-oriented FACTS material, but the U.S. SIS page does not document a general inventory register; treat it as regional or unverified.

#### Health and medical

Health Information Management stores vaccination records, medical conditions, medications and medical notes, supports medication scheduling and parent notification for medical events. FACTS released a redesigned medical interface on 27 May 2025, added at-a-glance views and prevented overwriting of medical notes [2] [5].

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Behavior workflows record incidents, conferences and interventions, automate family notifications and preserve centralized documentation. Dashboard Builder includes behavior and at-risk views. Pastoral-care terminology is not used consistently in public documentation, but discipline and intervention records are native [2] [5].

#### Special education and safeguarding

Role-based access, behavior/health records and compliance-oriented reporting can support safeguarding processes. A dedicated IEP/special-education case-management module, mandated-incident workflow or child-protection register was not publicly verified; schools requiring those functions should plan an integration or specialist tool.

#### Alumni and fundraising

FACTS Giving/Donor Services is a connected ecosystem product rather than a clearly native SIS screen. It can use SIS family/contact data, offer giving options and plan tiers, track donors/projects and provide campaign reporting. The 2016 DIA acquisition added website/CMS and fundraising tools [23] [26].

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

FACTS IQ provides cross-system enrollment, financial and academic dashboards. The SIS Dashboard Builder uses embedded Power BI-style reporting, live SIS data, configurable filters and sharing; prebuilt views include student information, medical, behavior, admissions and at-risk dashboards. Current FACTS materials claim 30+ dashboards, more than one million customization combinations and no extra dashboard charge. Analytics cover yield, retention, delinquency, affordability and financial-aid impact [5] [20].

#### AI features

FACTS advertises AI models and admissions yield predictions, plus an AI-supported roadmap for surfacing patterns and automating proactive alerts such as attendance changes. FACTS has said it is building secure data pipes for schools’ existing AI tools and targeting an AI beta, rather than describing a production conversational assistant. Therefore, predictive/decision analytics are evidenced, but a full production AI assistant is not [6] [20].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Reporting exports support compliance reviews, and Australia-oriented Core Intelligence mentions government reporting. Public U.S. documentation does not enumerate every state/federal template; schools should confirm state and diocesan submissions during procurement [1] [5].

#### Mobile apps

FACTS Family App is available on iOS and Android with grades, homework, attendance, announcements, calendar, classes, schedules, report cards, lunch, medical and billing/tuition. School-branded apps can send push notifications and accept payments; separate native staff/teacher apps are not documented [4] [12] [13].

#### Integrations and APIs

FACTS exposes a documented OneRoster v1.1 REST API with OAuth authorization and endpoints for sessions, classes, courses, grading periods, demographics, enrollments, organizations, schools, students, teachers, terms and users. FACTS also claims Ed-Fi support and open APIs; SchoolDay documents a FACTS OAuth integration and CSV/SFTP alternative. Google Classroom and Canvas are listed integrations, while FACTS’s public materials do not verify LTI, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Microsoft 365 or WhatsApp support [14] [15] [19].

#### Security and privacy

FACTS reports encryption at rest/in transit, testing, DDoS defenses, intrusion controls, restricted data-center access, backups, redundancy and disaster recovery. It cites PCI DSS Level 1 and SSAE 18, and describes ISO 27001 alignment; an independent ISO certificate or SOC 2 report was not found. The 4 Nov 2026 privacy policy addresses school-directed processing, FERPA, COPPA and deletion/access; GDPR is addressed in data terms, while India DPDP coverage and hosting regions are not expressly identified. No confirmed public breach was found; BBB complaints concern email and login operations [3] [16] [17] [18].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Connected FACTS IQ operating layer:** Unifies SIS, admissions, finance, engagement, analytics and integrations around one record [1].
- **Single-database heritage:** FACTS says the original single-database design remains central, reducing duplicate entry between academics, enrollment and billing [3].
- **Power BI-style Dashboard Builder:** Lets school users build and share live-data dashboards without exporting spreadsheets [5] [20].
- **Admissions yield and retention intelligence:** Dashboards connect inquiry, yield, affordability, aid, delinquency and retention patterns [20] [22].
- **Family App plus payments:** Families can combine grades, attendance, alerts, forms and tuition payments in a branded mobile hub [4].
- **Medical and behavior workflow depth:** Medical notes, medication scheduling, incident documentation, interventions and family alerts sit alongside academic records [2] [5].
- **OneRoster v1.1 API:** The public Swagger endpoint is more concrete than a generic “API available” claim and exposes detailed roster resources [15].

### Pricing Details

FACTS does not publish a current SIS price card, tier table, per-student rate or standard implementation fee; sales quotation is required. Software Advice shows a “starting price” of $1,000 but labels pricing available upon request, so it is not a reliable unit price or official quote [9]. GetApp reports no price information [24].

The FACTS Family App listing states **$4.99 per family annually**, checked 24 Nov 2026; this is not the SIS license [12] [25]. SchoolDay reports **$500 annually for an API connection**, with CSV/SFTP as an alternative; this is a third-party charge [14]. G2’s review-derived implementation data most commonly shows 1–3 months; onboarding and conversion fees require a quote [11].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

The strongest verified capability is the public OneRoster 1.1 API with OAuth and SchoolDay integration. FACTS claims OneRoster and Ed-Fi support plus open APIs. Google Classroom and Canvas are listed, and the ecosystem links admissions, enrollment, payment, aid, giving and Family App. No public evidence was found for LTI, SIF, Clever/ClassLink, Microsoft 365, WhatsApp or a broad marketplace; Premier integration’s SSO protocol is unspecified [14] [15] [19].

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

FACTS publishes encryption, secure facilities, monitoring, vulnerability and penetration testing, backups, redundancy and disaster recovery. The SIS fact sheet identifies SSAE 18 auditing and PCI DSS Level 1 validation. The newer security page discusses ISO 27001 alignment and regular audits but does not provide a certificate number; SOC 2 was not publicly confirmed. FERPA and COPPA are directly discussed in the 4 Nov 2026 privacy policy, while GDPR is addressed in the security/data-protection material. FACTS’s 20 Nov 2026 Data Protection Terms include a DPA, API/integration terms and AI feature terms. Data hosting regions, India DPDP coverage and a public incident register were not disclosed. Operational complaints in 2025–2026 include email delivery/authentication, repeated logins, account synchronization, bugs and support handoffs, with BBB records showing some issues resolved [16] [17] [18].

### Strengths

- Broad private-school coverage spanning academics, admissions, tuition, aid, family engagement, cafeteria and health.
- Deep FACTS-native connections reduce duplicate data between SIS, applications, enrollment, payment plans and aid.
- Strong practical recordkeeping: configurable grading, transcripts, attendance codes, medical records and behavior documentation.
- Public OneRoster API, OAuth roster endpoints and claimed Ed-Fi/open-API direction are better than a closed SIS.
- Reviewers frequently praise customer service, centralization and the ability to keep family, academic and financial data together [9] [10] [11] [24].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is quote-only, and independent listings disagree or provide only ambiguous starting-price figures.
- Users report a learning curve, click-heavy navigation, bugs, outages and difficult reports [10] [11] [24].
- Capterra reviewers cite unclear roadmap communication, updates that prioritize parent experience over daily school users, clunky reports, limited trend views and no two-way parent/student communication [10].
- Apple reviews repeatedly report forced reauthentication, password resets, delayed grades, device switching problems, crashes and confusing navigation; the app is rated only 3.4/5 despite its broad feature list [13].
- Transport, library, boarding, payroll, IEP/special-education and state-reporting depth is not clearly documented as native.
- The wide ecosystem can feel like multiple products and logins; reviewers also describe setup work and a learning curve [11].

### Key Milestones

- **1986:** FACTS founded by David Byrnes and Stanley Phillips to serve one parochial school with tuition-payment services [8].
- **2002:** FACTS added Financial Aid Management [6].
- **2005:** Nelnet acquired an 80% interest in FACTS; the company reported more than 3,500 institutions and 650,000 families/students at the time [8].
- **2014:** FACTS acquired RenWeb; RenWeb then served more than 3,000 schools and brought admissions, scheduling, billing, attendance, gradebook, health and parent-portal capabilities [7].
- **2016:** RenWeb acquired Dynamic Internet Applications, adding School Site/CMS and fundraising-related capabilities [26].
- **2018:** FACTS renamed the RenWeb product FACTS SIS [3].
- **2025:** SIS released scheduling enhancements and a medical-module redesign; Dashboard Builder and MFA rollout were announced in the Q2 roadmap [5].
- **2026:** FACTS positioned FACTS IQ as the connected intelligence layer, refreshed its privacy/data-protection terms in November, and continued expanding dashboards, APIs and AI-supported insights [6] [17] [18] [20].

## #6. Workday Student (Workday, Inc.)

App-store ratings cover the wider Workday app, not only Student. |

### Overview

Workday Student is Workday’s cloud student information system for higher education. It brings recruiting, admissions, academic foundation, curriculum, registration, records, advising, financial aid, and student financials onto the same data model used by Workday Human Capital Management and Workday Financial Management [3] [8] [9].

The product matters because higher education has unusually complex academic calendars, program rules, transfer-credit policies, aid calculations, and financial transactions. Workday emphasizes real-time data, configurable business processes, mobile self-service, and AI-guided actions.

Workday was founded by former PeopleSoft executives Dave Duffield and Aneel Bhusri in 2005. Workday announced its intention to build Student in 2013, is described by independent market research as launching Student in 2016, and identifies 2018 as the first higher-education deployment. Workday’s later acquisitions—such as Platfora, Adaptive Insights, Peakon, and HiredScore—strengthened analytics, planning, engagement, and talent capabilities around the platform, but none is presented as the origin of the Student SIS [10] [12].

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser/cloud delivery:** Workday describes Student as a single cloud-based system. Student hubs and many self-service tasks are accessed in a browser, with role-based security domains and configurable profiles. The documentation specifically notes that Student Hubs are browser-only and are not available through the mobile app [2] [9].
* **Hosting:** Workday does not publicly identify one cloud provider or one hosting region for every Student tenant in the product pages reviewed. Hosting, regional availability, and tenant configuration therefore need to be confirmed in a contract and security review. Workday does publish enterprise cloud security/compliance material and a current trust center [23] [27].
* **Desktop/on-premise:** No native desktop client or on-premise Student edition is publicly documented. The delivery model is SaaS/browser-based.
* **Native mobile:** The exact shared app name is **Workday**. Workday links both the Apple App Store listing and Android package `com.workday.workdroidapp`; the app provides role-dependent mobile access, push notifications, dashboards, and selected student/employee transactions. Workday cautions that not every web feature is mobile-enabled [20] [21] [22].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Academic foundation, curriculum, and master scheduling

The academic foundation defines academic units, levels, programs of study, academic calendars, periods, locations, and policies. Curriculum and registration support course catalogs, sections, prerequisites, eligibility rules, reserve capacity, registration appointments, waitlists, concurrent academic lifecycles, stackable credentials, program-of-study relationships, and schedule planning. The student-records page also describes course-demand visibility and planned-versus-actual enrollment analytics for staffing decisions [7] [8]. This is higher-education course scheduling rather than a K–12 bell timetable.

#### Recruiting, admissions, and enrollment

Student Recruiting and Admissions cover prospect and applicant profiles, recruitment notes, events, campaign effectiveness, application management, configurable online applications, routing and evaluation, admission decisions, cohort tracking, financial-aid action items, transfer-credit evaluation, and digital onboarding. Prospects can register for events, complete requirements, view financial-aid tasks, and continue into the student record without a separate handoff. Workday also supports admissions analytics such as application trends, recruitment spend, enrollment funnels, and unmet applicant need [5] [9].

#### Student information and academic records

Student profiles are configurable composite views with contact, personal, education, application, recruitment, financial-aid, history, holds, notes, athletics, and other conditional groups. Records cover academic history, multiple GPAs and GPA calculations, leave-of-absence questionnaires, documents, competencies, program changes, honors, privacy settings, student holds, duplicate management, and third-party access for family or friends. Transfer-credit tools maintain equivalencies individually or in bulk, capture context, support pre-matriculation evaluation, provide an administrator troubleshooting console, and re-evaluate equivalencies when a student changes program [7] [9].

#### Registration and academic progress

Students can check eligibility before registration, save planned schedules, register from a saved schedule or academic planner, join waitlists, and receive push notifications when a seat becomes available. Academic Requirements and Academic Planning evaluate degree requirements, planned and unregistered courses, ineligible courses, expected completion, cohorts, advisors, and progress toward credentials. Students can see holds, contacts, appointments, academic history, and registration tasks in the Academics Hub [7] [8] [9].

#### Grading, assessment, examinations, transcripts, and credentials

The public Student pages explicitly document grading and GPA calculations, grade entry/management, academic history, progress reports, transcript processing, academic requirements, honors, and credentials. The 2026 Student Administration Agent is designed to automate transcript processing, transfer-credit evaluations, and academic-requirements management [3] [7]. Workday’s public feature pages do not establish a standalone LMS-style gradebook, assessment authoring environment, or examination-proctoring module; those are scope questions for an institution’s integration design.

#### Academic advising and student journeys

Advisors can be assigned to students and use academic progress reports, academic requirements, academic plans, cohorts, and student profiles. Workday Student Journeys/engagement paths guide orientation, registration, financial-aid completion, program exploration, onboarding, and other milestones. Engagement overviews show whether students respond to journeys and meet milestones. Academic, financial, and extracurricular information can be carried from admissions into advising [5] [6] [8].

#### Financial aid

Financial Aid includes ISIR processing and verification, action-item assignment, cost-of-attendance assignment, need- and merit-based packaging, private-scholarship automation, a calculation engine, proactive alerts, real-time account refresh, built-in SAI calculation, enrollment-change recalculation, residency-aware changes, nonstandard academic periods, instruction-week calculations, Pell-table/regulatory updates, award rules, disbursement, work-study awards, job search/application, and links to Workday HCM and Payroll for hours, limits, and pay [4].

#### Student finance, fees, billing, payments, and accounting

Student Financials/Finance Hub brings tuition, housing fees where configured, charges, payments, balances, holds, refunds, billing schedules, financial-aid information, and payment actions together. Students can view real-time account information and make payments; authorized parents or payers can receive billing alerts through configured access. Student financial transactions connect to Workday Financial Management for broader accounting, reporting, and institutional finance, rather than representing a separate small-school bookkeeping product [3] [6] [8] [18].

#### Engagement and communication

Workday documents personalized communications through email, text/SMS, in-app messages, push notifications, alerts, reminders, targeted audiences, engagement plans, and journey milestones. Examples include registration reminders, financial-aid requirements, onboarding tasks, and waitlist availability. No WhatsApp channel is identified in the reviewed official documentation [3] [6] [7].

#### Portals and role-based access

The external student site provides an interactive portal for students and prospects. Academics Hub, Financials Hub, Campus Engagement Hub, and Student Config Hub centralize tasks and reports. Faculty, advisors, administrators, and student workers see role-specific tasks; configurable secure third-party access supports family and friends. Workday does not market separate named parent, teacher, and student apps; these personas are served through role-based browser experiences and the shared Workday mobile app [8] [9].

#### Analytics, dashboards, and reporting

Operational and academic insights include enrollment trends, course demand, applicant-pool health, recruitment spend, student progression, retention, degree progress, financial-aid awards, student revenue by academic period, refunds, budget, workload, and program profitability. Workday’s unified employee, finance, and student data model supports real-time reports, segmented dashboards, configurable reports, and cross-campus analysis [1] [3] [7].

#### AI features

Current materials describe AI-powered search and assistance in Student Hubs, AI guidance and recommendations, predictive views such as at-risk-student and top-application signals, and a Student Administration Agent for transcript processing, transfer-credit evaluation, and academic requirements. Workday’s broader responsible-AI platform supplies guardrails and deterministic, auditable business processes; some agents were announced as new capabilities, so institutions should distinguish generally available features from roadmap items in the order form [1] [3] [25] [26].

#### Workday HCM, staff, payroll, and employee-student identity

Student is unified with Workday HCM, Payroll, Financial Management, Adaptive Planning, and Grants Management. This enables one person/Universal ID across student and worker roles, campus-job eligibility and hours, pay slips, financial reporting, and workforce processes. These are powerful suite integrations, but HCM and payroll are not Student-only modules [8] [9] [26].

#### Mobile apps

The shared Workday iOS/Android app supports authorized role-based access, tasks, notifications, dashboards, time and pay actions, and selected Student functions. Native app scope is tenant- and role-dependent; the documentation says Student Hubs remain browser-only, and the app store listing warns that not all Workday features are available on mobile [9] [20] [21] [22].

#### Integrations, APIs, compliance reporting, security, and scope boundaries

Workday offers REST, SOAP, and Graph APIs, OpenAPI specifications, API Gateway/OAuth patterns, Workday Extend, and a partner Marketplace [19] [1]. Public materials support SSO/IAM and configurable domain security, but do not establish native OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, or ClassLink certification for Student. Government and regulatory support is strongest in financial aid (ISIR, Pell tables, compliance updates) and configurable institutional reporting. No native Student modules are publicly evidenced for attendance registers, K–12 homework/LMS, transport, library circulation, hostel/boarding administration, inventory/asset management, health/medical records, behavior/discipline, special education/safeguarding, or alumni/fundraising; those typically require other Workday products or integrations [3] [8] [18] [19].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **Unified student-worker identity:** Universal ID connects a student’s academic and employee roles, including campus-job eligibility, hours, funding, and pay [9].
* **Financial-aid recalculation:** Registration, residency, or other student changes can trigger immediate attendance-cost and aid-package recalculation [4].
* **Transfer-credit lifecycle:** Applicants can evaluate transfer credit before matriculation, administrators can troubleshoot equivalencies, and program changes can trigger re-evaluation [7].
* **Configurable, no-custom-code processes:** Workday’s business-process framework and configurable application/academic rules adapt workflows across departments [3] [5].
* **AI administration agents:** Student Administration Agent targets transcript, transfer-credit, and academic-requirements work, while Student Hubs provide AI search/assistance [3].
* **Cross-campus data core:** Student, employee, finance, grants, and planning data can support real-time institutional decisions [1] [26].

### Pricing Details

Workday does not publish a Student price list, tier table, per-student annual price, per-school monthly price, implementation fee, or public free trial. G2 lists one “Basic” configuration as “Contact Vendor for Pricing,” while Software Advice reports one custom-priced plan and pricing available on request [15] [16]. The commercially relevant unit is therefore a negotiated institutional subscription, normally shaped by institution size, modules, countries, integrations, implementation services, and existing Workday HCM/Financials scope; no verified third-party dollar range was found in the reviewed sources. Pricing checked November 24, 2026.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Workday exposes REST APIs for smaller self-service transactions, SOAP APIs for large scheduled imports/exports, and a Graph API for targeted data retrieval. The developer portal provides live API explorers and OpenAPI specifications [19]. Workday Extend and the Workday Marketplace support partner-built extensions, while Workday Student connects natively to HCM, Payroll, Financial Management, Adaptive Planning, Grants Management, and Workday identity/security [1] [26].

The reviewed public evidence does not verify 1EdTech OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, or ClassLink certification for Workday Student. Institutions should expect integration work for an LMS, alumni system, library, identity provider, payment gateway, data warehouse, and state reporting feed. SSO and role-based security are supported at platform level, but exact protocols, payment processors, accounting mappings, and API entitlements are tenant/contract dependent.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Workday’s compliance page explicitly includes Student in the scope of its ISO/IEC 27001:2022 information-security, ISO/IEC 27017 cloud-security, ISO/IEC 27018 public-cloud PII, ISO/IEC 27701 privacy-management, and ISO 42001 AI-management coverage. Workday also publishes SOC 1/SOC 2/SOC 3 materials for Workday enterprise products and an updated trust center listing SOC, ISO, GDPR, FedRAMP Moderate, NIST, CSA STAR, and other badges [23] [27].

Workday’s privacy statement describes international-transfer safeguards, standard contractual clauses, EU–U.S./UK/Swiss Data Privacy Framework participation, access/correction/deletion/portability rights, and regional controllers including Workday Limited in Ireland and Workday, Inc. in the United States [24]. The reviewed public pages do not explicitly claim COPPA, India’s DPDP Act, or a FERPA certification for Workday Student; FERPA obligations remain a shared institutional/vendor-contract responsibility. Workday does not publish one universal Student hosting region, so data residency must be confirmed per tenant and order.

No verified Student-specific security incident was identified in the reviewed official, review, and higher-education news sources through November 24, 2026. This is not evidence that no incident has ever occurred; it means no incident was sufficiently verified for inclusion here.

### Strengths

* Broad, genuinely higher-education-native lifecycle coverage from recruiting through registration, aid, billing, advising, and graduation.
* Strong integration with Workday HCM, Payroll, Financial Management, planning, grants, identity, reporting, and security.
* Real-time academic and financial data, configurable rules, transfer-credit handling, and aid recalculation address complex university policies.
* Current AI direction is unusually concrete for an SIS, including search/assistance, recommendations, predictive signals, and administration agents [3] [26].
* Adoption is material and growing: more than 200 institutions and 5.8 million Student records were claimed in April 2026 [26].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* Reviews repeatedly describe confusing navigation, slow page loads, and a steep learning curve. G2 includes a 1/5 review calling registration clunky, slow, and dated; its review summary also asks for clearer navigation, faster performance, and better onboarding [15].
* Capterra and Software Advice both show ease of use around 4.0 despite higher overall/functionality scores; reviewers report duplicated paths, unintuitive menus, and the need to learn where tasks live [14] [16].
* Mobile access is useful but incomplete: reviewers report that mobile/tablet functionality is materially narrower than the web experience, with occasional loading delays and downtime around upgrades [14] [15].
* Large implementations are expensive and institutionally disruptive. Inside Higher Ed reported Ohio State abandoning its Workday Student effort in 2021, with analysts estimating sunk costs in the tens of millions and describing next-generation SIS deployments as unusually difficult [17].
* The product is not a complete K–12 school-management suite; schools needing transport, library, health, discipline, special education, boarding, or alumni functions will need integrations or other products.

### Key Milestones

* **2005:** Dave Duffield and Aneel Bhusri found Workday [10] [11].
* **2008:** Workday acquires Cape Clear Software, strengthening integration capabilities [10].
* **2012:** Workday becomes publicly traded [10] [11].
* **2013:** Workday announces its intent to build Workday Student, described as a “campus in the cloud” [12].
* **2016:** Independent higher-education market research records Workday Student as launched; Workday also acquires Platfora for analytics [10] [12].
* **2018:** First higher-education institution deploys Workday Student; Workday acquires Adaptive Insights, adding planning depth [10] [12] [26].
* **2021:** Workday completes the Peakon acquisition and announces/acquires VNDLY, expanding employee engagement and workforce capabilities [10].
* **2022:** Ohio State drops its Workday Student implementation effort, becoming a prominent public warning about SIS complexity [17].
* **2023:** Workday surpasses 10,000 customers worldwide as a company; Student adoption continues to expand [10].
* **2025:** Workday reports more than 650 higher-education institutions selecting the broader platform, more than 85 Student institutions live, and more than 3 million Student records; it announces AI agents including Academic Requirements Agent and Student Administration Agent [25].
* **2026:** Workday reports more than 200 institutions on the Student journey, nearly 100 live, and more than 5.8 million student records; it is named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Higher Education SIS [13] [26].

## #7. Synergy Education Platform (Edupoint)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Edupoint Educational Systems, LLC |
| Headquarters | Mesa, Arizona, United States [24] |
| Company founded (year) | 2003, founded by Bob Weathers [3] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | Not publicly disclosed. Edupoint describes more than 35 years of leadership experience in student data systems, but does not publish a distinct Synergy launch year [3] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud-hosted, web-based K–12 platform with native iOS and Android role apps; customer-managed/on-premise deployment is not clearly described on current public product pages [7] [12] |
| Primary segments | K–12 public and private school districts, state-approved/statewide deployments, regional service agencies, and education service centers; not positioned as a higher-education SIS [3] [21] |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | More than 5.5 million students in 21 U.S. states and 7,000+ customer schools (official site, viewed November 24, 2026); a March 23, 2026 release says 36 Tennessee districts/185,000 students and more than 5.5 million students in 21 states [1] [31] |

Capterra Synergy LMS: 3.0/5 from 3 reviews (October 21, 2026 page, viewed November 24, 2026) [25]. Apple App Store: ParentVUE (New) 1.7/5 from 229 ratings; StudentVUE (New) 1.7/5 from 1K ratings (viewed November 24, 2026) [28] [29]. Google Play ParentVUE (New): score and review count were not exposed in the accessible listing; listing showed 100K+ downloads and a last update of August 17, 2026 (viewed November 24, 2026) [30] |

### Overview

Synergy Education Platform is Edupoint’s integrated K–12 student-data, learning-management, assessment, student-support, communication, and district-productivity ecosystem. Its core design is a centralized database shared by Synergy SIS, Teaching & Learning, Special Services, and related modules, so enrollment, attendance, grades, interventions, special-education documents, and analytics can be used across role-based workflows without repeated data entry [1] [32]. Its users are district administrators, school leaders, teachers, counselors, nurses, special-education teams, students, and families.

Synergy’s importance is its combination of SIS, instruction, assessment, intervention, special services, and analytics. Edupoint reports 5.5M+ students in 21 states and 7,000+ schools; Tennessee alone had 36 districts and 185,000 students in March 2026 [1] [31]. Bob Weathers founded Edupoint in 2003, but no separate Synergy launch year, acquisition history, or funding history is publicly disclosed [3].

### Platform Classification Explained

**Browser and cloud.** ParentVUE and StudentVUE are explicitly available as web portals, while Edupoint’s cloud-hosting service manages the Synergy software and server OS, upgrades, fixes, monitoring, patching, backup, and disaster recovery [8] [12]. The hosting options are Synergy Cloud, Premium Cloud, Premium Plus Cloud, and Consortium Hosting. Edupoint says its cloud uses Amazon Web Services, geo-redundant data centers, and a 99.99% uptime SLA [11] [12].

**Desktop and on-premise.** Current public pages emphasize browser access and Edupoint Cloud. They do not clearly document a desktop client or a current on-premise licensing option. Districts can have direct database access in some Premium Cloud tiers through a point-to-point VPN, but that is not the same as an on-premise product [12].

**Native mobile.** Edupoint lists eight native iOS and Android apps: StudentVUE, TeacherVUE, ParentVUE, AdminVUE, SEVUE, HealthVUE, CounselVUE, and KioskVUE [4] [7]. They use the same credentials as the web portals and support device capabilities such as camera access. ParentVUE and StudentVUE support iPhone and iPad as well as Android; the new Apple listings require iOS/iPadOS 15.6 or later [8] [28] [29].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Synergy SIS: student administration and records

The SIS covers enrollment, demographics, family/guardians, attendance, health/immunizations, discipline, courses/requests/history, mass and walk-in scheduling, report cards, academic/career plans, transcripts, graduation, lockers, groups, fees, and portals. District tools include calendars, role security, state reporting, emergency management, audit trails, inter-district exchange, CTE, surveys, workflows, dashboards, reports, and integrations; performance tools include test history, analysis, standards, LMS/assessment, and ELL support [2].

#### Enrollment, registration, lottery, and athletics

Online Registration provides family registration/re-enrollment, multilingual adaptive forms, uploads/approvals, school preferences, progress tracking, pause/resume, boundary/immunization validation, authorizations, queues, alerts, required/pre-filled/read-only fields, duplicate prevention, and real-time SIS enrollment [13]. Lottery handles open-enrollment, magnet, and charter selection with weighted/points rules, filters, waitlists, placement, multilingual communication, packets, audit trails, and Synergy Mail updates [14]. Athletics adds athlete registration, uploads/signatures, GPA/course/boundary/physical eligibility, approval queues, tryout rosters, team placement, coach access, and email notifications [15].

#### Scheduling, attendance, and school operations

The SIS includes calendars, course creation/requests, mass and walk-in scheduling, course history, graduation tracking, attendance, emergency management, student groups, and lockers [2]. TeacherVUE adds seating charts, attendance, hall passes, substitute access, discipline referrals, conferences, course recommendations, test-group analysis, and emergency response [16]. Transport and bus routing are not identified as native modules.

#### TeacherVUE Portal & Gradebook

TeacherVUE is the teacher portal and gradebook. It combines a 360-degree student profile, teacher-created and district course content, assignment content, online grading, traditional and standards-based grading, rubrics, report cards with AI-assisted comments, performance analysis, reports, Synergy Actions, Google Classroom integration, and third-party LMS integration [16]. Teachers can customize analysis bands, filters, color schemes, and gradebook organization; they can also use generative AI for lesson plans and content.

#### Synergy LMS and learning resources

Synergy LMS supports district course authoring and distribution, scope-and-sequence curriculum planning, drag-and-drop curriculum calendars, shared content banks, teacher teams, teacher modification of district content, synchronous and asynchronous/blended learning, recorded video classes, Quick Tests, badges, instructional-tool authorization and usage management, and personalized study guides. Content can embed videos, Google Drive files, Microsoft OneDrive files, assignments, images, calendars, graded discussions, and nearly 400 LTI learning apps. StudentVUE provides 24/7 access to course content and assignments [17].

#### Synergy Assessment, gradebook, and examinations

Synergy Assessment provides district/school/classroom test management, customizable banks, 12+ question types, technology-enhanced items, standards/scoring, live dashboards, breakout groups, online tests, bubble sheets/webcam scanning, PDF conversion, zoom/color/text-to-speech accommodations, and ParentVUE/StudentVUE feedback. Reporting includes 20+ pre-built reports, subgroup/standard analysis, drill-downs, and Synergy Analytics; optional banks are Inspect Plus and Mastery Item Bank [18].

#### Report cards, transcripts, and parent/student portals

The core SIS supports report cards, transcripts, course history, graduation status, academic/career plans, and progress tracking [2]. ParentVUE and StudentVUE provide one-login, real-time access to calendars, schedules, class websites, assignments, scores, grades, assessment results, attendance, administrative records, health and immunization records, discipline, transcripts, graduation status, fees, course requests, documents, and multilingual Synergy Mail. Depending on district configuration, StudentVUE supports assignment uploads, tests, flex periods, digital locker, hall passes, and counselor visits; ParentVUE supports absence reporting, alerts, conferences, fee payment, registration, information updates, lottery placement, athletics registration, MTSS progress, and special-education signatures/progress [8] [30].

#### Communication and workflow automation

Synergy Mail is an in-platform messaging system with automatic language translation and two-way translation in teacher/family communication. The platform also has notifications, reminders, automated tasks, business rules, mandatory fields, workflow customization, alerts, digital acknowledgements, and role-based dashboards [2] [3] [9]. Public pages document email, in-app messages, portal notifications, and push notifications. They do not document native WhatsApp messaging; SMS is not presented as a core platform channel, so districts should verify any local notification integration.

#### MTSS, early warning, behavior, discipline, and pastoral support

Synergy MTSS includes district screeners, scheduled screening windows, risk filtering, AI-assisted plan creation, configurable early-warning categories/data sources/weights, stakeholder notifications, referrals, tiered plans, accommodations, intervention delivery logs, progress graphs/flags, outcome capture, progress reports, fidelity analysis, custom forms, and complete history. PBIS/CICO features include goals, feedback schedules, behavior points, classroom/school reward stores, family visibility, and redemption in StudentVUE/TeacherVUE. It also includes incident documentation, recurring-behavior observations, and an Emotion Tracker for student-reported AM/PM emotions [19].

#### Special education, 504, health, and safeguarding-related records

Synergy SE supports collaborative IEP creation, including Gifted IEP, process and ad hoc documents, document packets, archives, compliance verification, guided workflows, translation, event notifications, progress alerts, Medicaid provider/service tracking and extracts, interactive error validation, simultaneous editing, caseloads, team summaries, service tracking, parent communication, goal libraries, mail merge, and configurable documents/data fields. Synergy 504 supports visual timelines, 504 process documents, accommodation plans, and shared data with SE. AI Assist applies to narrative fields such as prior written notices and progress summaries [6]. Health features include immunizations, health records, nurse visits, medication/refill alerts, screenings, health notes, and HealthVUE access [7] [23]. The reviewed pages support privacy, discipline, health, emergency, and student-support workflows, but do not claim a standalone safeguarding/child-protection case-management module.

#### Fees, payments, accounting, and other administrative domains

Synergy SIS and ParentVUE expose fee records, balances, and payment; MySchoolBucks and SchoolPay are listed integrations [10]. No native general ledger, procurement, HR/payroll, transport, library, hostel/boarding, inventory/assets, alumni, or fundraising module is identified publicly.

#### Analytics, dashboards, reporting, and compliance

Synergy Analytics supports pre-built/custom dashboards, longitudinal and subgroup analysis, and data from enrollment, attendance, discipline, GPA, tests, SEL, EWS, interventions, digital/parent engagement, demographics, Google Sheets, and other databases. Users can pivot, drill through, combine media with data, and restrict views by student, class, school, or district [20]. SIS adds 350+ reports, SSRS, report writer, ad hoc reporting, queries, audits, and role dashboards [2]. Federal/state reporting, CRDC, accountability, immunization, IDEA/504, standards, and mandated health services are supported [23].

#### AI features

Generative AI is in production across Synergy SIS, TeacherVUE, MTSS, LMS, Assessment, and Special Education/504. Documented uses include assignment/course/test/study-guide creation, lesson plans, intervention plans, report-card comments, discipline and health notes, special-education progress summaries, and help composing Synergy Mail. Edupoint says AI output requires user review, follows existing role permissions, and replaces personally identifiable information with non-identifying tokens before sending prompts to ChatGPT by OpenAI [9].

#### Mobile apps

The eight role apps cover core workflows: ParentVUE (grades, attendance, assignments, messages, health/discipline, fees), StudentVUE (uploads, assessments, course requests, hall passes), TeacherVUE (attendance, assignments, discipline), AdminVUE (ID scanning, tardies, discipline, emergency accountability), HealthVUE (medication, visits, screenings), SEVUE (IEP/BIP, meetings, behavior, Medicaid), KioskVUE (tardy/detention/health check-in, IDs, reunification), and CounselVUE (graduation, scheduling, conferences, CICO) [7].

#### Integrations, APIs, and extensibility

Synergy integrates with Google Classroom/Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Zoom, Teams, Clever, MySchoolBucks, SchoolPay, Inspect, Mastery Item Bank, and nearly 400 LTI apps. Edupoint states that SIS is OneRoster 1.1 certified for rostering/grade passback, Ed-Fi certified, and SIF 2 enabled; it also provides a selected-LMS API and development toolkit/source-code capability [10] [3].

#### Security and privacy

Edupoint reports field-level security, encryption, role access, 2FA, audits, restoration, business rules, AWS hosting, 24/7 operations, vulnerability scanning, intrusion prevention, geo-redundant centers, 99.99% uptime, and annual SOC 2 recertification [11] [12]. Its privacy policy addresses FERPA, COPPA, district control, deletion/return, and no sale of confidential data [23]. ISO 27001, GDPR, India DPDP Act, and named incidents were not publicly claimed in reviewed sources.

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Single database:** Shared real-time data spans enrollment, instruction, assessment, interventions, special services, and reporting [1].
- **Guardrailed generative AI:** AI assists content, notes, plans, comments, and summaries with review and PII tokenization [9].
- **Configurable MTSS/EWS:** Districts define data, weights, workflows, forms, fidelity measures, and CICO supports [19].
- **Assessment-to-action:** Live results drive grouping, re-teaching, standards analysis, accommodations, and family feedback [18].
- **Special-education depth:** IEP/504, compliance, Medicaid, caseloads, alerts, mobile, and classroom context connect natively [6].
- **Eight role apps:** Mobile coverage spans families, students, teachers, administrators, nurses, counselors, special educators, and kiosks [7].
- **District configurability:** Custom fields, reports, rules, dashboards, and workflows support local processes [2] [19].

### Pricing Details

Edupoint publishes no product price list, tier table, per-student rate, per-school monthly price, or public implementation-fee schedule. Its official route is a district-specific demonstration and purchasing-timeline form, which confirms that pricing is quote-based and scoped to the SIS, special education, LMS, services, and selected modules [34]. Capterra lists Synergy LMS as “Get Price,” with no free trial and no free version [25]. Gartner describes subscription pricing generally based on enrolled students or school sites, with customized modules and possible implementation/support add-ons, but gives no verified dollar range [26]. Therefore, no reliable public currency, unit price, tier name, or setup fee can be reported as of November 24, 2026.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Synergy is unusually standards-oriented for a district SIS. Edupoint states that Synergy SIS is 1EdTech OneRoster 1.1 certified for rostering and grade passback, Ed-Fi certified, and SIF 2 enabled. It also advertises Google for Education/Classroom, Microsoft OneDrive and Microsoft 365-related directory work, Clever, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, nearly 400 LTI learning tools, MySchoolBucks, SchoolPay, Inspect, and Mastery Item Bank integrations [10] [11]. An API supports secure exchange with select LMS products, and premium cloud customers can purchase point-to-point VPN database access; however, Edupoint does not present a broadly documented public developer portal or an open marketplace in the reviewed pages. SSO is supported, including district Google login for StudentVUE and role-based access across the platform [8].

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The strongest public evidence is Edupoint’s SOC 2 certification, AWS-hosted cloud operations, field-level security, encryption, MFA/2FA, audit logging, vulnerability scanning, intrusion prevention, backup/disaster recovery, geo-redundant data centers, and 99.99% uptime claim [11] [12]. Edupoint states compliance with FERPA and HIPAA and describes COPPA handling in its privacy policy: districts retain control, Edupoint processes data for authorized educational purposes, and confidential data is not sold [23]. The platform supports IDEA/504 documentation, state reporting, CRDC, immunization tracking, learning standards, and Section 508/JAWS accessibility testing [23]. Hosting is described as AWS and geo-redundant, but no specific AWS region is published. No publicly reported breach or other security incident was identified in the sources reviewed. ISO 27001, GDPR, and India DPDP Act conformity are not publicly claimed on the reviewed pages and should be contractually verified.

### Strengths

- Broad K–12 coverage across SIS, enrollment, gradebook, LMS, assessment, MTSS, special education/504, analytics, portals, and mobile.
- Centralized data reduces duplicate entry across instructional and support workflows [32].
- Strong configurability, state reporting, health, special-education, and compliance support [6] [23].
- OneRoster, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, Google, Microsoft, LTI, payment, and LMS connections [10].
- Scale: 5.5M+ students, 7,000+ schools, and 750+ implementations claimed [1] [21].
- Gartner praises support; SoftwareReviews reports 7.2/10 composite and 7.6/10 CX [26] [27].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- G2’s 72-review profile is 2.7/5; complaints cite slowness, errors, inconvenience, and wasted time, while attendance and gradebook integration receive praise [24].
- Capterra’s three Synergy LMS reviews average 3.0/5; value for money is 2.0/5 and customer service 2.5/5. Reviews cite a less-friendly new gradebook, glitches, and iPad printing limits [25].
- SoftwareReviews users praise customization but cite a steep learning curve, complex implementation, and payment-gateway concerns [27].
- Gartner calls it not the most user-friendly platform and notes some desired functions are unavailable, despite excellent support [26].
- ParentVUE and StudentVUE iOS apps are each rated 1.7/5; complaints include missing features, duplicate notifications, freezing/loading, and interface regressions [28] [29].
- Quote-only pricing and customer-gated documentation increase buying and onboarding effort [21] [22] [25] [30] [34].

### Key Milestones

- **2003:** Bob Weathers founded Edupoint [3].
- **2006:** Edupoint and CPSI partnered on a certified Synergy SIF agent [10].
- **2010s:** Edupoint expanded mobile, registration, assessment, analytics, MTSS, and special-education workflows; individual launch dates are not published [3].
- **2020s:** Version 10, Synergy Mail, expanded LMS/EWS, lottery, athletics, and generative AI arrived [3].
- **2024:** Edupoint described generative AI across teaching, administration, communication, and special services [9].
- **February 2025:** Edupoint and ParentSquare announced SFTP and planned API integration [10].
- **December 2025:** Synergy won THE Journal’s SIS Product of the Year; that release cited 22 states versus the current 21-state claim [33].
- **March 2026:** Tennessee renewed Edupoint; 36 districts/185,000 students were using Synergy, with six new districts added [31].
- **June 2026:** Synergy won EdTech Breakthrough’s Next-Gen School Solution of the Year [32].
- **November 2026:** Current official positioning reports 5.5M+ students, 7,000+ schools, and 21 states; launch year and acquisitions remain undisclosed [1] [3].
