## #8. Veracross (Veracross LLC)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Veracross LLC; privately held and backed by BV Investment Partners after a 2019 recapitalization, according to Sage Consultancy [21]. |
| Headquarters | 701 Edgewater Drive, Suite 330, Wakefield, Massachusetts 01880, United States [1]. |
| Company founded (year) | 2003 [17] [21]. |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | 2002 as the founder's web-based “SIMS” (School Information Management System); the first paying Veracross customer followed in 2003 [2]. |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud SaaS and 100% browser-based/web-based; native mobile apps are available through Veracross-family/Digistorm products. No desktop client or on-premise deployment is publicly documented [1] [2] [3]. |
| Primary segments | Private and independent K–12 schools; boarding, international, parochial and other independent schools; medium-to-large schools are especially visible in independent implementation coverage [1] [21]. |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | 3,300+ schools and 70+ countries on the current home page, viewed 24 November 2026 [1]. Older pages use lower figures, so this is the current headline claim. |
| Official website (full URL) | https://www.veracross.com/ |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://www.veracross.com/veracross-360/ |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | https://community.veracross.com/ |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | https://www.veracross.com/pricing/ — public page exists, but it publishes no prices; pricing is tailored/quote-based [15]. |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | G2 seller profile: 4.5/5 from 122 reviews, viewed 24 November 2026; the Veracross product page itself shows 38 reviews [17]. Capterra: 4.3/5 from 13 reviews, viewed 24 November 2026; ease of use 4.1/5 and value for money 3.9/5 [18]. Apple App Store: “Veracross Directory for Admins” 1.2/5 from 14 ratings; “Veracross + Digistorm” had too few ratings to display an overview, both viewed 24 November 2026 [24] [25]. Google Play’s Veracross developer page did not display a Veracross SIS app rating or review count when viewed; it surfaced ePraise, so no Play Store score is asserted [26]. |

### Overview

Veracross is a school-specific, all-in-one information-management platform built around a “one-person, one-record” database. It links admissions, enrollment, academics, student life, communications, billing, accounting, advancement, health and selected school operations instead of requiring each department to maintain disconnected records. The vendor positions Veracross 360 as a platform for private and independent K–12 schools, with a single database, 200+ integrations and a 99% customer-retention claim [3].

The product began when founder Elliott Breuer built a web-based system for a K–8 independent school in summer 2002. The initial release had faculty, parent and student portals; the first paying customer followed a 2003 demonstration [2]. Company-founding references use 2003 [17] [21].

History requires careful disambiguation. Veracross publicly confirms its acquisition of Firefly Learning in February 2023 [14]. Sage Consultancy reports BV Investment Partners’ 2019 recapitalization and says the wider Veracross group has integrated Magnus, Firefly and Digistorm [21]. Ravenna was not a Veracross acquisition in the evidence reviewed: GeekWire reports that Education Brands acquired Ravenna Solutions in 2017 [23]. Full Measure Education was also not acquired by Veracross: Government Technology reports that StudentBridge acquired it in 2023 [22]. Ravenna remains a Veracross integration partner for admissions rather than a verified Veracross acquisition [12].

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser/cloud delivery:** Veracross describes itself as 100% web-based and available anywhere, and its history describes hosted delivery that removed server support from school IT departments [1] [2]. Sage independently characterizes it as proprietary, cloud-based SaaS [21]. The cloud provider and exact hosting regions are not publicly identified in the pages reviewed.
* **Desktop and on-premise:** No desktop client, self-hosted package or on-premise edition is publicly documented.
* **Mobile:** The family-facing strategy is a custom-branded Digistorm app with SSO, news, events, athletics, classes, grades, schedules and logistics requests [11] [20]. Apple also lists Veracross Directory for Admins and Veracross + Digistorm [24] [25].
* **Portals:** Parent/guardian, student, teacher, billing and solicitor portals are browser-based and configurable, not desktop products [10].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

The Admission Portal supports inquiries, applications, event and visit management, statuses, decision letters, deposits, file review, candidate profiles, pipeline reports, custom queries, branded email, automated reminders and re-enrollment. Enrollment data flows into academics and tuition management. Ravenna and SchoolAdmin are integrations, not Veracross-owned products [5] [12].

#### Student information and records

The core record connects students, households, guardians, faculty, staff, alumni and prospects, with rosters, directories, schedules, activities, academic documents, permissions and role-based access.

#### Attendance

Attendance is available in teacher workflows and family-facing schedules/reports; advanced monitoring can connect to partners such as Intellischool [4] [19].

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Scheduling covers rosters, calendars, course/teacher assignments, locations and daily routines; the family app exposes live schedules and assessments. Complex flex scheduling may require a partner [4] [11].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Teachers collect homework, manage class pages, record grades and use weighting/averaging; families see grades and assessments. No standalone high-stakes examination engine is publicly documented [4] [19].

#### Report cards and transcripts

The Teacher Portal supports report cards, progress reports, configurable academic documents and comments. Grades and report cards remain in Veracross even when teaching occurs in another LMS [4] [12]; a standard transcript format is not publicly specified.

#### Learning management and homework

The built-in LMS provides class pages, lesson planning, assignments and teacher-managed grades. Firefly Learning, acquired in February 2023, is complementary; Canvas and Google Classroom are named partners [4] [12] [14].

#### Communication

Native communication includes branded email, targeted messages, announcements, automation, reminders, confirmations and alerts stored against constituent records. SMS is referenced in the privacy policy; no native WhatsApp connector was found. Push is provided through Digistorm [5] [7] [11].

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Parent portals expose schedules, assignments, reports, calendars, extracurriculars, behavior notes, directories and household data; student portals provide homework access; teacher portals combine gradebook, reports and attendance. Billing and solicitor portals are separate role-specific views [4] [9] [10].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Tuition Management handles enrollment fees, deposits, tuition and incidentals, automatic payments, saved accounts, reminders, billing portals and payer support. Accounting includes general ledger, accounts payable, budgets, cash processing, purchase requests, property control, project/development accounting, reporting, reconciliation and FASB/GAAP-oriented statements plus 1099/1096 files [8] [9]. Sage reports international limitations in multi-currency, gateways, bank reconciliation, budgeting and localization [21].

#### HR, staff and payroll

Veracross records faculty/staff and can support contracts, benefits and HR workflows, but Sage reports that payroll is limited or non-existent for many non-U.S. schools and that onboarding is basic [21]. HR/payroll appears in the official partner directory, so schools should distinguish the core record from partner payroll functionality [19].

#### Transport

Transportation management is listed in the academics feature inventory, and family workflows can include transportation plans and absence requests. Dismissal and bus-attendance depth is a documented international-school gap in Sage’s implementation review [4] [21].

#### Library

No native library-management module or public feature page was identified in the reviewed Veracross materials. Libraries may connect through the Open API or partner ecosystem; this should be treated as an integration requirement, not a confirmed native module.

#### Hostel and boarding

Veracross markets boarding schools as a segment and its partner directory includes Boarding, but the public core feature pages do not detail room allocation, residential duty, meals or boarding attendance. Those capabilities should be verified as configuration or partner functionality rather than assumed native coverage [1] [19].

#### Inventory and assets

Accounting includes Property Control, and Sage discusses a fixed-asset module. Sage’s international-school review reports that the module can be costly and difficult to maintain, leading some schools to use external systems [8] [21].

#### Health and medical

Magnus Health, a Veracross-family health-record solution, supplies digital forms, reminders, immunization sync, treatment notes, Magnus911 emergency response, medication administration, check-in, counseling templates, athletic-injury tracking, reporting and SportsWare integration [13]. It is a connected product, not a claim that every medical workflow is in the base SIS.

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Epraise supplies positive and negative behavior capture, points, badges, certificates, rewards store, leaderboards, student self-report forms, intervention management, family communication, seating plans, dashboards and school-wide trend reporting, with Veracross SIS integration [10]. It is stronger on motivation and pastoral visibility than on a publicly documented statutory discipline case-management module.

#### Special education and safeguarding

No native special-education/IEP or safeguarding case-management module was publicly documented in the reviewed core pages. The partner catalog includes wellness, emergency-management and Education Modified student-support offerings, so schools should scope accommodations, child-protection workflows and audit requirements separately [19].

#### Alumni and fundraising

Development includes donor, pledge, soft-credit and tribute management; funds, campaigns and events; appeals; solicitation/moves management; wealth-screening data; donor acknowledgements; targeted communications; constituent history; event registration and reporting. The one-person record joins alumni, family, prospect and donor activity for long-term relationship management [6].

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Self-serve queries, point-in-time reports, visualizations, pipeline and financial reporting are central differentiators, with saved/shared workspaces and claimed data-hygiene scripts. Sage says some schools build data warehouses because dashboards can be insufficient internationally [3] [10] [21].

#### AI features

VC Studio is an AI analytics studio using natural-language questions to generate reports, charts, dashboards and visualizations; compare data; surface gaps; and explain results. Examples cover admissions, academics and development. Rollout scope, model, limits and pricing are not public [16].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Public materials document FERPA/COPPA-oriented privacy practices and FASB/GAAP financial statements, but no broad state-reporting catalog, Ed-Fi certification or SIF certification was found. State-specific attendance, assessment, special-education and government exports should therefore be verified by jurisdiction [7] [8].

#### Mobile apps

Digistorm provides custom-branded iOS and Android family apps with SSO, push, calendar, contacts, classes, grades, schedules, athletics and logistics. Apple also lists Veracross Directory for Admins and Veracross + Digistorm; ratings are uneven [11] [20] [24] [25].

#### Integrations and APIs

The Open API supports two-way sync, partner scopes, documentation, secure onboarding and school-built connections across LMS, admissions, health, emergency, websites/apps, boarding, parent engagement, invoice automation, college/career, cafeteria/POS and procurement [12] [19].

#### Security and privacy

The Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3 Type 2, PCI DSS, CCPA and COPPA resources. The September 2025 policy says Veracross does not sell student data or use it for behavioral advertising, deletes records within 30 days after termination and notifies schools within three days of discovering unauthorized disclosure [7] [27].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **One-person, one-record architecture:** A single constituent record connects admissions, academics, billing, development, communications and alumni history [3].
* **VC Studio AI analytics:** Natural-language prompts create dashboards, charts and reports with transparent result logic [16].
* **Admissions automations:** Triggered, targeted email sequences move families from inquiry through enrollment without redundant reminders [5].
* **School-specific development depth:** Moves management, soft credits, tributes, wealth-screening data and solicitor access are unusually deep for a K–12 SIS [6].
* **200+ partner ecosystem:** The Open API and partner portal support two-way exchange rather than only periodic file export [12] [19].
* **Cross-department financial reconciliation:** Tuition payments can be tagged to invoices and reconciled into connected accounting workflows [8] [9].
* **Configurable constituent portals:** Portal structures can be tailored for parents, students, staff, bill payers and solicitors [10].

### Pricing Details

The official pricing page is quote-only. It says Veracross tailors pricing to school size, type, modules and budget; it publishes no unit price, tier names, setup fee or implementation fee [15].

Capterra displayed a “Basic” starting price of $500 per month on 24 November 2026, but this is an aggregator estimate; it also says no free trial/version is available [18]. A comparison article reports estimated $15,000–$50,000+ full-suite deployments plus implementation/customization costs [28].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

The strongest evidence is for a rich proprietary Open API, two-way synchronization, SSO, a partner portal and 200+ partner connections. Named examples include Canvas, Google Classroom, Ravenna and SchoolAdmin, plus Magnus Health, Firefly, Epraise, Digistorm and specialist tools across health, boarding, emergency, payments, POS and procurement [12] [19]. The partner directory explicitly lists SSO, HR/payroll, LMS, reporting/analytics, payments, transportation, scheduling and website/CMS categories [19].

No public evidence reviewed confirms formal OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF certification, nor native Clever or ClassLink certification. Google Workspace appears through Google Classroom integration, but a full Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 connector catalog is not published. Payment processing is native through Tuition Management, while named gateway details are not public. The interoperability score therefore rewards API/SSO/marketplace breadth but does not assume standards certifications that were not found.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Veracross’s Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3 Type 2, PCI DSS, COPPA and CCPA resources [27]. Its September 2025 policy describes Veracross as a FERPA school official, provides COPPA guidance, prohibits selling student data/behavioral advertising, and says records are deleted within 30 days after termination [7].

The public materials reviewed do not establish ISO 27001 certification, India DPDP Act compliance, a specific data-hosting region, or the name of the cloud infrastructure provider. No publicly reported major security incident was identified in the sources reviewed through 24 November 2026; absence of a found report is not proof that no incident has ever occurred. Schools should request the current SOC report, DPA, subprocessor list, retention schedule, breach-notification terms and regional transfer mechanisms directly from Veracross.

### Strengths

* School-specific breadth spans admissions, SIS, academics, billing, accounting, development, health, behavior and integrations.
* The one-record model reduces duplicate household and student data and makes cross-department reporting possible.
* Admissions-to-enrollment-to-tuition workflows and advanced development/advancement tools are credible differentiators.
* The Open API, partner portal and 200+ integration network are unusually strong for a private-school SIS.
* Browser delivery avoids local server maintenance and desktop deployment.
* G2’s 4.5/5 seller rating and Capterra’s 4.3/5 product rating indicate generally positive user sentiment, though the sample sizes and product bundles differ [17] [18].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* Pricing is opaque: the vendor publishes no official rates, tiers or implementation fees; Capterra’s $500/month field and other ranges are third-party estimates [15] [18] [28].
* Sage reports rigid customization, vendor dependency, engineering delays, limited dashboards, weak multi-currency/payment localization, limited non-U.S. payroll and support-hour misalignment [21].
* Sage also reports weak fixed-asset maintenance, no dedicated withdrawals workflow and gaps in dismissal/bus-attendance tracking for some international-school deployments [21].
* Capterra reviewers praise the clean, unified interface but cite limited customization, workarounds, inability to email multiple course sections at once and difficulty exporting calendars to Google Calendar; one reviewer said two-factor authentication cost extra [18].
* The older Apple Veracross Directory for Admins app was rated 1.2/5 from 14 ratings and contains complaints about crashes, dark-mode behavior and limited parent usefulness [24]. The newer Veracross + Digistorm listing had too few ratings to display a score [25].
* TrustRadius users value the one-stop SIS, portals, assignments, grades and APIs, but its 8.4/10 score is based on 20 reviews and is a different methodology from G2/Capterra [29].

### Key Milestones

* **Summer 2002:** Elliott Breuer begins building the web-based SIMS system for a K–8 independent school [2].
* **2002–2003:** Initial SIMS release launches faculty, parent and student portals; the first paying customer follows, while company references use 2003 as the founding/serving-since year [2] [17].
* **2017:** Ravenna Solutions is acquired by Education Brands, not Veracross; Ravenna later appears as a Veracross admissions integration [12] [23].
* **2019:** Veracross is recapitalized/acquired by BV Investment Partners, according to Sage Consultancy [21].
* **2023:** Veracross announces its acquisition of Firefly Learning in February 2023; Firefly adds complementary K–12 LMS and engagement capability [14].
* **2023:** StudentBridge acquires Full Measure Education; this is a separate higher-education transaction, not a Veracross acquisition [22].
* **2024–2025:** Veracross 360 emphasizes the one-record database, 200+ integrations and 99% retention; the current Product Privacy Policy is effective September 2025 [3] [7].
* **2026:** Veracross home page claims 3,300+ schools and 70+ countries; VC Studio is presented as a new AI-powered analytics studio [1] [16].

## #9. Focus School Software (Focus School Software)

| Vendor / owner | Focus School Software LLC; private company. Andrew Schmadeke is founder and CEO; no parent company or acquisition is publicly disclosed in the reviewed company materials. [1] |

Apple and Google Play show many district-branded Focus apps, so no comparable platform-wide store score is reported. [5] [6] [7] [8] [9] |

### Overview

Focus School Software is a U.S.-focused student information and enterprise resource planning suite built primarily for large and midsize public-school districts. Its integrated SIS covers enrollment, student records, scheduling, attendance, gradebook, assessment, discipline, health, reporting and family portals, while Focus ERP adds finance, purchasing, assets, HR, payroll and employee self-service. The vendor also sells adjacent CTE/adult-education, special-student-services, analytics, communications, before/after-care, document-management, hall-pass and attendance-device solutions. [1] [2] [10]

The company says Andrew Schmadeke founded it in 2006 and launched the K-12 SIS that year. Current materials describe 180 employees, 3.7 million students across 16 states, and large implementations including Hillsborough, Fort Worth, Los Angeles Unified and Miami-Dade. No acquisition-led ownership history is disclosed. In February 2026, Focus added a state-approved Tennessee procurement route. [1] [3] [11]

### Platform Classification Explained

**Browser access and hosting.** Focus describes a web-based system available from any device through one login, interface and database. Its three-tier database/business-logic/presentation architecture uses a SQL relational database. Districts can use customer-owned servers or remote Focus servers, while the vendor also offers AWS-partner cloud hosting; this supports a hybrid rather than cloud-only classification. [2]

**Desktop and on-premise.** No installed desktop client is documented, but customer-owned servers are explicitly supported, so on-premise or district-hosted deployment exists. [2]

**Native mobile.** Focus describes a native Mobile Community/Focus App for iOS, Android and Windows. Apple’s developer page shows many district-branded Education View applications rather than one universal app. Mobile portals expose grades, attendance, schedules, assignments, messages, alerts, billing and other role-based functions. [2] [8] [12]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions, enrollment and school choice

Online enrollment and registration supports district-configured applications, supporting-document collection, multilingual forms, configurable edit rules, approvals, re-enrollment and school-choice applications. The school-choice workflow includes lottery assignment and parent/student notification. [13]

#### Student information and records

The core SIS holds configurable state/federal and district-specific fields, searchable student demographics, unlimited contacts and addresses, custody, emergency, legal-guardianship, pickup and communication-preference flags. Administrator documentation also exposes enrollment history, re-enrollment, vouchers, instructional method, threat classification, postsecondary placement, communication logs, letter logs, uploaded files, student summaries, change requests, seating charts, magnet/special assignments, Title I eligibility, ID badges and audit trails. [14]

#### Attendance and tardy management

Teachers can take attendance from desktop or phone in list or seating-chart views. Administrators receive missed-attendance alerts, edit records, manage excuse notes and contact parents; families receive real-time late/absence notifications and can upload excuse notes. Focus Kiosk handles sign-in/out for school, classes, clinics and offices, while the Mobile Scanner reads student-ID barcodes, marks tardies, prints slips and can print detention instructions. [15] [16]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Elementary scheduling supports constraints such as students together/apart, teacher assignment, behavior and testing criteria, an Optimize function for distributing students using gender, discipline and assessment data, and drag-and-drop placement. Secondary Master Schedule Builder supports periods, teacher availability, room use, course defaults, automated, teacher-approved and student-entered requests, scenario/build reports, sections, mass scheduling and drag-and-drop teacher schedules. Students, parents and teachers can view course-list or weekly-planner schedules. [17]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Focus Gradebook supports configurable calculations, categories, assignment types, completion and extra credit, student groups, assignment uploads, annotation, grading by standards, rubrics, points, percentages, correct/incorrect responses and proficiency. The assessment system supports district, school and teacher-created formative and benchmark assessments, state/national result imports, Student Portal delivery, live progress reporting, immediate results, 52 item types, accommodations and IEP-driven text-to-speech assignment. Learnosity and Certica Navigate Item Bank are named assessment partners. [18] [19]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Report cards can be published to portals or printed/mailed at school or district level. Students and parents receive real-time grades and progress reports, and can download or print unofficial transcripts from the portal. [20]

#### Learning management and homework

Focus is not presented as a standalone full LMS, but includes lesson planning, assignments, class resources, work upload and a student planner. A standalone Gradebook and Scheduling solution is listed; Moodle, Canvas, Schoology, Blackboard, Google Apps for Education and OneNote connections are documented. [1] [2] [5]

#### Communication

The communications module provides two-way messaging among students, parents, teachers and administrators; targeted announcements; SMS, email, portal alerts and letters; secure messages; scheduled one-time or recurring sends; automatic translation into more than 70 languages; polls with multiple-choice, reactions, true/false and free-response modes; sign-ups; message reporting; and voice/text-to-speech calling. No official WhatsApp integration was found. [10] [12]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Role-based portals provide alerts, announcements, news, recent/favorite programs, searches, knowledge-base access and the SIS menu. Student and parent portals expose enrollment, schedules, attendance, grades, assignments, calendar, news, events, class resources, links, forms, alerts, messages, report cards, transcripts and billing. Teacher portals support attendance, gradebook, lesson planning, messages, classroom resources and caseloads. [12]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Student Billing provides a sales/transaction-history/customer-ledger view and a portal/app shopping cart for courses, trips, parking permits, band, library and other fees. Parents, staff and teachers can pay by card or e-check; Focus Wallet stores payment methods, supports default settings, automatic payments and assigning cards to students through Authorize.net. ERP adds budgets, journal entries, purchase orders, invoices, checks, receipts, deposits, bank reconciliation, vendor tax forms and board-packet reports. [21] [22]

#### HR, staff and payroll

Focus ERP maintains pay steps, positions, leave banks, deductions and benefits; processes hourly/daily timecards, leave, adjustments, raises, bonuses and reimbursements; and gives employees self-service access to leave requests, pay stubs, benefits, workers’ compensation claims and tax forms. [22]

#### Transport

Transportation is not documented as a native operational module in the current feature pages. The technology page lists Versatrans, Trapeze Mapnet and EDULOG as integration targets, so transport interoperability exists but a native routing/fleet feature should not be claimed. [2]

#### Library

Library management is likewise not documented as a native Focus module. Follett Destiny Library Manager and Destiny Textbook Manager are listed as integrations. [2]

#### Hostel and boarding

No native hostel, dormitory or boarding-management module was found in the reviewed official feature pages or public administrator documentation.

#### Inventory and assets

ERP supports inventory reports, scheduled inventory, asset transfers and asset depreciation. The finance page also names purchasing, invoices, receipts and packing-slip document management. [22]

#### Health and medical

The Health module stores immunization and health records individually or in bulk, accepts parent-uploaded health documents, manages health forms, physician notes and alerts, medication needs and dispensing logs, screenings, consultations, assessments, medication administrations and clinic kiosk check-in/out. [23]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Discipline/PBIS supports online referrals, district rules and consistent consequences, automatic detention for excessive tardies, portal alerts, minor-infraction logging, positive-behavior badges, parent opt-in notifications and trend reports combining discipline with demographics, attendance and assessment data. Pastoral-adjacent workflows include mental wellness and threat assessment in Special Student Services. [24] [25]

#### Special education and safeguarding

Special Student Services covers IEPs, gifted and service plans, Section 504, threat assessment, mental wellness, MTSS/RTI for academic and behavior response, English-language learners, student services and medical processes. The configurable Form Builder offers validation, cloning, configurable headers, text areas, radio/checkbox groups, e-signatures and dropdowns; caseloads, events, portal alerts and compliance checks are built into workflows. [25]

#### Alumni and fundraising

No native alumni-relations or fundraising/advancement module was found in the reviewed Focus materials.

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Every SIS module has built-in reports; Ad Hoc Reports provide drag-and-drop design; District Custom Reports use SQL queries. Optional Analytics provides seven data areas, more than 40 dashboards, district/school/student snapshots, subgroup filtering, raw-and-visual views, nightly refreshes and teacher-scoped reporting. “What-if Analysis” projects enrollments from five prior years and can incorporate county population projections for five years. [26] [27]

#### AI features

No production AI assistant, generative-AI copilot or machine-learning assistant was identified in the official product pages, documentation or current press material. Focus’s predictive “What-if Analysis” is a rules/statistical projection feature, not evidence of an AI assistant. [26]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Point-of-entry validation, verification summaries, drill-down corrections and upload-ready extracts are core features. Official coverage includes Arizona AzEDS/Ed-Fi; California CALPADS; Florida DOE/FES/WDIS/FTE, ELL, exceptional-student, assessment, discipline, SESIR and FLEID; Massachusetts SIMS/EPIMS/SCS/SSDR and SIF; Maryland; New Hampshire I4See; New Jersey NJ SMART; Pennsylvania PIMS; Texas PEIMS/TREx/TSDS/STAAR; Utah UTRex; Missouri MOSIS; Ohio EMIS; and developing Washington, Louisiana, New York and Tennessee coverage. [2]

#### Mobile apps

The native Mobile Community/Focus App and district-branded iOS/Android applications provide portal access, messages, alerts, grades, attendance, schedules, billing and hall-pass actions. The technology page also states Windows support. Focus documentation separately covers kiosk, handheld, mobile and attendance apps. [2] [8] [28]

#### Integrations and APIs

Focus states that it supports API calls, OneRoster and Ed-Fi certification, secure FTP, batch processing and Manage Integrations tools. Named integrations include Canvas, Schoology, Blackboard, Google Apps for Education, Microsoft OneNote, Clever, ClassLink, Moodle, special-education systems, food-service systems, transportation systems, library systems and alert providers. Administrator documentation exposes Ed-Fi setup, descriptor maps, resource synchronization, logs, Blackboard APIs, Moodle API setup, Google Drive/OneDrive export and SSO. [2] [14] [28]

#### Security and privacy

Public security claims include MFA, encryption at rest and in transit, field-level security, high-profile-student information hiding, automatic backups, SAML/SSO and audit trails. The May 20, 2024 privacy policy says the website is hosted in the United States and describes U.S. transfers, COPPA treatment and reasonable safeguards. The reviewed materials do not establish SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification, GDPR/India DPDP compliance, a more specific data-center region, or a public security incident. [2] [29] [30]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **State reporting at district scale:** validation, extracts, IDs, submissions and verification workflows span many jurisdictions. [2]
- **No-code configuration:** Form Builder and workflow triggers support validations, approvals, e-signatures and alerts. [25] [28]
- **Predictive enrollment planning:** What-if Analysis uses five years of history and county population inputs. [26]
- **Unified SIS/ERP:** student, finance, HR and payroll data share one login, interface and database. [2] [22]
- **Advanced scheduling and assessment:** elementary optimization, secondary scenarios, 52 item types and IEP-linked accommodations. [17] [19]
- **Accessible operations:** mobile tardy hardware and two-way translation in 70+ languages extend the core platform. [10] [16]

### Pricing Details

Focus publishes no district SIS/ERP subscription rate card, tier names, per-student price or implementation fee. Capterra and Software Advice list pricing as contact-vendor, with no free trial or free version. [5] [6] [7] The guide’s approximately $3,000 SourceForge reference could not be verified and is not treated as subscription pricing. Hardware prices checked November 24, 2026 are $569 for a Focus Attendance Kiosk and $329 plus $14 shipping for a Mobile Scanner; these are not SaaS rates. [16]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Focus publicly claims OneRoster and Ed-Fi certification, API calls, secure FTP, batch processing and a Manage Integrations tool. Ed-Fi Alliance independently lists Focus SIS as certified for the Student Information Systems API for Data Standard v5 through February 19, 2027, with implementation verification in Glendale Union High School District and Higley USD, Arizona; earlier v4 and Suite 3 certifications are also listed. [2] [28] The public administrator help center documents Ed-Fi ODS credentials, version detection, resource and school synchronization, descriptor maps, debug transfers and logs. [14] Named ecosystem connections include Clever, ClassLink, Google Apps for Education, Canvas, Schoology, Blackboard, OneNote, Moodle, food service, library, transportation, alert, special-education and assessment systems. No 1EdTech marketplace, LTI certification or SIF certification beyond the specific Massachusetts state-reporting note was established. [2]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The technology page claims MFA, encryption at rest/in transit, field security, restricted visibility, AWS Partner status and backups. Its responsible-disclosure policy provides a vulnerability channel and typical 90-day remediation period. [2] [30] The May 20, 2024 privacy policy says the website is hosted in the U.S. and addresses COPPA, U.S. transfers and safeguards. Focus markets FERPA, HIPAA and COPPA alignment, but no public SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, DPDP, PCI-DSS attestation or incident disclosure was found. [2] [29]

### Strengths

- Deep K-12 public-district coverage with documented support for complex state reporting across many U.S. jurisdictions. [2]
- Strong adoption evidence: more than 3.7 million students, 16 states and several very large districts as of 2026. [1] [3]
- Broad native SIS/ERP scope, including finance, HR, payroll, health, special services, assessment, communications and portals. [1] [22]
- Configurability through custom fields, SQL/ad-hoc reports, Form Builder, workflow triggers and district-specific forms. [25] [26]
- Ed-Fi and OneRoster interoperability, open API claims, SSO options and numerous legacy education-system integrations. [2] [28]
- Users commonly praise one-place access to student data, simple grade entry and attendance, and strong reporting flexibility. [5] [6] [7]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is quote-only; neither Focus nor the major review sites expose a district subscription baseline, complicating procurement comparisons. [5] [6] [7]
- Reviewers report crashes, slowness or intermittent outages, although one reviewer noted that stability improved after modifications and another said downtime might be district-specific. [5] [6]
- Navigation can feel cluttered or dated, with many tabs, too many clicks, unclear workflows and limited screen personalization. [6] [7]
- Teachers report feature discoverability, training and support gaps; Capterra users cite difficult report-card printing and support access. [5] [6] [7]
- The product has no publicly evidenced native transport, library, hostel/boarding, alumni/fundraising or AI-assistant module; several rely on integrations or are not documented. [2]

### Key Milestones

- **2006:** Andrew Schmadeke founded Focus School Software; the company’s current anniversary release dates the K-12 SIS launch to 2006. [1] [3]
- **2010:** Company biography identifies development of the Focus ERP solution by 2010. [1]
- **2010s–2024:** Focus expanded from SIS into CTE/adult education, special services, ERP, assessment, communications, analytics and mobile; reviews and documentation show continuing Ed-Fi, SSO, workflow, forms and analytics work. [1] [3] [5] [6] [14]
- **February 19, 2026:** Focus was selected as an awarded vendor under Tennessee’s state SIS procurement, creating a state-approved purchasing pathway. [11]
- **May 4, 2026:** Focus announced its 20th anniversary, more than 3.7 million students, 16 states and more than 75% of Florida districts. [3]
- **August 21, 2026:** Public administrator documentation updated the Ed-Fi setup article, confirming active implementation guidance for current Ed-Fi integrations. [14]
- **November 2026:** G2 showed 4.0/5 from 13 reviews; no production AI assistant was documented in reviewed product pages. [7]

### Overview

Blackbaud K–12 Education Management is a connected suite for private and independent schools. Its core is the Student Information System (SIS), with Learning Management System (LMS) included, plus Enrollment, Billing/Tuition, Financial Aid, Financial Edge NXT, Raiser’s Edge NXT, and School Website options. The design goal is one core record, role-based access, and data flow from inquiry through alumni engagement [4] [9].

Blackbaud began in 1981 with student billing [3]. It acquired WhippleHill in 2014, adding cloud front-office, student-information, enrollment, learning, and content-management capabilities; WhippleHill reported 450+ schools [10]. Its 2015 $190 million Smart Tuition acquisition added tuition payments and accounts receivable for thousands of schools and 300,000+ families [11]. Launch dates for today’s named SIS/LMS are not publicly disclosed.

### Platform Classification Explained

**Browser and cloud.** Current pages describe a cloud platform with role-based portals and shared SIS/LMS data [1] [4] [9].

**Hosting and deployment.** Blackbaud does not name the cloud provider or K–12 data-residency region in the reviewed pages. WhippleHill was cloud-based, while the broader 2014 portfolio included cloud and on-premise products [10]; no current K–12 desktop or on-premise option was found.

**Mobile.** SIS/LMS and Billing are mobile-friendly [4] [9] [12]. School Journey is a separate branded iOS/Android partner app using Blackbaud ID, SKY API, roles, and push notifications [13], not a native Blackbaud K–12 app. Blackbaud Mobile documentation found here is for Fundraiser Performance Management [14].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment — Blackbaud Enrollment

Customizable application forms; school-level-specific checklists; inquiry and applicant tracking; automated reminders; configurable workflows; staff task management; committee review hub and candidate feedback; self-scheduling for visits, interviews, tours, and events; application status tracking; individualized enrollment contracts; deposits and payment-plan selection; integrated financial-aid awards; one-step reenrollment; dashboards and reports for inquiries, applications, contracts, and year-over-year enrollment progress [15].

#### Student information and records — Blackbaud Student Information System

A 360° Student View combines academics, activities, attendance, medical records, grades, graduation progress, and family information. Core records include students, parents/guardians, relationships, faculty, staff, advisors, classes, activities, athletics, and schedules. The family portal supports personal and medical information; roles limit records by relationship and security group [1] [4].

#### Attendance

Faculty can record class attendance, use daily bulk entry, and review attendance history. The suite includes dismissal and pre-excuse management; 2026 help-center updates document parent-submitted attendance. SIS/LMS screens and G2 reviews also describe attendance views, student photos, and attendance reporting [1] [5] [16].

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Administrators can configure complex schedules, assign classrooms and time slots, avoid conflicts, create schedule sets, and support rotations, custom days, and partial days. Students and advisors submit course requests; administrators review and approve them. “Find Me Now” locates students and teachers against the actual day schedule. Athletics adds game/practice locations, transportation information, and cancellation notices [1] [9].

#### Gradebook, assessment, and examinations

LMS provides a Gradebook with shortcuts, bulk actions, automated assessment grading, flexible grading methods, numeric or letter grades, criteria/mastery-oriented assessment, self-assessment, comments, quizzes, interactive assignments, discussions, online submissions, and assessment workflows. Blackbaud documents LockDown Browser support for assessments. The official pages do not establish a dedicated high-stakes examination-management module or public exam-board integrations [1] [9] [16].

#### Report cards and transcripts

SIS supports configurable grading formulas, role-based grade approval before faculty publication, report cards, recommendations, transcripts, graduation progress, and historical coursework. G2 users describe flexible grading output and report cards/transcripts, but also report that complex grading plans and customized reports require substantial configuration [5].

#### Learning management and homework

The integrated LMS includes a centralized assignment center, missing-work alerts, self-directed tasks, course pages, syllabus and content hosting, topics, stored coursework year over year, interactive assignments, group discussion, submissions, assessment, and feedback. It also supports advising, residential/community pages, groups, activities, extracurriculars, and athletics. Blackbaud positions it as included with SIS rather than a separate mandatory LMS purchase [9].

#### Communication

In-system messaging and real-time updates connect teachers, students, families, faculty, staff, administrators, advisors, coaches, and group leaders. Enrollment includes applicant-specific communication, automated reminders, and status updates. Financial Aid Management documents automated email and text reminders; Billing includes configurable payment notifications. Push notifications are evidenced for the third-party School Journey app. No official evidence was found for native WhatsApp integration; SMS/text is documented, while email and app push are supported in relevant workflows [13] [17].

#### Parent, student, and teacher portals

One parent/family portal shows all children’s records, grades, coursework, schedules, activities, messages, medical information, transcripts, contracts, financial aid, and tuition payments. Students get one login for assignments and resources; teachers get one login for classes, assignments, grades, attendance, and communication. The unified calendar is personalized by role and family relationship. Role-based access supports users with multiple personas, such as parent and teacher [1] [4].

#### Fees, billing, payments, and accounting

Billing Management is an accounts-receivable subledger: integrated enrollment contracts; payment plans and modalities; split payments by payer, percentage, or fee level; tuition, fees, incidentals, and shopping-cart items; bulk charges by class/program/team; financial holds; invoices; payment approvals; payment metrics; automated reconciliation; financial-aid discounts; and posting to Financial Edge NXT. Billing documents 256-bit encryption, PCI-DSS Level 1, MFA, and FDIC-insured custodial accounts [12].

#### Financial aid

Financial Aid Management supports need- and non-need-based awards, customizable applications and calculations, English and Spanish family applications, secure document upload, IRS integration for tax data, budgets by award source, disbursement tracking, batch awarding, automatic reallocation of unaccepted awards, verification/review services, reminders, reports, and integrated display of awards on contracts and payment portals [17].

#### HR, staff, and payroll

Staff/faculty records, role groups, faculty resources, and employee access are included in the record model. Native K–12 HR, payroll, benefits, or time-and-attendance was not evidenced [4] [18].

#### Transport, athletics, and activities

The LMS/SIS supports athletic rosters, practice/game scheduling, locations, transportation management, one-click cancellation notifications, team messaging, activities, advising, residential pages, and community groups. This is event/athletics transport coordination, not a documented standalone bus-routing or fleet module [9].

#### Library, hostel/boarding, inventory/assets, and health

The 360° view includes medical records; LMS includes residential/group pages; Marketplace partners cover medical records and lunch [4]. Native library circulation, hostel administration, inventory/assets, and full clinical-health modules were not documented, so schools should verify partner or configuration coverage.

#### Behavior, discipline, pastoral care, special education, and safeguarding

Student-life notes, advising, activities, role-based access, and conduct data are evidenced [5]. Capterra lists classroom management and special education, but no reviewed official page details dedicated special-education case management, safeguarding, incident, or pastoral-care modules; verify configuration or partners [7].

#### Alumni and fundraising — Raiser’s Edge NXT

The connected suite can carry family/student information into alumni status and the fundraising CRM. Raiser’s Edge NXT manages constituent records, giving history, campaigns, gifts, memberships, planned giving, events, donor reporting, prospect insights, stewardship, and donor communications. It integrates with enrollment and SIS so advancement teams can steward graduates and families; Financial Edge NXT connects fundraising and fund accounting [4] [18].

#### Analytics, dashboards, and reporting

Cross-department statistical dashboards cover enrollment, academics, finance, billing, and fundraising. Enrollment dashboards show funnel KPIs and trends; Billing dashboards show payments, cash flow, and net tuition; SIS/LMS provides lists, academic reports, report cards, transcripts, and school-wide calendars. Financial Edge NXT adds configurable financial dashboards, templates, drill-down reports, and role-based/view-only access. Users report that some report-building and query workflows are dated or less flexible than desired [5] [7].

#### AI features

Current Blackbaud positioning includes strategic automation, AI-driven financial-aid document review, AI-powered reconciliation and financial insights in Financial Edge NXT, predictive fundraising insights in Raiser’s Edge NXT, and natural-language assistance across Blackbaud AI page. The K–12 pages do not establish a production, K–12-specific AI tutor or universal student-facing assistant. AI is strongest in finance, fundraising, document review, and enterprise analytics rather than a dedicated classroom copilot [4] [17] [18] [19].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

It provides configurable records, attendance, grades, transcripts, reports, and financial reporting. No reviewed page confirms state-reporting, Ed-Fi, SIF, or a named government package; verify extracts.

#### Mobile apps

The core experience is web-based and mobile-friendly. For K–12, School Journey is the documented partner-based native route, using Blackbaud ID, roles, SKY API, branded apps, and iOS/Android push notifications [13]. Blackbaud Mobile documentation is for Fundraiser Performance Management, not K–12 SIS/LMS [14].

#### Integrations and APIs

Marketplace provides vetted partners including Google, Canvas, Microsoft, Turnitin, Respondus, Schoology, Magnus Health, Orah, Ravenna, Tableau, and specialized apps. The open-source SKY API and Microsoft Power Platform support custom development and automation. Blackbaud Education Management supports OneRoster and LTI 1.3 on the LMS page. Blackbaud’s older ON API is REST-based but reaches end of life March 31, 2027; new work should use SKY API. JSON Web Token SSO allows third-party applications to use Education Management as the identity provider [9] [20] [21].

#### Security and privacy

Trust Center badges and documents show SOC 2 Type II, SOC 1 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, CSA, HECVAT, NIST CSF, TX-RAMP, StateRAMP, and VPAT materials, plus MFA, centralized IAM/SSO, annual third-party penetration testing, incident response, subprocessors, deletion-on-request, and a DPA. Its Privacy Resource Center says customers remain responsible for controller obligations and applicable laws. No public K–12 hosting-region commitment was found [22] [23].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **360° Student View:** unifies academics, activities, attendance, medical records, grades, and graduation progress.
- **Enrollment-to-cash workflow:** contracts, aid, billing, payments, and ledger posting share data and login.
- **Independent-school scheduling:** rotations, partial/custom days, approvals, athletics, and “Find Me Now.”
- **Standards and extensibility:** OneRoster/LTI 1.3, SKY API, SSO, Marketplace, Microsoft Power Platform, and 50+ vetted partners [3] [4] [9].
- **AI in finance and aid:** automated document review, reconciliation, dashboards, and insights [17] [18].
- **Advancement continuity:** student records can flow into alumni and donor stewardship through Raiser’s Edge NXT.

### Pricing Details

Blackbaud’s pricing is quote-based and varies by organization size, users, modules, support, and services. The official page gives no currency, tier, per-student rate, setup fee, or school-monthly price, though it says implementation, training, and support are typically included [24]. Capterra displayed a third-party $21,000-per-year starting estimate on November 24, 2026; scope was unspecified, so it is not an official price [7]. G2 reports seven months average SIS implementation time [5].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Blackbaud documents OneRoster, LTI 1.3, SKY REST API, JSON Web Token SSO, Blackbaud ID, Marketplace apps, and Microsoft Power Platform [9] [20] [21]. Named connections include Google, Canvas, Microsoft, Turnitin, Respondus, Schoology, Tableau, Magnus Health, Orah, and Ravenna, plus Blackbaud Enrollment, Billing, Financial Aid, Financial Edge NXT, and Raiser’s Edge NXT. Ed-Fi and SIF certification, and certification on three or more listed standards, were not documented.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Blackbaud advertises SOC 1, SOC 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, NIST CSF, HECVAT, TX-RAMP, StateRAMP, and VPAT materials, plus monitoring, MFA, OWASP-oriented development, and Trust Center documentation [22]. FERPA, COPPA, India DPDP Act, and K–12 hosting-region commitments were not specifically documented; schools remain responsible for applicable legal compliance.

The 2020 incident is verified. BBC reported a May ransomware attack affecting at least 10 universities and other organizations, ransom payment, and July external disclosure [25]. The FTC said the breach went undetected for three months, exposed personal data of millions, involved 24 Bitcoin (about $250,000), and led to an order requiring deletion, an information-security program, and a retention schedule [26]. Reuters reported a $3 million SEC settlement in 2023 over misleading disclosures affecting 13,000+ customers [27]. Blackbaud’s 2024 release says the FTC settlement required no payment and involved no admission or denial [28].

### Strengths

- Broad private-school coverage from admissions and academics through billing, accounting, websites, and advancement.
- Strong shared-record, role-based, single-login architecture.
- Deep scheduling, grading, athletics, advising, and enrollment workflows.
- Mature Financial Edge NXT/Raiser’s Edge NXT extensions.
- Public SKY API, LTI 1.3/OneRoster, Marketplace, SSO, and partners.
- G2 SIS is 4.2/5 from 29 reviews, with praise for centralization [5].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Implementation is demanding: G2 reports seven months average SIS implementation, while reviews describe difficult startup and steep learning curves [5] [6].
- Capterra reviewers cite templated onboarding, inflexible configuration, and schools doing much of the implementation work [8].
- Users report inconsistent interfaces, dated/buried reporting, limited queries, slow imports, too many clicks, and clunky calendars [5] [6] [7].
- Support is mixed, with complaints about live chat and difficulty reaching higher-tier engineering [5] [6] [8].
- Cost, paid implementation, and cross-module dependencies recur in Capterra reviews [7] [8].
- The 2020 ransomware incident and later regulatory actions remain vendor-risk considerations [25] [26] [27].
- Native K–12 mobile coverage is unclear; schools may need a partner app [13] [14].

### Key Milestones

- **1981:** Founded; first project was private-school student billing [1] [3].
- **2004:** Initial public offering [2].
- **2014:** Acquired WhippleHill; its private-school business reported 450+ schools [10].
- **2015:** Announced $190 million Smart Tuition acquisition; it served thousands of schools and 300,000+ families [11].
- **2020:** May ransomware attack; July external disclosure [25] [26].
- **2023:** $3 million SEC settlement over disclosures [27].
- **2024:** FTC settlement announced; Blackbaud said it paid no FTC fine [28].
- **2025–2026:** Materials emphasized 5,000+ schools, SKY API, OneRoster/LTI 1.3, and AI [3] [4] [9].

## #11. Bromcom (Bromcom Computers plc)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Bromcom Computers plc, a UK public limited company (Companies House no. 02040690). |

[15] [19] [20] [21] [22] [23] |

### Overview

Bromcom is a UK school management information system (MIS) that combines pupil and staff records, attendance, assessment, examinations, behaviour, safeguarding, communication, parent and student engagement, reporting, finance and trust-level analytics. Its positioning is deliberately “one-stop shop”: the MIS, integrated school finance, MyChildAtSchool parent services, Student Portal, Teacher App, MAT Vision and Power BI are intended to reduce the number of bolt-on systems a school must operate. [1] [6] [8] [9]

The company was founded by Ali Guryel in 1986. Its milestones distinguish the complete Bromcom School MIS (2005) from the first UK cloud MIS (2011), so the company’s age should not be confused with the cloud product’s launch date. Bromcom also says MyChildAtSchool launched in 2002; Wikipedia’s independently sourced history dates the parent portal to June 2000. Public evidence reviewed here confirms Bromcom as a long-established supplier rather than a recently launched SaaS product. [2] [26]

Bromcom remains privately controlled according to independent market reporting, although the legal entity is a public limited company. It has expanded into integrated finance, MAT Vision, HR and AI-assisted workflows. Its latest public customer claim is 5,600+ schools, but independent reporting is more conservative and dated; buyers should reconcile “schools,” “users,” and active paid institutions. [1] [17] [18]

### Platform Classification Explained

- **Browser/cloud delivery:** The MIS and free apps are accessible from an online device with a web browser. Bromcom describes the service as fully managed and hosted on Microsoft Azure, with real-time access for staff, parents and students. [6] [7] [12]
- **Cloud provider and region:** Bromcom’s Trust Center identifies Microsoft Azure as the cloud provider and lists the hosting location as UK for the Bromcom MIS service. [24]
- **Desktop client:** No current Windows/macOS desktop client is identified in Bromcom’s current product pages or documentation portfolio. The reporting and administration tools are described as web-based.
- **On-premise option:** Bromcom markets cloud delivery and does not present a current on-premise edition. Hosting is included in the annual service charge and covers Azure costs. [12] [13]
- **Native mobile apps:** The exact named apps are **MyChildAtSchool - Parent App** for parents, **Bromcom Student App** for students, and **Bromcom Teacher App** for teachers. All three appear in Apple’s developer catalogue; the three corresponding Android listings are also present. [19] [20] [21] [22] [23]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrolment
Admissions is listed as a core module. Student tools support pre-admission search, onboarding, profiles, groups, contacts and school-specific fields; a full prospect CRM or online application funnel is not publicly evidenced. [4] [12]

#### Student information and records
The student record covers profiles, contacts, photographs, demographics, groups, characteristics, medical information, documents, permissions, flags, interventions, FSM and EAL. Dynamic groups can automatically add or remove students as attendance, assessment, behaviour or demographic criteria change. [4] [7] [12]

#### Attendance
Attendance covers statutory AM/PM, lesson, class, club and trip registers; quick registers; missing-register monitoring; code/subcode configuration; letters and notifications; scheduled reports; threshold groups; DfE benchmarking; dashboards; and mobile/tablet registration. [6] [7] [12]

#### Timetable and master scheduling
Cloud wTimeTable creates timetables from user-defined rules and relationships, flags clashes and blank sessions, supports timetable queries and connects to cover management. Parent/student timetable views, curriculum structures, room/equipment booking and a school diary are also included. [7] [12]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations
Assessment provides configurable marksheets, formative/summative tracking, headline figures, custom templates, calculations, colour-coded Primary Tracker marksheets, EYFS/test scores, statutory stages, cohort analysis and Excel import/export. Secondary examinations cover base-data imports, seating, submissions, results and internal/external workflows. [7] [12]

#### Report cards and transcripts
Student report cards are explicitly included for special schools. Reporting can attach Word templates, generate letters, certificates and reports, publish results to MyChildAtSchool and use mail merge. The reviewed public material does not confirm a higher-education-style transcript, credit or degree-audit function. [12]

#### Learning management and homework
Classroom Management includes assignments, homework and quizzes, lesson plans, seating plans, detentions and teacher dashboards. Bromcom AI can draft lesson plans, quizzes and homework; approved quizzes can be assigned to students and automatically marked. Bromcom is not presented as a full standalone LMS with a public LTI course catalogue. [10] [12]

#### Communication
The Communications module supports email, SMS, SMS Text Back, push notifications, school announcements, a school diary, parent/student/staff messaging, communication logs and automated messages driven by attendance, behaviour, watchlists or policies. SMS and email services can incur separate charges; the G-Cloud price sheet lists SMS bundles and SMTP packages. WhatsApp is not publicly documented as a native channel. [4] [12] [13]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals
MyChildAtSchool gives parents real-time timetable, homework, attendance, behaviour, assessment, clubs, trips, announcements, consent, parents’ evenings, payments, dinner money and school-shop access. Student Portal exposes attendance, timetable, behaviour, exams, lesson plans, events, clubs, documents and detentions. The Teacher Dashboard/App provides registers, behaviour events and messaging. [1] [4] [12] [19] [20]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting
Bromcom Finance is an integrated cloud accounting system with purchases, accounts payable/receivable, refunds, debit-card transactions, bank/VAT reconciliation, cost-centre and ledger links, budget profiles, payment mapping, dashboards, CFR/EFSA reporting and staff-contract salary data. MCAS supports dinner money, trips, clubs, wraparound care, instalments, shop products and stock control. [9] [12] [13]

#### HR, staff and payroll
The MAT Enterprise offer includes HR, while the MIS includes staff profiles, contracts, salary spine/base-pay structures, qualifications, background checks, CPD and Single Central Record (SCR) management. Bromcom documents workforce census and HR reporting. A complete native payroll engine is not clearly evidenced in the public material; Bromcom lists Access Education, Jane and other HR/payroll partners instead. [8] [11] [12]

#### Transport
No native transport-routing, fleet, bus-pass or vehicle-management module was found in Bromcom’s public product portfolio or reviewed documentation. Schools may integrate third-party systems through the API/partner ecosystem. [4] [5] [11]

#### Library
No native cataloguing, circulation, acquisitions or library-management module was identified in the reviewed public portfolio. [4] [5]

#### Hostel and boarding
No native hostel, boarding-house, room-allocation or residential-life module was identified in the reviewed public portfolio. [4] [5]

#### Inventory and assets
The core platform supports equipment and room booking, document management, school-shop product and stock control, and finance-linked purchasing. It is not publicly described as a full fixed-asset register or warehouse-management suite. [12] [13]

#### Health and medical
Health and Medical is a listed core feature for special schools. MyChildAtSchool lets parents update medical data; the MIS provides restricted access, documents and safeguarding records. Bromcom’s Trust Center states that customer personally identifiable, personal health and credit-card information are data categories it protects. [12] [24]

#### Behaviour, discipline and pastoral care
Behaviour Management records positive, challenging and neutral events, configurable policies, automated actions and follow-ups, points/tallies, certificates, dashboards, trend lines, rolling averages and cohort drill-down. Detention Management, suspensions, pathways, watchlists, alerts and behaviour communications are supported. [7] [12] [4]

#### Special education and safeguarding
SEND/SEN/ALN management, interventions, provision mapping, IEP/EHCP/IDP/PEP writing, statement-level tracking, student support and safeguarding are documented. Safeguarding includes incident logs, incident type, other agencies, body maps, attachments, timelines, restricted access and configurable alerts. [12] [5]

#### Alumni and fundraising
No alumni CRM, advancement, donor management or fundraising module was identified in the reviewed public portfolio. Online payments and school-shop functions are operational collections tools, not evidence of a fundraising suite. [4] [5] [12]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting
Analysis and Reporting combine ready-made reports, Quick Reports, Advanced Report Builder, ad-hoc joins, conditional formatting, charts, mail merge, scheduling and Excel/Word export. Dashboards cover attendance, behaviour, attainment, demographics, safeguarding, KS2/KS4/KS5, benchmarking, pupil groups and finance. MAT Vision adds cross-school consolidation, drill-down, central configuration, exports, live feeds and embedded Power BI; Tableau is also referenced. [1] [8] [12]

#### AI features
Bromcom AI is a production school co-pilot integrated into the MIS. It uses Microsoft Azure/OpenAI services for general queries, multilingual translation, lesson plans, quizzes, homework, letters and emails, with prompts, tone/length controls and automatic quiz marking. Internal-data insight, trend analysis and pupil-report summaries are publicly described as coming soon, so predictive analytics should not be treated as fully shipped. [10] [13]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance
Bromcom supports DfE School Census, Workforce Census, statutory returns, validation and summary reports, Consistent Financial Reporting, Welsh Census, Hwb integration and Catholic Census. The platform is designed around UK statutory reporting rather than US state reporting. [6] [9] [12]

#### Mobile apps
The parent, student and teacher apps provide native iOS and Android access. The Student App exposes attendance, timetable, behaviour, exams, lesson plans, events, clubs, documents and detentions, and supports Microsoft/Google SSO where enabled. The Parent App handles engagement, messaging, attendance, payments and school information; the Teacher App supports daily teacher tasks. [19] [20] [21] [22] [23]

#### Integrations and APIs
Bromcom publishes a secure web-service API and API-partner programme. Documented connections include Google, Office 365, Microsoft/Google/Active Directory login, Power BI, Tableau, Excel add-in, Hwb, SIMS Connector for Vision, payment providers and partners for HR/payroll, analytics, admissions, catering, identity, visitors, safeguarding and communications. OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever and ClassLink certification is not publicly evidenced. [4] [5] [11] [12]

#### Security and privacy
Role and field-level permissions, audit trails, time/location controls, two-factor authentication, SSO, restricted safeguarding areas and secure APIs are documented. Bromcom’s Trust Center lists ISO 27001:2022, Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus, Azure UK hosting and a public subprocessors list. Its privacy policy treats Bromcom as a processor for school/MAT data and cites UK GDPR rights. [12] [24]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Integrated MIS plus Finance:** A single cloud data model links pupil, staff, purchasing, budgeting, statutory finance and parent payments rather than requiring a separate FMS. [9]
- **MAT Vision:** Trust teams can consolidate data across Bromcom and non-Bromcom schools, drill from trust to school, cascade configuration and embed Power BI dashboards. [8]
- **AI content workflows:** Bromcom AI can draft lesson plans, quizzes, homework, emails and letters inside the MIS, translate them and auto-mark approved quizzes. [10]
- **Dynamic groups and automated workflows:** Attendance, behaviour, assessment and demographic rules can create cohorts, alerts, letters and follow-up actions without manual re-keying. [6] [7]
- **UK statutory depth:** DfE, workforce, Welsh, Catholic and CFR/EFSA reporting is unusually central to the platform’s UK-market design. [6] [9] [12]
- **One parent account across children:** Parents can view multiple children, book appointments, provide consent and pay for clubs, trips, meals and shop products from MCAS. [12]

### Pricing Details

Bromcom’s public pricing page is per-pupil and quote-based. Standard includes core MIS, assessment, attendance, census, communication, cover, exams, reports, statutory returns, teacher app and timetable; Plus adds analysis, behaviour, classroom management, clubs/trips, dinner, MCAS, Primary Tracker, Power BI and Student Portal; One-Stop-Shop adds advanced reporting, AI, CPD, Google/Office 365, Options and Safeguarding. [3]

The February 2025 G-Cloud 14 schedule is a dated public-sector reference. Combined MIS and Finance is **£6.55/£9.55/£11.55 per primary pupil** for Standard/Plus/One-Stop-Shop and **£9/£10/£12 per secondary pupil**; support is separate and Azure hosting is included. [13]

The schedule lists primary onboarding at £250/£600 and secondary at £250/£1,100 depending on migration, £500 academy-conversion fees per MIS or Finance, online payments at 1.275% per transaction, SMS from £300 per 5,000 and SMTP from £99 annually. Re-quote because the document is dated. [13]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Bromcom has a public API partner programme and secure web-service API. Documented connections include Azure, Microsoft 365, Google, Active Directory, Microsoft/Google SSO, Power BI, Tableau, Excel, Hwb, SIMS Connector for Vision, payments, SMS/SMTP and partners for HR/payroll, analytics, admissions, catering, identity, visitors, safeguarding and communications. [11] [12] [24]

The reviewed material does not verify OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever or ClassLink certification. Its API ecosystem is open, but public evidence does not support a claim of multi-standard certification.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Bromcom’s Trust Center lists ISO 27001:2022, Cyber Essentials, Cyber Essentials Plus, UK Azure hosting, technical/organisational measures and subprocessors. Its privacy policy describes Bromcom as a processor for school, LA and MAT data under UK GDPR and recognises data-subject rights and transfer safeguards. [24]

No public evidence was found for SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA or India DPDP Act certification. Schools remain data controllers for pupil data.

Bromcom disclosed a September 2026 SSO-registration incident. Its FAQ says an unauthorised party accessed a separate component and retained some registration email addresses, but not passwords, tokens, MIS data or authentication services; Bromcom withdrew the legacy function, added checks and improved logging. [25]

### Strengths

- Broad native UK-school coverage spanning MIS, assessment, attendance, behaviour, safeguarding, parent engagement, finance and MAT oversight.
- Azure cloud delivery, browser access and native apps reduce dependence on school servers.
- Integrated Finance, parent payments, activities, statutory reporting, MAT Vision, Power BI, workflow automation and a public API ecosystem can replace bolt-ons.
- Public trust centre, ISO 27001:2022 and Cyber Essentials/Plus evidence support procurement due diligence.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- G2 had no verified reviews and EdTech Impact had no reviews when checked, so independent enterprise-user evidence is thin. [14] [15]
- Trustpilot was 1.5/5 from 42 reviews on 24 November 2026; complaints included slow loading, crashes, login problems, a confusing interface, difficult reporting and term-start reliability. [16]
- Google Play and Apple reviews cited student login failures, lag, homework/attendance/timetable problems and crashes; an Apple Teacher review reported register-taking crashes. [20] [21] [23]
- The public pricing page is quote-based; only a dated G-Cloud schedule exposes numbers, making like-for-like budgeting difficult.
- Transport, library, hostel/boarding, alumni/fundraising and full payroll are not evidenced as native modules, and major interoperability standards are not publicly certified in the reviewed sources.
- The September 2026 SSO incident, although Bromcom says it was limited to registration email addresses and did not affect the MIS, creates additional due-diligence work for schools. [25]

### Key Milestones

- **1986:** Ali Guryel founded Bromcom in London; Companies House records incorporation on 24 July 1986, initially as Shoebox Ltd. [2] [18]
- **2000/2002:** MyChildAtSchool parent-portal launch is dated 2000 by Wikipedia’s independent history and 2002 by Bromcom’s own milestones. [2] [26]
- **2005:** Bromcom launched its complete School MIS. [2]
- **2011:** Bromcom launched the UK’s first cloud-based MIS for schools. [2] [17]
- **2012:** Bromcom won a place on a DfE £575m framework for cloud MIS and learning-platform services to local authorities. [2]
- **2024:** Bromcom reported an Education Authority Northern Ireland contract covering 1,100+ schools. [2]
- **2025:** Wrexham became the first Welsh local authority to select Bromcom’s cloud MIS for 71 schools; the G-Cloud pricing schedule was prepared in February. [2] [13]
- **2026:** Bromcom celebrated 40 years, launched/expanded Bromcom AI and disclosed the September SSO-registration incident in an October FAQ update. [1] [10] [25]
