| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | Viewed 24 Nov 2026: G2 3.9/5 from 95 Jenzabar reviews; Capterra Jenzabar One 4.0/5 from 33 reviews, with ease of use 3.6 and customer service 3.9; Apple App Store Jenzabar Mobile 1.8/5 from 5 ratings; Google Play Jenzabar Mobile rating/review count was not exposed in the opened page text, but the listing showed 1K+ downloads [11] [12] [13] [14] |

### Overview

Jenzabar is a Boston-based, higher-education-only ERP/SIS vendor whose current umbrella is Jenzabar One: a unified ecosystem combining ERP, student information, CRM, LMS, analytics, AI, finance, financial aid, HCM, advancement, communications, retention, workflow, and continuing-education commerce. It is a higher-ed lifecycle platform, not a K-12 school-management suite [6] [15].

The company began in 1998 with an internet portal for course enrollment and assignments, then used acquisitions to assemble a broader portfolio. ListEdTech identifies RJM Systems/SONIS as a 2015 acquisition; Jenzabar’s current portfolio also reflects later acquisition of Spark451 for enrollment marketing. Jenzabar One was publicly prominent as a cloud-ready platform by 2018, but its first commercial launch year is not disclosed [4] [5] [16].

Jenzabar targets small and mid-sized higher-education institutions, especially schools with 5,000 or fewer students, while also serving public, specialized, online, and non-traditional programs. Its latest company claim is more than 1,400 campuses worldwide (August 2026), but it does not publish a student total or a country-by-country customer count [9].

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser/cloud:** Jenzabar One and J1 Web are browser-accessible applications. Jenzabar One SaaS says Jenzabar hosts and manages the software in an always-available cloud environment, with nightly backups and 24x7x365 monitoring [6].
* **Hosting provider:** Jenzabar Cloud Services identifies top-tier Google Cloud commercial data centers, 99.95% minimum uptime, failover, rolling 30-day backups, immutable ransomware-protection backups, and 24x7x365 infrastructure monitoring [7].
* **Desktop:** The official help center still documents J1 Desktop modules for accounts payable/receivable, admissions, advising, budget, financial aid, fixed assets, general ledger, HR, payroll, registration, student life, security, and web administration. Independent reviews describe the desktop client alongside the newer J1 Web interface [8] [12].
* **On-premise/hybrid:** The documented J1 Desktop estate and migration language show a hybrid transition path, but a current separately priced on-premise tier is not stated and should not be assumed for a new purchase.
* **Mobile:** Jenzabar Mobile is a native iPhone/iPad and Android app. Depending on institutional configuration, it provides announcements, blogs, calendar, directory, groups, maps, tours, notifications, forums, targeted messages, eLearning attendance/coursework/gradebook, registration add/drop, grades/transcripts, financial aid, and bill payments [13] [14]. Jenzabar also produces institution-branded apps through its mobile platform.

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions, recruitment, and enrollment

Jenzabar Recruitment is a cloud CRM for constituent capture, engagement histories, personalized outreach, recruitment strategy tracking, and a mobile-first applicant portal. Students can start, track, complete, and submit applications. Registration supports catalogs, availability, prerequisites, non-course prerequisites, holds/warnings, add/drop/cancel, transfer-course evaluation, reactivation, GPA rules, student classifications, honors/probation, and self-service or walk-in registration [15] [17].

#### Student information and academic records

Jenzabar Student is the core SIS with centralized student information, catalogs, real-time records, competency-based education, micro-credentials, badging, open-entry/open-exit programs, curriculum trees, degree requirements, classifications, batch processing, watermarked/unofficial transcripts, and IPEDS/NCES reporting [17].

#### Attendance, timetable, and scheduling

Attendance is exposed through eLearning and the mobile course experience and is used as a retention signal. Registration handles course offerings, conflicts, prerequisites, add/drop dates, and availability. No distinct K-12 master timetable or bus-style bell scheduler is documented [13] [17].

#### Gradebook, assessment, and examinations

Jenzabar eLearning includes gradebook, coursework, course organizer, syllabi, forums, course information, and attendance. Jenzabar Student supports unlimited grading options, multiple GPAs, academic standing, grading dates, and degree evaluation. Public pages do not claim a separate secure examination-proctoring product [13] [17].

#### Report cards and transcripts

The SIS provides unofficial/watermarked transcripts, real-time academic history, GPA calculations, degree audits, completion status, academic plans, graduation processing, and transcript/grade visibility in the mobile app. Traditional K-12 report-card terminology is not used; higher-ed academic records and transcripts are the native equivalent [13] [17].

#### Learning management and homework

Jenzabar eLearning is the LMS for online, in-person, or hybrid courses. It includes course management, calendars, syllabi, coursework/homework, forums, classmates, attendance, gradebook, and academic-data integration [13] [18].

#### Communication

Jenzabar Communications consolidates profiles, engagement histories, two-way messaging, SMS/texting, email, email tracking/deliverability analysis, interaction feeds, internal comments, notifications, and targeted messages. No reviewed page verifies native WhatsApp support or a specific push vendor; centralized notifications are present in Jenzabar Mobile [19] [20].

#### Parent, student, and teacher portals

Student self-service covers registration, academic plans, degree progress, grades, transcripts, aid requirements, document upload, offer acceptance, bills, payments, and mobile access. Faculty/staff use J1 Web/Desktop, eLearning, advising, alerts, workflows, and HR self-service. A separate parent portal is not publicly identified [13] [17] [21].

#### Fees, billing, payments, and accounting

Jenzabar Finance includes General Ledger, Budget, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Purchasing, and Fixed Assets. Student-facing functions include bills, payments, payment plans/financial-account messaging, and transactions. Campus Marketplace adds registration, secure payment, orders, credits, and non-traditional-program commerce. Capterra reviewers have complained about the absence of a native payment gateway in some deployments, so scope should be confirmed contractually [12] [22].

#### HR, staff, and payroll

Jenzabar HCM has Personnel and Payroll: applicant tracking, position definitions, search-committee workflows, tasks/messages/notifications, staff directory, HR calendar, multiple positions, shifts/differentials, benefits, time and attendance, overtime, salary histories, electronic forms, pay statements, W-2s, 1095-Cs, wage/tax reports, accruals, leave workflows, and compensation adjustments [23].

#### Transport

No native transport, routing, vehicle tracking, or bus-parent notification module was identified in the reviewed Jenzabar One product list. The Student product does include vehicle registration, permits, fines, and sanctions for campus vehicles [17].

#### Library

No native library-management or circulation module was identified in the reviewed current product pages or official help index. Library services would require an integration or separate system.

#### Hostel and boarding

Student Life Residence Life covers housing applications, applicant groups, roommate matching, lotteries, student self-selection, assignments, occupancy dashboards, check-in/check-out, room-condition reports, damage billing, keys, and housing-related incidents [17].

#### Inventory and assets

Finance Fixed Assets manages acquisition, lifecycle, disposal, depreciation, and asset processing. Purchasing and Accounts Payable cover vendor activity and purchasing control. General inventory/warehouse management is not advertised as a separate module [22].

#### Health and medical

Student Life Student Health tracks immunization requirements, emergency contacts, health-insurance information, and health requirements for classes/programs. This is student-health administration, not a clinical electronic medical-record system [17].

#### Behavior, discipline, and pastoral care

Student Conduct provides incident reporting for housing, faculty, Title IX, and other matters; case management; violations; sanctions; appeals; and federally compliant campus-crime reporting. Retention and advising provide alerts, case ownership, interventions, meetings, and outcomes, which together support pastoral/student-success workflows [17].

#### Special education and safeguarding

The reviewed materials do not identify a dedicated special-education IEP/504 module. Safeguarding-related capabilities are indirect: conduct and Title IX incidents, sanctions/appeals, health records, permissions, alerts, and role-based access. Institutions needing K-12 safeguarding casework should validate fit rather than assume it.

#### Alumni and fundraising

Jenzabar Advancement manages constituent profiles, prospect identification/cultivation, gift and scholarship information, campaigns, gift accounting, donor stewardship, alumni relations, dashboards, communications, and campaign-effectiveness analysis [24].

#### Analytics, dashboards, and reporting

Jenzabar Analytics has Insights, Data Lake, and AI Assist for Analytics. Insights covers program health, admissions funnels, financial health/CFI, and retention. Retention Risk uses predictive modeling and risk scores; Data Lake uses Azure Databricks with ERP/LMS/CRM connectors and supports Tableau and Power BI [25].

#### AI features

Jenzabar Chatbot uses natural-language processing, hundreds of preconfigured question/answer patterns, configurable answers, and satisfaction surveys. AI Assist for Analytics answers plain-language questions over governed data. Student materials also describe AI-powered administrative tools with institutional guardrails and human oversight. The privacy policy identifies OpenAI, Databricks, and Google as providers in certain modules and says client data is not used to train providers’ models without permission [17] [26] [27].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Student supports IPEDS and NCES reporting; Financial Aid imports Department of Education data, manages funds to/from COD, recalculates cost of attendance, and supports compliance-oriented reporting. HCM provides federal/state wage and tax reports; Conduct provides federally compliant campus-crime reporting [17] [21] [23].

#### Mobile apps

Jenzabar Mobile is the named cross-platform native app, with institution-specific connection codes. It exposes campus content, learning, self-service registration, grades/transcripts, aid, and payments. The Apple listing showed 1.8/5 from five ratings on 24 Nov 2026; the Google Play page showed 1K+ downloads but no visible rating count in the opened page [13] [14].

#### Integrations and APIs

Jenzabar One API enables secure access to and manipulation of data. Jenzabar Unity Platform is a low-code/no-code iPaaS powered by Boomi. Campus Marketplace advertises a public API, and Softdocs provides an integration toolkit and API framework for document management, electronic forms, and workflow. Jenzabar also advertises connectors to Tableau, Power BI, ERP/LMS/CRM systems, and the Department of Education/COD [6] [22] [25] [28].

#### Security and privacy

Jenzabar Cloud Services reports SOC 2 for SaaS offerings; Google Cloud facilities with annual SOC-1, SOC-2, and SOC-3 audits; PCI and HIPAA compliance; ISO 27001, ISO 27017, and ISO 27018; encryption, network segmentation, EDR, backups, and 24x7 monitoring. The privacy policy describes Jenzabar as a processor for client data, secure cloud storage, international transfers using safeguards such as standard contractual clauses, role/permission controls, and client-directed processing. FERPA, COPPA, and India’s DPDP Act are not expressly claimed in the reviewed public materials. No publicly reported Jenzabar security incident was found in the reviewed sources [7] [27].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **AI Assist for Analytics:** Plain-language questions over governed institutional data reduce dependence on SQL and ad-hoc reporting [25].
* **Predictive retention:** Retention Risk assigns risk scores so staff can prioritize early interventions [25].
* **Production AI chatbot:** Configurable NLP question-answering provides always-on student self-service and satisfaction feedback [26].
* **Low-code/no-code integration:** Unity Platform, powered by Boomi, connects tasks and systems without every workflow becoming custom code [6].
* **Higher-ed-specific data model:** Curriculum Trees, degree audits, holds, transfer evaluation, financial-aid eligibility, and student-life records share an institutional system of record [17].
* **Continuing-education commerce:** Campus Marketplace combines branded storefront, waitlists, payments, subscriptions, dual-enrollment workflows, and public API access for non-degree programs [22].

### Pricing Details

Jenzabar has no public list-price page, per-student rate, named tier, free plan, or implementation-fee schedule. Its public call to action is contact-sales, and Gartner describes modular pricing based on enrollment, modules, and subscription versus perpetual licensing [6] [10] [29]. Pricing is therefore quote-based and institution-specific; Capterra mentions support pricing as a pain point but provides no verifiable currency or unit rate [12].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Jenzabar publishes a Jenzabar One API, the Boomi-powered Unity Platform iPaaS, a public API for Campus Marketplace, and a partner integration toolkit/API framework through Softdocs. Named interoperability points include Tableau, Microsoft Power BI, Google Cloud/Azure Databricks, Department of Education/COD, external ERP/SIS/LMS/CRM systems, and document-management/workflow partners [6] [21] [22] [25] [28]. The reviewed public sources do not verify certification or native support for OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, or ClassLink; Microsoft 365/Google Workspace and payment-gateway breadth are also not specified as formal standards-level integrations. This is a rich API/partner ecosystem, but not evidence for a standards-certified open ecosystem.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Jenzabar’s cloud-services sheet reports Google Cloud, 99.95% minimum uptime, 24x7x365 monitoring/EDR, rolling and immutable backups, SOC 2 for SaaS, and Google Cloud claims for SOC-1/2/3, PCI, HIPAA, and ISO 27001/27017/27018 [7]. Its privacy policy states that it processes client data at client direction, uses encrypted cloud servers, supports EEA/UK/Swiss safeguards, and transfers data internationally as needed [27].

The sources do not explicitly claim FERPA, COPPA, or India DPDP Act compliance, nor do they specify customer-selectable hosting regions. No publicly reported Jenzabar breach or material security incident was identified in the sources opened for this profile; that is not a guarantee that none has ever occurred.

### Strengths

* Broad higher-ed lifecycle coverage: admissions through registration, aid, learning, retention, finance, HCM, advancement, and alumni.
* Strong student-success toolkit combining degree audits, curriculum rules, early alerts, predictive retention, communications, and workflow automation.
* Credible cloud operating model with Google Cloud, backups, monitoring, EDR, high-availability claims, and published ISO/SOC evidence.
* Good fit for small and mid-sized institutions: modular purchasing and replacing point systems are recurring positives [4] [12].
* Continuing-education commerce and Spark451 enrollment marketing broaden the platform beyond a conventional SIS.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* The user experience is uneven across generations: Capterra reviewers describe the legacy interface as dated, “clunky,” and click-heavy, while other reviewers like the newer web experience [12].
* Cloud migration and feature parity are works in progress; reviewers report that some desktop functions are not yet available in J1 Web and that rollout across modules has been slow [12].
* Training and change management can be demanding because the product is broad and some areas retain older interaction patterns; Gartner reviewers also describe help-desk support as inconsistent and HCM as less built out [12] [29].
* Performance, updates, and support pricing are recurring concerns in reviews; one reviewer cited slower processing, another cited frequent updates/downtime, and another cited support cost linked to enrollment bands [12].
* eLearning is not a substitute for a best-of-breed LMS in every institution: a reviewer said it was cumbersome for instructors and that publisher tools did not integrate well [12].
* Mobile-app sentiment is weak in the small Apple sample (1.8/5, five ratings), including a complaint that the app crashed at login; the sample is too small to generalize to all branded deployments [13].

### Key Milestones

* **1998:** Jenzabar founded; its first concept was an internet-based course-enrollment and assignment portal [2] [4].
* **Early 2000s:** The company expanded through acquisitions in college administrative software [4].
* **2015:** Jenzabar acquired RJM Systems/SONIS, which retained the SONIS name [4].
* **2017:** Jenzabar announced new Advancement tools, expanding the lifecycle suite beyond SIS and ERP [5].
* **2018:** Jenzabar One was publicly positioned as a cloud-ready unified student system with mobile access, analytics, workflow, messaging, ERP/finance/HR/SIS integration, and eLearning [5].
* **2018–2020:** Partnerships with Docubase and Softdocs expanded document management, electronic forms, and workflow interoperability [5] [28].
* **2019:** Jenzabar introduced Analytics with dashboards and data-driven decision support [25] [30].
* **2020s:** Jenzabar acquired Spark451 and made enrollment marketing and non-traditional-program growth part of the broader portfolio [4] [9].
* **2021:** Jenzabar Communications Plus added two-way texting, email tracking, constituent interaction histories, and internal comments [20].
* **2025:** Jenzabar reported more than 200 solutions selected and more than 50 implementations during the year; the current SaaS page reports 200+ solutions selected in 2025 and 300+ institutions on Jenzabar One [6].
* **2026:** Jenzabar reported more than 200 solutions selected, 19 institutions live in H1, and more than 1,400 campuses worldwide [9].

### Overview

Infinite Campus is a U.S.-focused K–12 SIS combining a district student database with instruction, family engagement, communications, payments, food service, workflows, analytics and state exchange. Campus SIS is the core; Campus Learning adds an LMS, and Campus Parent/Student provide family access. The vendor advertises 1,500+ tools and a vetted Extension Marketplace. [4] [9]

The company began in 1993 when founder Charlie Kratsch worked with his former Minnesota district on student administration. Its history records expansion beyond the SIS into Food Service, Online Payments, Online Registration, Messenger and learning management, followed by machine-learning dropout prediction. [1] Infinite Campus says it has not acquired another SIS or company and remains employee-owned. [10]

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser and cloud delivery:** Campus SIS is described as web-based and as a single, cloud-based platform in independent and government descriptions. The North Carolina Department of Public Instruction says its statewide implementation was completed on 1 July 2025 as a unified cloud-based platform. [5] [11]
* **Hosting:** Customer data is in secure U.S.-based data centers, with separate databases and daily backups/30-day snapshots; no cloud provider is named publicly. [3]
* **Desktop/on-premise:** No current desktop client or customer-managed on-premise option was identified; treat it as web/cloud software unless a district contract says otherwise.
* **Native mobile:** The exact consumer app names are **Campus Parent** and **Campus Student**, available for iPhone/iPad and Android; **Campus Mobile Payments** is a separate iOS/Android app for Bluetooth card-reader payments. The parent and student apps expose announcements, assignments, attendance, grades, schedules, notifications, and other district-enabled items. [7] [8] [12]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

Campus Online Registration supports new and returning student applications, open enrollment, responsive questions, parent access through Campus Parent, district websites, mobile devices and kiosks, status emails, uploads such as utility bills, birth certificates and transcripts, application/enrollment reports, and approval that writes directly into Campus Census. It can collect tuition agreements and payment plans when paired with Campus Payments. [13]

#### Student information and records

Campus SIS is the real-time record for census/demographics, households, enrollments, calendars, schedules, attendance, grades, assessments, programs, documents, behavior, health, special programs, graduation plans, transcripts, staff and courses. Role permissions govern access. Data Suite adds validation rules, change history and access auditing. [3] [14]

#### Attendance

The SIS supports daily/class attendance and absence history. Workflow adds parent absence requests, badge/barcode/kiosk check-in and appointment-linked attendance; attendance also feeds Analytics risk predictions. [15] [16]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

The SIS covers course/section setup, calendars, student/staff schedules, course masters, schedule changes and schedule-driven notifications. Product and third-party materials reference a Schedule Wizard; independent reviews praise central scheduling but flag class scheduling usability. [6] [17]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Teacher tools include gradebook, assignment categories, standards-based grading, missing/late work, assessments, multi-type quizzes, resubmission, individualized assignments, discussions, Progress Monitor, Score Analysis and third-party grade passback. [9] [18]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Campus supports report cards, transcripts, graduation plans, standards, courses, historical records and parent/student delivery. CCS Backpack publishes custom documents; Report Translation supports teacher comments and multilingual report cards. [19] [20]

#### Learning management and homework

Campus Learning Suite provides Planner, Discussions, individualized assignments, Curriculum Library, enhanced Quizzes, resubmission, feedback-based reassignment, Progress Monitor, Engagement Check-In and Score Analysis. It is SIS-native but supports Canvas, Google Classroom, Schoology, Brightspace and other OneRoster/LTI partners. [9] [18]

#### Communication

Messenger sends scheduled, automated or emergency email, phone and SMS from current SIS contact data, with templates, sender controls and parent preferences. Parent/Student push notifications cover grades, assignment scores, attendance and schedules; translation tools address language access. [19] [21]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Campus Parent and Campus Student are web portals plus mobile apps. Parents can view grades, assignments, attendance, schedules, announcements, food balances, fees, school stores and activities where enabled; students receive a learner view and notifications. Teachers use browser-based Instruction tools. District permissions control menu visibility. [12] [18]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Campus Payments covers course/lab/event/yearbook/trip fees, donations, activities, athletics, permission slips, stores, tickets, fundraisers, dependent care and tuition plans/discounts/scholarships. Food Service covers cafeteria POS, balances, limits, allergy alerts, FRAM meals and family payments. A full general-ledger accounting/ERP product was not publicly evidenced. [22] [23]

#### HR, staff and payroll

State Edition lists Staff Management and stores staff, qualification, employment and HR data; the ODS retains historical HR information. Public pages do not document standalone recruiting, payroll, benefits or time-and-attendance, so payroll should not be assumed native. [24]

#### Transport

No dedicated transportation-routing, fleet, bus GPS, eligibility or ridership module was identified in the reviewed official Campus SIS, Extension Marketplace or state-system pages. External transport integration is possible but unverified.

#### Library

No dedicated library-circulation, catalog, acquisitions or serials module was identified in the reviewed official sources. Any library integration is unverified.

#### Hostel and boarding

No hostel, dormitory, room-allocation or boarding-management module was publicly documented. It is not a residential-management suite.

#### Inventory and assets

School stores and cafeteria/POS inventory-adjacent transactions are documented, but no general equipment, fixed-asset, purchasing or warehouse-management module was identified. The Extension Marketplace page does not present inventory/assets as a standalone product. [25]

#### Health and medical

The SIS and State Edition include health data, health alerts and nurse workflows; Workflow can check in at a nurse location and the ODS retains historical health data. Clinical records, medication, immunization and telehealth were not specified publicly. [24]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Campus SIS includes behavior records and behavior-management workflows. SpotLight adds positive/minor behavior entry, dashboards by district/school/classroom, filters by who/what/when/where, barcode mobile entry, multi-year reports, positive reinforcement, a School Store and drill-down to Behavior Management. BTAM adds multidisciplinary threat-assessment teams, staff concern entry, configurable triggers/notifications, dashboards, pattern/trend reporting and preventative workflows. [26] [27]

#### Special education and safeguarding

The statewide product inventory lists IEP and PLP; the system supports special-education status, IEP data, accommodations and state reporting. The 504 Module tracks eligibility, referrals, meetings, annual reviews, reevaluations, manifestations, forms, documents, accommodations, parent/staff input, electronic signatures, dashboards and automated state extracts. MTSS tracks academic/behavioral tiers, domains, interventions, meetings and progress monitoring. BTAM provides the safeguarding/threat-assessment layer. [24] [28] [29]

#### Alumni and fundraising

Campus Payments supports donations, fundraisers and donation drives, but no dedicated alumni CRM, constituent history, campaign management or advancement module was identified. Fundraising should therefore be understood as transaction functionality rather than a full alumni/foundation suite. [22]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Analytics provides daily, localized risk predictions from attendance, behavior, academics and stability, plus visualizations for assessment, attendance, behavior and classroom performance. Premium Surveys supports files, emotions, signatures, ranking, sortable lists, external links and 40+ languages; core reporting includes ad hoc queries, validation and certification. [16] [24]

#### AI features

The documented intelligence is predictive, not generative: algorithms forecast graduation persistence/dropout risk and support at-risk funding models. Agile Flow/Agile Learning are roadmap directions; no production conversational copilot was identified. [2] [10] [16]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

State Edition serves 10 state agencies with a real-time ODS, multi-year history, validation/certification, IDs, custom pages/forms, assessments, graduation pathways, overlap detection, cross-district enrollment, transfers and third-party exchange. North Carolina completed its cloud implementation on 1 July 2025; North Dakota selected it for 120,000 students in November 2024. [11] [24] [30]

#### Mobile apps

Campus Parent and Campus Student are the exact parent/student apps, each available on iOS and Android, with district-controlled notifications. Campus Mobile Payments supports iOS/Android card-reader transactions. Mobile functionality is strongest for family access, alerts, payments and selected workflow/behavior entry; teacher/admin operations remain primarily browser-based. [7] [8] [12] [22]

#### Integrations and APIs

The platform supports its Extension Marketplace, 1EdTech-certified OneRoster, LTI score passback/content selection, secure launch, and partners such as Canvas, Google Classroom, Microsoft Teams, Brightspace, Schoology, Clever, Edlink, Pearson, Renaissance and Turnitin. Direct API access is partnership-gated for many developers, not unrestricted public API access. [18] [31] [32]

#### Security and privacy

Security controls include role-based tool permissions, MFA for remote access, CAPTCHA and breached-password detection, separate customer databases, daily backups, vulnerability scanning, monitored logs, U.S. data centers, annual SOC audits and a SOC 2 report available under NDA. Infinite Campus states FERPA compliance, direct district control over education records, no sale/targeted advertising use of those records, annual privacy training and breach notification to the education agency. ISO 27001, formal GDPR/India DPDP commitments and a named public breach were not established. [3] [33]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **Single-database ecosystem:** SIS, learning, family access, payments, food service, messaging and workflow share current district data rather than relying on nightly file exchanges. [9] [23]
* **Predictive dropout prevention:** Campus Analytics Suite produces daily risk predictions localized to district context and reports category scores for attendance, behavior, academics and stability. [16]
* **Statewide real-time ODS:** State Edition links SEA and LEA data with cross-district enrollment, certification, custom forms, IDs and historical records in one operational store. [24]
* **Extension Marketplace:** The vendor’s differentiator is a vetted, integrated extension layer rather than a closed SIS or a loosely connected app directory. [10]
* **Workflow automation:** Events and Actions can trigger notifications and follow-up actions for enrollment, special-education status, scheduling/grading and homeless-status changes; appointments can auto-create hall passes. [15]
* **Strong family transaction surface:** One family app can combine academic updates with food balances, fees, activities, stores and donations where enabled. [22]
* **Data governance tools:** Data Validations, Change Tracker and Access Tracker make data quality and privacy auditing operational rather than purely policy-based. [14]

### Pricing Details

No current official price list, tiers or standard rate is published; buyers request a demo/quote. Gartner describes subscription pricing, typically per student per year, with module-dependent quotes and possible implementation/setup fees. [34] SaaSworthy lists a quotation-based “Infinite Campus Custom” plan with no free trial, but its details were last updated 11 November 2020 and are stale estimates. [35]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Infinite Campus says it was the first SIS certified by 1EdTech for OneRoster and CASE and requires certified digital-learning partners. The catalog documents roster provisioning, grade passback, LTI launch/content selection and OneRoster Assessments. Canvas confirms OneRoster 1.2 credentials, nightly provisioning and grade passback. [18] [31]

Named connections include Canvas, Google Classroom, Schoology, Brightspace, Microsoft Teams, Clever, Pearson, Renaissance, Turnitin, Edlink and others. The Extension Marketplace supplies an integrated partner model. Edlink’s independent technical review says Infinite Campus supports OneRoster 1.1 and 1.2 variants but direct API access generally requires a partnership-level commitment; therefore public API openness is weaker than the vendor’s marketplace and standards story. [32] No public evidence was found in the reviewed sources for a certified Ed-Fi or SIF implementation, a named accounting connector, WhatsApp integration, or a universally available district SSO standard.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Infinite Campus states that districts control education records, the vendor acts as a contracted school official, data is housed in the U.S., and annual external SOC 2 Type II reports are available under NDA. [33]

The security page (20 January 2025) lists MFA, endpoint protection, intrusion prevention, monitoring, vulnerability scanning, separate databases and daily backups. The privacy policy (24 September 2026) says the apps collect limited crash/technical data, encrypt in transit and do not sell or use it for targeted advertising. [3] [36]

FERPA and COPPA-related handling is described, including education-agency control for children under 13. Public sources did not confirm ISO 27001, formal GDPR/India DPDP commitments, non-U.S. hosting or a public breach. Validate these contractually for non-U.S. use.

### Strengths

* Broad K–12 coverage on a single SIS foundation spanning enrollment, academics, family access, payments, food service, workflows, analytics and state reporting.
* Strong state-agency architecture: real-time SEA/LEA exchange, certification, historical ODS and cross-district operations are unusually deep. [24]
* Native Campus Learning avoids mandatory third-party LMS licensing while supporting OneRoster/LTI partner choice. [9] [18]
* Family engagement through distinct Campus Parent and Campus Student apps with real-time academic, attendance and notification access.
* The vendor reports 99% renewal and 3,400+ conversions; support is in-house and won HDI’s 2024 Best Service and Support Culture Award. [1] [37]
* Marketplace and governance tools reduce point-to-point integration and provide auditable data access/change controls.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* G2 users praise centralized records but report difficult navigation, permissions confusion, interface relearning and cumbersome grade/report workflows. [5]
* Capterra reviewers flag complex navigation, too many steps, limited customization, time-consuming grades, difficult reports, session timeouts and add-on fees for smaller districts. [6]
* Mobile ratings are materially lower than desktop review-site scores: Campus Parent 3.3 and Campus Student 3.6 on Google Play as viewed 24 November 2026. Review counts were not exposed in the opened listing, so app sentiment should not be over-generalized. [7] [8]
* Pricing opacity and module-by-module quoting make total cost difficult to compare; sources describe custom quotes and possible implementation fees. [34] [35]
* The product is strongest in K–12 SIS/state reporting; transport, library, boarding, general assets, alumni CRM, full payroll/accounting and a generative-AI assistant were not documented as native modules.
* Edlink says direct API access is partnership-gated and OneRoster implementations vary, increasing integration effort. [32]

### Key Milestones

* **1993:** Charlie Kratsch founded Infinite Campus after working with his former Minnesota district on student administration. [1]
* **1993–2001:** The company developed its relational-database/browser SIS foundation; the founder dates the first statewide data-sharing solution to 2001. [1] [2]
* **1996:** Infinite Campus says it introduced the first web-based SIS with integrated applications and SaaS pricing. [2]
* **2002:** The company moved to an Arden Hills office and began State Edition work with South Dakota. [1] [24]
* **2006–2007:** Bureau of Indian Education, Montana and Kentucky expanded statewide use. [24]
* **2008:** Infinite Campus opened its national headquarters. [1]
* **2009–2016:** Food Service, Online Payments, Online Registration, Messenger and learning-management capabilities expanded the product family. [1]
* **2015–2021:** Hawaii, Nevada and the Northern Mariana Islands joined State Edition. [24]
* **2018:** The founder describes a near-real-time collaborative-intelligence platform milestone; later Campus Analytics applied machine learning to dropout prevention. [2]
* **2023:** Delaware selected Infinite Campus as its statewide SIS/IEP and data-exchange partner. [24]
* **2023–2025:** North Carolina selected Infinite Campus in November 2023 and completed statewide cloud implementation on 1 July 2025. [11]
* **2024:** North Dakota selected Infinite Campus on 7 November 2024, becoming the tenth SEA customer for about 120,000 students. [30]
* **2024:** Infinite Campus won HDI’s Best Service and Support Culture Award. [37]
* **2026:** The vendor promotes the integrated Extension Marketplace and Agile Flow/Agile Learning roadmap. [10]

## #14. Skyward (Skyward, Inc.)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Skyward, Inc.; family-owned, founded by Jim and Jean King [2] [4] |
| Headquarters | Stevens Point, Wisconsin, United States [2] [33] |

| Primary segments | U.S. K–12 public school districts, municipalities, teachers, students, families, school administrators, finance/HR offices, and international K–12 schools [1] [2] [5] |

### Overview

Skyward is a long-established K–12 administration platform combining a Student Information System (SIS) with a school-business ERP. Its current-generation Qmlativ Education Management System covers student administration, teacher and family access, finance, HR, payroll, assets, reporting, and mobile access; SMS 2.0 remains a supported legacy product line. The value proposition is consolidation: one district database for records, grades, attendance, family engagement, finance, and workforce operations rather than a collection of disconnected point systems [1] [3].

Skyward began in 1980 as Jim King & Associates in Stevens Point. The first school product was developed in 1981 for Merrill Area Public School District to manage personnel and salary negotiations, after which the software spread to other Wisconsin districts. It adopted the Skyward name in 1994, acquired Texas Educational Consultative Services in 2000, partnered with cloud host ISCorp, and became entirely web-based in 2009 [4].

Qmlativ was announced at the end of 2016, had been in live production for more than two years by January 2017, and was designed from scratch with a new database and technology stack rather than as a visual clone of SMS 2.0 [6]. Current public materials do not publish a consistently updated country-by-country customer table [2].

### Platform Classification Explained

- **Browser/web:** Skyward states that its solution became entirely web-based in 2009; Qmlativ presents browser dashboards, portals, and web-based payroll [4] [24].
- **Cloud:** Qmlativ’s product material strongly recommends secure cloud hosting. Skyward identifies ISCorp as its exclusive hosting provider and describes cloud hosting, backups, automatic updates, and security controls [3] [31].
- **Desktop/on-premise:** No standalone native desktop client is identified in the current product pages. SMS 2.0 has legacy district-hosting and Windows/IIS/MSSQL deployment references in third-party reviews, but Skyward’s current public material does not establish a new on-premise option for Qmlativ [34].
- **Mobile:** The exact primary app is **Skyward Mobile Access**, with Family Access, Student Access, Educator/Teacher Access, and Employee Access functions. The official app page lists iOS, Android, and historical Windows Mobile availability; the current Apple and Google Play listings are for Skyward Mobile Access [27] [36] [37].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

Online Enrollment and Registration supports custom forms, new and returning student applications, registrar review/update/processing, personalized workflows, and requirements. Parents can register children online, reducing paper and office visits [9].

#### Student information and records

The core SIS stores student records, demographics, contacts, schedules, courses, academic history, health information, discipline, interventions, and other data in a district-wide record. The Family Access design exposes a controlled whole-child view, while privacy policy language confirms support for student, parent, employee, health, and financial information [15] [32].

#### Attendance

Attendance includes teacher entry, custom seating charts with student pictures, real-time counts by district/building/classroom, parent absence notifications, custom messages and intervention letters, audit/correction workflows, and dashboards showing attendance trends. Student ID scanning/wanding is reported as an available add-on [12] [35].

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Scheduling manages multiple entities, mass scheduling, auditing, real-time roster changes, student course requests, and conflict reduction. Online Course Requests are designed to give students more ownership and work with teacher recommendations; curriculum can be linked to graduation plans [10] [14].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Teacher Gradebook provides quick scoring, teacher-controlled assignment/grade visibility, categories, weights, customized grading methods and scales, real-time progress reports for activities/athletics/groups, and standards-based or traditional grading. Third-party product documentation also reports assessment management, tests/assessments, online assignments, gradebook cloning, and automatic posting of grades to report cards; a Google Classroom grade-export integration is publicly described [11] [29] [35].

#### Report cards and transcripts

Report Cards & Transcripts provides real-time data without imports, multiple GPA storage, progress notes, customizable branding, extensive reporting options, and up-to-date transcripts [41]. Report Writer uses a drag-and-drop editor, access to every field, layouts/branding, and controlled distribution through email, Message Center, or a network location [7].

#### Learning management and homework

Skyward is not positioned as a full standalone LMS, but it has built-in classroom management, online assignments, course management, collaboration/message features, and assignment/grade visibility. Software Advice lists built-in LMS and learning-management capabilities [8] [35].

#### Communication

Message Center supports individual or class-wide secure messages, announcements, audit trails, and continuous parent-teacher communication. Family Access and the mobile app provide messages, notifications, attendance alerts, grade-threshold alerts, and missing-assignment alerts. Public materials document email/message-center workflows and push-style app notifications, but do not document a native WhatsApp channel [13] [16].

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Family Access is the parent portal for grades, assignments, attendance, behavior, upcoming events, course requests, graduation planning, enrollment, fees, and payment/account activity. Student Access exposes grades, schedules, assignments, and communication. Teacher Access is a self-contained portal with a personalized dashboard, live alerts, gradebook navigation, attendance, behavior referrals, and mobile access [8] [14] [15] [27].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Fee Management covers food-service, textbook, activity, tuition, and other fees; collection reports; account activity; payment plans/discounts; and parent visibility. The ERP adds accounts payable, accounts receivable, activity accounting, purchasing, budgeting, general ledger, automated approvals, real-time financial information, and financial controls [22] [42].

#### HR, staff and payroll

Human Resources includes applicant tracking, job openings, position requests, position management, staff planning, position budgeting and what-if scenarios, benefit enrollment/invoices, substitute tracking, employee growth/history, and ACA compliance including 1094/1095 submissions. Payroll supports complex wage plans, electronic timekeeping, job-code/time-status changes, approvals, and ACA-aware processing [23] [24].

#### Transport

No native student transportation or bus-routing module was identified in the public Skyward feature catalog reviewed. Treat transportation as an integration or separate system unless a district-specific proposal says otherwise.

#### Library

No native library-management module was identified in the reviewed official product pages or independent feature list.

#### Hostel and boarding

No native hostel, dormitory, or boarding module was identified. Skyward’s public positioning is K–12 district administration rather than residential-school management.

#### Inventory and assets

Asset Management tracks location, status, value, depreciation, audits, warehouse stock, ordering-to-depletion lifecycle, real-time inventory, and low-stock notifications [25].

#### Health and medical

Health Services tracks immunizations/vaccinations, nurse logs with freeform notes, medication administration, state-required health fields, and student accountability while in the health office. Skyward states that the module is HIPAA and FERPA compliant [18] [31].

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Behavior Management removes referral paperwork, allows teachers to document non-escalated events, alerts administrators, exposes offenses to parents through Family Access, and supplies reporting and live dashboard tiles [19].

#### Special education and safeguarding

Skyward publicly identifies Special Education and has discussed Section 504 enhancements; Qmlativ updates also cover evaluation/IEP-manager visibility. MTSS supports observations, referrals, configurable concerns, intervention teams, Watchlist thresholds, intervention plans, progress tracking, and parent visibility. A distinct safeguarding case-management module is not publicly documented [6] [20] [33].

#### Alumni and fundraising

No native alumni-relations or fundraising module was found in the current public catalog.

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Skyward provides Report Writer, live tiles, state/federal reports, attendance/behavior dashboards, and DistrictPulse, a Qmlativ SIS analytics solution built with AWS and Amazon QuickSight. DistrictPulse supplies dashboards, author/reader roles, trend forecasting, staffing/intervention analysis, and custom reports; ERP availability was still listed as coming later [12] [19] [26] [43].

#### AI features

The Qmlativ Help Center uses AI to turn technical support into a guided learning experience. DistrictPulse uses AWS/QuickSight analytics and forecasting language, but Skyward does not publicly claim a general-purpose generative AI assistant embedded in district workflows or a validated predictive-risk model [3] [43].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Skyward maintains state-reporting specialists, state-specific compliance updates, federal reporting including Civil Rights Data Collection, built-in state reports/e-files in budgeting, webinars, and preferred-provider status in Washington, Tennessee, and Rhode Island. It reports work with more than 20 states and multiple international locations [26].

#### Mobile apps

Skyward Mobile Access supports students, parents, and staff with grades, attendance, behavior, Family Access, payroll history, time sheets, tax forms, time off, and other employee functions. Family Mobile adds grades, messages, notifications, attendance, behavior, and calendar; Teacher Mobile and Employee Mobile bring role-specific access to phones [16] [27].

#### Integrations and APIs

Skyward supports OneRoster 1.1, Ed-Fi API v4 certification for Qmlativ, SIF certification, 1EdTech Trusted Apps data-privacy certification, partner integrations, LMS/API access, grade passback work, and Google Classroom grade export. SMS 2.0 has read-only LMS API access plus a licensed read/write option; Qmlativ’s OneRoster API was described as read-only in the cited announcement [28] [29] [30].

#### Security and privacy

Skyward documents encryption, firewalls, access limitations, physical controls, cloud backups, district-controlled permissions, annual employee training, security reporting, and return/destruction of customer data at contract end. It publicly claims COPPA, FERPA, and HIPAA compliance and identifies ISCorp as exclusive cloud host. The reviewed Trust Center did not publish a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certificate, and no public incident disclosure was found in the reviewed sources [31] [32].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Qmlativ from-scratch architecture:** A new database and technology stack rather than a superficial redesign of SMS 2.0 [6].
- **DistrictPulse analytics:** AWS/QuickSight-backed dashboards, authoring, trend forecasting, staffing analysis, and intervention targeting inside Qmlativ [43].
- **Configurable intervention Watchlist:** District-defined thresholds can surface students based on grades, absences, and discipline, then route them into intervention plans [20].
- **Standards-based interoperability:** Ed-Fi API v4, OneRoster 1.1, SIF, and 1EdTech TrustEd Apps certification claims reduce bespoke rostering work [28] [29] [30].
- **User-configurable forms and workflows:** Enrollment forms, report layouts, approvals, and task workflows support district-specific processes [9] [22].
- **AI-assisted support:** The Help Center uses AI for technical-support guidance, but this is not the same as a classroom or administrative AI copilot [3].

### Pricing Details

Skyward does not publish official Qmlativ or SMS 2.0 price cards, per-student rates, tiers, implementation fees, or hosting fees. The official route is a school-pricing request to sales [7]. Software Advice, viewed 24 November 2026, reports one Basic plan at **$30,000 per year**; Capterra shows the same starting figure. These are third-party estimates, not a Skyward quote, and the unit is not verified as per-student [34] [35]. Setup, migration, training, and optional API/module fees are not publicly itemized [29] [43].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Skyward’s strongest documented interoperability is standards-based: Qmlativ has Ed-Fi API v4 certification; SMS 2.0 and Qmlativ are listed as 1EdTech OneRoster-compliant and data-privacy certified; and the company lists SIF certification. OneRoster exports/APIs, LMS API access, Google Classroom grade export, and partner integrations are documented. A complete current connector matrix or developer marketplace is not public [28] [29] [30] [34].

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Skyward publicly claims COPPA, FERPA, and HIPAA compliance, district-controlled access permissions, cloud hosting, backups, encryption, firewalls, least-privilege access, physical controls, annual security/privacy training, and vulnerability reporting. The product privacy policy says the school/district owns and controls protected information and Skyward processes it under contract [31] [32]. No public SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 certificate, GDPR/DPDP statement, data-residency region, or dated breach register was located. This is a documentation gap, not evidence of non-compliance.

### Strengths

- Broad K–12 SIS plus finance/HR/ERP coverage, with one data estate spanning student and business operations [1] [5].
- Large, established customer footprint: 7.8 million students and 2,700 customers claimed as of the 2026 About page [2].
- Strong state-reporting specialization and a long U.S. K–12 implementation/support history [26].
- Useful native family, teacher, employee, mobile, fee, payroll, health, behavior, MTSS, asset, and reporting tools [8] [17] [21].
- Standards certification and API options are more open than a closed SIS, particularly for Ed-Fi and OneRoster [28] [29].
- Reviewers often value the consolidated data, comprehensive functionality, support, and ability to manage grades/attendance/records in one place [33] [34] [35].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- User experience is uneven: G2 is 3.8/5 and Capterra’s ease-of-use score is 3.9; reviews repeatedly describe legacy screens, clutter, steep learning curves, and difficult navigation [33] [34] [35].
- Mobile sentiment is particularly weak: Apple is 1.8/5 and Google Play is 2.9/5; recent reviews cite 503/login failures, freezing, biometric problems, outdated UI, and repeated relogins [36] [37].
- Configuration and migration complexity matter: Skyward’s own Qmlativ transition guidance says reports, security, and workflows may not transfer directly, while feature parity and state readiness affect migration timing [6].
- Rostering can be awkward for A/B-day or period-based schedules, and some reviewers report slow or expensive reports, difficult reporting, and problems with expense reimbursement or student/teacher management [34].
- Price transparency is poor. Public sources show a $30,000/year catalog estimate, but not a verifiable per-student formula, implementation fee, or module-by-module price [34] [35].
- Skyward is not a clear replacement for a full LMS, transport, library, boarding, alumni, or fundraising suite; several of those modules are not publicly evidenced as native.

### Key Milestones

- **1980:** Jim and Jean King establish Jim King & Associates in Stevens Point, Wisconsin [4].
- **1981:** First school-management project for Merrill Area Public School District manages personnel and salary negotiations [4] [5].
- **1984:** Company incorporates as School Administration Software, Inc. (SASI) [4].
- **Late 1980s–1990s:** Expansion into school software; a 1994 Matrix Computers acquisition is reported in the independent history, and the company adopts the Skyward name [4] [38].
- **2000:** Skyward acquires Texas Educational Consultative Services and partners with ISCorp for cloud hosting [4].
- **2001:** WSIPC selects Skyward as Washington’s statewide SIS/ERP partner [4] [38].
- **2006:** First international customer, American Embassy School in New Delhi, according to the independent history [38].
- **2009:** Skyward solution becomes entirely web-based [4].
- **2011–2013:** Preferred-provider status expands through Texas, Rhode Island, and Tennessee [4] [26].
- **2016:** New Stevens Point world headquarters opens; Qmlativ announcement and pilot work begin [4] [6].
- **2017:** Qmlativ is in live production and supports fully web-based payroll at early districts; migration roadmap covers Illinois, Minnesota, Texas, and Washington [6].
- **2019:** OneRoster 1.1 certification work and API availability are announced; Skyward is named EdTech Digest Company of the Year [5] [30].
- **2020:** 40th anniversary release reports 2,000+ customers, 7+ million students, 21 states, and 10 countries [5].
- **2024:** Qmlativ receives Ed-Fi API v4 certification [29].
- **2025–2026:** Qmlativ continues feature releases, including IEP/evaluation visibility and DistrictPulse analytics; in October 2026 Mountain Brook Schools becomes Skyward’s first Alabama customer [2] [39] [43].

## #15. Compass Education (Compass Education)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Compass Education Pty Ltd; founders John de la Motte and Lucas Filer. EQT invested through its Mid-Market Growth fund in 2024, while founder John de la Motte remained a significant shareholder. [1] [2] |
| Headquarters | Level 2, 36–38 Burwood Road, Hawthorn, Victoria 3122, Australia. [3] |
| Company founded (year) | 2010, according to the company history; the founders began building the product in 2009. [1] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | 2011: the first version of CompassKiosk was released. The company does not separately disclose a first release date for the later full Compass platform. [1] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud SaaS and web-based, with native iOS/iPadOS and Android apps. No desktop client or on-premise deployment is publicly documented. [2] [4] [5] |
| Primary segments | Australian government, Catholic and independent K–12 schools; multi-campus schools and education groups; also schools in the UK, Ireland and New Zealand. [2] [6] |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | 5,000 schools and 5M users worldwide on the official site, viewed 24 November 2026; the user figure includes parents, teachers and students rather than students alone. The 20 August 2024 EQT announcement reported 3,000+ schools and more than 4M parents, teachers and students in Australia, the UK and Ireland, with New Zealand also referenced in the company’s market history. [1] [2] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://www.compass.education/ |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://www.compass.education/features/ |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | https://www.compass.education/support/support-centre/ |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | No public pricing page; official sales flow is demo/contact-led. |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | G2: 4.0/5 from 1 review; Capterra: no customer rating/review score displayed; Apple App Store Australia: 4.6/5 from 90K ratings; Google Play: 3.4/5 from 18.5K reviews and 1M+ downloads. All viewed 24 November 2026, except the store pages’ displayed update dates. [7] [8] [9] [10] |

### Overview

Compass Education is an Australian school management information system that combines SIS/student records, attendance, wellbeing, teaching and learning, communications, family engagement, events, payments and financial management. It is positioned as a single source of truth for government, Catholic and independent K–12 schools, replacing a collection of administrative tools with a connected cloud platform and mobile experience. [2] [4]

John de la Motte and Lucas Filer founded the company in 2010 after beginning product work in 2009. The first documented product release was CompassKiosk in 2011; the mobile app followed in 2012, and CompassPay also launched in 2012. The timeline records 1,000 schools in 2015, Ireland in 2016, England in 2021 and a 2,000th school in 2021. [1] The business’s ownership changed materially when Advent Partners exited and EQT announced its 2024 investment. In February 2026, Compass acquired Inklass to strengthen school-branded mobile apps and connect communication, attendance, wellbeing, learning and payments in a more unified family experience. [2] [6]

### Platform Classification Explained

Compass is a multi-tenant, cloud-based SaaS platform. The official company description calls it a “full-suite, cloud-based school management platform,” and the parent guide says the service is available in any modern web browser through a school-specific portal. [2] [5] UK government procurement material describes horizontally scalable services, per-customer databases, multi-cloud and Tier-3 data centres, asynchronous worker pools, automated failover and a 99.9% availability commitment for that service. [11]

There is no public evidence of a Windows/macOS desktop client; staff and families use the browser portal. There is also no public on-premise edition. The platform has native mobile applications named **Compass School Manager** on Apple platforms and Google Play. The parent guide identifies iOS and Android apps and documents news, messages, timetables, calendars, Learning Tasks, conferences, attendance notes, reports, widgets, live class changes, Apple Pay in Australia, and light/dark/system appearance. [5] The acquired Inklass capability adds a school-branded mobile-app route, but the principal store listing remains Compass School Manager. [6] [9] [10]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrolment

**Enrolments Pro** supports an end-to-end journey from expression of interest through enrolment, with a mobile-friendly family experience, admissions pipeline dashboard, application-fee capture through finance integration and connections to third-party enrolment tools. [4] Compass also lists EnrolHQ, Digistorm Funnel and Enquiry Tracker integrations. [3]

#### Student information and records

People Management supplies the central people/student record and acts as the data foundation for enrolment, attendance, wellbeing, reporting and communications. Configurable forms, family/contact data, student profiles, documents, custom flags, role-based permissions and exportable records are evidenced across the product and procurement description. [4] [8] The parent-facing Student Profile brings together today’s classes, activities, observations, tasks, attendance, surveys and reports. [5]

#### Attendance

Attendance provides digital roll marking, centralised attendance management, absenteeism tracking, attendance notes, unexplained absence and lateness workflows, class-by-class summaries, daily snapshots of whereabouts, custom classes, events, Sickbay entries and early departures. Parents can submit reasons, times, comments and attachments, and schools can send absence SMS links for explanations. [4] [5]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Schedule Builder creates and changes school timetables; Calendar manages class sessions and rolls; Room Swap manages room allocations and changes from a class page; Resource Bookings prevents double-booking of laptops and other resources. Compass also integrates with Edval and Timetabler. [3] [4]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Learning Tasks supports assessment-task creation, distribution, student submissions, marking, feedback and evidence. Compass supports configurable assessment frameworks, curriculum structures and reporting models, but a separate high-stakes examination module is not publicly described. [4] [8]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Semester Reports provides integrated end-of-semester report writing and publication. Progress Reports show performance over time; longitudinal reporting can follow a student from Kindergarten through Year 12. Families can download academic reports as PDFs. A dedicated higher-education transcript/degree-audit function is not evidenced. [4] [5]

#### Learning management and homework

Learning Tasks is the named learning-management module for assignments, due dates, submissions, marking, feedback, resources and parent visibility. Course overviews can link tasks, rubrics and materials; families can see upcoming and overdue work, and semester reporting can draw on learning evidence. Integrations include Canvas, Google Classroom/Hapara, Toddle, SchoolBox, Edrolo and Turnitin. [2] [3] [4]

#### Communication

News Feed provides a central announcement stream. SMS Communication supports bulk SMS, email and push notifications to staff, parents/carers and students; the official feature page explicitly names email, SMS and push, while the parent guide documents messages, alerts and school news. WhatsApp is not publicly listed as a native channel. [4] [5]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

The parent portal and mobile app expose news, attendance, timetables, calendar, tasks, reports, conferences, events, consent, payments, wallet and contact-detail updates. Staff use role-specific portal access for administration, attendance, wellbeing, teaching, meetings and finance. Students can access their timetable, Learning Tasks, feedback and reports where the school enables those functions. Portals can be school-branded with logos, colours and terminology. [4] [5] [8]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Billing Management, Debtor Management, CompassPay and CompassFMS cover contribution/fee invoices, debtor creation, fee splits, receipts, payment history, payment plans, donations, family Wallet top-ups and automatic top-ups. Event Payments and Consent handles excursions and approvals; Online Orders supports canteens; Shop supports uniforms and books. Finance capabilities include general ledger, accounts receivable/payable, fixed assets, budgets, purchase orders, cash flow, balance sheets, bank-transaction validation, receipting and financial dashboards. [2] [4] [5]

#### HR, staff and payroll

People Management, Time Card, Professional Development and Meetings cover staff records, arrivals/departures through Kiosk, development goals/training, meeting agendas, delegated actions and progress tracking. CompassFMS says it includes payroll, but the public feature material does not provide payroll workflows or a standalone HR/payroll product page; it should therefore be validated in procurement. [1] [4]

#### Activities, events and extracurricular management

Events supports excursions, permissions, consent, payments and attendee tracking. The calendar consolidates activities; Compass lists clubs, co-curricular programs, staffing allocations, extras, duty changes, ticketed events and online sales. Clipboard was announced as an extracurricular-management acquisition in the current site’s news feed, while the Inklass acquisition states that it will deepen Clipboard integration. [2] [6]

#### Transport, library, hostel and boarding, and inventory/assets

Compass lists Busminder as a transport integration and Oliver/Accessit for library-related connectivity, but no native route planning, fleet, library-catalogue, hostel or boarding-management module is publicly evidenced. Resource Bookings covers equipment/resource reservations, and finance includes fixed assets. These areas should not be counted as full native modules without a vendor confirmation. [3] [4]

#### Health and medical

Chronicle Sickbay records health incidents such as illness or injury, treatments and a student’s Sickbay presence. The feature set supports an audit trail, parent notifications and daily whereabouts visibility. [4] [5]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Chronicle monitors student behaviour and wellbeing; Chronicle Meetings records student meetings and automatically generates attendance; Custom Flags highlight vital information; Digest gives selected-student wellbeing updates. Role-based access and audit trails protect sensitive pastoral records. [4]

#### Special education and safeguarding

Compass publicly describes confidential wellbeing workflows, granular permissions, audit trails and safeguarding/duty-of-care controls. A 2026 case study references sharing Individual Education Plans with base schools, indicating support for special-education workflows, but there is no separately branded special-education module or public IEP specification. [2] [4]

#### Alumni and fundraising

The independent-school offering describes alumni records, campaigns, donations, community outreach, events and a dedicated portal. Donations can also be requested alongside school contributions and payment plans. The public material is stronger on community/fundraising workflows than on a full advancement CRM. [2] [4]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Pulse provides data visualisation, dashboards and school-wide insights across attendance, learning and wellbeing, with cohort/year-level comparisons and exports. Chronicle and Digest provide operational wellbeing views; finance offers live reporting, cash flow and balance sheets. Public material does not claim predictive analytics, machine-learning forecasts or an AI assistant. [2] [4]

#### AI features

No production AI assistant, generative AI workflow, predictive model or AI tutor is publicly documented in the official Compass feature catalogue or the reviewed procurement listing. Capterra’s page labels some content “AI summary,” but that is Capterra editorial metadata, not a Compass product capability. [4] [8]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Compass advertises state curriculum reporting for government schools. The UK procurement listing documents statutory and non-statutory exports, including XML census returns, CTF, CSV and other formats, plus pre-built extracts for ParentPay. The Australian site does not publish a complete state-by-state return matrix, so schools should confirm their jurisdiction’s required reports. [2] [11]

#### Mobile apps

Compass School Manager provides native iOS/iPadOS and Android access for staff, students and parents. Features include news, alerts, messages, timetable, calendar, Learning Tasks, conferences, reports, attendance notes, live class changes, payments, Wallet and Apple Pay in Australia. Inklass adds branded app design and deeper real-time integrations. [5] [6] [9] [10]

#### Integrations and APIs

Compass publishes a robust public RESTful API, API documentation and a sandbox/test environment in the UK procurement record. Named integrations include TechnologyOne, Sage Intacct, Xero, MYOB Acumatica, Canvas, Turnitin, Google Classroom/Hapara, Edval, Timetabler, PaperCut, Oliver, Accessit, Busminder, Digistorm Funnel, EnrolHQ, Victorian Student Register, Edrolo, MSP Photography, RollCall, Clipboard and Music Monitor. [3] [11]

#### Security and privacy

The platform uses TLS/encryption, granular role groups, MFA, identity federation, audit information and Australian data centres for the Australian service. Compass states PCI DSS Level 1 compliance for payment handling. The UK service description adds ISO/IEC 27001, Cyber Essentials, annual external penetration testing, encrypted backups, secure erasure and at least 12 months of audit/system-log retention. [4] [5] [11] The Australian privacy policy explains Compass’s processor/service-provider role for client data and the categories of identity, contact, financial, transaction, technical and profile data it may process. [12]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Pulse school-wide analytics:** real-time visualisation of attendance, learning and wellbeing, with cohort and year-level comparisons and exports. [2]
- **50+ connected modules:** the company’s current positioning is an unusually broad K–12 suite spanning administration, learning, wellbeing, community and finance. [1] [4]
- **Configurable workflows and branded portals:** schools can configure wellbeing, pastoral, assessment, reporting and portal settings, with role-governed administration. [8]
- **Embedded school payments:** event consent, contributions, payment plans, donations, Wallet, canteen orders and Shop are connected to the family experience. [4] [5]
- **Public REST API with sandbox:** the API and test environment support custom integrations beyond the named partners. [3] [11]
- **Inklass mobile-app acquisition:** the 2026 transaction adds a school-branded, real-time app strategy across multiple school systems. [6]
- **Operational resilience:** the UK service describes per-customer databases, auto-scaled workers, failover and a 99.9% availability target. [11]

### Pricing Details

Compass does not publish list prices, tiers, per-student rates or implementation fees. The official site routes prospects to a demo and information pack, while G2 says pricing is unavailable and Capterra lists “Contact vendor for pricing,” with no free trial or free version shown. [7] [8] No reliable public third-party price range was found, so no estimate is supplied. Pricing and implementation scope should be requested as an AUD or local-currency school/group quote, with modules, data migration, training, support, payment processing and any school-branded app separated in the proposal. Checked 24 November 2026.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Compass has the strongest public evidence for a rich REST API, documentation, sandbox and a large partner ecosystem rather than for formal education-data-standard certification. The named ecosystem covers finance/accounting (TechnologyOne, Sage Intacct, Xero and MYOB Acumatica), learning (Canvas, Turnitin, Google Classroom/Hapara, Toddle, SchoolBox and Edrolo), timetabling (Edval and Timetabler), enrolment, photos, transport, library, printing and co-curricular management. [3] [11]

No source reviewed confirms OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF certification, nor Clever/ClassLink marketplace certification. The UK listing does document identity federation with an existing provider such as Google Apps and built-in data exports in XML, CSV, CTF, PDF and other formats. Google Workspace/Microsoft 365 should be treated as integration-specific rather than assumed platform-wide; WhatsApp is not publicly documented. [3] [11]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Compass states that its Australian service is hosted in Australia-based data centres, uses industry-standard encryption and meets PCI DSS Level 1 obligations for payments. The privacy policy identifies Compass Education Pty Ltd as the Australian entity and describes school/client responsibility for the legal basis and notices applicable to client-uploaded student data. [4] [5] [12]

The UK government listing reports ISO/IEC 27001-aligned security governance, Cyber Essentials, MFA, identity federation, annual external penetration testing, TLS 1.2+, encrypted backups, secure deletion and audit logs retained for at least 12 months. It reports EEA storage/processing for that UK service. [11] This should not be generalized to every Compass geography without contract confirmation. No public SOC 2 report was found. The reviewed sources do not establish FERPA, COPPA or India DPDP Act certification/attestation; GDPR/UK GDPR controls are described in the UK procurement material, not as a global certification. No publicly reported security incident was identified in the reviewed official, procurement or review sources through 24 November 2026.

### Strengths

- Broad, genuinely connected coverage for Australian K–12 operations: SIS, attendance, wellbeing, learning, family communication, payments and finance. [2] [4]
- Current official adoption claim of 5,000 schools and 5M users, with a 99%+ retention claim and 270+ Australia-based staff. [1]
- Strong local fit: Australian data-centre positioning, Australian state reporting, local support, Apple Pay Australia and education-specific partners. [2] [4] [5]
- A large public partner catalogue and REST API reduce the risk of being completely locked into one vendor. [3] [11]
- Native mobile apps cover parents, students and staff, while Inklass expands branding and cross-system mobile access. [5] [6]
- Finance is unusually deep for a school MIS, extending from family billing and consent to general ledger, budgets, purchase orders and fixed assets. [2] [4]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is quote-only, with no public tiers, per-student rate or implementation price, making comparison and budgeting difficult. [7] [8]
- Review evidence is thin on G2: only one verified review is shown, so the 4.0/5 rating is not statistically meaningful. [7]
- The Android listing is materially weaker than iOS at 3.4/5 from 18.5K reviews; users report sign-outs, difficult login, attachment crashes, inconsistent navigation and a dated or confusing interface. [9]
- Apple reviews praise reliable schedules and frequent updates but report poor mobile access to resources/feedback, awkward payment confirmation, staff email-account behaviour and repeated card-entry/batch-payment friction. [10]
- The mobile experience can diverge from the browser experience, and some workflows depend on school configuration or optional modules; families may need workarounds when schools enable only part of the suite. [5] [10]
- Transport, library, hostel/boarding, formal examination management and standards certification are not publicly evidenced as native capabilities; integrations should not be mistaken for built-in modules. [3] [8]

### Key Milestones

- **2009:** John de la Motte and Lucas Filer begin building Compass from a garage in Vermont South. [1]
- **2010:** Compass is founded by de la Motte and Filer. [1] [2]
- **2011:** First version of CompassKiosk is released; the team moves into its first office. [1]
- **2012:** First interstate customer; Compass Mobile App and CompassPay launch. [1]
- **2014:** New Android and iOS mobile apps launch. [1]
- **2015:** Compass reaches 1,000 schools and is selected as the student-management solution for more than 700 Catholic schools. [1]
- **2016:** First Irish school launches; Compass Guardian launches; TechnologyOne partnership and Compass Billing begin. [1]
- **2018:** Cashless Canteens and Online Ordering launch. [1]
- **2020:** Pulse launches. [1]
- **2021:** Compass launches in England, reaches 2,000 schools and grows to 200 employees. [1] [2]
- **20 August 2024:** EQT announces investment through its Mid-Market Growth fund; Advent Partners exits. The announcement reports 3,000+ schools and 4M+ users at that date. [2]
- **8 October 2025:** The current company history/news feed records Music Monitor joining Compass; the acquisition adds school music-department management. [4]
- **11 February 2026:** Compass announces acquisition of Inklass to strengthen school-branded mobile apps and integrations. [6]
- **November 2026:** Official site claims 5,000 schools and 5M users worldwide, plus 50+ modules. [1] [4]
