### Overview

Classter is a modular, all-in-one student information system (SIS), school management system (SMS), learning management system (LMS), education ERP and academic CRM. It follows one student record from inquiry and admission through enrollment, attendance, grades, billing, graduation and alumni engagement. Its intended users are administrators, registrars, faculty, finance teams, students, parents, agents, employers and alumni. The product matters because it replaces disconnected spreadsheets and point systems with shared records, portals, workflows and role-based access [1] [9].

The company says it began in Greece in 2015 with Core, Academics, Billing and CRM modules [2]. The European Investment Fund reported more than 400 institutions by May 2018 after Odyssey Venture Partners and EIF-backed JEREMIE Greece investment [11]. In October 2025 Banyan Software acquired Vertitech, the legal entity operating Classter [10].

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser/web access:** Role-specific portals run online; an independent directory lists Safari, Chrome, Internet Explorer and Firefox and categorizes deployment as SaaS/cloud [6] [11].
* **Cloud hosting:** Classter documents Microsoft Azure cloud hosting, scalability, monitoring, backup and disaster recovery. The company’s SIS page also states a 99.9% uptime SLA and EU data residency on request; these are vendor claims rather than independently audited findings in the reviewed sources [8] [9].
* **Desktop client:** No separate Windows, macOS or Linux client was found; desktop use is browser-based [11].
* **On-premise:** Classter explicitly offers on-premise installation for institutions needing control of infrastructure and data. This makes the overall product hybrid in deployment options, although the primary commercial positioning is cloud SaaS [8].
* **Native mobile:** The companion is called “Classter” on Google Play and “Classter – School Management App” in Apple’s store. It supports Android, iPhone and iPad; the mobile app is complementary rather than feature-equivalent to the web platform. The original Android/iOS launch announcement dates to 4 March 2020 [17] [18] [19].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Core, student information and records

Core centralizes student, parent, sibling, teacher, employee and contact records. It covers demographics, passport/nationality/language data, family relationships, multiple statuses/programs/classes, curriculum and study plans, subjects/groups, elective self-enrollment, year-to-year transfers, extracurricular/billable services, Azure Files documents, age/activity consents, permissions, accounts, templates, bulk import/export, CSV/PDF reports, custom fields and academic-period configuration. Medical data includes vaccinations and COVID testing, but this is not a full clinical record system [5] [30].

#### Admissions and enrollment

Admissions provides applicant, parent, student and agent portals; self-sign-up; quick admission and lead capture; multiple intakes/applications; program preferences; dynamic fields; qualification and eligibility rules; scoring/benchmarking; status workflows and checklists; interviews and entrance exams; document upload; GDPR, financial and data-sharing consents; fees; enrollment/re-enrollment; conditional offers; e-signed contracts; and record-linked communications. Family credentials can cover multiple children [31] [9].

#### Attendance, timetable and master scheduling

Attendance supports subject/session attendance, absence, presence, tardiness, QR-code and RFID check-in/out, attendance reports and parent/student visibility. Timetabling covers drag-and-drop editing, teacher/classroom/resource allocation, unlimited timetables, ad-hoc sessions, extra events and staff meetings, room and resource booking, teacher substitutions, clash and missing-session detection, and synchronization with attendance and academics. The help center lists an AI timetable scheduling engine; the public materials do not disclose its optimization method or an independent deployment case [5] [23].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Academics & LMS includes configurable gradebooks/scales, weighted and hierarchical criteria, rubrics, outcomes, GPA, marking periods, feedback, blind marking, assessment workflows, external re-marking, assignment/quiz/presentation/exam scheduling, online exams, retakes, deferred classes, overload controls, outcomes tracking, grade exports and emailed reports. It also supports report-card PDFs, promotion, performance statistics, badges and behavior points [5].

#### Learning management and homework

The LMS side provides course/subject syllabi, lesson planning, sessions and lessons, learning rooms (course microsites), uploaded teaching materials, discussion boards, homework assignment/submission/feedback, learning feeds, LMS data feeds, online and hybrid learning, and connections to external Moodle, Canvas, Brightspace and Blackboard environments. Native authoring is less fully documented than the SIS functions; institutions should confirm content-authoring depth during evaluation [5] [9].

#### Communication and Academic CRM

Academic CRM connects students, parents, educators, employees, agents and alumni through announcements, events, meetings, internal messages, email, SMS, push notifications, feedback and surveys. Communication templates can be customized and messages can be logged on the relevant record. Mailgun is the documented email/SMS example; WhatsApp is not identified as a native channel in the reviewed official materials, so it should not be assumed [1] [4] [5].

#### Parent, student, teacher and other portals

Separate portals serve students, parents, applicants, educators, employees, alumni, agents and employer/partners. They expose role-specific classes/homework/grades/attendance, calendars, reports, payments, communications, consents, enrollment, timetables, leads, commissions and internships [1] [4].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Billing covers arrangements, installment plans, contracts, flexible pricing, payers/activities, mass billing, invoices, online payments, cash-flow/balance reports, forecasts, expenditures, payment imports, SEPA and barcodes. Classter Payments, built with Nuvei, launched cards in Europe, the UK, Canada and the US in November 2026; standing orders, ACH and SEPA were roadmap items [20]. Stripe, PayPal, BlueSnap, DIAS and WooCommerce are named integrations. A full general ledger is not publicly evidenced.

#### HR, staff and payroll

The HR module now documents centralized employee records, personal data, qualifications, contracts and job roles; attendance and check-in/check-out; absence/late/early notifications; payroll calculations, deductions, bonuses and digital payslips; performance/appraisals; professional goals and training; recruitment; applicant tracking; and onboarding [26].

#### Transport

Transportation Management handles student transportation, bus routes, fleet and vehicle records, student assignments and integrated transport administration. The public page confirms routes, fleets and student transportation, while the help center exposes a dedicated transportation settings section. GPS/live vehicle tracking is not publicly confirmed [25] [6].

#### Library

Library covers physical and online libraries, barcode book records, lending and charging, online search and reservation, personal student/teacher library portals, course-specific libraries, course literature, teaching-session connections, ISBN integration and book-health/status tracking [24].

#### College and higher-education administration

The College module covers configurable curricula, programs, subjects, semesters, credits, enrollment, progression, transcripts, grading, examinations, thesis and internships. Public materials do not establish research administration, grants, faculty workload or campus-facilities ERP [4] [33].

#### Internship, thesis, alumni and careers

Internship & Thesis provides employer matching, opportunities, applications, dashboards, workflows, logbooks, contracts, thesis guidance and grading [27]. Alumni have records, portal, communications and community engagement; dedicated fundraising is not documented.

#### Surveys and quizzes

This module includes subject quizzes, smart marking, online questionnaires and surveys, admissions surveys, quiz builder, question banks, teacher evaluations, online exams and control tools. The page also states anonymous surveys, which are useful for course/teacher feedback [28].

#### Protocols and e-signatures

The module index lists Protocols and Signatures, and the help center provides configuration manuals. E-signed contracts are documented in admissions, but protocol numbering, routing and signature-vendor details require confirmation [4] [6] [9].

#### Agents

Agents is a dedicated module/portal for external representatives: lead capture, application tracking, applicant status, communications and commission visibility. It is especially relevant to international recruitment and higher education, but public evidence does not specify commission accounting rules or agent marketplace size [1] [4].

#### Analytics, dashboards, reporting, AI and advanced configuration

Advanced Features includes multi-campus management, adaptive terminology, BI dashboards, custom pages/fields, report builder, lists/reports, notifications, unique IDs, templates and open API [22]. The help center lists five AI articles: Early Warning, Attendance Summary, Exam Scheduling, Teaching Companion and Timetable Scheduling [23]. Public sources do not provide model names, accuracy benchmarks or a separate AI price.

#### Government/state reporting, compliance, special education and safeguarding

The SIS page claims QQI, Ofsted, EHEA and national-accreditation export templates plus audit logs [9]. Consents and permissions are configurable, but no reviewed public source establishes dedicated special-education case management, statutory safeguarding workflows or state-reporting certification. Behavior points/remarks/badges and pastoral mentors are documented [5].

#### Mobile apps

The mobile app provides dashboards, push notifications, calendars, announcements, attendance, timetables, assessments, homework, leave applications, digital cards, messaging, learning resources, consents, reports and financial overview; teachers also manage classwork and students. It requires an institution subscription and login [17] [18] [19].

#### Security, privacy and interoperability

Security features include role permissions, consent management, audit logs, Azure Files, backup/disaster recovery and configurable access. Vertitech’s privacy notice describes processing under applicable data-protection laws and says the services are not directed at children under 16 [21].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **One longitudinal student record:** admissions through alumni can remain connected without re-keying [9].
* **Configurable academic model:** programs, terms, criteria, grading, credits and progression are institution-defined [5].
* **Multi-campus operation:** centralized administration can span locations with period-specific configuration [22].
* **AI scheduling and early warning:** the help center documents AI teaching, timetable/exam and Early Warning tools [23].
* **Deployment choice:** Azure SaaS and on-premise installation support different infrastructure needs [8].
* **Embedded payments:** Classter Payments is designed around recurring education payment terms [20].
* **Open Consumer API:** customers can read/write data and browse live API calls [7].

### Pricing Details

Classter has a public pricing page but not a standard tier card. The official example, checked 24 November 2026, prices a 1,000-student higher-education institution at **€8.50 per active student per year for Core**, **€6.50 for Academics & LMS**, and **€6.50 for Surveys & Quizzes**, totaling **€25,500 per year or €21.50 per active student per year** [3]. It is an example, not a universal rate. Annual or bi-annual billing is available, with up to 20% discount for two years; setup and implementation fees are not itemized [3].

Capterra and G2 label current pricing “contact vendor”; G2 describes per-student monthly/yearly pricing and one Core edition [12] [14]. An eLearning Industry directory last updated April 2023 lists an estimated €1.50 per active student per annum, but this is stale and conflicts with the current example [11].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Classter advertises 40+ integrations and an open API, including Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Teams, Zoom, Webex, Moodle, Canvas, Brightspace, Blackboard, Turnitin, HubSpot, DocuSign, Mailgun, Stripe, PayPal, BlueSnap, DIAS, Xero, WooCommerce, OneLogin and Power BI [1] [13] [16] [34]. The Consumer API reads/writes data; bulk tools cover students, staff, groups, subjects, books, timetables, payments and grades [7] [23].

An independent 2023 directory lists AICC, IMS Common Cartridge, IMS LTI/QTI, PENS, RTWS, SCORM, Section 508 and xAPI [11]. These are directory claims, not current 1EdTech certifications. Public sources do not establish Ed-Fi, SIF, OneRoster, Clever/ClassLink or a public developer marketplace. Reviewers report Microsoft 365 SSO, but no complete SSO matrix is published [13] [16].

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Classter states that it runs on Azure with Azure Backup, role access, audit logs, secure documents and on-premise deployment. Its SIS page says “ISO 27001 & GDPR Ready,” 99.9% uptime and EU residency on request [8] [9]. “Ready” is not a published Classter ISO certificate or SOC 2 report. The reviewed sources do not verify SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA, DPDP or an independent penetration test. GDPR consents and the privacy notice are documented [5] [21]. No public incident report was located as of 24 November 2026.

### Strengths

* Broad, modular coverage across SIS, LMS, admissions, finance, CRM, HR, transport, library and higher education.
* Strong configuration of curricula, grading, admissions workflows, portals, terminology, reports and institution-specific fields.
* Azure cloud, on-premise choice, backup/disaster-recovery claims and a read/write API suit institutions replacing legacy systems.
* Reviewers consistently praise support, centralization, customization and breadth: Capterra reports 4.6/5 from 115 reviews, GetApp 4.7/5 from 114, and Software Advice 4.7 [12] [15] [16].
* A meaningful higher-education layer—credits, transcripts, internships, thesis and employer portal—differentiates it from basic K-12 administration tools.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* Implementation and configuration can be time-consuming. G2 reviewers praise support but mention setup difficulty, bugs, integration issues and limited customization in some workflows [13].
* Capterra reviewers report that nonstandard institutions may find workflows rigid and features non-obvious without training; one 2026 reviewer cited Canadian tax-receipting fit [12].
* Reviewers note finance/logistics reports may need tweaking, and that the platform’s many features can confuse less technical students or administrators [13] [15].
* Moodle integration has had interface problems for at least one higher-education reviewer, although the reviewer said Classter worked on improvements [13].
* Mobile sentiment is materially weaker than web review sentiment: Apple is 2.4/5 from 13 ratings and Google Play shows roughly 3.4–3.5/5, with complaints about limited app functionality, re-authentication after updates and homework not appearing reliably [17] [18].
* Public compliance evidence is incomplete: reviewed sources do not publish SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA or DPDP attestations.
* Pricing is customized and module-based, so buyers cannot calculate a reliable total cost from a standard rate card; implementation fees are not disclosed [3].

### Key Milestones

* **2015:** Classter/Vertitech founded in Greece by Nikolaos Nikou; the product began with Core, Academics, Billing and CRM [2] [10].
* **2015–2017:** Odyssey Venture Partners and EIF-backed JEREMIE Greece financing supported product development and international sales [11].
* **By 2018:** EIF reported more than 400 institutions across the Balkans, southern Europe, Africa, the UK and Germany [11].
* **2018 onward:** Admissions, transportation, library and alumni capabilities were added as the platform expanded; Classter later passed 400 active institutions [2].
* **4 March 2020:** Classter announced its Android and iOS mobile application [19].
* **2023:** Classter reported entering the United States and receiving early industry awards; the current About page presents this as a milestone [2].
* **2025:** Classter’s current site reports 500+ institutions and 300,000+ users; Banyan Software announced acquisition of Veritech on 10 October 2025 [9] [10].
* **17 November 2026:** Classter Payments card processing went live in Europe, the UK, Canada and the US with Nuvei; standing orders, ACH and SEPA were announced as staged roadmap items [20].

[13] [14] [16] [17] |

### Overview

openSIS is OS4ED’s student information and school-management system. It centralizes student, family, staff, admissions, academic, attendance, grading, scheduling, communication, billing and reporting workflows for K–12, higher education, trade schools and virtual programs. The current commercial positioning is cloud-hosted, staff-account pricing with unlimited student and parent accounts, while the Community Edition remains open source under the GNU GPL. [1] [2] [5] [12]

OS4ED states that openSIS has served institutions since 2008 and now describes the product as AI-powered, with a live AI lesson-plan builder, natural-language search, reporting assistance, predictive insights and the “Piloo” guide. The company also offers openIntel for data warehousing and business intelligence. No public acquisition, institutional funding round, or separate product-company merger was found; Crunchbase lists OS4ED as active, private and for-profit. [2] [9] [15] [20]

The supplied guide is directionally right about the hybrid/open-source model and 2008 product history, but several claims need correction. It labels 2008 as the company founding year even though the primary source only dates openSIS service; its “thousands” adoption statement omits the current official 1,200+ institutions, 1M+ students and 80+ countries claims; its $500 setup fee is not on the current official price card; and its AI, openIntel, ISO 27001:2022 and WhatsApp claims are supported by current official pages, but should be described as vendor claims rather than independently audited product capabilities. The guide also implies a fuller ERP breadth than the public catalog supports: no native transport, library, hostel, inventory/assets, payroll/HR, alumni/fundraising or complete special-education/safeguarding module is publicly evidenced.

### Platform Classification Explained

The SaaS edition is browser-accessible and cloud-hosted. The Microsoft Marketplace listing says openSIS is hosted on Microsoft Azure and uses Azure security and scalability features; the “Why openSIS?” page claims 99.99% uptime backed by Azure. These are vendor/channel statements, not an independently verified SLA. [3] [21]

The Community Edition is a PHP/MySQL web application that can be installed independently. The GitHub repository identifies Community Edition 9.3, released June 2, 2026, and lists Apache 2.4+, MySQL/MariaDB and PHP 8.x requirements. It is GPL-licensed. OS4ED separately describes Professional Edition as licensed on-premises software and SaaS as a managed cloud service. [2] [12]

The official mobile product is **openSIS SaaS Mobile Connect**. The Apple listing supports iPhone and describes student, parent and teacher access to attendance, schedules, grades, assignments, announcements and institutional communication. Google Play lists the same named Android app and records Google and Microsoft SSO plus PayPal and Stripe payment support. There is one role-aware app rather than separately named Parent, Student and Teacher apps. [13] [14]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### School, institution and multi-school administration

The School Information module supports school dashboards, unlimited custom fields, marking periods (year, semester, quarter, trimester or custom ranges), summer-school dates, multi-calendar and bell-schedule management, holiday/event notifications, notices, course/program/subject/section setup, rooms and capacity, grade-level equivalencies, role-based access control, menu-level permissions, access logs, Excel export, reports, year-end rollover and “Copy School” templating for similar schools. Multiple school enrollment and district/enterprise rollups are available in the catalog; district dashboards and data warehouses are custom/enterprise options. [4] [6]

#### Student information and records

Student 360 stores identifiers, photos, demographics, contacts, family/custody and sibling links, documents and comments. It supports unlimited custom fields, masked Social Security numbers, enrollment/transfer history, rolling retention, multiple-school and multi-program enrollment, 504/SpEd/LEP and economic-disadvantage/free-lunch indicators, advisor assignment, mass updates, Excel imports, historical grades, saved searches, edit history, administrator impersonation and Boolean custom report queries. ID cards can include barcodes and QR codes. [4]

#### Admissions and applicant processing

Admissions includes dashboards for received, processing, enrolled and rejected applications; gender/program charts; customizable multi-page forms with CAPTCHA, custom fields, tags, staff assignment and export; process steps for academic/financial checks, interviews, acceptance/rejection and wait-listing; event-triggered email templates; medical fields; multilingual translation; conditional logic; multiple forms; CSS styling; fee refunds/subscriptions; and transfer of applicant fields into the enrolled student record. [4] [7]

#### Course, curriculum and timetable/master scheduling

Course Manager handles programs, subjects, courses, sections, prerequisites, learning outcomes and catalogs. Scheduling supports fixed, variable-day, custom-date, year-round/summer, block, rotating, mosaic and multi-period models. Administrators can group schedule/drop students and teachers, reassign teachers, manage team teaching, identify open periods, distinguish required/elective and Honors/AP/college tracks, support homeschooled and before/after-school students, permit conflict exceptions and accept course requests. [4] [19]

#### Attendance

Attendance provides unlimited codes and categories, excused/unexcused/tardy marks, teacher comments, administrator overrides and override comments, advance absence entry, missing-attendance monitoring, administrator entry on behalf of teachers, period or homeroom attendance, one-click whole-class marking, state/district minute rules, full-day/half-day recalculation and canned attendance reports. [4] [7]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

The gradebook supports multiple grade scales, percentage/letter grading, weighted assignments, teacher-defined scales, multi-term weighting, Common Core or school standards, effort/performance grades, honor roll, exemptions, rounding, exam grades, GPA, historical grades and prerequisite validation. The catalog documents exam-grade entry and calculation into final report-card grades, but not a separate examination-management suite. [4]

#### Report cards, transcripts and degree audit

Report cards can use canned and teacher comments, GPA and AI-assisted comment generation. One-click report-card and transcript generation, four-year consolidated academic history, trade-school transcript records, historical grade entry and progress reports are supported. Graduation/Degree Audit lets institutions define programs, credit categories and course requirements, support multi-program enrollment, schedule students into requirement-linked courses and expose Graduation Progress to students and administrators. [4] [19]

#### Learning management, homework and lesson planning

openSIS has lesson plans and curriculum tools, but LMS capability is primarily integration rather than a full native LMS. Teachers can create, copy, edit, align, attach and publish lesson plans for student/parent viewing; AI assists lesson-plan, curriculum and syllabus generation. Moodle, Canvas and Google Classroom integrations synchronize users, courses, assignments, lessons, schedules and grades with mapping, REST configuration, sync controls and LMS SSO. [4] [8] [9]

#### Communication

Communication supports SMTP/provider APIs, broadcast groups, email, attachments, notices, SMS through gateways such as Twilio and WhatsApp through Meta Cloud API. AI can translate messages by recipient language and draft in selectable tones. Push notifications are documented for the mobile app, but no separate push service is publicly described. [4] [8] [14]

#### Teacher, student and parent portals

Teacher Portal workflows cover attendance, gradebook, final grades, lesson plans, course information and classroom dashboards. Student Portal provides profile, schedules, grades, attendance, course requests, lesson plans, curricula, syllabi and graduation progress. Parent Portal provides linked-student information, academic progress, attendance, communications, lesson plans, curricula, syllabi and billing/payment access. Permissions, portal disablement, password rules and SSO are configurable. [4] [7]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Billing supports fee assignment, fee types/due dates, invoices, cash/check/card/EFT, ledgers, statements, aging, reminders, waivers/voids, refunds, deposits, scholarships/grants, payment links, Excel exports, recurring subscriptions and role-based fund deposits. Institutions can define a general-ledger chart and subaccounts. Stripe handles subscriptions; QuickBooks can synchronize charges, invoices and payments, and PayPal/Authorize.net are listed. This is school billing with accounting connectivity, not a full general-ledger ERP. [4] [8]

#### Staff and teacher management

Staff records include demographics, IDs, photos, masked SSNs, employment history, schools, grade levels, subjects, addresses, emergency contacts, documents and teacher certifications with expiry tracking. Administrators can search, filter, report, impersonate and act for teachers in attendance and grading. The public materials do not evidence a full HR recruitment, benefits, timekeeping or payroll module. [4]

#### Health and medical records

Health captures physicians, dentist and eye-doctor contacts, insurance and policy data, preferred facilities, critical alerts, immunization/physical dates, infirmary visits and nurse notes, with report filtering. Medical fields can also be collected in admissions. OS4ED describes these as education-administration health records, not a covered healthcare system. [4] [10] [11]

#### Behavior and discipline

Behavior records support incident categories, date/time/location, involved students and witnesses, action plans, detentions, suspensions, interventions, follow-up, parent notifications, custom forms, access-level controls, reports, exports, historical records and trend analysis. Public documentation does not establish a separate safeguarding/child-protection case-management suite. [4] [7]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Built-in dashboards cover admissions, collections, overdue balances, attendance and academic operations. Custom reports can query fields with Boolean/comparison logic, save filters, select columns and export to Excel. Academic Analytics is described as dashboards, KPIs, visual summaries and trends. District/enterprise customers can add advanced reporting, data visualization, data warehouse/BI and openIntel; the higher-education page claims enrollment, program-outcome, completion, retention and predictive insights. [4] [6] [8] [19]

#### AI features

Current production-facing AI claims include Piloo, natural-language Smart Search, reporting support, multilingual communication, workflow guidance, AI lesson-plan generation and AI-assisted report-card comments. OS4ED also describes predictive early-warning analytics for academic failure, attendance, enrollment and course demand. Curriculum Builder and Syllabus Builder are described as recently released, while broader intelligent workflows are marked coming soon. These are vendor claims; independent reviews do not yet validate their performance. [9] [20]

#### Mobile apps, integrations, APIs and security controls

The role-aware openSIS SaaS Mobile Connect apps cover attendance, schedules, grades, assignments, announcements, communication and payments. The integration catalog names Moodle, Canvas, Google Classroom, Microsoft Teams, Office 365, Microsoft Entra ID/Azure AD, Google Workspace, Zoho CRM, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, PayPal, Authorize.net, QuickBooks, Twilio/SendGrid and openIntel. Advanced pricing includes API access with full documentation; the help center describes API endpoints, keys, OAuth, synchronization and integration logs. No public evidence was found for OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF certification, Clever or ClassLink. [5] [7] [8]

The platform has RBAC, custom profiles, menu-level permissions, audit/access logs, password controls, optional MFA, SSO, masked sensitive identifiers, data import/export and rollover. Transport, library, hostel/boarding, inventory/assets, alumni/fundraising and payroll/HR are not publicly evidenced as native modules; state reporting is a custom district/enterprise option rather than a broadly documented built-in capability. [4] [6]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- Staff-based pricing leaves student and parent accounts unlimited. [5]
- GPL Community Edition self-hosting sits alongside SaaS and Professional deployments. [2] [12]
- “Copy School,” rollover, conditional admissions workflows and bidirectional LMS integrations support institutional scale. [4] [8]
- AI spans lesson planning, communication, search, reporting and early-warning analytics; openIntel adds custom BI/data warehousing. [2] [9] [20]

### Pricing Details

The current official price page, checked November 24, 2026, offers a 15-day free trial and staff-based pricing in U.S. dollars. Essential annual is $480 total per year with five staff accounts included and additional staff at $8 per month billed annually; Essential monthly is $50 total per month with five staff included and additional staff at $10 per month. Advanced annual is $1,440 total per year with ten staff included and additional staff at $12 per month billed annually; Advanced monthly is $140 total per month with ten staff included and additional staff at $14 per month. The page’s repeated “per staff / month” label is a presentation error; the adjacent totals and included-staff language make clear that $480 and $1,440 are plan totals, not five- or ten-fold charges. [5]

Community Edition is free and GPL-licensed. Professional on-premises and District/State/Enterprise SaaS pricing is quote-based. Custom options can add white labeling, dedicated data isolation, custom modules/integrations, data warehouse/BI, district dashboards, state reporting, advanced reporting, implementation, training, account management and fixed annual or per-student pricing. The guide’s optional $500 setup-service claim was not found on the current official pricing page; it should be treated as unverified. [2] [5] [6]

Capterra and G2 display annual reference tiers of $4, $8 and $12 per user per month, corresponding to the public Core/Startup, Essential and Advanced labels, but both are marketplace listings rather than a separate official rate card. [16] [17]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Named integrations include Moodle, Canvas, Google Classroom, Microsoft Teams, Office 365/Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID/Azure AD, Google Workspace, Zoho CRM, Salesforce, HubSpot, QuickBooks, Stripe, PayPal, Authorize.net, Twilio/SendGrid, WhatsApp via Meta Cloud API and openIntel. The product supports SSO, OAuth, documented API access on Advanced, REST-based LMS connectivity, Excel/CSV import-export and integration/synchronization logs. [7] [8]

No verified OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF certification was found, and no public Clever/ClassLink connector was found. Capterra lists seven integrations and G2 lists six, so marketplace counts vary by catalog scope. [16] [17]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

OS4ED states that it is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified and markets FERPA, GDPR and COPPA alignment. Its March 1, 2026 privacy policy describes AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, RBAC, administrator MFA, penetration testing, network controls, Azure/Stripe subprocessors and 30-day post-termination student-data deletion. OS4ED acts as processor for institution data and offers DPA/SCC mechanisms for GDPR transfers. [1] [3] [10] [11]

The policy discusses FERPA, COPPA, PPRA, GDPR/UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA and state privacy laws. It describes HIPAA-consistent safeguards, not HIPAA certification. No public SOC 2 scope, data-region list, OneRoster/Ed-Fi certification, India DPDP statement or public security incident was found. Google Play says no third-party sharing, encryption in transit, possible financial/health collection and that data cannot be deleted, a notable tension with the web policy. [10] [14]

### Strengths

- Broad core SIS coverage and a choice of GPL self-hosting, SaaS and Professional deployment.
- Predictable staff-based pricing with unlimited student and parent accounts.
- Strong customization through fields, forms, reports, roles, workflows and school templates.
- Named integrations across LMS, identity, messaging, payments, CRM and accounting, plus a broad AI roadmap.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Independent review volume is extremely small and ratings are weak: G2 is 2.9/5 from five reviews and Capterra is 1.0/5 from one review. [16] [17]
- G2 reviewers cite an outdated or less user-friendly interface, difficulty contacting support, limited support/resources, missing application management, limited rules/configuration, slow bug fixes and extra effort for scheduling changes. [17]
- A 2026 Capterra/G2 reviewer alleges that a discontinued free account led to deletion of four years of academic data without effective warning; the allegation conflicts with current Terms promising 14 days’ notice and export before inactive free-tier deletion, but it remains a material user-risk signal. [11] [16] [17]
- SourceForge users praise breadth and usefulness but report installation problems, bugs, low support/design scores and historical billing gaps in older Community Edition releases; those comments are dated and should not be read as a direct evaluation of SaaS 2026. [18]
- The public product is not a complete school ERP: transport, library, hostel, inventory, payroll/HR, alumni/fundraising and full special-education/safeguarding workflows are not evidenced.
- Standards interoperability is less transparent than leading district SIS vendors: no verified OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF certification was found.

### Key Milestones

- **2008:** OS4ED’s official history says openSIS began serving educational institutions; the company’s own incorporation year is not publicly disclosed. [2] [3]
- **2018:** The public OS4ED/openSIS-Classic GitHub repository was created, preserving the self-hosted Community Edition codebase. [12]
- **2020s:** OS4ED continued Community, Professional on-premises and SaaS editions and positioned openIntel as a companion BI/data-warehouse product. [2] [8]
- **March–June 2026:** Current Terms/Privacy documents became effective; Community Edition 9.3 was released June 2, 2026. [10] [11] [12]
- **June–November 2026:** OS4ED published AI positioning and listed the SaaS Mobile Connect app for iOS and Android. [9] [13] [14] [20]
- **Funding/acquisitions:** No verified transaction was found in reviewed sources.

## #18. iSAMS (IRIS Software Group)

| Field | Detail |

### Overview

iSAMS is a UK-origin, web-based school management information system (MIS/SIS) for independent, international, online and multi-school K–12 organisations. It keeps student, academic, pastoral, admissions, communication, HR and financial information in a core database, then exposes it through administration screens, portals, apps, reporting and APIs. It is especially aimed at schools with multiple curricula, time zones, languages, campuses and fee-paying workflows [1] [2].

The company says it was founded by Rugby School alumni in 2005 and commercially launched its first web-based product that year. Later additions included HR, portals, SMS, mobile apps, fee billing, census, data protection, wellbeing, iFinance and Central analytics [3]. iSAMS acquired prep-school specialist CJM Software in September 2018 [5], then IRIS acquired iSAMS in October 2020; IRIS reported more than 1,000 schools across 80 countries at that point [4].

### Platform Classification Explained

iSAMS is primarily browser-based cloud software. The current site calls it 100% cloud-based, and EdTech Impact identifies Microsoft Azure as its hosting environment [1] [6]. No current desktop client is documented. A historical on-site hosting option is not a current on-premise offer [3].

The mobile layer includes native iParent, iStudent, iTeacher and iReport apps [29]. iParent and iStudent provide timetables, attendance, exams, reports, behaviour and notifications [30] [31]. Newer Parent and Student Cloud Portals are responsive progressive web apps with push notifications and custom branding [28].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

The Admissions Cloud Portal is a branded, mobile-responsive website connected to the Admissions module and core MIS. It supports 24/7 enquiry and registration forms, multiple applicants on one account, applicant tracking, campaign/conversion reporting, registration-fee payment, outstanding-fee flags, document upload, personalised and automated email notifications, real-time reporting and automatic synchronisation into iSAMS [16].

#### Student information and records

Student Manager stores current/former-student records, family trees, admissions/census data, discipline, passports/visas, contacts, transport, health, SEN, documents and alumni information. It provides search, custom fields, result grids, group operations, exports, Email Wizard, section permissions and audit history [20].

#### Attendance and registration

Attendance is available through school and lesson registration, future absences, medical exemptions and off-games/absence information. Attendance appears in Student Manager, Parent/Student Portals, iParent/iStudent and Central reporting; the student portal also gives students real-time attendance visibility [26] [27] [30] [31].

#### Timetable, curriculum and cover

Timetable Manager creates unlimited draft, preliminary, published and archived timetables; supports students, forms, teachers, rooms, subjects, departments, years and teaching sets; adds meetings, tutorials, year schedules, preparation periods and teacher availability; detects clashes and missing links; logs changes; and exports/prints PDF, HTML and Excel. It imports Nova-T 4/6, TimeTabler, Edval, Timetabling Solutions, Skolaris, GP-Untis, ASC Timetable and Excel. Curriculum Manager links imported timetables and sets to automatically generate gradebooks. Cover Manager handles staff absence cover [21].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

The product includes Curriculum Manager, Teaching Manager and Gradebooks for enrolment, courses, sets and academic tracking. Internal and external examination information includes entries, arrangements, candidate details, timetables and results. Students and parents can view these data through portals and apps [20] [26] [27] [30] [31]. iSAMS does not present itself as a full built-in LMS; instead, its LMS strategy is integration with Canvas, Google Classroom, ManageBac, Schoolbox, Toddle and Microsoft Teams [12].

#### Report cards and transcripts

School Reporting publishes reports and assessment data to the Parent and Student Portals. Recent portal controls allow staff to publish or withdraw reports for selected students and manage exceptions. iReport is the dedicated teacher reporting app, while portal/app users can view published reports and assessment history [26] [27] [28] [29].

#### Homework and learning-management boundary

The new Homework module lets staff create assignments, set deadlines and attach documents or links. Homework is surfaced in Student Cloud Portal and Parent Cloud Portal widgets. This is native homework/assignment management, but iSAMS explicitly says it does not offer a built-in LMS; it connects to external LMS/VLE products instead [12] [28].

#### Communication

Email Wizard sends database-driven email using live correspondence permissions, merges sibling households where appropriate, splits personalised child messages and logs every email to the student record. SMS Gateway supports templates, authorisations, sender identities, budget limits, detailed logs, scheduled messages and emergency broadcasts through third-party mobile providers. Portals and apps add email, SMS, push notifications, news, bulletins, calendars, photo galleries and electronic forms [11] [26] [30]. No official WhatsApp module was found in the reviewed product pages.

#### Parent, student, teacher and admissions portals

The Parent Portal supports branded content, timetables, teaching groups, attendance, future absences, reports, assessment, exams, activities, discipline, rewards, electronic forms, documents, online invoices/payments, email/SMS groups and visitor analytics. The Student Cloud Portal adds homework, push notifications, contact updates, timetable export, attendance, behaviour, exams, reports, forms, documents and usage analytics. The Admissions Portal is described above. Teacher-facing access is delivered through the web system and iTeacher/iReport apps rather than a separately documented teacher web portal [10] [26] [27] [29].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Fee Billing generates bills and charges for applicants, current students and alumni, individually or by batch; supports split billing, recurring charges, discounts, VAT, nominal structures, multiple-student invoices, applicant filters, invoice history, notes, traffic-light status and export to Excel, Word and PDF. iSAMS Payments provides integrated cashless/online payments. iFinance adds general ledger, multi-currency, bank feeds, reconciliation, AP Inbox, invoice processing, workflow approvals, recurring invoicing, deferred income, BI dashboards, audit trails, fixed assets, stock, expenses and multi-entity/group consolidation [2] [19] [22].

#### HR, staff and payroll

HR provides employee records, automated outdated-data alerts, staff absence dashboards, calendars and reports, Single Central Record checks, multi-school SCR sharing, case management for flexible working/disputes/appeals, policy distribution and acceptance, read reminders and audit trails. IRIS/iSAMS also markets UK-focused payroll and pensions integration, although the detailed HR page reviewed concentrates on HR rather than pay-run mechanics [2] [18].

#### Activities, calendar and bookings

Activities Manager and Calendar Manager feed activity groups, events, sports and calendars into portals/apps. The November 2026 iSAMS Bookings launch adds parent-evening scheduling, video meetings, events, clubs and wraparound-care bookings; the new functionality is visible on the Parent Cloud Portal page [1] [26].

#### Inventory and assets

iFinance contains Stock Management, purchasing/ePOS/CRM integration, stock-level tracking, Fixed Asset Register, asset documents, leases/loans, maintenance/renewal dates, depreciation journals, fixed-asset schedules and CapEx forecasting [19].

#### Health and medical

Student records include dental, eye, hearing, vaccination, BMI, medical notes, public-health notes, conditions matrices, trip fields and health alerts with restricted access. The product navigation also identifies a Medical Centre module, and the portal can expose medical exemptions/attendance information. The Student Manager health record is the clearest publicly documented detail [20] [22].

#### Behaviour, discipline and pastoral care

Reward & Conduct supports configurable commendations, detentions, positive/negative incidents, house points, instant notifications, iTeacher entry and cross-record analysis. Student Wellbeing tracks life events, indicators, flags, care contributors and strict viewing permissions. Portals/apps expose appropriate rewards, detentions, conduct and pastoral records [17] [26] [27] [30].

#### Special education and safeguarding

SEN details are held in student records and Central provides an SEN report. Wellbeing analytics can compare conduct and concerns. Data Protection manages consent registers, parental consent, image-sharing permissions and DSAR workflows, while HR’s Single Central Record supports staff safeguarding checks [17] [18] [23].

#### Alumni and fundraising

Student Manager retains former-student records including occupation, family, education and donations. This is an alumni/contact and donation record capability, not evidence of a full fundraising CRM, campaign-management suite or donor-payment system [20].

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Central is built on Microsoft Power BI and iSAMS APIs. It provides visual dashboards, behaviour/wellbeing analytics, real-time updates, SEN reporting, assessment-data expansion and multi-school/group oversight. iSAMS announced Central in September 2023 and reported adoption by more than 100 schools by June 2024 [15].

#### AI features

Central’s 2024 AI update added a natural-language Q&A visualisation: users type a prompt and Central generates a report that can then be customised. This is a production AI reporting assistant, not evidence of an AI tutor, automated grading engine or predictive-admissions system [15].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Census Manager was created for UK and international census requirements. Data Protection supports GDPR consent and DSAR processes; iFinance is UK VAT-ready; payroll is designed for UK HMRC and pension schemes according to the product overview [2] [3] [23]. No public evidence was found in the reviewed pages for Ed-Fi state reporting, US FERPA/COPPA certification or India DPDP Act-specific compliance.

#### Mobile apps

The native app set is iParent, iStudent, iTeacher and iReport. iParent/iStudent cover information access and push notifications; iTeacher supports classroom tasks such as registers, rewards, communication and cover/timetables; iReport supports teacher grades, assessments and reports. iParent and iStudent are listed on both iOS and Android channels; iSAMS also has cross-platform PWA portals [29] [30] [31] [32].

#### Integrations and APIs

iSAMS exposes REST API for real-time reads/writes and Batch API for standardised extraction and synchronisation. It offers SSO/social login, a developer portal and a marketplace with over 200 integration partners. Named LMS/VLE connections include Canvas, Google Classroom, ManageBac, Schoolbox, Toddle and Microsoft Teams; payment partners shown include Stripe, Esenda, Flywire and TransferMate [12] [19].

#### Security and privacy

The vendor states that iSAMS holds BSI ISO 27001:2022 and Cyber Essentials certification; its privacy policy identifies Azure as the hosting processor and describes GDPR-oriented safeguards. App listings state encryption in transit or encrypted app data. No SOC 2 report, FERPA/COPPA certification or precise hosting-region commitment was found [24] [25] [30] [32].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Central natural-language Q&A:** prompt-generated Power BI report visualisations [15].
- **Single core database:** cross-functional academic, pastoral, finance and HR data [2] [4].
- **REST plus Batch APIs:** real-time integration and standardised synchronisation [12].
- **200+ partner marketplace:** extensions for LMS, facilities, security and sports [12].
- **International-school design:** multi-curriculum, multi-calendar and multi-currency support [1] [6].
- **Configurable wellbeing and consent:** indicators, role-based viewing, consent and DSAR records [17] [23].
- **PWA portals:** cross-device access, push alerts, branding and low maintenance [26] [27] [28].

### Pricing Details

No official public tiered price, per-student price, implementation fee or setup schedule was available when checked on 24 November 2026; the official pricing URL returned a verification page rather than rates. iSAMS remains quote/demo-led, with price depending on size, modules, integrations and implementation.

Third-party figures are estimates, not official quotes: GetApp lists a flat starting price of **6,000 per year** without a currency [8]; Software Advice Australia says **GBP 6,000/year** with no free version or trial [9]; EdTech Impact says **£5,000/year** and requests a quote [6]. These conflict and are not a standard price; implementation is reported at one to six months [6].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

iSAMS has a public developer portal, REST API, Batch API, SSO/social login and a marketplace claiming more than 200 partners [12]. Named LMS/VLE integrations are Canvas, Google Classroom, ManageBac, Schoolbox, Toddle and Microsoft Teams; payment ecosystem references include Stripe, Esenda, Flywire and TransferMate [12] [19]. iSAMS says it connects through open APIs and roster standards, but the reviewed pages do not name a certified OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF implementation. No evidence was found for Clever or ClassLink certification, nor for a formal accounting marketplace beyond iFinance and payment partners. The practical interoperability proposition is therefore rich API plus marketplace/SSO, not standards certification.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

iSAMS publicly claims BSI ISO 27001:2022 and Cyber Essentials certification [25]. Its privacy policy identifies Microsoft Azure as the hosting service for client data, lists subprocessors, describes security controls and supports GDPR subject-access requests and deletion requests [24]. The dedicated Data Protection module covers GDPR consent, parental consent, consent registers, data-subject access requests and portal visibility [23]. The app listings state encryption in transit and app-level confidentiality controls [30] [32].

The reviewed public material does not substantiate SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA or India DPDP Act compliance, and it does not publish a precise Azure region/tenant-location commitment. No publicly reported incident was identified in the reviewed official, review, app-store and press sources; this is an evidence limitation, not a guarantee that no incident has occurred.

### Strengths

- Broad native MIS coverage for independent and international schools, including admissions, academics, wellbeing, finance, HR and communications [2] [4].
- Strong international fit: multilingual portals/apps, multiple curricula, local time zones, multi-currency finance and a 95+ country vendor claim [1] [3] [6].
- Genuine interoperability through REST/Batch APIs, SSO and a 200+ partner marketplace [12].
- Central’s Power BI dashboards, natural-language Q&A, and ISO 27001:2022/Cyber Essentials claims provide credible analytics and assurance differentiators [15] [25].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Independent review averages are modest: G2 2.5/5, GetApp 3.2/5 and Software Advice 3.2/5, with small samples [7] [8] [9].
- Reviewers describe navigation and workflows as clunky or long-winded, citing complicated registers, timetable setup, reporting and limited flexibility [7].
- EdTech Impact reviewers report an ageing interface, limited bulk import/export, paid custom reports, unreliable Email Wizard behaviour and unaddressed ideas [6].
- US reviewers report rigid regional formats and terminology; Software Advice reviewers cite poor support, difficult customisation and weak reporting/downloads [6] [9].
- iParent/iStudent reviews include login, loading, crashing and glitch complaints [30] [31].
- No built-in LMS or public price book means external learning-platform costs and a bespoke quote [12].

### Key Milestones

- **2005:** iSAMS is founded by Rugby School alumni and commercially launches its first web-based MIS with curriculum, timetable, assessment, reporting and admissions [3].
- **2006–2015:** HR, parent/student portals, cloud hosting, Reward & Conduct, Tracking Manager, international deployments, SMS Gateway, iSAMS mobile, iCommunity, Fee Billing, Census Manager and the iOS/Android app suite are added [3].
- **2016–2018:** Marketplace, Admissions Portal, ManageBac integration, iReport, GDPR/Data Protection, Wellbeing Manager and iFinance are added; iSAMS acquires CJM Software in 2018 [3] [5].
- **2020:** IRIS Software Group acquires iSAMS; the announcement reports over 500 UK independent and over 500 international schools across 80 countries [4].
- **2023–2024:** Central, powered by Microsoft Power BI and APIs, launches; natural-language AI Q&A is added in 2024, and iSAMS reports adoption by 100+ schools [15].
- **2025:** iSAMS launches the redesigned Student Cloud Portal/PWA and native Homework module [28].
- **2026:** The official site reports 1,800+ schools/groups, 1.7M+ student profiles and 95+ countries; recent roadmap items include Central Manage, AI reporting, Schools BI partnership and iSAMS Bookings [1] [3].

## #19. Anthology Student (Ellucian; formerly Anthology Inc./Campus Management)

| Field | Detail |

No Anthology Student-specific native iOS/Android app was publicly verified as of November 24, 2026. |

No public Anthology Student-specific App Store or Google Play rating was verified; Apple’s Anthology Inc. listing showed Blackboard Education View only [6] [7] [8] [9] |

### Overview

Anthology Student is a higher-education student information system (SIS) and ERP-oriented platform that manages the lifecycle from prospect and admission through registration, academics, financial aid, student accounts and completion. Its strongest fit is an institution that needs a detailed, enrollment-centered record for conventional, online, flexible-term and competency-oriented programs rather than a K–12 school-management suite. The system’s newer web client adds responsive workflows, configurable views, forms, workflow automation, APIs and cloud delivery. [6] [10]

The product descends from Campus Management’s CampusNexus Student. Campus Management began as Integrated Solutions in 1988 and accumulated SIS, financial-aid, CRM, finance and HR capabilities; Anthology was formed in 2020 by combining Campus Management, Campus Labs and iModules. Anthology and Blackboard merged in October 2021. In 2025–2026, Anthology entered Chapter 11 restructuring: Blackboard retained the teaching-and-learning business, Ellucian acquired Student/Finance & HCM, and Encoura acquired Reach and the lifecycle-engagement/student-success portfolio. [1] [2] [4] [5]

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser/web:** The current Student web client is the primary user experience. Anthology’s help center documents a web app with tiles, student profiles, responsive self-service pages and role-based authorizations. The G2 profile describes the product as SaaS-based, and the 25.2 release was deployed to Anthology Cloud 1.0 and Cloud 2.0 customers. [6] [10]
* **Cloud hosting:** Anthology Student Cloud 1/2 is documented; AI services use Microsoft Azure OpenAI, with primary hosting in the United States and possible service resources in Canada, the United Kingdom or France. Ellucian separately states that its cloud services use AWS security controls and ISO/SOC programs, but product-specific hosting terms should be confirmed contractually. [11] [12]
* **Desktop/on-premise:** This is not a desktop-only product, but legacy CampusNet and on-premise clients remain supported in release documentation. The documentation suite also lists Installation Manager, replication/upgrade/availability groups and database tools; database tools are explicitly for older on-premise releases. [10]
* **Mobile:** Student self-service pages are mobile-friendly and Capterra lists web, Android and iPhone/iPad deployment, but no dedicated Anthology Student native app name or store listing was verified. Apple’s Anthology Inc. developer page showed “Blackboard Education View,” which is a different product. [7] [9]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment
Prospect and inquiry records, lead/source tracking, expected start dates, admissions representatives, interviews and tasks, document tracking with requested/received/approved/expiration status, programs and program versions, applicant-to-student conversion, application data, enrollment statuses and enrollment reporting are documented. Anthology Student supports configurable admissions-to-academic-record relationships and registration, including waitlists, registration restrictions and enrollment changes. [10] [13]

#### Student information and academic records
The Contact Manager/Student Profile centralizes personal, contact, recruitment, previous-education, citizenship/nationality, athlete, veteran and international-student indicators, notes and SMS subscription fields. Academic Records covers campuses, terms, programs, areas of study, courses, sections, prerequisites, transfer work, degree requirements, degree progress audit, degree pathways, elective pools, requirement rules, course repeats, graduation status and holds. [14] [15]

#### Attendance
Attendance records are attached to student courses and include date, start time, time attended, time absent, excused-absence status, type, unit and notes. Standard views include term-attendance grids/charts, and attendance violations can stop financial-aid disbursement through hold groups. [15] [16]

#### Timetable and master scheduling
Academic calendars, terms, class sections, meeting patterns, buildings, rooms, locations, instructors, secondary instructors, days/times, seat capacity, waitlists, registration relationships and cross-listed/course-sharing rules are supported. The Class Scheduling AI Assistant analyzes historical registration and section data to identify section demand and faculty-hire needs. [15] [17]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations
Student course records store letter, numeric, midterm and final grades, grade points, pass/fail, credits, hours, repeats, withdrawals and last date of attendance. Grade-change reasons and grade reports are available as standard views. A full LMS assessment/exam-authoring product is not part of the verified Student SIS feature set; Blackboard Learn is a separate portfolio product. [15]

#### Report cards and transcripts
Degree progress audits, academic history, grades, credits and degree-awarded records support transcript and completion operations. Hold codes can block transcript printing or release and can prevent graduation-status changes. K–12 report-card workflows are not documented as a native module. [16]

#### Learning management and homework
Anthology Student is an SIS/ERP, not a replacement for an LMS. Course and registration data can integrate with learning systems, while course materials, homework, discussion forums and online assessment belong to Blackboard Learn or another LMS. The G2 page contains user comments about learning resources, but those comments should not be read as proof that Student itself is Blackboard Learn. [6]

#### Communication and contact management
Contact Manager stores tasks, activities, notes, notification triggers and communication history. Student information includes SMS subscription and provider fields; the broader Anthology portfolio includes communication tools, but no verified native WhatsApp or push-notification module was found for Student. Email/SMS workflows and institution-configured alerts are supported; WhatsApp is not publicly documented. [14] [15]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals
The Student/Portal documentation supports student self-service, including registration, schedules, account summary, statements, payment access and other profile/account pages. The 25.2 release added a mobile-friendly My Finances account summary with posted balance, pending charges, expected funding and estimated balance. There is no evidence of a K–12 parent portal; staff/faculty access is role-based in the web client. [10] [18]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting
Student Accounts includes ledger cards, charges, payments, payment schedules, electronic drafts, ACH/credit-card holds, refunds, stipends, student statements, third-party invoices, subsidiary accounts, account aging, general-ledger posting detail and expected financial-aid funding. The product can export general-ledger files and process Title IV-related student-account transactions. Anthology Finance & HCM is the separate institutional finance/ERP product, not merely a Student billing screen. [10] [16] [18]

#### Financial aid
Financial Aid supports FAFSA/ISIR data, Student Aid Index, academic years, award years, term and non-term programs, clock-hour programs, loan periods, payment periods, packaging methods, auto-packaging, manual awards, Pell/SEOG/TEACH/Direct Loan workflows, disbursement schedules, MPN data, COD and NSLDS reporting, crossover packaging, satisfactory-academic-progress/pace evaluation and R2T4/refund calculations. [19]

#### HR, staff and payroll
Faculty Workload is a separately documented integrated product. Anthology Finance & HCM documentation covers human capital management and payroll, including employee/staff records and payroll processes; the 2025 release notes document synchronizing a worker’s “Known As” field into Student staff records. HR/payroll is therefore available in the broader Anthology ERP footprint, not necessarily in the core Student license. [10] [20]

#### Housing/hostel and boarding
Student Services includes Housing, housing status, roommate matching and room placement. Housing holds can prevent automatic roommate matching or placement, while manual placement remains possible. This is higher-education housing rather than a full K–12 hostel/boarding-management suite. [16] [18]

#### Career services
Career Services is a native help-center module with placement records, candidate search, employer-facing placement workflows, graduation/placement holds and placement salary reporting. [10] [16]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting
Views is a distinctive Student feature for building reusable grid and chart views from related data across Academic Records, Admissions, Career Services, Contact Manager, Financial Aid, Student Accounts and Student Services. Users can filter, pin, export and query related objects through OData; standard views cover prospects, documents, active students, grades, attendance, course sections, degrees and aid disbursements. Power BI configuration is documented. [15]

#### AI features
The production AI Product Guide/Help AI is an opt-in sidecar for Cloud 1/2 customers, powered by Azure OpenAI GPT-4o and curated product documentation; it does not access student or school data. The Class Scheduling AI Assistant uses Azure OpenAI to answer constrained section-demand questions from class-seat projections and recent registration history. These are scoped assistants, not a general autonomous student-success agent or proven predictive-retention engine. [11] [17]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance
Regulatory US and 1098-T Processing are separate documented release streams. Student includes Title IV, COD, NSLDS, FAFSA/ISIR, SSCR, R2T4, Gainful Employment, SAI, 1098-T and enrollment-reporting processes. Internationalization includes English, Spanish (Latin America) and French (Canada) system locales. State-specific reporting beyond documented regulatory products should be validated with the institution’s configuration. [10] [19] [20]

#### Integrations and APIs
Anthology Student provides REST APIs, OData queries, SOAP/WCF Service Catalog services, an object library, student data-model/ERD documentation, Connector Configuration and GitHub resources. REST access requires an Azure Active Directory account, a Student staff record, Security Console permissions and an application key. APIs are licensed-campus only; third-party public use is prohibited without Anthology/Ellucian consent. [10] [21]

#### Security, permissions and privacy
The Security Console provides staff groups, roles, authorizations, hold overrides and granular module permissions. Anthology Student’s AI documentation says the product is ISO 27001/27017/27018 certified and pursuing ISO 27701; Ellucian’s current cloud program reports SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001:2022, PCI DSS and other controls. FERPA, GDPR and state privacy obligations remain shared institution/vendor contractual responsibilities; no Student-specific public certification for COPPA or India’s DPDP Act was verified. [12] [17]

#### Not native or not publicly verified
No native Student modules were found for school transport, library circulation, inventory/assets, health/medical records, behavior/discipline, special education/safeguarding, alumni fundraising or a dedicated homework/LMS product. Anthology/Encoura has separate Reach, Encompass, Advance, Raise and student-success/advancement products, and Blackboard has a separate LMS. [1] [2]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **Cloud 1/2 web client:** The modern browser interface combines role-based tiles, student profiles, responsive self-service and release-managed SaaS deployment.
* **Views and OData:** Administrators can build reusable grid/chart views across related objects rather than relying only on fixed reports. [15]
* **Complex aid engine:** Term/non-term, clock-hour, crossover, COD, MPN, R2T4 and automated packaging logic make it unusually specialized for U.S. postsecondary financial aid. [19]
* **AI Product Guide:** An opt-in documentation assistant uses Azure OpenAI GPT-4o without accessing student data. [11]
* **Scheduling AI Assistant:** Constrained natural-language analysis of seat projections identifies undersubscribed or over-demand sections and additional-section needs. [17]
* **No-code extension layer:** Forms Builder and Workflow Composer provide configurable forms and process automation; the exact workflow catalog is institution-specific.
* **Detailed control model:** Security Console, student groups and cross-module hold codes support operational controls such as blocking registration, transcripts, disbursements or housing placement. [16]

### Pricing Details

There is no public Anthology Student price list, free tier, trial or published per-student/per-year rate. Capterra listed “Contact vendor for pricing” and no free trial on August 20, 2026; G2 also showed no numerical public price. Implementation, migration, training, managed services, modules, hosting and support fees are quote-based and should be requested from Ellucian. A Capterra review reports that migration from CampusVue to CampusNexus was “tremendously expensive” and that managed services could also be expensive, but this is historical user commentary rather than a current price. [6] [7]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Documented interoperability includes Student REST APIs, OData, SOAP/WCF Service Catalog, Azure Active Directory authentication, an ERD/object library, Connector Configuration, Power BI and integration with Anthology Reach, Finance & HCM, Occupation Insight, Portal, Forms Builder, Workflow and Student Verification. Blackboard SIS integration is a separate pathway. I found no public evidence that Anthology Student is certified for OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF, nor a public Clever/ClassLink marketplace certification. SSO is supported through the documented AAD path; payment and accounting exports are institution/configuration dependent. [10] [21]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The strongest public evidence is Anthology’s product AI documentation, which states ISO 27001/27017/27018 certification for Anthology Student and Azure OpenAI controls that do not use client prompts for model retraining. Current Ellucian cloud documentation reports SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001:2022, PCI DSS, NIST 800-171, CSA and HECVAT-related controls, with AWS monitoring and incident-response tooling. These are vendor/cloud-program claims and do not replace a customer’s contract, DPA or security review. FERPA and GDPR are relevant obligations; the sources reviewed did not verify COPPA or India DPDP Act certification, a named Student data-hosting region, or a publicly reported Student-specific breach. The 2025–2026 restructuring and ownership transfer are material governance events, but the Ellucian FAQ says existing hosting, security protocols, compliance requirements, integrations and contracts continued without immediate change. [12] [17] [21]

### Strengths

* Deep higher-education SIS coverage, including admissions, academic records, financial aid, student accounts, housing and regulatory reporting.
* Handles complex U.S. aid and non-term/clock-hour program models that many general school platforms do not.
* Strong data model, configurable Views, OData, REST/SOAP APIs, Forms Builder, Workflow Composer and granular permissions.
* Cloud modernization is meaningful: Help AI, scheduling AI, responsive self-service and current release cadence are documented.
* Reviews recognize breadth, centralization, student records and routine usability; SoftwareReviews recorded 95% positive emotional sentiment across 17 reviews. [8]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* UX is uneven across the installed base: G2 users cite occasional slowness, dated appearance, complexity, downtime and limited mobile functionality; the current G2 average is only 3.4/5. [6]
* Capterra users report slow or frustrating support, duplicated inquiries, unintuitive schedule lookup and difficult history filtering; ease of use is 4.1/5 and customer service 3.7/5. [7]
* SoftwareReviews users praise reliability and the portal but cite limited customization, unintuitive multi-step workflows and the need for training. [8]
* Pricing is opaque and implementation/managed-services costs can be significant; there is no public rate card or standard package. [7]
* The 2026 split among Ellucian, Encoura and Blackboard creates roadmap and contract-governance uncertainty, even though continuity was promised for existing SIS/ERP customers. [1] [2] [5]
* Core Student is not a full school-management suite: transport, library, medical, discipline, special education, alumni/fundraising and native LMS/homework functions require other products or integrations.

### Key Milestones

* **1988:** Campus Management’s predecessor, Integrated Solutions, was founded with Class Software. [4]
* **1995–2018:** Campus Management expanded through acquisitions including Spectrum Software, Donor2 Fundraising, Talisma and TopSchool. [4]
* **2020:** Campus Management, Campus Labs and iModules combined to form Anthology; CampusNexus Student became part of the unified portfolio. [3] [4]
* **2021:** Anthology announced its Blackboard merger on September 13 and completed the merger on October 25. [3] [5]
* **2025:** Anthology Student 25.2 added Help AI, data-view enhancements, aid and student-account changes; Anthology later filed Chapter 11 during its financial restructuring. [18]
* **February 2, 2026:** Encoura closed its acquisition of Anthology’s Lifecycle Engagement and Student Success portfolio, including Reach, Encompass, Advance and related products. [2]
* **March 2, 2026:** Blackboard announced emergence from Chapter 11 and confirmed the sale of Enterprise Operations, including Anthology Student and Finance & HCM, to Ellucian. [1]
* **2026:** Ellucian’s welcome page stated that 260+ Anthology SIS/ERP customers joined Ellucian, with existing contracts, integrations, hosting and security controls continuing immediately after close. [5]

## #20. SIMS (Education Software Solutions (ESS))

| Field | Detail |
