[15] [16] [17] [18] [19] [20] |

### Overview

SIMS is the long-running UK school management information system (MIS) used to hold pupil, staff, attendance, assessment, behaviour, timetable, examination, safeguarding and statutory-return data. Its importance is less about being a general global SIS than about its deep fit with English, Welsh and Northern Irish school administration, including DfE census workflows and a large network of approved support units and technical integrators. [1] [6]

The current product is a two-track transition. SIMS 7 remains the established desktop/local product, while SIMS Next Gen is a ground-up cloud rebuild delivered through phased modules. ESS was carved out of Capita: Capita announced the sale in December 2020, Montagu completed the acquisition in 2021, and the CMA approved the merger with ParentPay in July 2021. [10] [11] ParentPay Group is the current owner and combines SIMS with ParentPay payments, Schoolcomms engagement, finance, catering, library and data-protection products.

### Platform Classification Explained

* **SIMS 7 desktop/on-premise:** The partner documentation describes local SIMS 7 installations, local backup services, .NET/WinForms-style integrations and applications sitting on a school server or proxy. The model can be locally hosted and is not a pure SaaS service. [5] [6]
* **SIMS Next Gen web/cloud:** ESS describes Next Gen as cloud-native and the independent 2025 rollout account describes 100% cloud access, automatic updates and use on any device. It is being rolled out module by module, so schools may run it alongside classic SIMS during transition. [1] [23]
* **Finance:** FMS is offered as cloud-based finance software with backups, upgrades, anytime access, automatic reconciliation, statutory reporting and local-authority data exchange; the partner portal also documents legacy FMS 6 local backup. [4] [6]
* **Native mobile apps:** SIMS Parent (iOS and Android) exposes homework, calendars, timetables, activities, assessment, attendance/truancy, behaviour, reports, messaging and safeguarding information; it requires a school invitation. SIMS Student is an iOS app for invited students. SIMS Teacher is an iPad app for registers, timetables, pupil details, conduct and assessment, with encrypted data. [17] [18] [19] [20]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment
SIMS 7 supports admissions import and update, including ATF/AIF workflows, applicants and pre-admission records. It is designed for school admissions and transfer rather than university-style applicant relationship management. [6]

#### Student information and records
The core database stores pupil and staff records, linked adults and contact priority, identifiers, groups, photographs, documents/attachments, medical information, attendance, behaviour, achievement, assessment and timetable data. SIMS Parent can expose selected records and let parents update information held by the school. [6] [17]

#### Attendance
SIMS provides class and lesson registers, attendance marks and codes, late minutes, historical register views, unexplained-absence workflows, attendance analysis and KPI/trend monitoring. Attendance is one of the live Next Gen modules and connects to statutory returns and parent messaging. [1] [6] [23]

#### Timetable and master scheduling
SIMS 7 Timetabling supports period-based timetables; the modern package includes timetabling, options and cover. Teacher access includes current timetables, while Next Gen roadmaps add flexible seating plans and real-time fire registers. [3] [6] [20]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations
Assessment Manager provides configurable marksheets, templates, assessment data collection, progress/performance analysis and intervention tracking. Examinations functionality covers entries, candidate information, exam timetables and results-related workflows. Assessment, exams and interventions are included in the current Optimise package. [1] [6] [15]

#### Report cards and transcripts
SIMS supports report creation using report templates/Word data tags, profile reports, exports and detailed report writing. Capterra users specifically value reports and assessment data, but describe report-building as training-intensive and sometimes error-prone. A dedicated higher-education transcript module is not publicly evidenced. [16]

#### Learning management and homework
SIMS is not documented as a full LMS with course authoring, content delivery or built-in lessons. Homework is visible in SIMS Parent/Student, and the current Engage package labels homework a priority roadmap feature rather than a mature core module. [1] [17]

#### Communication
The connected ecosystem supports SMS/email messaging, in-app notifications, attendance and unexplained-absence messaging, smart forms, consent collection, calendar updates and message history through Schoolcomms. WhatsApp integration is not publicly evidenced; native messaging is not presented as a WhatsApp channel. [1] [7]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals
SIMS Parent provides a multi-child, cross-school parent view; SIMS Student provides an invited student view; SIMS Teacher provides iPad classroom access. Browser access also exists for parent services, while SIMS ID and school-managed invitations provide identity and access control. [5] [17] [18] [20]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting
FMS covers suppliers and supplier payments, income and debtors, budgets, chart of accounts, period/year end, audit and statutory reporting. ParentPay/Schoolcomms add dinner money, meals, clubs, trips, wraparound care, shops, donations, single-basket checkout, top-up and payment reporting. Full tuition-fee billing is not described as a SIMS core feature. [1] [4] [7]

#### HR, staff and payroll
SIMS stores staff data and has Staff, HR and HR Assistant integration documentation; the current package includes staffing and personnel links. Payroll processing itself is not publicly documented as a native SIMS payroll engine. [1] [6]

#### Transport
No native transport-routing, fleet, bus-pass or vehicle-management module was identified in the official SIMS feature pages or partner documentation reviewed.

#### Library
Library/resource management is part of the wider ParentPay Group portfolio, including Reading Cloud, but it is not presented as a native SIMS MIS module. SIMS can participate in the wider group ecosystem and exchange selected data. [2] [22]

#### Hostel and boarding
No native boarding-house, room-allocation or residential-life module was publicly evidenced.

#### Inventory and assets
FMS includes equipment/asset management and loans, plus transactional reporting and audit trails. This is finance-linked asset control rather than a full facilities or warehouse-management suite. [1] [4]

#### Health and medical
Student medical information and conditions can be held in the MIS and shared selectively through connected engagement/reporting services. The public material does not describe clinical records, care-plan authoring or a medical scheduling module. [6] [22]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care
SIMS 7 supports behaviour and achievement records; Next Gen Conduct Management records incidents, automates workflows and provides dashboards/insights. The roadmap also names pastoral care for secondary schools. [1] [3] [6] [8]

#### Special education and safeguarding
SEND management is included in the Optimise package. The data model supports flags and pupil information used for safeguarding, while SIMS Parent highlights safeguarding-related updates and emergency information. A full statutory child-protection case-management product is not publicly specified. [1] [17]

#### Alumni and fundraising
No native alumni relations or fundraising module was found. ParentPay provides shops, donations pages and payments, but those are not an alumni CRM or donor-management system. [1]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting
Reporting and Insights combines attendance, behaviour, SEND and other data in filterable charts, drill-down pupil/staff views and benchmarking against national averages. MAT Group Hub is described as providing central access, trust-wide dashboards and configurable Power BI dashboards. [3] [8]

#### AI features
No production AI assistant, generative reporting assistant or documented predictive model was identified. ESS promotes an AI-themed education webinar, but EdTech Impact records that the SIMS team had not stated whether the product uses AI; score this conservatively as not publicly evidenced. [2] [24]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance
SIMS includes census and statutory returns, with school census guidance and support. FMS adds DfE validation and automatic submission for Consistent Financial Reporting and Accounts Returns. This UK compliance depth is a major differentiator. [1] [4]

#### Mobile apps
SIMS Parent, SIMS Student and SIMS Teacher are the named native apps. Parent supports homework, calendar, timetable, activities, assessment, attendance, behaviour, reports and messaging; Teacher supports registers, timetables, pupil details, conduct and assessment. Parent has 500K+ Android downloads but poor store ratings; the iOS app is free and has 1.8k ratings. [17] [18] [19] [20]

#### Integrations and APIs
SIMS 7 exposes partner APIs, reporting/command export, attendance, assessment, timetable, student, behaviour, admissions, staff/HR and dinner-money interfaces. Next Gen APIs are web-based and OData-compliant; the ecosystem documents OneRoster, SIMS ID single sign-on and a technical-integrator programme. ParentPay, Schoolcomms, FMS, e-procurement and budgeting are first-party connections. [5] [6] [7]

#### Security and privacy
ParentPay Group reports ISO 27001, ISO 9001, Cyber Essentials Plus and PCI-DSS Level 1 certifications for relevant group services. It describes UK/EEA data centres, UK GDPR/EU GDPR Article 28 processing, TLS 1.2, encryption at rest and in backups, RBAC/least privilege, MFA for employees, penetration testing, monitoring, incident response and disaster recovery. [21] [22]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **Deep UK statutory fit:** Census and DfE financial-return workflows are embedded rather than bolted on.
* **Two-speed migration:** Schools can keep SIMS 7 while adopting cloud Next Gen modules with shared data exchange.
* **Large partner ecosystem:** OneRoster, OData web APIs, SIMS ID SSO, local APIs and technical-integrator accreditation support third-party products.
* **Trust-level oversight:** Group Hub and Power BI dashboards are aimed at MAT-wide attendance, demographics, performance and policy control.
* **Integrated school operations:** SIMS, FMS, ParentPay and Schoolcomms connect records, engagement, money and reporting.
* **Long operational history:** ESS cites 40+ years of SIMS experience and a £50 million rebuild investment. [1] [3]

### Pricing Details

ESS publishes no public price list, per-pupil tariff, tier price or implementation-fee schedule. Current pages offer a demo or quote and describe packages such as Optimise, Engage, Pay, Finance and Secure without public amounts; support is sold in Foundation, Advanced and Complete levels, also without public prices. [1] [2] [6]

As a third-party estimate only, EdTech Impact’s page, last updated 23 November 2026, reports a paid subscription starting at £350 and example bands of £350 plus £2 per pupil and £400 plus £3 per pupil. The page does not clearly state the billing term or reconcile those bands with ESS’s current package structure, so it should not be used as an official quote. [24]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Public documentation confirms OneRoster, OData-compliant Next Gen web APIs, SIMS ID SSO, local SIMS 7 APIs, reporting/command export, and a technical-integrator programme with partner accreditation and support. ParentPay, Schoolcomms, FMS, e-procurement, budgeting and dinner-money connections are documented. The reviewed public sources do not claim 1EdTech certification for LTI or SIF, Ed-Fi certification, or named Clever/ClassLink connectors. Google Workspace/Microsoft 365 security reviews are offered through the group, but a deep native productivity-suite integration is not publicly detailed. [5] [6] [7]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

ParentPay Group reports ISO 27001 certification, ISO 9001, Cyber Essentials Plus and PCI-DSS Level 1 for relevant services; it states that customer data is held in UK or EEA data centres, uses UK/EU GDPR processor agreements, and maintains encryption, least-privilege access, MFA for employees, penetration testing, monitoring, backups and incident-response controls. [21] [22] The evidence reviewed does not establish SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA or India DPDP Act compliance for SIMS, and no product-specific hosting-region schedule beyond UK/EEA was found. No confirmed ESS/SIMS data breach was identified in the reviewed sources. The CMA investigated contract and switching conduct: its 2024 press release stated that no conclusion should be drawn that the law had been broken, while the earlier 2022 case closed in January 2023 after binding commitments concerning three-year contracts and break clauses. [12] [13]

### Strengths

* Exceptionally broad UK school administration coverage, especially attendance, assessment, behaviour, timetabling, examinations, census and reporting.
* Mature data model and partner documentation, with OneRoster, OData, local APIs and a substantial integrator ecosystem.
* Strong statutory and finance fit through census returns, FMS, DfE validation and ParentPay-linked payments.
* Current cloud rebuild offers a path away from local servers while preserving SIMS 7 data and workflows.
* Current official claims indicate substantial scale: 10,000+ schools, 700,000+ users and 40+ countries. [1]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* The product is in a long phased transition: independent coverage said in 2025 that attendance, behaviour, census and assessment were live for early adopters while reporting, communications and finance were still on the roadmap, and WhichMIS reported that the final cloud modules were expected only by end-2026. [14] [23]
* Capterra reviewers praise registers, data depth and reporting but report a clunky or dated interface, difficult report/marksheet configuration, unreliable reports/glitches, slow performance and very poor support experiences. [16]
* G2 reviewers value timetabling, cover, attendance, fees and parent apps but mention frequent updates and limited troubleshooting resources. [15]
* SIMS Parent is rated only 1.3/5 from 1.8k UK App Store ratings; reviews describe login loops, random logouts, stalled messages, missing content and dinner-money access problems. [18]
* The iOS SIMS Student listing is 2.3/5 from three ratings, including a complaint that it is glitchy; SIMS Teacher has too few ratings to display a score. [19] [20]
* Contract and switching concerns have attracted CMA scrutiny, including complaints that database transfer could be complex or error-prone; the CMA’s notices record commitments but no finding of infringement. [12] [13]

### Key Milestones

* **1984:** Independent MIS-sector coverage dates SIMS’s origin to 1984; ESS’s current site describes more than 40 years of experience. [3] [14]
* **11 May 2020:** Education Software Solutions Ltd incorporated; the legal entity was formerly Capita ESS Ltd. [9]
* **December 2020:** Capita announced agreement to sell ESS to Tiger UK Bidco/Montagu for up to £400 million, with £298 million payable at completion. [10]
* **Early 2021:** Montagu acquired ESS in a carve-out from Capita. [11]
* **July 2021:** CMA approved the merger of ESS and ParentPay; ESS joined ParentPay Group, with databases then used in more than 19,000 schools according to Montagu’s announcement. [11]
* **April 2022–January 2023:** CMA investigated the move from one-year to three-year contracts and accepted binding commitments, including an adjudicated 12-month break clause for eligible schools; the case closed 10 January 2023. [13]
* **May 2024:** CMA opened a separate investigation into alleged switching/data-transfer conduct and described ESS as holding approximately 50% of England’s market; the press release expressly stated there was no finding of infringement. [12]
* **June 2025:** Independent School Business Services described Next Gen as rolling out gradually, with core attendance, behaviour, census and assessment live for early adopters and other modules still developing. [23]
* **July 2025:** WhichMIS reported 8,140 UK schools and 30.1% UK market share from summer 2025 census analysis, down from SIMS’s historic peak. [14]
* **November 2026:** ESS/ParentPay’s current official pages claim 10,000+ SIMS schools, 700,000+ users, 40+ countries and a £50 million Next Gen rebuild investment; pricing remains quote-based. [1] [3]

## India #1. MasterSoft ERP (MasterSoft ERP Solutions Pvt. Ltd.)

### Overview

MasterSoft ERP is an Indian education ERP/SIS suite from MasterSoft ERP Solutions. It combines admissions, academics, examinations, fees, scholarships, student services, alumni, LMS, OBE, HR/payroll, finance, procurement, hostel, library and administration for schools, colleges and universities. The older catalog names RF-CAMPUS, CCMS, CSMS and online admissions as its principal product lines [1] [4] [5].

Founder Sham Somani previously led Nagpur University’s computer center and built examination, accounts, payroll and administration software there. Gartner identifies the private company as founded in 1995, but no source gives a separate ERP first-launch year. No public acquisition or funding announcement was found [1] [11].

### Platform Classification Explained

- **Cloud/web SaaS:** Official pages describe centralized cloud delivery, anywhere access, automatic backups and no customer hardware; Business-Software independently classifies it as SaaS [4] [5].
- **Hosting:** The FAQ cites Government of India Meghraj-policy cloud hosting. The October 2026 policy names Microsoft Azure, with institution-selected regions and regional backup/disaster recovery [6] [14].
- **Browser access:** The registered-user student portal is a live web application owned by MasterSoft ERP Solutions [15].
- **Desktop/on-premise:** No current public evidence of a downloadable desktop client or customer-managed on-premise option. Gartner’s “hybrid experience” describes product access, not a documented deployment choice [4] [11].
- **Mobile:** Student Diary Cloud is linked to Google Play; the Faculty Management App page claims Google Play and iOS availability. Android/iOS store-level ratings for the official apps were not exposed [12] [13].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

No-code/low-code forms with validation, conditional fields and uploads; programs, intakes, quotas and eligibility; entrance exams, interviews, LORs, approvals, offers, waitlists, SMS/email/WhatsApp reminders, funnel dashboards and direct handoff to enrollment, fees and academics [17].

#### Student information and records

Central profiles for demographic, academic, fee, scholarship, hostel, library and lifecycle data; role-based access, documents, exports, dashboards and reports for administrators, faculty, students and parents. Health records are mentioned, but not a detailed clinical module [6] [18].

#### Attendance

RFID, biometric, QR, OTP, mobile and geolocation attendance; course/session mapping, absentee alerts, parent visibility, hostel attendance and reports. HR attendance links to leave and payroll [6] [19].

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Conflict-managed class and exam timetables; faculty, room, course and session mapping; weekly schedules; curriculum execution; absence replacement; multi-campus scheduling; majors, minors, electives, prerequisites, credit-load checks and CBCS/NEP-aligned selection [12] [19].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Offline/online exams; registration, permits, question banks, MCQ/descriptive/quiz/formative patterns, encryption, timers, randomization, webcam/proctoring, halls, evaluator workflows, bulk marks, absolute/relative/hybrid grades, SGPA/CGPA, grace/carry/backlog/classification, scrutiny, re-evaluation and grade-improvement petitions [20] [21].

#### Report cards and transcripts

Automated report cards, grade cards, merit lists, gazettes, transcripts, certificates and hall tickets; Word/Excel/PDF export; QR-verified digitally signed credentials; SMS/email delivery of results [20] [21].

#### Learning management and homework

Course/topic organization; PDF, presentation, audio and video content; syllabus, teaching plans, assignments, submissions, grading, rubrics, quizzes, polls, surveys, forums, internal chat, webinars/live classes and recordings; gradebook and learning-gap analytics. Microsoft Teams is mentioned for online lectures [5] [22].

#### Communication

SMS/email alerts for attendance, homework, events, exams, dues and results; push notifications; text, picture, PDF and voice messages; teacher-parent/student communication; meeting alerts. Admissions explicitly claims WhatsApp automation; named UPI/Razorpay/Paytm connectors were not verified [12] [17].

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Role-based portals provide schedules, attendance, assignments, exams, fees, scholarships, documents, requests and progress. Parent tools cover attendance, fees, homework, events and performance; faculty tools cover attendance, schedules, notifications, leave and payroll [6] [12] [18].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Course/campus fee structures; tuition, annual, exam, hostel, library, sports and miscellaneous fees; installments/EMIs, concessions, scholarships, sponsors, refunds, write-offs, dues, collection centers, invoices, receipts, reconciliation and collection reports. Cash, payment centers, gateways and wallets are described, but not named UPI/Razorpay/Paytm. Taxation appears in finance copy, without a specific GST-invoicing claim [5] [17] [23].

#### HR, staff and payroll

Employee records, onboarding-to-retirement, service books, biometric attendance, leave/OD/comp-off, salary revisions, arrears, supplementary bills, payslips, tax, Form 16, 24Q, PF, PT, statutory registers, self-service and payroll reports [1].

#### Transport

Vehicle, registration, insurance, permits, tax, logbook, routes, passengers, fuel, maintenance, trips, rented vehicles, bookings and alerts; school bus live tracking and parent notifications [6] [24].

#### Library

Procurement, accessioning, cataloging, classification, disposal, barcode/RFID circulation, reservations, renewals, kiosks/mobile self-check, OPAC/M-OPAC, fines, due reminders, visitor records, SMS/email, audit logs, AACR2/MARC21 and multi-campus reporting [25].

#### Hostel and boarding

Online admissions, dormitory/room/wing/floor definitions, allocation, occupancy, fees, defaulter reminders, tracking, attendance, leave/outdoor passes, parent updates, gate passes, visitor management, mess bills, canteen, refunds, certificates and end-semester settlement [26].

#### Inventory and assets

Procurement, suppliers, contracts, purchase book, internal invoices, taxation, stores, inventory, asset register, capitalization, disposal, depreciation, maintenance and accounting integration [23].

#### Health and medical

Health records and a university Health Center/Healthcare Management module are listed, but public pages do not describe appointments, prescriptions or clinical workflows [12] [18].

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Student Services records offenses, disciplinary actions, appeals, academic holds and escalation; the portal supports grievances. Detailed K-12 pastoral-care controls are not documented [27].

#### Special education and safeguarding

No dedicated IEP, special-education or child-safeguarding module was publicly documented. The free offer for specially-abled schools is an eligibility criterion, not feature evidence [28].

#### Alumni and fundraising

Alumni onboarding, profiles, directory, news/events, jobs, internships, mentoring, referrals, chapters, donations, pledges, campaigns, receipts, donor dashboards, elections, e-voting and audit trails [29].

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

BI dashboards and exports for enrollment, attendance, academics, fees, payroll, finance, library, accreditation and engagement; audit logs, gap analysis, rubrics, scoring, dropout prediction and at-risk-student identification are claimed [1] [8] [11].

#### AI features

MS AI Copilot, AI Agents, universal search, adaptive advising, dropout/at-risk analytics, AI fee configuration, scholarship/document checks, payroll validation and query management are vendor claims; model providers and tier availability are not public [1] [6] [17] [30].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Accreditation Data Management supports NAAC/NBA data, NIRF reports, multi-year evidence, proof uploads, Excel/PDF/link outputs, dashboards, rubrics and audit trails. School ERP supports CBSE, ICSE, State Board, IB and Cambridge and produces grade lists/mark sheets. AISHE workflows, UDISE+, APAAR ID and a NEP 2020 holistic progress-card template were not publicly verified [6] [8].

#### Mobile apps

Student Diary Cloud and Faculty Management App provide student/parent/faculty access to timetable, attendance, assignments, exams, fees, scholarships, library, grievances, notifications, leave, payslips, LMS and bus tracking. Android is directly linked; iOS is claimed for the faculty app [12] [13].

#### Integrations and APIs

Internal links cover SIS, admissions, finance, HR/payroll, LMS, examinations, OBE, accreditation, library, hostel and mobile; named technologies include payment gateways, net banking, RFID, biometrics, QR/OTP and Microsoft Teams. APIs are mentioned in policy materials, but no public API reference, marketplace, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink or Tally documentation was found [5] [14].

#### Security and privacy

Role-based access, OTP/password controls, HTTPS/TLS, encryption-at-rest capabilities, MFA where applicable, Azure privileged access, WAF/firewalls, backups, restore testing, audit logs, masking/pseudonymization and time-limited support access are documented. Institutions can export their data [14] [17].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Accreditation Data Management:** dated evidence, proof attachments and NAAC/NBA/NIRF-ready reports are tailored to Indian higher education [8].
- **OBE/CBCS/NEP engine:** CO/PO/PSO/PEO mapping, Bloom’s Taxonomy, attainment and credit validation connect compliance with daily academics [18] [29].
- **Exam integrity:** configurable grading, proctoring signals, audit trails and QR-verified credentials support examination offices [19].
- **Agentic AI:** Copilot, workflow agents, universal search and adaptive advising go beyond conventional MIS reporting, but independent production evidence is limited [1].
- **Multi-campus and Indian operations:** affiliated-college data sharing, Meghraj-policy language, statutory payroll and RFID/biometric attendance are locally distinctive [5] [8] [18].

### Pricing Details

There is no public pricing page, plan table or implementation fee. The official FAQ gives a general Indian school-ERP range of ₹0–₹250 per student per year, not a MasterSoft quote; no USD price is listed [6]. Business-Software and TechJockey say contact vendor/price on request, with quotes varying by personalization, features, users and deployment [4] [9]. The M-Initiative offers free school software only to qualifying government girls’ schools, specially-abled schools, non-profit NGO schools and Sainik schools below 500 students [27]. Prices checked 24 November 2026; no reliable MasterSoft-specific third-party estimate was found.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Public evidence is strongest for internal ERP links: admissions to enrollment/fees/academics; curriculum to registration, exams, LMS, attendance, fees and degree audit; accreditation to SIS/ERP; finance to fees, hostel, library and HR/payroll; and library to student/finance records [8] [18] [22] [24]. Payment gateways, net banking, RFID, biometrics, QR/OTP and Microsoft Teams are named. No public API reference, marketplace, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Google Workspace, Tally, UPI, Razorpay or Paytm certification was found.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The October 2026 policy treats the institution as controller and MasterSoft as processor, prohibits advertising/sale/data brokerage/general-purpose-AI training on institutional data, and describes Azure-region hosting, backups, TLS, encryption, MFA where applicable and incident response. The DPA adds just-in-time production access, approval records, 12-month support-access logs, masking/pseudonymization and regional controls [14] [15]. The material supports GDPR-oriented readiness and references ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls, but does not prove ISO certification or SOC 2. FERPA/COPPA are not claimed; DPDP Act 2023 is not explicitly named. No public breach disclosure was found.

### Strengths

- Broad school and university coverage, with unusually deep Indian examination, accreditation, OBE, CBCS, affiliation and multi-campus functionality.
- Cloud delivery, mobile access, configurable workflows, role-based access and implementation/support options.
- Named institutional customers and substantial vendor-reported adoption, with positive Gartner and TechJockey ratings [7] [9] [11].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Quote-only pricing and unclear plan boundaries make comparison difficult [4] [9].
- G2’s 3.4/5 sample reports repeated refreshes, app freezing, attendance glitches, weaker mobile compatibility, peak-time performance concerns and a need for a more advanced mobile app; it also says the LMS/CRM trail Blackboard/Canvas and Salesforce/HubSpot [10].
- Gartner’s public summary includes “cross integration challenges” and inability to cross-integrate modules despite praise for customization and analytics [11].
- Public documentation is marketing-led: no API reference, standards certifications, named payment connectors, public SLA or audited adoption dataset was found.
- Adoption claims conflict: 1,100+ institutions/1.5M active students versus 2,200+ implementations/10M+ users, so definitions should be requested [1] [7].

### Key Milestones

- **1990–2000:** Founder Sham Somani led Nagpur University’s computer center and built examination, accounts, payroll and administration software [1].
- **1995:** MasterSoft is identified as founded by Gartner, TechJockey and Business-Software.com [2] [3] [4].
- **2019:** A cloud-versus-on-premise article documents the cloud positioning, not a launch date [30].
- **2023:** Gartner described a mobile-first SIS covering admission through alumni [11].
- **2024:** G2 recorded both positive customization feedback and mobile/refresh/performance complaints [10].
- **2025:** Gartner displayed a review about dropout prediction/student management [11].
- **2026:** The public site foregrounds agentic AI, OBE and financial-aid automation; Privacy Policy v2.0 and DPA 2026.10 became effective 6 October 2026 [1] [14] [15].
- **Acquisitions/funding:** No public acquisition or funding milestone was found.

## India #2. Camu (Octoze Technologies)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Octoze Technologies Private Limited (Camu is the flagship product). |
| Headquarters | Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India is the operating/developer base reported by Gartner and the app listing; Camu announced a Singapore headquarters move in December 2020, while the current Octoze site lists an Austin, Texas legal address. [1] [2] |
| Company founded (year) | 2013. [3] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | 2014, when Camu went live with its first customer. [4] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud SaaS, web-based, multi-tenant; native iOS and Android mobile apps. No public evidence of a desktop client or customer-managed on-premise edition. [5] |
| Primary segments | Higher education (colleges, universities and multi-campus systems), K–12 schools, vocational/skills institutions, online and distance learning, and government education bodies. |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | Octoze’s current product pages claim 700+ institutions across 10+ countries and separately describe the SIS as behind 2.3 million students; the company’s story page gives 700+ institutions/10 countries, while the 2020 Entrepreneur report recorded 400+ institutions/1 million students/six countries. Claims accessed 24 November 2026 and should not be treated as independently audited. [1] [2] [4] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://camudigitalcampus.com/ |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://camudigitalcampus.com/college-management-erp-software/ |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | https://camudigitalcampus.com/school-management-system-knowledge-center/ and support form at https://camudigitalcampus.com/camu-support/ |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | No public pricing page found; sales/demo contact is required. |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | Capterra 4.5/5 (6 reviews; listing last updated 2 June 2024); GetApp 4.5/5 (6; page accessed 24 November 2026); Software Advice 4.5/5 (6; accessed 24 November 2026); Google Play MyCamu Lite 4.1/5 (259 reviews; accessed 24 November 2026; updated 1 September 2026); Apple MyCamu and Camu Staff App: not enough ratings/reviews to display an overview. [6] [7] [8] [9] [10] |

### Overview

Camu is Octoze’s cloud digital-campus platform: a unified student information system (SIS), learning management system (LMS), examination/Controller of Examinations (CoE), finance and fee collection, admissions, attendance, accreditation, and student-engagement environment. It is positioned most strongly for higher education and multi-campus universities, but the vendor also markets school ERP, K–12 LMS and government offerings. [1] [3]

The company started in 2013 after the founders’ healthcare software work; Camu’s first customer went live in 2014. The product added mobile in 2015, OBE and CBCS in 2016, virtual classroom in 2020, LMS 2.0 in 2022 and AI capabilities in 2025. Camu’s 2020 move of headquarters from Chennai to Singapore reflected ASEAN expansion, while development, support and business-development operations remained in Chennai. No acquisition is publicly disclosed in the reviewed company history. [2] [4]

### Platform Classification Explained

Camu is a hosted, multi-tenant SaaS product with microservices, auto-scaling, encrypted multi-region backups and a vendor-claimed 99.99% uptime. Octoze says it is hosted on Amazon Web Services and supports web access from a computer or mobile device. Its integration page describes secured, documented REST APIs, webhooks and an LTI-compliant LMS. [5] [12]

Native mobile delivery is evidenced by the iOS “MyCamu - Student Parent App,” iOS “Camu - Staff App,” Android “MyCamu Lite,” and the company’s generic Camu Mobile/ MyCamu descriptions. MyCamu covers assignments, exams, report cards, attendance, holidays/events and billing; the staff app exposes schedules, events, holidays, payment approvals and management analysis. [9] [10] [13]

No desktop application, customer-installed on-premise package or offline server edition was found in the official material. eLearning Industry labels the offering SaaS/cloud, mobile and desktop application, but its “desktop” entry is best interpreted as browser access rather than a separately installed client. [14]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

Online enquiry and application portals support configurable forms for multiple programs and intakes, UG/PG/diploma/lateral-entry workflows, document upload with validation/version control, eligibility rules, merit lists, quota/category/reservation handling, interviews, counselling, panel allocation, offer letters, waitlists, automated email/SMS/in-app status updates, fee collection, partial payments, refunds, scholarships, seat confirmation and SIS/LMS onboarding. [15]

#### Student information and records

Camu maintains centralized academic, personal, enrolment, document, account and staff records. Concrete tools include self-profile updates with approval, mandatory-document checklists, mail-merge document generation, e-portfolios/CV templates, student services with SLA and multi-level approvals, hold-and-clearance controls, scholarship applications and payment scheduling, advising/counselling notes, graduation lists and no-dues validation. [16]

#### Attendance

Attendance can be captured by session, course or day through QR code, biometric fingerprint, face recognition, mobile marking, check-in/check-out and geofencing. The system timestamps entries, supports late marking and retakes, sends absence notifications to parents, and provides dashboards, compliance reports and the “Heads Up” attendance summary. Faculty attendance is also supported through HR integration. [17]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

The platform provides course/class scheduling, timetable and academic-calendar views, workload and faculty allocation, conflict-aware course registration, schedule changes and timetable dashboards. Students can see lecture timetables and examination schedules in MyCamu; the review evidence also identifies class scheduling and online calendar features. [6] [9]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

LMS assessments include quizzes, reusable question banks, timed/randomized tests, auto-grading, rubrics, outcome mapping and continuous assessment. The CoE adds exam applications, automated multi-course scheduling, hall tickets, seat allocation, nominal rolls, MCQ/descriptive questions, remote and AI-assisted proctoring, anti-cheating activity tracking, mobile answer-sheet upload, dual/online mark entry, moderation, normalization, relative and multiple grading models, result compilation, publication, analytics, review and revaluation. [18] [19]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Camu publishes results and report cards through the student/parent portal, generates transcripts and consolidated mark statements, supports graduation/no-dues processing, and exposes report and document delivery through mobile. For K–12, the vendor says its CoE can generate holistic, all-round report cards, but a detailed CBSE/ICSE template catalogue was not publicly documented. [9] [20]

#### Learning management and homework

The unified LMS organizes lectures, documents, multimedia, SCORM packages, lesson plans, structured learning paths, assignments, submissions, deadlines, feedback, discussion/chatrooms, virtual classes with video/chat/recording, attendance, progress and performance analytics. It supports synchronous, asynchronous, blended and distance learning. [20] [14]

#### Communication (SMS, email, push, WhatsApp)

Camu documents automated email, SMS and in-app notifications for applicants, parents, staff and students, along with announcements, circulars, reminders, chatrooms, course messaging and push notifications. Email gateways include SendGrid, Microsoft Outlook SMTP and Google SMTP. Pay attention to scope: WhatsApp is not named in the reviewed official integration list, so WhatsApp support is not verified. [12] [15]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

MyCamu gives students and parents attendance, timetable, assignments, exams, report cards, fees/billing, holidays, events, announcements and teacher chat. Faculty can mark attendance, create plans and assignments, evaluate papers, compute marks and give feedback. Management dashboards cover academic, staff and financial monitoring. [13]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Fee functionality includes configurable structures and components, course/credit/flat fees, installments, concessions, scholarships, multiple payers, daily collection, fee registers, automated receipts, due reminders, outstanding/pending reports, reconciliation, billing history and financial dashboards. Official integration evidence names Paytm and Razorpay, plus regional gateways; MyCamu supports cards and net banking. The privacy policy says cardholder data is handled by PCI-DSS-compliant third-party gateways, not stored by Camu. Tally, GST e-invoicing and UPI were not specifically verified, although Paytm/Razorpay may expose local payment methods depending on gateway configuration. [21] [12] [22]

#### HR, staff and payroll

The HR module, delivered through partner systems, covers employee information, recruitment/onboarding, employee self-service, biometric integration, attendance, leave, payroll with tax/statutory compliance, performance management, workload analysis and exit management. Partner delivery means institutions should confirm the exact payroll engine, Indian statutory coverage and implementation boundary. [23]

#### Transport

SIS documentation says Camu covers transportation and the privacy policy describes GPS use for bus location when enabled. A dedicated transport page with route, vehicle, driver, fee and live-tracking subfeatures was not found, so transport is best treated as an available operational capability whose depth requires confirmation. [16] [22]

#### Library

The partner-integrated library capability provides centralized cataloguing, circulation, union catalogues, advanced search, issue/return/renewal, due notices, acquisitions, budgets, vendor tracking, multi-branch/multi-patron support, bulk operations and usage analytics; Koha is named as an integration. [23] [12]

#### Hostel and boarding

Hostel operations include online accommodation registration, room/bed allocation by availability, gender, course or preference, occupancy and maintenance visibility, student room history, biometric/RFID attendance, hostel fee structures, payment tracking, receipts, reminders, visitor logs, gate passes, notices and dashboards. [24]

#### Inventory and assets

Camu’s school knowledge center lists inventory management as a supported school resource, and the college ERP page names inventory among campus operations. Public detail on stock ledgers, purchase orders, asset depreciation or barcode workflows is limited; those subfeatures are not independently verified. [20] [25]

#### Health and medical

Health management is listed as a school knowledge-center resource and Camu’s privacy policy recognizes health/disability information as sensitive data where applicable. A dedicated public medical module specification, such as clinic visits, immunization or medication workflows, was not found. [25] [22]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

The “Hold and Clearance” feature can restrict access or services for anti-disciplinary activity, while student advising records counselling sessions, observed improvements and mentoring reports. [25] [16]

#### Special education and safeguarding

The platform can store disability information where applicable and offers role-based access, approvals, encryption and audit-oriented records. No public evidence was found for a dedicated special-education plan, individualized education plan, child-protection case workflow or statutory safeguarding register. [22]

#### Alumni and fundraising

Alumni management is listed by Capterra/GetApp, and the accreditation module includes an alumni database with activities, contributions and forums. The reviewed sources do not document a standalone donor CRM, campaigns, online giving or fundraising payments. [6] [7] [20]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Camu provides real-time academic, financial, admissions, attendance, examination, accreditation, HR, library, hostel and operational dashboards; drill-down/custom reports; scheduled/exportable reports; performance and retention analytics; audit-ready reporting; and Tableau, Google Data Studio and Power BI embedding. [5] [12] [18]

#### AI features

Camu Intelligence/AI Content Studio is embedded in the LMS. Faculty upload syllabi, PDFs, PPTs and documents to generate chapters, subchapters, quizzes, assignments and outcome-aligned courses, then edit, approve and publish. Other documented capabilities include adaptive assessments, contextual conversational learning, audio-visual/avatar experiences, flashcards, short video snippets and browser code editors/compilers. The vendor says Gemini and ChatGPT can be connected through open APIs and that personal data is not used for model training. [20] [26] [22]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Camu markets NAAC/NBA/ABET accreditation workflows, SSR/AQAR/criterion-wise/annexure reporting, OBE attainment, CBCS, NIRF readiness and multi-year evidence capture. Its India/NEP page documents UGC alignment, Academic Bank of Credits, DigiLocker/NAD templates, single student ID, bi-annual admissions, dual degrees, multilingual support and holistic K–12 progress assessment. Explicit UDISE+, APAAR ID, state-board report-card templates, GST invoicing and AISHE submission workflows were not publicly verified. [27] [28]

#### Mobile apps

The native iOS/Android family comprises MyCamu for students/parents, MyCamu Lite and Camu Staff App. Features include attendance, assignments, assessments, schedules, results/report cards, billing/payment, notifications, faculty marking, payment approvals, staff schedules and management analysis. Android shows 500K+ downloads for MyCamu Lite. [9] [10] [13]

#### Integrations and APIs

Documented interoperability includes REST APIs, webhooks, LTI, SCORM import/export, Microsoft AD, Google Authentication, Keycloak, OAuth 2.0, SendGrid, Outlook SMTP, Google SMTP, Canvas, Koha, Pi360, Jaspersoft, Power BI, Google Data Studio, Tableau, Paytm, Razorpay, AmBank and DragonPay. OneRoster, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Google Workspace as a certified SIS standard, Microsoft 365 as a packaged suite integration, Tally and a public marketplace were not verified. GetApp’s profile says no API, which conflicts with Camu’s current official API claim; buyers should request current API documentation and tenant-specific availability. [12] [7]

#### Security and privacy

Official claims include AWS hosting, encryption, role-based access, multi-region backups, 99.99% uptime, ISO 27001 compliance and GDPR alignment. The April 2026 privacy policy identifies Octoze as processor for institution-owned data, describes PCI-DSS payment processors, data deletion/retention controls, overseas-access safeguards, and regional storage in India, Singapore, Ohio and potentially in-country deployments. DPDP Act readiness is not explicitly named, and no public SOC 2 or FERPA/COPPA certification was found. [5] [22] [11]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Unified SIS + LMS:** academic records, teaching, assessments, attendance and finance share one student lifecycle record. [1]
- **OBE/CBCS and choice-based enrollment:** outcome mapping, attainment and flexible course choice are unusually central to the product. [27]
- **Accreditation automation:** NAAC/NBA evidence capture, criterion mapping and SSR/AQAR generation are positioned as a core product rather than an export workaround. [27]
- **AI Content Studio:** source-material-to-course generation with faculty review, approval and one-click LMS publication. [26]
- **Flexible attendance:** QR, biometric, facial recognition, mobile and geofencing can be combined around institutional policy. [17]
- **NEP/ABC/DigiLocker alignment:** the vendor documents credit transfer, single student ID, dual degrees and bi-annual admissions. [28]

### Pricing Details

Camu has no public official pricing page, tier matrix or published implementation fee. The reviewed official site routes prospects to a demo/sales form. Third-party directories display a nominal **₹25 flat rate per year** as a starting/basic price, but do not state a per-student, per-school or per-campus unit, inclusions, limits or implementation charges; it should not be used as a dependable quote. Capterra and Software Advice both show ₹25/year, while eLearning Industry says “contact us for pricing.” No USD price was listed; figures were checked 24 November 2026. [6] [8] [14]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Camu has the strongest documented interoperability story in LTI/SCORM, webhooks, REST APIs, OAuth 2.0, Microsoft AD, Google Authentication and analytics/payment connectors. Named products include Canvas, Koha, Pi360, Jaspersoft, Tableau, Power BI, Google Data Studio, Paytm, Razorpay, AmBank, DragonPay, SendGrid and SMTP gateways. However, the public evidence does not establish certification for OneRoster, Ed-Fi or SIF; does not show Clever/ClassLink, Tally or an app marketplace; and conflicts with GetApp’s “no API” field. Treat API access as a sales-validation item rather than an assumed entitlement. [12] [7]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Camu claims ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance, encryption, RBAC, AWS hosting, encrypted backups and 99.99% uptime. Its April 2026 privacy policy provides regional hosting claims: India users’ data in India; users in the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, UAE and Hong Kong in Singapore; the Americas/Africa in Ohio; and possible in-country hosting by contract. It describes institution ownership, processor/controller roles, PCI-DSS payment processors, retention/deletion, DPO contact and no use of personal data to train AI. The reviewed materials do not explicitly claim DPDP Act readiness, SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA, or a public incident history. [5] [22]

### Strengths

- Broad native higher-education coverage, especially SIS/LMS/CoE/OBE/CBCS/accreditation.
- Strong India relevance through NEP 2020, ABC/DigiLocker, UGC, NAAC/NBA, multilingual and regional-hosting claims.
- Mature mobile footprint for parents/students and staff, with Android scale and iOS counterparts.
- Detailed exam, fee, attendance and accreditation workflows rather than generic “ERP” labels.
- Customer evidence supports ease of use, reporting, payments and responsive support, with Capterra’s six reviews averaging 4.5/5. [6]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is opaque; the ₹25/year directory figure is not decision-useful, and implementation or module fees are undisclosed. [6] [8]
- Review volume is tiny: six directory reviews and no Apple overview, so ratings are not representative of a large installed base. [6] [7] [10]
- Capterra reviewers mention redirecting to another page to download subject modules, needing guidance from the vendor, slow updates, and a cumbersome staff-leave approval dependency; another reviewer says ease of use can improve and reports are limited/generic. [6]
- Google Play reviews report login/OTP failures, repeated logouts, crashes, stale details and slow loading. These are user reports, not independently reproduced defects, but they are material mobile pain points. [9]

### Key Milestones

- **2013:** Octoze Technologies begins with four employees. [3] [4]
- **2014:** Camu launches; first customer goes live. [4]
- **2015:** Customers added in Malaysia and Thailand; mobile app introduced. [4]
- **2016:** Dubai expansion; user base reaches 100,000+; OBE and CBCS introduced. [4]
- **2017:** User base exceeds 500,000+. [4]
- **2018:** African expansion begins with Ashesi University. [4]
- **2019:** Deshpande Education Trust becomes a customer for skills development. [4]
- **2020:** Virtual Classroom launches; company story says 700+ institutions, 1M+ users across 12 countries; Entrepreneur reports the Singapore headquarters move and 400+ institutions/1M students/six countries. [2] [4]
- **2021:** UAE market entry. [4]
- **2022:** LMS 2.0 launches; Thailand and Hong Kong expansion. [4]
- **2024:** Cambodia and Australia entry; CamuEngage skilling platform launches. [4]
- **2025:** AI capabilities introduced. [3] [4]
- **2026:** Current pages position Camu as a 700+ institution/10+ country SIS-LMS with 2.3M-student claim; AI Content Studio and expanded accreditation/attendance/hostel pages are public. [1] [16]

## India #3. Fedena (Foradian Technologies)

| Field | Detail |

The main Google Play “Fedena Mobile App” page exposed 100K+ downloads but no score in the fetched view. [7] [8] [9] [10] |

### Overview

Fedena is an education ERP/SIS rather than a pure learning-management system. It centralizes admissions, student records, academic scheduling, attendance, assessment, report cards, fees, HR/payroll, transport, hostel, library, inventory, communication and reporting for schools and higher-education organizations. Fedena’s help center explicitly says it is not an LMS, although it has assignment, online-exam, mobile-learning and video-conference functions and can integrate with LMS products such as Moodle. [11] [12]

Its history is unusually important for the Indian market. Foradian began in 2009, built a custom student-information system first called “Foredu,” installed Fedena in a Kasaragod school in August 2009, and released version 1.0 as Apache-licensed open source in April 2010. The commercial Fedena Pro/SaaS model subsequently funded hosted support, plugins, implementation and customization. [3] [5] The product launched a SaaS version in February 2013, a plugin marketplace in 2013, and raised $2 million from Fabindia managing director William Bissell in 2014. [3] Practically announced its acquisition of Fedena/Foradian in 2022; the acquisition report described Fedena as serving 40,000 institutions and 20 million users at that time. [1]

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser/web:** Fedena is explicitly described as entirely web-based, requiring no software installation. It runs across PCs, laptops, tablets and smartphones through a browser, with role-based logins for administrators, teachers, non-teaching staff, students, parents and management. [4] [6]
* **Cloud SaaS:** The current commercial plans include free cloud hosting, encrypted security, automatic updates, onboarding data/configuration and unlimited users. The product is described independently as cloud-based SaaS. [6] [12]
* **Self-hosted/on-premise:** Fedena’s official “101 reasons” page says customers can download and host it on their own server and URL; Docker installation is also documented. This is a deployment option, not a separate desktop client. [5]
* **Desktop client:** No native Windows, macOS or Linux desktop client is publicly documented; desktop access is through the browser.
* **Native mobile:** The current “Fedena Mobile App” is listed for iPhone/iPad and Android, with role-based experiences for administrators, teachers, parents and students. The older/demo Android listing is called “School Management App - Fedena” and describes FedenaConnect. [9] [10] [13]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

The Enquiry & Registration/add-on module captures online admission enquiries, embeds registration forms on an institution website, supports source/course/academic-year filtering, applicant stages (new, qualified, processed and rejected), counsellor assignment, subject-based registration, document verification, applicant communication by SMS/email, printable forms and fee receipts, and course/source/counsellor reports. Admission forms can be customized and accepted students assigned to courses or batches. [6] [14]

#### Student information and records

The SIS stores personal details, admission numbers, guardian/parent details, academic progress, documents, attendance, course and batch membership, user photos, health-related or extracurricular fields where configured, and historical academic-year data. Bulk CSV import/export supports student, parent, employee, examination score, attendance, library and inventory data; custom fields and user document storage support institution-specific records. [4] [5] [15]

#### Attendance

Teachers can mark day-wise or subject-wise attendance, view attendance history and leave records, and trigger parent alerts. Fedena supports biometric/RFID or swipe-card integration, biometric information APIs, leave applications, late/absence tracking and mobile attendance marking. [4] [5] [13]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

The timetable module manages courses, batches, subjects, teachers, class timings, custom weekdays, classroom allocation and teacher/subject allocation. Students, parents and teachers can view current and upcoming classes in dashboards and mobile apps; examination timetables and school calendars are separate scheduling surfaces. [4] [13]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Fedena supports exam groups, exam planners, term and planner exams, marks entry/import, grade calculation, CWA, GPA and CCE evaluation, group exams, grading levels, online objective and subjective exams, question creation/import, question rearrangement and randomization, publishing, student attempts, and exam reports. The online-exam help center documents question banks/workflows, while the history page records GPA/transcripts and online-exam enhancements. [3] [16]

#### Report cards and transcripts

The gradebook can produce exam reports, term reports and planner reports. Custom report-card templates, ICSE exam categories and IA/EA-style reporting are documented. Fedena 4.0 added GPA and transcripts. CCE reports are supported; the vendor says CCE was built after CBSE guidelines, including SA/FA marks. [3] [5] [17]

#### Learning management and homework

Fedena includes assignments/homework, teacher blogs, discussion groups, file attachments, online exams, mobile learning and a “Learn”/online-learning surface. It is not positioned as a full LMS; the help center explicitly distinguishes Fedena ERP from Uzity or other LMS products. Moodle integration is listed independently, and Zoom, Google Meet and BigBlueButton can support online classes. [11] [12] [18]

#### Communication

The system provides internal messaging, announcements/news, broadcast messages, email integration, bulk SMS, reminders, push notifications, blogs, polls, discussions and gallery posts. Messages can target parents, students, employees or groups, and alerts can cover exams, fees, attendance, assignments, events and announcements. WhatsApp integration is not publicly documented on the reviewed official integration/help pages; do not assume WhatsApp Business support. [5] [6] [13]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Separate logins and privilege controls provide dashboards for parents, students, teachers, administrators and employees. Parents can view attendance, homework, results, fees, receipts, calendars and announcements; teachers can manage attendance, assignments, gradebook, timetable, leave and student performance; students can access schedules, exams, results, assignments and notifications. Parent accounts can manage multiple children. [5] [13]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Finance and fees handle fee structures, scheduled and instant fees, fines, discounts, tax calculation, fee defaulters, receipts, fee imports, fee transaction reports and academic-year rollover. Online payment covers student, application-registration, hostel and transport fees. Official documentation names PayPal, Authorize.net, Stripe, Braintree, PayU, CCAvenue and Interswitch, with custom gateways; current release notes add Razorpay, and BBPS integration is documented. Account splitting can divert fees to multiple bank accounts through Razorpay or ATOM. Tally synchronization exports transactions by date range. GST-specific invoicing is not explicitly documented, although tax and invoice features are. Paytm and generic UPI support are not confirmed in the reviewed sources. [3] [6] [14] [19]

#### HR, staff and payroll

The HR module stores employee details, employee documents, departments and user access; manages leave types, leave applications, attendance, payroll groups, salary processing and payslips. Employee attendance has create/update/search/delete API actions. [4] [5] [15]

#### Transport

Transport supports routes, stops, vehicles, route-specific fields, transport fee collection, vehicle/route reports and GPS integration for real-time fleet visibility and parent/staff tracking. Transport search and vehicle APIs are public in the API playground. [4] [6] [15]

#### Library

The library module manages books, categories/classification, issue and return limits, availability, barcode scanning, overdue fines and anti-theft/identification workflows. Library records can be imported in bulk, and the API exposes book search. [4] [14] [15]

#### Hostel and boarding

Hostel management covers hostels, rooms, room allocation, hostel-specific custom fields, hostel fees and records of residents. Hostel search is available through the API; the vendor describes hostel management as a core use case. [11] [15]

#### Inventory and assets

Inventory/store functions manage store categories and types, items, stock and issue/receipt workflows, with item-kit management added in Fedena 4.2. Inventory details can be bulk imported, although one reviewer specifically complained that customized CSV upload was not supported in the inventory system. [3] [14] [8]

#### Health and medical

The SIS can store institution-defined health-record fields and guardian details, but a distinct, named medical/nurse/medication module was not found in the official feature tour or help-center index. Treat health as configurable student data rather than a verified native clinical workflow.

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

The Discipline plugin allows complaints/issues against teachers or students, assignee selection, attachments/evidence, discussion and action/solution tracking. Discussion, poll, task, blog and messaging tools support pastoral or community workflows, but a safeguarding case-management module is not publicly documented. [14]

#### Special education and safeguarding

No dedicated special-education/IEP, safeguarding, child-protection or accessibility case-management module was publicly verified in the reviewed official pages. Custom fields, documents, roles and audit logs can be configured, but they should not be treated as a native safeguarding suite.

#### Alumni and fundraising

The Alumni module retains alumni students, supports alumni events and communication by email/SMS, and is intended to connect alumni with current students. A fundraising/donations module was not publicly verified. [14]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Dashlets provide role-specific dashboards for attendance, dues, exams, schedules, news and finance. Reports include attendance, fees pending, examination results, placement, finance, graphical performance analysis and custom reports with selectable filters/columns. Multi-school management provides consolidated dashboards for groups of institutions, although the dedicated page was not extractable during review. [5] [6] [12]

#### AI features

No production AI assistant, generative-AI authoring, chatbot, predictive-risk model or AI analytics feature was verified in current Fedena official materials. A third-party directory lists generic AI feature labels for Fedena, but those labels conflict with Fedena’s own published product documentation and are not used here as evidence. [12]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Fedena has Indian-board functionality: official materials cite CBSE, ICSE and regional state boards, and the help center documents ICSE grading/report workflows and CCE reports. However, I found no current public Fedena documentation confirming direct UDISE+ submission, APAAR ID generation/synchronization, NEP 2020 Holistic Progress Card templates, or NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE reporting. Institutions should request a current implementation statement rather than infer these from generic custom-report capability. [4] [5] [17]

#### Mobile apps

The current “Fedena Mobile App” provides administrator, teacher, parent and student experiences: dashboards, attendance, assignments, gradebook, timetable, exams/results, fee payment/receipts, announcements, school calendar, leave approvals/requests, notifications and teacher communication. It is native on iOS and Android. The Android FedenaConnect demo listing separately exposes announcements with attachments, broadcasts, events, parent fee payment, teacher leave and attendance, and student switching for siblings. [9] [10] [13]

#### Integrations and APIs

The public API playground exposes token generation plus course, batch, attendance, employee leave/attendance, subjects, timetable, grading levels, exam groups/scores, books, events, finance transactions, biometric data, hostel, news, school, routes, vehicles, users and photo upload. OAuth/app-frame support lets third-party applications access Fedena with limitations. Google SSO and Microsoft Azure AD SSO are documented. [14] [15]

#### Security and privacy

Fedena documents encrypted stored data, backups, role/privilege controls, password recovery, custom URLs and audit plugins for activity, user and data changes. Its privacy policy provides access, rectification, deletion, portability, objection and restriction language, but the policy was last updated 24 May 2018. No public SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certificate, hosting-region statement, FERPA/COPPA attestation, DPDP Act readiness statement or public incident report was verified. [5] [6] [14] [20]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **Open-source core and plugin architecture:** Apache-licensed Fedena 1.0 and a plugin-friendly design allow self-hosting, custom development and third-party extensions. [3] [5]
* **Indian assessment support:** CCE, CBSE-oriented SA/FA workflows and ICSE IA/EA grading are unusually relevant for Indian schools. [5] [17]
* **Broad role coverage in one app:** The current mobile app unifies administrator, teacher, parent and student workflows rather than shipping only a parent companion app. [13]
* **Institution-group oversight:** Multi-school dashboards provide a consolidated management view for school groups. [5] [6]
* **No-code-style form and report customization:** Form Builder, custom reports, custom fields and import tools allow institutions to adapt data collection and reporting without changing the core code. [5] [14]
* **Public API and OAuth app frame:** Tokenized REST-style API actions and embedded external applications provide a practical extension path. [14] [15]

### Pricing Details

The official pricing page was checked 24 November 2026. It displayed a temporary 20% year-end sale ending 25 November 2026, with annual institutional pricing in USD and no per-student unit: Standard $800/year (approximately ₹74,778 at the 24 November 2026 Xe mid-market reference rate of $1 = ₹93.4728), Premium $1,120/year (approximately ₹104,690), and Ultimate $1,360/year (approximately ₹127,123). The INR figures are conversions, not official INR list prices. [6] [20]

Standard includes 20 core modules, 17 standard modules, unlimited users, one-to-one online training, automatic updates, email/phone support and onboarding data/configuration. Premium adds 10 premium modules; Ultimate adds 12 ultimate modules. Enterprise is quote-based and adds product source code; implementation is described in the FAQ as included, while mobile apps, gateways, SMS, biometric, GPS and other add-ons may depend on configuration and plan. A 14-day no-credit-card trial is offered. Third-party listings report older/alternative prices: Capterra $1,299/year, G2 $1,299/year and Software Advice $1,299/year; these should not override the official 2026 sale page. [7] [8] [9] [18]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Verified integrations include Tally, Moodle, Google SSO, Microsoft Azure AD SSO, Zoom, Google Meet, BigBlueButton, biometric devices, GPS/location services, bulk SMS and payment gateways including Razorpay, ATOM, BBPS, PayPal, Authorize.net, Stripe, Braintree, PayU, CCAvenue and Interswitch. Fedena has a public API playground, OAuth/app-frame support, XML/CSV export and a historical marketplace/plugin ecosystem. [5] [14] [15] [18] [19]

No evidence was found that Fedena is certified for OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF, or that it has Clever/ClassLink integrations or a current public marketplace with certification governance. Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 support is limited in the verified materials to Google/Azure SSO and Google Meet rather than a full productivity-suite integration.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Fedena claims encrypted stored data, backups, role-based privileges and audit trails, and the current pricing page says cloud hosting includes encrypted security. Its privacy policy offers data access, rectification, deletion, portability, objection and processing restriction, but it is dated 24 May 2018 and is primarily a website/service privacy notice. [6] [20]

No public evidence was verified for SOC 2, ISO 27001, FERPA, COPPA or a named GDPR certification. The policy includes GDPR-style rights but does not establish current GDPR compliance. No data-hosting region or cloud provider is disclosed in the reviewed official materials. There is no verified public security-incident disclosure in the sources reviewed. DPDP Act 2023 readiness—especially child-consent, purpose limitation, data-principal requests, processor contracts and breach workflows—is not publicly documented; Indian buyers should obtain current contractual and technical assurances.

### Strengths

* Long operating history, open-source roots and a proven Indian education focus.
* Very broad ERP coverage across academic, administrative, finance, HR and campus operations.
* Strong fit for CBSE/CCE and documented ICSE grading, with regional-board positioning.
* Unlimited users, self-hosting/customization and a public API can reduce lock-in for capable IT teams.
* Current native iOS/Android app covers all four principal roles.
* Public pricing, a no-card trial and included onboarding make initial evaluation straightforward.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* Capterra’s 19-review profile gives 4.0/5 for ease of use, 3.6/5 for value for money and 3.8/5 for customer service, below the headline 4.2 overall. [8]
* Reviews praise the breadth, admissions, communication and simplicity, but complain that the interface can feel like a maze, gradebook and inventory navigation are difficult, support/training can be slow or poorly presented, and large-data loading can hang. [7] [8]
* Users report pricing pressure for small organizations and request lower entry pricing; Capterra lists $1,299/year while the official page’s 2026 sale is different, so buyers should confirm the quote and included modules. [7] [8]
* The Android FedenaConnect demo is only 3.6/5 from 79 reviews and includes login/demo-account complaints; the App Store Fedena Mobile App is 2.5/5 from six ratings. [9] [10]
* The open-source/community edition is attractive for control but may lag the hosted commercial edition and requires technical maintenance; current feature parity and support should be confirmed before self-hosting. [8]
* Direct evidence for UDISE+, APAAR, NEP 2020 HPC, WhatsApp, Paytm, GST invoicing, higher-education statutory reporting, AI and DPDP readiness is missing from public materials.

### Key Milestones

* **2009:** Foradian Technologies founded in April; custom student-information system development began in May as “Foredu”; first successful Fedena school test run in August. [3]
* **2010:** Fedena 1.0 released publicly as Apache License 2.0 open source; version 2.0 later added HR and finance to the open-source edition. [3]
* **2011:** Kerala Government’s Sampoorna project used the open-source Fedena codebase across more than 15,000 schools, according to Foradian’s history. [3]
* **2012:** Fedena 2.3 added CWA, GPA, CCE and eight languages; Foradian won NASSCOM Emerge 10 and MIT TR35 recognition. [3]
* **2013:** SaaS version launched; plugin marketplace and secure API/app-frame capabilities launched; Fedena became available in Italian. [3]
* **2014:** Fedena 3.0 launched; Foradian raised $2 million from William Bissell and reached its five-year claim of 20 million students/teachers worldwide. [3] [18]
* **2015–2017:** Enterprise division launched; Fedena 3.5 added major functionality; Fedena Connect launched in 2017. [3]
* **2018–2019:** ID-card/certificate, skill-based gradebook, custom report-card templates and enquiry analytics were added; Fedena 3.8 launched in 2019. [3]
* **2020–2022:** Online-exam/mobile and academic improvements continued; Practically announced its acquisition of Fedena/Foradian in 2022. [1] [3]
* **2024–2025:** Fedena 4.4, 4.5, 5.0 and 5.1 releases added reporting, workflow, attendance and UX improvements. [3]
* **March 2026:** Fedena 5.2 added library access in parent profiles, student documents in the mobile app and Razorpay payment-gateway integration. [3]
* **November 2026:** Official pricing page displayed a 20% year-end sale through 25 November 2026; current public adoption claim was 40,000+ institutions and 200+ countries. [4] [6]
