G2/Capterra: no current, verifiable rating was found. SoftwareFinder: 2.7/5 from 3 verified reviews, last updated September 8, 2026. [5] [6] [7] [8] |

### Overview

NextOS is Next Education’s cloud-first school operating system, combining NextERP, NextLMS, NextAssessment, digital content, communication, and mobile access for administrators, teachers, students, parents, transport attendants, and security guards. [1] [3]

The company was founded in Hyderabad in 2007 and remains presented as Next Education India Pvt. Ltd.; the public company pages identify founders and operating offices but do not disclose an acquisition history. Older Next Education material calls the suite NextLearningPlatform/NextERP, while the current product site calls it NextOS. The current rebranding therefore should not be confused with a separately verified 2007 NextOS product launch. [2] [14]

Its India-specific positioning combines board-aligned content with configurable report cards, holistic progress cards, DLT messaging, Indian payment gateways, Tally, and optional RFID/NFC/biometric/GPS devices. UDISE+, APAAR, GST invoicing, and higher-education reporting are not documented on the reviewed official pages and should be validated in procurement.

### Platform Classification Explained

**Browser and cloud:** NextOS describes the ERP and K-12 Suite as cloud-based/cloud-first SaaS, accessible from anywhere and on any device. No cloud provider, tenancy architecture, uptime SLA, or on-premise installer is named publicly. [1] [3]

**Desktop and on-premise:** No Windows/macOS desktop client, self-hosted package, or on-premise option was found; Windows access is browser-based.

**Native mobile:** “NextOS (NextLearningPlatform)” is listed for Android and iOS. The unified app covers administrator, teacher, parent, student, vehicle-attender, and security-guard workflows, and the K-12 FAQ says it can be white-labelled with a school’s name, logo, and colours. [3] [5] [6]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions, enrollment, and CRM

Admissions supports online/walk-in enquiries, OTP verification, configurable multi-tier workflows, online forms, document collection, bulk uploads, fee collection, campaign capture, lead tracking, counsellor follow-up, and multi-branch oversight. Built-in SEO/campaign tools capture leads; no separate CRM connector is established publicly. [3] [14]

#### Student information and records

The SIS provides a 360-degree view of personal, academic, fee, examination, document, wellness, attendance, and performance information, plus searchable records, sibling mapping, document storage, NOCs, certificates, ID cards, and provisional promotion. [3] [14]

#### Attendance and leave

Schools can mark daily and period-wise attendance, use teacher mobile roll-call, auto-calculate present/absent/half-day states, alert parents of absences, and generate attendance reports. Hardware and identity options include RFID, NFC, biometrics, face recognition, wireless gates, and mobile geo-facial recognition. Staff attendance can use facial recognition plus geo-fencing without external biometric hardware. Leave supports configurable leave types, holiday restrictions, gender-specific maternity/paternity rules, staff/parent applications, admin entry of offline applications, leave encashment, and mobile approvals. [3] [14]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

NextOS supports manual and automated timetable creation, teacher competency mapping, permanent and ad-hoc substitutions, proxy management, extra classes and holiday scheduling, and attendance/leave-linked scheduling. It advertises aSc Timetable integration and automated substitution notifications. [3] [14]

#### Gradebook, assessment, and examinations

NextAssessment includes a question bank publicly described as 650,000+ questions, organised by difficulty, Bloom’s Taxonomy, and Webb’s depth, with multiple languages and formats including MCQ, subjective, comprehension, annotation, and activity-based questions. Teachers can generate or upload tests for online, offline, or hybrid delivery; restrict author access; shuffle questions; permit controlled retries/calculators; upload handwritten answers; auto-mark MCQs; annotate subjective responses; and sync marks, remarks, and grades into the ERP gradebook. Adaptive assessment uses Item Response Theory and Knowledge Space Theory claims to vary difficulty and produce concept, time, effort, and outcome analytics. [10] [14]

#### Report cards, transcripts, and holistic progress

Examination workflows support configurable terms, subjects, activities, rubrics, grading systems, weighted scores, supplementary exams, grace marks, hall tickets, weekly/monthly/annual progress reports, year-wise performance, digital publication, and more than 100 report-card designs claimed in the brochure. Holistic Progress Cards (HPCs) are described as publishable in line with board guidelines. The site has a separate CBSE/ICSE Result Analyzer for school-uploaded CBSE gazette text or ICSE/ISC tabulation PDFs; it applies a Best-5 calculation and processes the file in the browser. [3] [11] [14]

#### Learning management and homework

NextLMS offers course and lesson planning, ready-made or customised plans, learning objectives, resource uploads, classwork/homework assignment, attachment and deadline management, online submission/evaluation, feedback, “Turned In” and “Returned” states, parent alerts, self-paced learning, moderated Q&A forums, activity feeds, and real-time performance views. Live lectures can use Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams, with recorded sessions available for later access. [3] [4] [14]

#### Digital content and learning tools

TeachNext content is presented as board-aligned digital material covering CBSE, ICSE, IGCSE, Army Board, and 29 state boards, with multiple-language content claims. The LMS page lists 9,000+ hours, 25,000+ audiovisual modules, simulations, e-books, YouTube/Khan Academy links, SCORM and LTI support, an organism encyclopedia, periodic table, 2D graph plotter, log table, abacus, drawing/painting tools, and other subject tools. [3] [4]

#### Communication and engagement

Communication includes event-based SMS, email, push/in-app notifications, WhatsApp, in-app chat, group discussions, forums, document sharing, surveys, observation forms, templates, and a School Feed for photos, videos, voice notes, announcements, homework, lectures, and resources. DLT-enabled SMS is explicitly marketed. WhatsApp is publicly listed; Paytm is not. [1] [3] [14]

#### Parent, student, teacher, and administrator portals

The unified app and role-based web access give parents fee balances, payments, attendance, homework, reports, leave requests, messages, teacher chat, feeds, and bus tracking. Students receive schedules, resources, assignments, exams, answer sheets, reports, attendance, calendars, and quizzes. Teachers manage lessons, lectures, assignments, exams, grading, and parent communication; principals/admins get fee and operational dashboards. [5] [6]

#### Fees, billing, payments, and accounting

Fee management includes custom fee heads, concessions, scholarships, fines, sibling and staff-ward concessions, smart-pay rules, walk-in and online payments, cheque tracking, security deposits and refunds, collection locking, paid/due certificates, 45+ ready reports, and customised reporting. The Student Wallet lets parents pre-fund cashless fees, event charges, activities, inventory purchases, or pocket-money-like school expenses. Tally 4.1/Tally Prime integration is advertised. Gateways named by the official site include Razorpay, PayU, Atom, GrayQuest, HDFC CollectNow, Smart HDFC, eNACH, GQ/Zenda, and ICICI Eazypay; no public evidence was found for Paytm or a GST-invoice module. [1] [3] [14]

#### HR, staff, payroll, and leave

Staff records, hierarchy, competency mapping, staff ID cards, HRMS access, allowances/deductions, PF/ESIC formula logic, attendance/leave integration, salary locking, increments/decrements, loans/advances, payslips, full-and-final settlement, and bank-ready payroll reports are described. The brochure references 7th Pay Commission alignment. [14]

#### Transport

Transport covers routes, stops, trips, vehicle/fleet records, student allocation, driver/helper records, attendance and performance history, maintenance and fuel analysis, route-wise fees, receipts, live GPS, parent arrival/delay alerts, and targeted disruption messages. NFC cards tapped on a vehicle-attender phone can record boarding; mobile GPS is marketed as an alternative to dedicated GPS hardware. [3] [9] [14]

#### Library

The official reasons page and brochure describe barcode scanning, quick issue/return, ISBN auto-fetch, online browsing, location/category tagging including DDC, reservations, due reminders, and configurable membership policies. [14] [15]

#### Hostel and boarding

“Hostel Management” appears in the official feature navigation, but the reviewed public pages do not expose a detailed hostel workflow or sub-feature list. Room allocation, wardens, mess, and boarding reports should therefore be treated as unverified until shown in a demo. [1]

#### Inventory and assets

Inventory supports multi-store and supplier management, purchase workflows from requirement to payment, inward/outward and tagged items, stock transfers and adjustments, item issuance, school kits, asset/service management, location-based transfers, sales/returns, and audit reports. The official pages connect inventory transactions with fees and Tally. [14] [15]

#### Health, wellness, behavior, and discipline

The student profile and brochure describe medical/wellness records, health status, incidents, category-based discipline feedback and rewards, and discipline tracking. Public material does not establish a separate clinical, immunisation, safeguarding, or case-management subsystem. [14] [15]

#### Front office, visitors, projects, and tickets

Front Office provides OTP-verified visitor entry/exit, escort authentication, scheduled or on-the-spot visits, printed badges, event controls, security-guard mobile access, and audit history. Project and ticket tools track tasks, complaints, conversations, status, and resolution. [3] [14]

#### Analytics and reporting

Dashboards cover fees, attendance, examinations, student trends, class/subject performance, concept and learning-objective performance, discipline, and transport. NextLMS Analytics and Principal Reports are described as giving micro-level and school-wide views, with remedial-action planning and exports to Excel/PDF. Public evidence supports descriptive and diagnostic analytics; a separately documented predictive-risk engine was not found. [3] [4] [14]

#### AI features

AI-related capabilities include AI-proctored examinations, adaptive assessments, automated question-paper generation, mobile geo-facial staff attendance, and AI-powered doubt/learning assistance claims. A general-purpose production AI assistant, named predictive model, and public AI governance documentation were not found. [1] [10]

#### Mobile apps

The named app, NextOS (NextLearningPlatform), is available on Android and iOS. It supports multiple accounts/devices, automated alerts, fees, messages, homework, learning resources, exams, report cards, attendance, bus tracking, and role-specific workflows. White-labeling is offered for the K-12 Suite. [3] [5] [6]

#### Integrations and APIs

Documented integrations include Tally 4.1/Tally Prime, Razorpay, PayU, Atom, HDFC and ICICI payment services, GrayQuest, Zenda, eNACH, Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, YouTube, Khan Academy, aSc Timetable, RFID/biometric/face-recognition devices, GPS, SCORM, LTI, H5P, and ClassLink. The independent listing says no API is offered; no public developer portal, API reference, OneRoster/Ed-Fi/SIF certification, or app marketplace was found. [1] [3] [7]

#### Government reporting, standards, and India-specific compliance

Public evidence supports CBSE/ICSE result analysis, 29 state boards, NEP-aligned content, and holistic progress-card workflows. It does not verify UDISE+ export/API, APAAR ID, GST-compliant invoicing, Paytm, NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE reporting, or formal DPDP readiness. DLT messaging and Indian payment/Tally workflows are not statutory-reporting certification. [3] [4] [11] [14]

#### Security and privacy

Role-based access, encryption, automatic backups, secure cloud storage, and 256-bit encryption are marketed; detailed evidence is assessed below. [12] [13] [15]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Integrated ERP–LMS–assessment–content stack:** administrative records, learning workflows, examinations, and board-aligned content share one product family. [3] [4]
- **AI-proctored and adaptive assessment:** online, offline, and hybrid exams combine proctoring signals, adaptive difficulty, analytics, and gradebook sync. [10]
- **Geo-facial staff attendance:** mobile face verification plus geo-fencing can reduce dependence on separate biometric terminals. [3]
- **Student Wallet and school eStore:** parents can fund a traceable wallet and use a no-code store for uniforms, books, or school purchases. [1] [3]
- **NFC transport attendance:** vehicle-attender phones can tap student NFC IDs while GPS and parent alerts cover the journey. [3] [14]
- **White-labelled role-based app and website:** schools can publish branded Android/iOS and website experiences. [3]
- **Large India-oriented content and question bank:** the vendor claims 29 state-board mappings, 650,000+ questions, and extensive audiovisual resources. [4] [10]

### Pricing Details

There is no public rate-card or tier table. The official School ERP FAQ gives **₹7–₹155 per student per month** and **₹60,000–₹2,00,000+ per year** for next-generation packages; the LMS page gives **₹20–₹50 per student per month**. These are indicative, quote-dependent ranges; no USD price is listed. [3] [4]

The sales model is modular: a school can start with a single module and add others. The FAQ says proposals disclose setup, training, and support commitments and claims no hidden/setup charges; the LMS page says onboarding, training, and support are included at specified intervals. No free self-serve trial, implementation SLA, or separately priced premium tier is published. [3] [4]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Documented connectors include Tally, Indian payment gateways, Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, aSc Timetable, GPS/RFID/biometric systems, SCORM, LTI, H5P, ClassLink, YouTube, and Khan Academy. [1] [3] No public API reference, developer portal, marketplace, OneRoster, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, or certification statement was found; SoftwareFinder answers “No” to an API question. [7]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

NextOS claims cloud encryption, role-based access, backups, secure servers, and 256-bit encryption. The privacy policy discusses gateway-processed financial details, optional face data, India-based storage language, overseas service-provider transfers, access/correction, and grievance contacts. [12] [13] It is not a DPDP Act statement; DPDP readiness, deletion/retention tools, processor contracts, certifications, penetration tests, named cloud provider, and incident history require due diligence.

Google Play says the app may collect location and personal information, encrypts data in transit, and cannot delete data, while Apple displays “Data Not Collected.” These store disclosures should be reconciled with enterprise data-lifecycle terms. No public breach or security incident was identified.

### Strengths

- Broad India-focused coverage across ERP, LMS, assessment, content, mobile, fees, transport, and communications.
- Strong board and curriculum positioning, including CBSE, ICSE, IGCSE, Army Board, and 29 state boards.
- Useful local workflows: DLT SMS, Indian gateways, Tally, UPI-enabled gateway claims, concessions, scholarships, sibling rules, and wallet payments.
- Mature help centre with hundreds of topic articles across admission, fee, examination, attendance, communication, LMS, transport, library, payroll, and student areas. [16]
- Native iOS/Android access and a high-volume Google Play presence, with 4.5/5 ratings on both major stores as viewed on November 24, 2026. [5] [6]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is quote-based and the official ranges are broad; there is no published module-by-module rate card, SLA, or USD price.
- Public product language is stronger than public technical evidence for APIs, predictive analytics, statutory reporting, and formal security certifications.
- Independent SoftwareFinder feedback is mixed: the three-review average is 2.7/5; complaints cite lengthy setup/training, weak reporting, few integration options, support gaps, and high cost. [7] [8]
- Google Play reviews include reports of repeated key-expiry problems, frozen video/crackling audio, slow opening, and missing homework; Apple reviews mention false outstanding-fee alerts, error messages, and infrequent upgrades. These are user reports, not independently reproduced defects. [5] [6]
- App-store privacy disclosures are inconsistent, and the public privacy statement does not expressly address DPDP Act readiness, retention/deletion controls, or a named hosting provider.
- Hostel, special-education, safeguarding, alumni/fundraising, UDISE+, APAAR, GST invoicing, and higher-education NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE functions are not sufficiently documented for a confident feature claim.

### Key Milestones

- **2007:** Next Education founded in Hyderabad; the company’s history says the initial office operated as Helix Technology Solutions Pvt. Ltd. [2]
- **2009–2018:** The 2025 brochure shows product-development eras but does not identify a separately verifiable NextOS launch year. [14]
- **Pre-2026:** The family operated under NextLearningPlatform/NextERP, combining ERP, LMS, assessment, and digital content. [4] [14]
- **January 2026:** NextOS published an updated long-form explanation of the Next Learning Platform, describing ERP, LMS, assessments, courseware, live lectures, adaptive/static testing, OCR-assisted evaluation, and board-aligned content. [4]
- **2023–2024:** The current about page lists vendor-reported education and digital-transformation awards. [2]
- **July 15, 2026:** The Google Play app listing records its latest update date at the time viewed. [5]
- **November 24, 2026:** Current NextOS pages claimed 21,000+ institutions, 240,000+ educators, and 20,000,000+ learners; the older corporate page retained lower 18,000-school/12,000,000-student figures. [1] [2]

## India #5. Academia ERP (Serosoft)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Serosoft Solutions Private Limited, marketed as Academia by Serosoft [1] |
| Headquarters | Indore, Madhya Pradesh, India; Clutch lists 5th Floor, Milinda’s Manor, 2 RNT Marg, Indore 452001 [2] |
| Company founded (year) | 2008, according to Clutch; Serosoft’s 2026 site describes 18 years in education [2] [3] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | Not publicly disclosed. Independent trade coverage confirms Academia was the flagship product by October 2016; this is evidence of existence, not a launch date [4] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud SaaS and browser/web-based, with institution-specific native Android and iOS apps; a perpetual five-year license model is also offered with separate hosting setup, making deployment commercially hybrid. No public desktop client or customer-managed on-premise package is evidenced [5] [6] [7] |
| Primary segments | Higher education universities and colleges; K-12 schools and school groups; training, vocational/TVET and multi-campus education groups [1] [3] [4] |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | Vendor claims 400+ institutions, 1M+ learners and educators, 32 countries and four continents (site viewed 24 Nov 2026); a 2016 trade interview reported an India-first strategy and international expansion [3] [4] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://serosoft.com/ |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://www.academiaerp.com/modules/ |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | Public REST API documentation: https://api.academiaerp.com/resources/index.html . No public end-user help-center URL was located. |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | https://www.academiaerp.com/higher-ed-plans/ and https://www.academiaerp.com/k12-plans/ (module plans show Pro, Premium and Enterprise but no amounts) |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | G2 4.7/5 from 24 reviews (viewed 24 Nov 2026; profile updated 17 Nov 2026); Capterra 4.5/5 from 13 reviews, ease of use 4.2 and customer service 4.5 (page updated 29 Sep 2026); Apple App Store Academia @ IIT: not enough ratings/reviews to display an overview; Google Play Academia @ SIS: 10K+ downloads, no aggregate score shown; Google Play Academia @ CECOS: no aggregate score shown on the page viewed [8] [9] [10] [11] [12] |

### Overview

Academia is Serosoft’s centralized education ERP/SIS family. It spans enquiry through alumni across academics, attendance, fees, exams and student services. The site describes 40+ modules, AI dashboards, multi-campus, multi-currency and multi-language operations [1] [3]. It serves both higher education and K-12 through product variants such as Academia SIS, ERP, UMS, CMS, TMS, TVET and SMS [13].

Serosoft was founded in 2008. The company does not publish a separate Academia launch year; its CEO called Academia the flagship product in an October 2016 interview, so 2008 should not be misreported as the product launch year [4]. The current adoption figure is a vendor claim: 400+ institutions, 1M+ learners/educators and 32 countries as of 2026 [3]. No acquisition is identified in the official history or the independent sources reviewed.

### Platform Classification Explained

- **Browser/cloud:** Academia is described as cloud-native, with online portals, real-time data and SaaS access. Serosoft says its secure cloud infrastructure runs on Microsoft Azure data centers globally; its privacy policy identifies Central India, South Africa North and West Europe/North Europe production-backup arrangements [6] [14].
- **SaaS:** The SaaS model is an annual per-user-per-year subscription including hosting, updates, support and maintenance. Implementation covers configuration, data migration, API integrations, training and change management [5].
- **Perpetual/license option:** The license model is a five-year upfront license, usually linked to student volume, with fixed annual maintenance from year two. The page says “separate hosting setup,” but does not promise on-premise deployment or a desktop installer [7].
- **Mobile:** The platform has native institution-branded apps on both Android and iOS. Exact public examples include “Academia @ SIS,” “Academia @ CECOS,” and “Academia @ IIT.” Features include attendance, timetable, fees, results, assignments, documents and notifications; availability and feature scope vary by institution [11] [12].
- **Desktop:** No public desktop client was found. Administrative use is presented as web-based.

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

Campaigns and enquiry management, configurable web enquiry forms, multi-stage admissions, automatic stage progression, bulk application upload, applicant portal, mandatory/optional document collection, payment at application stages, offer-letter templates, accept/reject workflow and campaign-level dashboards are documented. The public REST API exposes enquiry, application, document, payment and status endpoints [15] [16].

#### Student information and records

A centralized student profile connects personal, guardian, address, identity, education-history, disability, nationality, caste-category, course, programme, document, hold and service-request data. The API includes student detail, documents, enrolments, courses, user roles and academic lookups [15].

#### Attendance

Attendance supports web entry, bulk upload, teacher mobile entry, QR scanning, RFID and biometric integrations. Reports can be student-wise, subject-wise, daily and monthly, with visual attendance insights and attendance-based detention/holds in examinations [17] [16].

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Programme, course, section and class scheduling are supported, with daily/weekly/monthly views in the student app. Public evidence confirms timetable management and course-wise/day-wise timetable access; a scheduling algorithm is not disclosed [11].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Institutions can create assessment schemes, multi-level marking structures, sum/average/best-of rules, exam schedules, seating plans and marks-entry windows. Marks may be entered manually or in bulk. The examination page supports unit tests, midterms, finals, practicals and external exams, with pass/fail rules, SGPA/CGPA, course and section ranks and analytics [16].

#### Report cards and transcripts

Academia generates customizable marksheets, grade cards, certificates and transcripts in bulk. It can publish results through portal, email or SMS and supports configurable templates aligned to institutional or higher-authority formats [16]. CBSE/ICSE/state-board report-card templates and NEP 2020 holistic progress cards are not explicitly documented on the reviewed product pages; institutions should validate these in a demonstration.

#### Learning management and homework

Assignment management, homework, course-material/document sharing, submission, feedback, session diary and learning-management integration are present. Academia’s public material does not establish a full native content-authoring LMS, so it is better characterized as SIS-linked coursework plus LMS interoperability rather than a replacement for a specialist LMS [11] [12] [18].

#### Communication

The messaging engine supports notifications, email and SMS; examination results can be distributed through email, SMS or portal. Serosoft also documents WhatsApp API integration for broadcast messages, media/documents and stakeholder communication, with the article dated 9 Nov 2022 [19]. Push notifications are evidenced in the apps. A named vendor gateway list is not publicly disclosed.

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Student, applicant, faculty/teacher and parent-facing portals are offered by plan and product variant. Students can view attendance, dues, schedules, assignments, results, hall tickets, placements and notifications; parents receive communication and performance visibility. Current K-12 plans list student, parent and teacher mobile applications, while higher-ed plans list student and faculty apps [11] [13].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Fee plans can be linked to programmes, batches, seat types, admissions, services and exams, with late penalties, discounts, scholarships, auto-invoicing, reminders, receipts, payment-mode analysis, outstanding/aging reports and drill-down dashboards. Online payment gateways are supported and payments can be automatically matched to student accounts [20]. The school product explicitly cites Tally, accounting software and online payment gateways; Razorpay, Paytm and UPI are not named on the reviewed pages, so their availability is unverified. GST invoicing is not explicitly documented.

#### HR, staff and payroll

Employee/faculty management, staff profiles, role allocation, faculty portals, workload-related academic operations, HR and payroll-related use cases appear in the catalog and plan lists. Payroll depth is not publicly disclosed; do not assume a full HRIS [9] [13].

#### Transport

Transport management is a named module in both the higher-ed and K-12 plan maps. Route planning, GPS, vehicle maintenance and parent bus tracking are not publicly enumerated and should be verified.

#### Library

Library management is listed by Capterra and was specifically praised by a reviewer for organizing college books. The official current module map emphasizes resource booking rather than describing library sub-features, while the school page names KOHA interoperability [9] [13].

#### Hostel and boarding

Hostel management is a named module; the API and admissions flow include hostel-required data. Room allocation, occupancy, mess, maintenance and visitor workflows are not detailed [15].

#### Inventory and assets

Resource booking, facility-management and security-gate modules are evidenced. A standalone inventory, procurement or fixed-asset ledger is not clearly described in the official module map; do not assume a full inventory/asset-management suite without confirmation [13].

#### Health and medical

Infirmary/medical-care management is a named module in both the general and K-12 maps. Clinical records, medication, consent and emergency workflows are not specified [13].

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Discipline management is named, and grievance management, surveys, tasks and committees provide adjacent student-support workflows. Detailed behavior points, pastoral case plans or safeguarding escalation rules are not publicly specified [13].

#### Special education and safeguarding

The Capterra catalog tags Special Education, but the official module pages reviewed do not describe an IEP, accommodations or child-safeguarding workflow. Disability fields exist in the admissions API, which is weaker evidence than a dedicated special-education module [9] [15].

#### Alumni and fundraising

Alumni management is part of the current product positioning and higher-ed lifecycle; scholarship and sponsorship management are named modules. Fundraising, donor CRM, campaigns and donation processing are not detailed publicly [1] [13].

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Academia claims 800+ customizable dashboards on its About page, while its 2026 India guide claims 800+ reports/dashboards and 400+ AI-powered reports. Analytics cover admissions, attendance, fees, performance, examinations, progression and operations, with drill-down, real-time data and multi-campus views [3] [21]. These are vendor claims, not independent audits.

#### AI features

The AI page names SERA-AI student assistant, natural-language reporting, real-time dashboards, predictive insights, AI enrollment bot, document-verification engine, workflow automation and retention-risk prediction. The vendor does not publish model-accuracy, data-retention or human-review benchmarks [22].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Academia supports configurable reports and local workflows, and its API contains Indian-relevant fields such as caste category, national ID, home/second language and disability. However, no reviewed official page explicitly confirms CBSE, ICSE, a particular state board, NEP 2020 holistic progress cards, UDISE+, APAAR, NAAC, NBA, NIRF or AISHE submission connectors. These should be treated as unverified rather than assumed. GST invoicing and exact UPI/Razorpay/Paytm support are likewise not publicly confirmed.

#### Mobile apps

Android and iOS institution-specific apps provide student/faculty access, timetable, attendance, fees, assignments, marksheets/results, documents and announcements. Google Play shows 10K+ downloads for Academia @ SIS; Apple’s Academia @ IIT listing says the app is exclusive to its institution and has insufficient ratings for an overview [11] [12].

#### Integrations and APIs

Serosoft claims 50+ out-of-the-box integrations plus custom connectors and APIs. Public integration examples include LMS, accounting software, Tally, payment gateways, KOHA, WhatsApp, RFID/biometrics and LimeSurvey. The public REST API is extensive across admissions, finance, programmes, courses, students, documents, users, faculty attendance and receipts [9] [15] [18].

#### Security and privacy

The vendor states ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 9001:2015 certification, encryption in transit/at rest, role-based access, two-factor authentication, backups, monitoring, data-quality dashboards, subject-access support and Azure hosting [6] [14]. Its certifications page says SOC 2 is actively being worked toward, while other pages label it “SOC 2 compliant”; this inconsistency warrants requesting the current report. GDPR, POPIA, PDPO and NITA alignment are claimed. The privacy policy, last reviewed 11 Feb 2026, defines Serosoft as processor, customers as controllers, names EU/UK representatives, states deletion on contract termination and gives regional Azure locations [14]. No DPDP Act readiness statement or public security incident was found.

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- AI student assistant, AI reporting and AI agents/bots extend beyond conventional SIS reporting [22].
- Low/no-code configurability allows institutions to shape workflows, forms and rules without technical dependency [18].
- Multi-center capability gives groups a unified view across campuses or institutions [18].
- QR, RFID, biometric and mobile attendance provide several capture modes [17].
- Five-year licensing with fixed AMC from year two gives a non-SaaS budget option [7].
- Institution-specific Android/iOS apps let each deployment expose its selected modules and branding [11] [12].

### Pricing Details

No public numeric vendor price was found as of 24 Nov 2026. The official higher-ed and K-12 pricing pages show Pro, Premium and Enterprise module plans, but each routes to “Request Demo” and gives no INR or USD amount [5] [13]. The SaaS model is annual per user per year and includes software access, hosting, updates, technical support and maintenance; implementation services and the first year’s subscription are paid up front [5]. The license model is a five-year upfront payment, usually calculated per student/license with tiered pricing, plus fixed AMC from year two; the page does not state the amount [7].

G2 records two quote-only editions: “License Model — Contact Us / 500 Users With One-Time Purchase” and “SaaS Model — Contact Us / 500 Users Per Year,” with no numeric USD or INR price and no free trial [8]. Capterra and Software Advice display ₹1 per year, but this is a directory placeholder rather than a credible vendor quote; it should not be used as the product price [9] [10]. Setup, migration and implementation are separately discussed by the vendor, but no fee is published.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Academia has a public REST API and claims 50+ out-of-the-box integrations, real-time synchronization and custom connectors [15] [18]. Named or evidenced connections include LMS platforms, finance/accounting tools, Tally, online gateways, KOHA, WhatsApp, LimeSurvey, RFID and biometrics. No public evidence was found for certified OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 or SSO. Interoperability is therefore strong at API/connector level but not standards-certified on the evidence available.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The strongest public controls are ISO 27001:2022, role-based permissions, secure login with optional two-factor authentication, encryption, backups, monitoring, Azure hosting and data-subject request handling [6] [14]. GDPR and regional privacy alignment are stated; FERPA and COPPA are not explicitly claimed. The privacy policy includes EU/UK representatives and regional Azure data locations, including Central India, but does not promise that every customer is hosted in India. DPDP Act readiness is not explicitly stated, and no publicly reported incident was located in the reviewed sources. SOC 2 wording is inconsistent: the security/about pages call it compliant, while the certifications page says Serosoft is actively working toward it [3] [6] [14].

### Strengths

- Broad, genuinely integrated coverage across admissions, academics, exams, fees, portals, transport, hostel, placement, alumni and analytics.
- Strong higher-ed orientation with programme/course structures, SGPA/CGPA, transcripts, OBE, thesis and placement workflows.
- Public API documentation is unusually concrete for an education ERP, including admissions, finance, student and faculty operations [15].
- Multiple delivery choices: annual SaaS or five-year license, plus Android/iOS apps and Azure hosting.
- Reviewers consistently praise breadth, support, automation, flexibility and campus-wide information flow [8] [9] [10].
- India-origin vendor with explicit Tally, payment-gateway, KOHA and WhatsApp references, although not every requested Indian connector is confirmed [13] [19].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is quote-only; the public “₹1 per year” directory entries are placeholders and do not help buyers budget [8] [9] [10].
- G2 users report occasional bugs, slow loading, slower-than-needed fixes and reporting that could be more customizable; G2 also summarizes limited customization and learning difficulty [8].
- Capterra reviewers mention time-consuming customization, slow dynamic reports, dated UI/facelift needs, limited student-mobile features and an employee-app gap in older reviews [9].
- One Capterra reviewer reported a severe implementation failure and inability to deliver promised customization; this is an older, isolated review but is material procurement risk [9].
- No public proof was found for UDISE+, APAAR, board-specific report cards, NEP holistic progress cards, NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE, GST, UPI, Razorpay, Paytm or DPDP readiness.
- Standards certification for OneRoster/LTI/Ed-Fi/SIF and public SSO/marketplace evidence are absent.

### Key Milestones

- **2008:** Serosoft founded, per Clutch; the founder/CEO is Arpit Badjatya [2].
- **By 2016:** Academia was Serosoft’s flagship product, offered in ERP/SIS, school-management and training-center variants; the company reported an India-first strategy with international expansion [4].
- **2016:** Trade coverage described student/parent portals, mobile apps, analytics, multi-campus, multi-currency and multi-language capability [4].
- **2018–2019:** Serosoft was recognized in Deloitte Technology Fast 500 APAC coverage, according to the vendor’s milestone pages [3] [14].
- **2020–2021:** Vendor pages cite Economic Times Growth Champions and Financial Times Asia-Pacific growth-list recognition [3].
- **2023:** BW Businessworld named Serosoft’s product Education ERP of the Year, according to the company’s awards list [14].
- **2024:** Vendor cites IDC MarketScape higher-ed cloud-enabled SIS recognition and Stanford Seed participation [3] [14].
- **2025–2026:** The company says Academia appeared in Gartner’s Magic Quadrant for SIS SaaS in both years; these are vendor-reported recognition claims. The site also cites TIME/Statista Top 500 EdTech 2026 and 400+ institutions across 32 countries [1] [3].
- **2026:** Public product pages added prominent AI assistant, natural-language reporting, AI agents and retention-risk positioning; no acquisition or funding event was identified in the sources reviewed.

## India #6. Skolaro (Buzzyears Education Pvt Ltd)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Buzzyears Education Pvt Ltd; Crunchbase identifies Ashish Dixit and Naini Singh as co-founders. [2] [18] |
| Headquarters | Registered office: 1049, Sector A, Pocket B, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi 110070, India; the vendor describes teams across India and the Middle East. [2] |

### Overview

Skolaro is Buzzyears Education’s cloud school and college ERP/LMS. It combines admissions, student records, academics, fees, HR/payroll, campus operations, communication, mobile portals, and reporting in one system. The vendor positions it for Indian, Gulf, and Middle Eastern institutions that want a single record across principals, teachers, parents, students, and finance teams rather than separate spreadsheets and registers. [1] [3]

The current product is marketed as AI-powered and as having 50+ modules. Strongest India-specific evidence covers board assessment, UPI/card/net-banking fees, statutory payroll, WhatsApp/SMS, Tally XML, and multi-account settlement. College pages advertise AICTE, UGC, and NAAC reporting, but do not publicly document UDISE+, APAAR, NEP 2020 holistic cards, GST/HSN-SAC, NBA/NIRF/AISHE, or DPDP readiness. [7] [9]

Guide-claim audit: the 2012 company claim, 1,800+ institutions, 100+ cities, four countries, 20,000-student group, 50+ modules, quote-based billing, seven gateways, Tally/NAV/Oracle, WhatsApp, and board templates are supported by current official pages. Product launch year remains undisclosed. The exact eight-language list, Aadhaar/PAN/EWS fields, CCE/FA/SA wording, UDISE+/APAAR, RTE, GST HSN/SAC, NEP 2020 holistic cards, dropout-risk alerts, and no-feature-gating claim are not all publicly evidenced. New Delhi is confirmed as registered office; a Gurugram office is not specifically confirmed. [2] [3] [4] [7]

### Platform Classification Explained

Browser access is explicit: the school ERP is available from a PC, smartphone, or tablet, with a web management portal and role-specific portals. Hosting is described as AWS cloud hosting, with daily backups and point-in-time recovery. [3] [4]

Native mobile delivery is explicit: parent, teacher, and student apps on iOS and Android, including a school-branded parent app. Public stores expose a general “Skolaro”/Buzzyears iBuzz listing rather than three clearly separate listings: Google Play package com.buzzyears.ibuzz and Apple listing “Skolaro.” [6] [16] [17]

No desktop executable or self-hosted installation guide was found. Capterra says cloud and on-premise, conflicting with the primary AWS/cloud description; treat on-premise as unverified directory metadata. [4] [15]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions
Configurable web and social-channel forms, online application payments, applicant tracking, merit lists, offer letters, document upload, and conversion from applicant to student. [3] [20]

#### Enquiry / Lead
Captures walk-ins, website, Facebook, Google-ad, referral, and social leads; supports follow-up tasks, counsellor SLAs, funnel views, WhatsApp cadence, and optional bidirectional LeadSquared sync. [20]

#### Student Information
One profile links personal and academic data, parents, attendance, fees, transport, library, results, and discipline; supports batches, divisions, sections, houses, roll numbers, imports, and transfer-certificate lifecycle. [24]

#### Family & Sibling
Parent linkage, multiple children under one parent login, sibling discounts, and consolidated parent visibility are documented; the guide’s specific Aadhaar/PAN/EWS fields are not publicly confirmed. [3] [6]

#### Attendance
Manual daily or period-wise attendance plus biometric, RFID, face-recognition, and QR capture; below-threshold flags and immediate SMS/push absence alerts are supported. [23]

#### ID Card
Configurable student, parent, and faculty ID-card templates, including fields such as photo, address, and blood group. [5] [24]

#### Certificate Builder
Customisable character certificates and student documentation are advertised; the full catalogue is not public. [5]

#### Alumni
The student lifecycle runs through alumni, and the college product includes an alumni database, engagement campaigns, and giving; a separate K-12 fundraising product is not documented. [1] [9]

#### Complaint Tracking
Web, app, email-to-ticket, and in-person intake; category routing, owner assignment, SLA escalation, closure feedback, and dashboard satisfaction scores. [30]

#### Classroom
Class, section, subject, teacher, and learner structures support access, attendance, coursework, and reporting; detail is limited. [3]

#### Lesson Planning
Annual planners, weekly trackers, curriculum coverage, learning-plan sharing, and parent/student visibility. [3] [5]

#### Time Table
Constraint-based automatic generation for teacher loads, rooms, labs, electives, games, prayer periods, and split sessions; drag-and-drop edits and conflict-aware substitutions. [25]

#### Substitution
When a teacher is absent, the system suggests available teachers, notifies them in-app, and records timetable changes. [25]

#### Assignment
Teachers assign work to classes or individuals, accept submissions, grade inline, and return feedback; parent apps expose homework. [21] [16]

#### Online Class
Live classes can be scheduled through Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams with attendance capture. [21]

#### Online Test
Reusable MCQ, short-answer, and essay banks with chapter, difficulty, and Bloom’s-level tags; timed tests, auto-evaluation, entrance tests, ranking, percentile, and proctoring options are described. [20] [21]

#### Result / Assessment
Internal and terminal exams, marks entry, moderation, weightages, grade boundaries, percentile, grace marks, CGPA/CBCS rules, audit trails, and trend analytics. [8]

#### Report Card Designer
Custom report cards for CBSE, ICSE, IB, IGCSE, Cambridge, and major/state boards; a use-case page claims 28 state-board templates. Scholastic and co-scholastic indicators are supported in the cited CBSE example. [8] [19]

#### Co-curricular Tracker
The module index includes co-curricular tracking, and the result workflow mentions co-scholastic indicators such as health, discipline, and work education; detailed activity rubrics are not public. [3] [8]

#### Library
Book master, ISBN/barcode labels, member cards, issue/return, configurable fines, overdue reminders, reservations, OPAC search, and fee integration. [27]

#### Digital Diary
Listed in the module index; apps expose feeds, messages, documents, calendar, and homework. [3] [16]

#### Fees
Configurable fee heads, instalments, late-fee slabs, sibling discounts, scholarships, transport/hostel-mess charges, online/offline receipts, dues tracking, and AI reminders. [4] [7]

#### Fee Concession
Scholarship rules, sibling discounts, staff-ward concessions, and auditable adjustments are documented; the guide’s RTE-quota tracking is not independently verified. [7]

#### Online Fee Collection
Cash, cheque, bank challan, UPI, cards, net banking, and online gateways; receipts, refunds, settlement reports, and original-instrument refund workflows are included. [7]

#### Multi-account Settlement
Fee heads can route to different bank accounts, useful for trusts and branch groups; class-wise Paytm merchants and bank reconciliation are advertised. [7]

#### Refunds
Approval workflow, audit log, tax-credit handling, and refund to the original payment instrument are stated in the online-collection workflow. [7]

#### Accounts / GL
Company and general ledgers, receivables, payables, bank reconciliation, budget, income/expenditure, day book, cash/bank payments and receipts are listed. [5]

#### Vendor & Purchase
Vendor master, purchase orders, goods-receipt notes, payment tracking, and accounting integration are documented in inventory workflows. [28]

#### Asset Register
Barcode/RFID asset tags, location/condition, department allocation, transfers, audit history, and straight-line or written-down-value depreciation. [28]

#### Staff Records
Staff master and faculty records are part of HR/payroll and role-based portals; field-level detail is not public. [3] [29]

#### Payroll
Attendance/leave/overtime-linked salary, PF, ESI, professional tax, TDS, payslips, Form 16, Form 24Q, bank advice, and Middle East end-of-service structures. [29]

#### Leave
Leave balances/applications connect to salary calculation; approval matrices are not public. [5] [29]

#### Staff Attendance
Attendance can feed salary calculation, with biometric/RFID/mobile options; staff-specific reports are not separately documented. [23] [29]

#### Appraisal
Listed in the official module index; rubric, workflow, and KPI detail are not public. [3]

#### Recruitment
Listed in the official index; admissions CRM detail is not an employee-recruitment specification. [3]

#### Transport (GPS)
Route and stop planning, bus/driver/conductor assignment, live GPS, ETA, boarding/alighting alerts, route compliance, passenger visibility, and route-level billing. [26]

#### Inventory & Stores
Stock-in/out, transfers, allocation, vendor purchasing, barcodes/RFID, maintenance/audit, and depreciation for classroom, lab, sports, and other assets. [28]

#### Gate Pass
Digital student exit approvals, pickup verification, and parent-linked gate passes are documented. [5]

#### Visitor Log
Visitor logbook and gate-pass workflows track visitor/pickup events; ID-verification controls are not public. [3] [5]

#### Hostel
Hostel records, rooms, meals, lodging, room transfers, in/out timings, parent notifications, hostel-mess fees, and college accommodation workflows are advertised. [5] [9]

#### Health & Infirmary
Listed in the index and as a CBSE co-scholastic indicator; medical fields, consent, and safeguarding workflows are not public. [3] [8]

#### Front Office
Front-office walk-in logging and conversion into the same admissions funnel as digital leads are documented. [20]

#### Event Calendar
Integrated calendar stores past, present, and future school events and exposes schedules in the parent app. [5] [16]

#### SMS / Email / Push
One composer can send SMS, email, push, and delivery-tracked messages with regional-language support, opt-outs, read/delivery status, and SMS fallback. [1] [6]

#### WhatsApp Notifications
WhatsApp Business API supports transactional fee receipts, attendance alerts, result notifications, configurable two-way messaging, and AI-drafted fee reminders. [6]

#### Parent App
Branded iOS/Android parent app with multi-child login, fees/receipts, attendance, homework, timetable, calendar, results, documents, chat, transport status, and notifications. [6] [16] [17]

#### Teacher App
Native teacher access covers attendance, feeds, messages, homework, tests, online annotation, grade entry, lesson plans, and parent communication. [3] [16]

#### Student App
Student access covers timetable, assignments, study material, tests, online classes, results, documents, and submissions. [3] [16]

#### Notices & Circulars
In-app announcements, circulars, feeds, groups, documents, gallery, and multi-channel notices are documented. [5] [16]

#### Reports & Analytics
200+ pre-built reports, real-time filters, PDF/Excel/CSV export, scheduled email delivery, dashboards, admissions funnels, fee/attendance/exam analytics, and direct API access for BI tools. [22]

#### MIS Dashboards
Management dashboards cover receivables, occupancy, attendance health, admissions, and exam outcomes; dashboard widgets can be personalised. [1] [5]

#### Audit Log
Assessment changes, result publication, complaints, refunds, and fee workflows are described as audit-trailed; a dedicated audit-log module is listed. [3] [7] [8]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance
Templates cover CBSE, ICSE, IB, IGCSE, Cambridge, and major/state boards; College ERP advertises AICTE, UGC, and NAAC formats. UDISE+, APAAR, NEP 2020 holistic cards, NBA, NIRF, and AISHE exports were not publicly evidenced. [8] [9]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Skolaro AI assistant:** surfaces fee dues, attendance dips, admission bottlenecks, and exam outliers, and drafts fee reminders; a public technical model card is not available. [1]
- **Indian fee-operations depth:** seven named gateways, EDC reconciliation, multi-account settlement, scholarship rules, and voucher-level Tally XML sync. [7]
- **No-code configuration:** embeddable admission forms and a drag-and-drop report builder reduce dependence on developers. [20] [22]
- **Multi-channel parent engagement:** WhatsApp Business API, SMS fallback, push, email, delivery status, and branded apps operate in one communication flow. [6]
- **Board and higher-education breadth:** CBSE/ICSE/IB/IGCSE/Cambridge/state-board templates plus CBCS, AICTE, UGC, and NAAC-oriented college workflows. [8] [9]
- **Cross-campus finance:** class-wise merchants and multi-account settlement suit education trusts with several branches. [7]

### Pricing Details

Skolaro publishes no price card or fixed tier names. The official FAQ says pricing is per student, billed annually or term-wise, with all 50+ modules included in the base plan and automatic scale discounts; implementation, training, and migration are included in that base plan. Customisation is separately chargeable for unusual workflows. Pricing is therefore quote-based and should be requested from sales. [4]

A May 2023 Skolaro blog post gives a broad, industry-level Indian school-ERP range of ₹0–₹250 per student per year, not a Skolaro tariff; it should not be used as a current quote. No USD price, setup fee, or public plan comparison was found. [19]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Named integrations include Razorpay, Paytm, BillDesk, ICICI EazyPay, CCAvenue, Atom, Axis EazyPay, Razorpay-HDFC EDC, Tally XML, MS Dynamics NAV via SOAP, Oracle Cloud via REST, LeadSquared, Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Power BI, and Tableau. Biometric/RFID and GPS hardware are supported, and an official blog says the in-house team can integrate APIs. [7] [19] [20] [21] [22]

No evidence was found of 1EdTech OneRoster/LTI certification, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, a public developer portal, SSO documentation, or an integration marketplace. The site claims direct API access, but public endpoint documentation and authentication details are not available. Interoperability is therefore richer than a closed ERP but below a standards-certified ecosystem. [22]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The FAQ and privacy policy state AWS hosting, ISO 27001-certified infrastructure, AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, daily backups, point-in-time recovery, vulnerability scans, annual penetration tests, role-based access, and restricted/audited production access. The vendor targets 99.9% uptime. The policy says Buzzyears is a processor acting under an institution’s direction for children’s data, does not sell personal information, and supports access, correction, and deletion requests subject to legal retention. [4] [10] [11]

This is not evidence that Buzzyears itself holds ISO 27001 certification; the wording is “hosted on ISO 27001-certified infrastructure.” No SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR, DPDP statement, India-only hosting region, or public incident was found. The privacy policy was last updated 1 Jan 2026. Google Play says data is not encrypted and cannot be deleted, while the vendor policy says encryption and deletion requests exist; schools should resolve this contractually. [10] [16]

### Strengths

- Broad native scope for Indian schools and colleges, with an official 50+ module index and role-specific portals. [3]
- Strong fee operations: UPI/card/net banking, seven named gateways, reconciliation, multi-account settlement, and Tally sync. [7]
- Useful board, exam, and report-card configuration across CBSE, ICSE, international curricula, and state boards. [8]
- Native parent/teacher/student apps and four-channel communication, including WhatsApp Business API. [6]
- Report builder, scheduled reporting, direct API claim, and cross-campus dashboards are distinctive for a mid-market Indian ERP. [22]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is quote-only; the only public ₹0–₹250 figure is a 2023 general-market estimate, not a current Skolaro price. [4] [19]
- Independent review depth is very thin: G2 has one review, Software Advice has no reviews, and Capterra has zero. [12] [13] [15]
- Mobile UX is uneven. Apple reviewers reported missing notifications, poor UI/performance, and inability to view or download PDFs; Google Play reviews include persistent loading and links that would not open, although other users praise homework usefulness. [16] [17]
- The vendor’s AI, 1,800+ adoption, outcome percentages, and standards/compliance positioning are primarily self-reported; public technical documentation and independent validation are limited. [1] [6] [7]
- UDISE+, APAAR, NEP 2020 holistic cards, DPDP readiness, and special-education/safeguarding capabilities are not publicly evidenced, despite the guide presenting several of them as available.

### Key Milestones

- **2012:** Buzzyears Education Pvt Ltd’s official CIN contains 2012; this supports the company year, but not a separately documented Skolaro launch year. [2]
- **2019:** The official blog archive records Skolaro product marketing and a “School ERP sneak peek,” showing the product was public by then; no first-launch date is established. [19]
- **2023:** Skolaro published its FAQ article with the ₹0–₹250 per-student-per-year Indian market estimate and described API, payment, biometric/RFID, GPS, Oracle, and SAP integration claims. [19]
- **2026:** Current product pages describe 1,800+ institutions, 50+ modules, AI, seven gateways, Tally/NAV/Oracle sync, and native apps; privacy and terms pages were updated 1 Jan 2026. [1] [7] [10] [11]
- **Funding/acquisitions:** No funding round, acquisition, or ownership change was found in the reviewed official pages or Crunchbase profile; Crunchbase lists the company as active and privately held. [18]

### Overview

Vidyalaya is Sapphire Software Solutions’ integrated school and campus ERP. It combines admissions, student records, attendance, timetabling, assessment, fees, accounting, HR/payroll, transport, library, hostel, inventory, communication, portals, LMS and reporting in a configurable web system. The stated users are management, administrators, teaching and non-teaching staff, students and parents, with role-specific dashboards and access rights. [2] [6] [7]

The product began as a Windows solution after a ten-school Banaskantha pilot in 2002, then moved to web/cloud delivery. The history page records SMS integration, a national rollout, international channel partnerships in Africa and Qatar, e-exam, mobile apps, GPS tracking and virtual classroom as successive milestones. It says Admission CRM launched in 2023, LMS/Alumni/WhatsApp Business integration in 2024 and Vidyamitra in 2025. Sapphire’s company page presents Vidyalaya as an in-house product; no acquisition of Vidyalaya or Sapphire was found. [1] [4]

**Guide check.** The guide’s 2002 launch, ten-school Banaskantha origin, Ahmedabad location, 2,000+ institutions, 1.8M students, 40+ modules, Vidyamitra-2025, NEP holistic card, mobile platforms and ₹5–₹50/student/month FAQ range are supported by current or historical vendor pages. Material qualifications: the adoption totals are self-reported and vary by page/date (1,300+, 1,700+, 2,000+ and 1.5M versus 1.8M students); “company founded” and “product launched” both resolve to 2002 rather than two independently dated events; and I found no primary confirmation of the guide’s “OTP login” wording. The cited ₹1,000/year directory price is a third-party reference, not an official rate card. [2] [4] [6] [9] [16]

### Platform Classification Explained

The vendor describes Vidyalaya as a “web based” and cloud solution, with automated backups and access from anywhere. The current product is therefore best classified as browser-accessible Cloud SaaS. The historical Windows product is evidence of a legacy desktop lineage, not proof that a new on-premise Windows client remains available. Vendor pages instead say the web system can integrate on-premises apps and data; an independent TechnologyCounter listing labels deployment cloud, on-premises and hybrid, but does not document a current self-hosted installer. [4] [6] [13]

Mobile access is offered through a role-based “School App, Parent App & Management App” experience. The official site links to the Google Play listing named **Vidyalaya Student App** and Apple’s **Vidyalaya** app; the store descriptions include students, parents, teachers and administrators, with admissions, attendance, exams, fees, library, transport, messaging and dashboards. The evidence supports one multi-role app/custom-branded deployments rather than three separately named native parent, student and staff products. [2] [3] [17] [18]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

Admission inquiry, online admission forms, follow-up, conversion of inquiry to confirmation, document management, applicant tracking and website-linked admission forms are documented. Admission CRM was added as a named product milestone in 2023; AI-assisted admissions are marketed as an add-on. [4] [7]

#### Student information and records

Student profiles include photographs, family/guardian details, uploaded documents, bulk import, automatic roll numbers, ID cards, custom searches and reports. The online portal exposes student information, health, activities, fees, presence, exam schedule, results, library and holiday information. Certificates include leaving, bonafide, first-trial, transfer, transcript and character certificates, with custom templates. [7]

#### Attendance

The system supports subject-wise, day-wise/repeat and quick attendance, daily/monthly/yearly, cumulative and percentage reports, SMS alerts to absentees, staff attendance and integrations for biometric, UHF/RFID, barcode and face recognition. [7] [19]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Timetable tools cover student and teacher schedules, teacher-occupancy alerts, subject-limit alerts, proxy/cover settings and AI timetable generation. [7] [20]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Assessment supports CBSE, ICSE, IB and state-board patterns, CCE, combined exams, marks conversion, user-defined mark sheets with 40+ designs, charts and statistics. E-exam supports question banks, term/chapter/practice tests, objective and subjective tests, online delivery and evaluation; bulk question import is a reported workflow. [7] [21] [22]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Report cards and mark sheets are generated from configurable designs, with result dashboards, transcripts and certificate templates. The Holistic Progress Card covers foundational, preparatory, middle and secondary stages, competency-based reporting, cognitive, physical, social-emotional and co-curricular development, teacher observations and parent feedback. The vendor says it aligns with NEP 2020, NIPUN Bharat and CBSE/ICSE/state-board needs; this is a vendor compliance claim, not a government certification. [7] [23]

#### Learning management and homework

Academic tools support daily classwork, homework, lesson plans, syllabus scheduling and completed-lesson updates. LMS and virtual classroom features provide digital assets, discussion, online classes, computerized tests, instant evaluation, reports, document storage and chat. [7] [24]

#### Communication

SMS and email alerts, app push/notice-board communication, circulars, announcements and parent-teacher interaction are supported. WhatsApp Business integration provides verified-school profiles, bulk broadcasts, rich media, encrypted chat, API integration and a chatbot for admissions and common queries. The vendor does not name a separate Paytm or Razorpay connector on the pages reviewed. [2] [25]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Separate role logins/dashboards are documented for parents, students, teachers, management and employees. Students can view assignments, homework, classwork, results, timetables, events, calendars, news, classmates and teachers; parents can access attendance, health, fees, results and other records. [2] [6]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Fees covers multiple categories, deposits, student-specific concessions/additions, multiple receipt books, automatic receipts, payment SMS, account mapping and reports. Online payment supports bank accounts, cards, net banking, wallets and cash, with OTP and a vendor-described PCI-DSS v2.0-certified gateway. The site does not specifically identify UPI, Razorpay or Paytm by name, so those should be confirmed in a commercial demo. Accounting includes ledgers, income/expense tracking, charges, deposits, loans and school tax-planning pages. [7] [26]

#### HR, staff and payroll

HR stores personal, job, statutory and communication data, supports bulk upload, employee IDs, recruitment-to-retirement records and employee searches. Leave includes leave types, grade-wise settings, forms, approvals and reports. Payroll supports configurable pay elements, departmental payroll, PF/tax deductions, payslips and monthly/yearly reports. Staff performance/appraisal is present in the product catalogue. [7] [27]

#### Transport

Transport includes routes, student assignments, fee linkage, bus attendance and GPS vehicle tracking. The vendor also markets AI transport management. [2] [28]

#### Library

Library is a named core/resource module and a portal feature; independent listings describe cataloguing, circulation and inventory. Detailed public field-level documentation was not found. [7] [10] [13]

#### Hostel and boarding

Hostel management is listed as a product/resource module by the vendor and independent listings. The public pages do not expose detailed boarding workflows such as room allocation, mess billing or attendance, so implementation scope should be confirmed. [2] [10]

#### Inventory and assets

Inventory and asset management are named modules, with stock/resource management and inventory reporting. A Capterra review specifically requested an inventory dashboard, indicating that reporting depth may vary by deployment. [7] [9]

#### Health and medical

Health supports check-up records, student health histories, customizable templates, abnormality reporting and immunization charts. [7]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Discipline management is listed in the official sitemap and independent directories; event/activity management includes calendars, enrollment and mobile integration. A detailed public discipline workflow or pastoral/safeguarding specification was not found. [2] [10] [13]

#### Special education and safeguarding

No publicly documented native IEP, 504, special-education case-management or safeguarding workflow was found. Health and role-based access should not be treated as a substitute for those capabilities.

#### Alumni and fundraising

Alumni Management is listed and was introduced as part of the 2024 next-generation solutions; AI alumni engagement is separately marketed. No dedicated fundraising, donor CRM or advancement module was found. [4] [7]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

MIS dashboards provide class capacity, new admissions, left-out students, student strength and attendance status, with graphical/real-time institutional and financial views. The platform advertises 1,800+ reports and customizable searches/templates. [2] [7]

#### AI features

Vidyamitra, launched in 2025, is described as a 24×7 administrative education assistant for instant staff queries. Separate AI pages cover timetable, lesson plans, fees, admissions, attendance, accounting, transport, inventory, alumni, homework checking, exam seating, holiday planning, payroll, assessment, push notifications, photo editing and happiness-index prediction. These are vendor feature claims; public technical model, governance, accuracy or deployment documentation was not found. [4] [6]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Board-pattern support covers CBSE, ICSE, IB and state boards, and the HPC page claims NEP 2020/NIPUN Bharat alignment. The higher-education IQAC module says it can create customizable reports aligned with NAAC and other accreditation requirements and its FAQ mentions NAAC/NBA. I found no public evidence of UDISE+, APAAR ID, NIRF or AISHE integrations/exports. GST invoicing is not specifically documented, although school tax planning and accounting features exist. [7] [23] [29]

#### Mobile apps

Native distribution is evidenced by the Google Play **Vidyalaya Student App** and Apple **Vidyalaya** listing, plus vendor links for a School App and Management App. Features include attendance, fees, circulars, homework, results, online tests, calendar, live notices, discussions, transport and dashboards. [2] [17] [18]

#### Integrations and APIs

Named integrations include SMS/email, WhatsApp Business, Tally, online payment gateway, biometric/UHF/RFID, barcode, GPS vehicle tracking, online exams, virtual classroom, LMS, mobile app and online portal. The official Tally page documents fee-transaction transfer, one-click voucher creation, fee-head/ledger mapping, data migration and Tally 7.2+ compatibility. No public developer API reference, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink or marketplace certification was found. [13] [25] [30]

#### Security and privacy

Vendor pages claim cloud storage, automated backup, encryption, role-based access and privacy controls; the payment page cites a PCI-DSS v2.0-certified gateway. Sapphire’s corporate page says the company is ISO 27001:2013 certified, but this is a company-level claim and not proof of a current product certification. The Apple listing says the developer reports no data collected, while Google Play’s data-safety panel reports no data shared/collected but also “data not encrypted” and “data cannot be deleted”; buyers should reconcile store disclosures with the contract and DPA. No public SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR, DPDP Act readiness statement, hosting region, breach notice or incident report was found. [1] [17] [18] [31]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Vidyamitra AI assistant:** The vendor says the 2025 assistant answers administrative queries 24×7 and reduces staff workload. [4]
- **NEP/NIPUN holistic reporting:** A multidimensional HPC spans academic, cognitive, physical, social-emotional and co-curricular development. [23]
- **India-oriented board configuration:** The assessment module advertises CBSE, ICSE, IB and state-board patterns, CCE and 40+ mark-sheet designs. [7]
- **Tally fee posting:** Fee transactions can be transferred to Tally with mapped ledgers and one-click vouchers. [30]
- **WhatsApp chatbot and broadcasts:** WhatsApp Business API features include verified profiles, rich media, bulk messages and admission-response automation. [25]
- **Multi-modal attendance and safety:** Biometric, UHF/RFID, barcode, face-recognition and GPS vehicle tracking are offered as integrations. [19] [28]
- **Higher-education IQAC:** The IQAC module targets NAAC/NBA-style quality documentation, dashboards and accreditation reporting. [29]

### Pricing Details

Vidyalaya has no public vendor price sheet or named tier structure. Its official FAQ says Indian school ERP pricing generally ranges from **₹5 to ₹50 per student per month**, depending on modules and support; this is a market range, not a binding Vidyalaya quote. [6]

Third-party references are inconsistent and should not be treated as like-for-like plans. Capterra lists **₹1,000 flat rate per year** for Vidyalaya School Software, while Software Advice repeats ₹1,000/year; a separate Capterra record named **VidyalayaERP** lists Basic ₹7,500/year, Premium ₹13,500/year and Professional custom quote, which may be a different listing/product record. No setup, implementation or USD price was publicly stated. [9] [16] [32]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

The strongest public interoperability evidence is practical rather than standards-based: SMS/email, WhatsApp, Tally, online payments, biometric/UHF/RFID, barcode, vehicle tracking, online exam, virtual classroom, LMS and mobile/portal integration. Tally 7.2+ support and mapped fee-ledger posting are specifically documented. Google Workspace/Office 365 alignment is mentioned on the about page, but connector scope is not specified. No public OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink certification, open API documentation, SSO specification or app marketplace was found. [6] [13] [30]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Sapphire states that it is ISO 27001:2013 certified; Vidyalaya separately claims encrypted cloud storage, automated backup and role-based access. The payment page claims a PCI-DSS v2.0-certified gateway. There is no publicly accessible product security whitepaper, SOC 2 report, ISO certificate scope, penetration-test summary, data-residency statement, DPDP Act readiness assessment, GDPR/FERPA/COPPA statement or breach/incident disclosure in the sources reviewed. Store privacy disclosures are limited and should be validated contractually, especially for minors’ data, retention, deletion and subprocessors. [1] [17] [18] [31]

### Strengths

- Broad native ERP coverage for Indian schools, with configurable board assessment, fee, attendance, HR and resource modules. [7]
- Strong practical India fit through Tally, SMS, WhatsApp, biometric and online-payment integrations. [13] [25] [30]
- 2002 product lineage and a credible migration path from Windows to web/cloud delivery. [4] [5]
- NEP/HPC and higher-education IQAC positioning broaden the product beyond a basic SIS. [23] [29]
- Independent reviews consistently praise ease of use, fee management, dashboards and support, although ratings are concentrated in older reviews. [8] [9] [10] [11] [12]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is not transparent: the vendor provides only a broad ₹5–₹50/student/month FAQ range, while directories show conflicting flat-rate figures and quote-based sales. [6] [9] [16] [32]
- Public adoption figures vary materially by page and year, and no independent institution/student audit was found. [2] [4] [6]
- Reviewers mention occasional server maintenance, lag, unknown errors, slow report opening, limited mobile-library functionality, Excel-heavy question entry, incomplete report/dashboard customization and occasional support delays. [8] [9] [10] [11] [12]
- An Apple reviewer reported crashes soon after opening and another reported the gallery not working; the App Store score was only 3.1/5 from 21 ratings when viewed. [18]
- There is no public evidence for UDISE+, APAAR, a developer API, 1EdTech/Ed-Fi standards, separate specialist-education workflows, or DPDP readiness. This limits verifiable interoperability and compliance confidence.

### Key Milestones

- **2002:** Sapphire Software Solutions established; first Windows-based Vidyalaya version/pilot began in ten Banaskantha schools. [1] [4] [5]
- **2000s:** First major Banaskantha installation; Gujarat government appreciation and initial SMS integration are recorded by the vendor. [4]
- **2010s:** Web-based rollout outside Gujarat, international Africa/Nigeria and Qatar channel relationships, e-exam, GPS tracking and mobile app milestones. [4]
- **2019:** Vendor records “Most Innovative School Management ERP” and Best Digital Transformation in Education recognitions. [4]
- **2020:** Virtual Classroom/Virtual School capability was introduced during the pandemic; a SoftwareSuggest interview says integration for schools was completed in 15 days. [4] [10]
- **2022:** History page records 1,700+ institutions, 40+ modules and 10+ integrations. [4]
- **2023:** Admission CRM launched. [4]
- **2024:** LMS, Alumni Management and WhatsApp Business Integration introduced as next-generation solutions. [4]
- **2025:** Vidyamitra AI-powered education assistant launched. [4]
- **2026:** Current vendor pages claim 2,000+ clients, 1.8M students and 96% retention; G2 page updated 17 November 2026 and Capterra page 19 October 2026 provide current review snapshots. [2] [8] [9]
