### Overview

MyClassboard (MCB) is an India-focused school ERP and LMS suite that combines student information, academics, admissions CRM, finance, HR/payroll and parent communication. Its current product catalogue is organized around ERP, LMS, Admissions, Finance, HR, Connect and the separate VED AI product, with safety/security and curriculum-specific solutions layered on top. [1] [3]

The company’s official history places establishment in 2008, first client in 2009 and major mobile milestones in 2013–2015. YourStory describes the business as founded in Hyderabad in 2010, names Ajay Sakhamuri as founder, and reports a 2021 pre-Series A round of ₹4.5 crore from ICICI Bank. No acquisition of MCB by another company was found; current third-party company profiles describe it as active, private and unlisted. [2] [25] [26]

MCB matters in the Indian market because it connects operational ERP with board-specific gradebooks, NEP-style holistic progress cards, local payment gateways, Tally, WhatsApp and Indian school safety hardware. Current scale claims have moved from the 2020 independent report of 2,500 schools and 1.5M students to the official 2026 claim of 3,200+ schools and 2.1M+ students; the figures are not directly comparable because they are different dates and sources. [1] [25]
### Platform Classification Explained

The official privacy policy describes MCB as a web-based and mobile application service, and the company markets cloud access from anywhere. Its public materials support browser access and SaaS delivery, but do not identify a cloud provider, region-specific tenancy architecture, customer-controlled hosting, or an on-premise edition. [15] [17]

The native mobile portfolio is role-oriented: MCB PARENT APP for parents, MCB SMART SCHOOL/SMART MCB for teachers and classroom updates, Smart MCB App for Admins, and MCB ADMISSIONS PLUS/Pre-Admission Mobile App for admissions. The official mobile page explicitly lists Parent Apps, Smart MCB App for Admins and Pre-Admission Mobile App; both major parent and teacher apps have Android listings, while the parent and Smart MCB apps have iOS listings. [14] [18] [19] [20] [21]

No Windows/macOS desktop client, packaged installer or verified on-premise option was found; admin and pre-admission apps are confirmed by the official catalogue, not independently reviewed store pages. [14] [22]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

Admissions Plus CRM covers lead capture, lead staging, lead nurturing, follow-up, click-to-call, IVRS, WhatsApp engagement, campaign management and chatbot-oriented admission journeys. The Pre-Admission Mobile App supports data collection, document uploads and application management. LeadSquared and Meritto are listed as admissions integrations. [3] [7]

#### Student information and records

The SIS stores student, parent/family and staff-linked information, supports filters, branch transfers, promotion/demotion, student-account controls, RTE and special-needs requests, parent information, portfolios and document attachments. It produces transfer, bonafide, no-due and income-tax certificates from templates. [29] [4]

#### Attendance

Attendance is available in the SIS and can be linked to parent communication. MCB advertises biometric and RFID integrations for attendance accuracy and security, with daily attendance conveyed to parents. [29] [30]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Timetable management is listed by SoftwareSuggest and represented in parent-app functionality, although public official detail is limited. [20] [24]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

The LMS includes assessments, objective exams, assignments, Bloom’s Taxonomy tagging, online exams, online classes, course management and teaching plans. Curriculum-specific gradebooks are listed for CBSE/state boards, ICSE, IB, IGCSE, Cambridge, Montessori and higher education. Examcell creates curriculum-aligned question papers using AI plus manual question-bank selection, configurable sections and marks, difficulty balancing, exam scheduling, individualized papers, PDF output and web-based tests. [5] [9]

#### Report cards and transcripts

MCB supports standard report cards and a Holistic Report Card with foundational, preparatory, middle and secondary stages. Higher education adds semester/evaluation report cards, transcripts and course-attainment reports. [10] [13]

#### Learning management and homework

The LMS provides course management, teaching plans, content management, assignments, online classes, remote-learning connections, online exams and curriculum gradebooks; the parent app exposes assignments, events, announcements and progress report cards. [5] [18] [25]

#### Communication

Connect includes SMS, email, push notifications, school diary, announcements, Student Wall, school calendar, voice calls, click-to-call, WhatsApp and photo/video gallery functions. MCB also advertises multilingual translation through VED AI, including Telugu, Hindi, Tamil and Kannada; this is not the same as a fully localized administrative UI. [8] [11]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

The SIS describes separate student and parent login profiles, Google-account login, parent information and PTM collaboration. Public app evidence confirms parent and teacher mobile experiences; MCB positions the web ERP, parent app and Smart School teacher app as connected surfaces. [29] [18] [19]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Finance includes fee management, budgeting/reporting, connected banking, post-dated-cheque management, expense management, student loans, school store, cashless canteen and school services. The payment gateway page lists PayU, CCAvenue, Airpay, Rakbank, Ingenico and Razorpay; it does not explicitly name UPI or Paytm. Tally integration synchronizes fee data, receivables, collections and collection cancellations. GST-specific invoice generation was not publicly verified. [6] [11] [12]

#### HR, staff and payroll

HR includes core employee records and documentation, staff assessment, Staff Wall, praises and feedback, HR Plus payroll and compliance. Public pages do not publish detailed Indian payroll statutory tables or a clear PF, ESI, TDS and professional-tax rule list. [7]

#### Transport

Transport includes transportation management and VTS real-time GPS vehicle tracking, marketed as a parent-facing safety feature. [4] [14] [25]

#### Library

Library management is a named ERP module for cataloguing and school-resource access; independent listings also classify it as supported. [4] [22] [24]

#### Hostel and boarding

Hostel Management is a named ERP module for hostel administration and communication; detailed room, mess, attendance and warden workflows are not public. [4]

#### Inventory and assets

Inventory provides school-resource management; the catalogue also includes school store, merchandise transactions, Dynamic Forms and digital documents. Detailed asset depreciation and purchase-order functions are not public. [3] [4] [6]

#### Health and medical

Infirmary is a named safety/security solution for medical records and services; Visitor Management, RFID and vehicle tracking are also campus-safety controls. Immunization, medication and clinical interoperability were not verified. [14] [30]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

The SIS can record disciplinary infractions, alert parents, maintain student portfolios and archive behavior records for pattern analysis; it also supports reporting forms, inquiry procedures and anti-bullying investigations. [29]

#### Special education and safeguarding

MCB references special-needs requests, RTE, visitor management, RFID, biometrics, infirmary and anti-bullying investigations. A dedicated IEP/SEND module was not verified. [29] [30]

#### Alumni and fundraising

Alumni Management supports continuing contact, opinions, ideas, contacts and engagement with former students. A distinct fundraising, donor CRM or advancement module was not found. [4] [29]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

MCB advertises live dashboards, student-performance insights, fee/admissions reporting and VED AI data-driven/predictive insights. Exact KPI and data-warehouse details are not public. [8] [17] [27]

#### AI features

VED AI provides grammar correction, lesson-plan/content suggestions, YouTube summarization, text simplification, tone changes, multilingual translation and extraction from PDFs, images and spreadsheets. Examcell adds AI-generated questions, curriculum alignment and difficulty balancing; model providers and evaluation controls are not disclosed. [8] [9]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

MCB advertises CBSE/state/ICSE/IB/IGCSE/Cambridge gradebooks, NEP 2020-style Holistic Progress Cards, SQAA workflows, and higher-education NBA/NAAC reporting with outcome-based education, CO–PO/PSO mapping and attainment calculations. No public official evidence was found for UDISE+, APAAR ID, NIRF or AISHE exports. [5] [10] [13] The product also does not publicly confirm GST invoice compliance beyond payment/accounting integrations.

#### Mobile apps

The named mobile products are MCB PARENT APP, MCB SMART SCHOOL/SMART MCB, Smart MCB App for Admins and MCB ADMISSIONS PLUS/Pre-Admission Mobile App. Parent Android adoption is 1M+ downloads, but iOS and teacher-app ratings are materially lower than directory-review scores. [14] [18] [19] [20] [21]

#### Integrations and APIs

The public integration catalogue names Tally, payment gateways, Zoom, Google Meet, LeadSquared, Meritto, biometrics and RFID. The company also claims APIs and API integration for forms and applications. No public developer portal, API reference, marketplace, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever or ClassLink certification was verified. [1] [3] [12] [17] [27]

#### Security and privacy

The SIS lists data masking, IP allow/deny lists, MAC-enabled security, role-based access control and two-factor authentication. The privacy policy says MCB acts as processor for customer data, supports access/correction/erasure requests, uses HTTPS and reasonable security measures, may transfer data cross-border, and does not store card data on its servers. [15] The company reports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification for educational SaaS development, and a linked certificate records ISO/IEC 27701:2025, issued 9 November 2026 and expiring 8 November 2029. [16] [17] No public SOC 2, FERPA or COPPA attestation, India-specific DPDP Act statement, hosting-region commitment or publicly reported breach was found.

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **VED AI:** A school-oriented assistant suite combines writing support, multilingual translation, document extraction and teaching-content assistance rather than limiting AI to chat.
- **Examcell:** AI-generated, curriculum-aligned question papers can be mixed with a manually controlled question bank, custom sections, schedules and individualized papers. [9]
- **NEP Holistic Progress Card:** Stage-specific foundational, preparatory, middle and secondary assessment structures go beyond a conventional marksheet. [10]
- **Higher-ed OBE reporting:** The college module claims built-in CO–PO/PSO mapping, attainment calculation, backlog/supplementary handling and audit-ready NBA/NAAC reports. [13]
- **India-native communications:** SMS, WhatsApp, voice, click-to-call, diary and push channels are combined in one Connect suite. [11]
- **Franchise and multi-branch control:** Franchise Management provides centralized oversight for education chains. [4] [27]
- **Hardware-linked safety:** VTS, RFID, biometrics, visitor management and infirmary functions connect software workflows to campus operations. [14] [30]
- **Tally and local payments:** Fee receivables, collections and cancellations can be exchanged with Tally, alongside Indian payment gateways including Razorpay. [11] [12]

### Pricing Details

MCB has no public official rate card or pricing page; the official buying path is a demo and sales consultation. [1] [31] The company should therefore be treated as quote-based, with price determined by modules, student count, campuses, implementation and integrations. No official setup, migration, training, support or per-student tariff was found.

Third-party figures are inconsistent and should not be used as a budget without a written quote. YourStory reported ₹300–₹500 per student annually in 2021. [25] Capterra and Software Advice display a $3,000 per-user-per-month “Basic” card, not corroborated by an official MCB price sheet; treat it as unvalidated directory metadata. [22] [23] The supplied guide’s ₹4,720 entry point and ₹25,000–₹4,00,000 annual TCO bands were not corroborated. No official USD price is listed.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Verified named integrations are Tally, Razorpay and other payment gateways, Zoom, Google Meet, LeadSquared, Meritto, biometrics and RFID. MCB claims APIs and forms/application integration, and PitchBook also describes an API. [3] [11] [12] [27] There is no public evidence of OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF certification; no Clever/ClassLink, Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 connector was documented in the current opened product pages, although YourStory reported Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams connections during the pandemic. [25] MCB therefore has useful Indian operational integrations but not a publicly evidenced standards-led interoperability ecosystem.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

MCB’s public privacy policy identifies the school/customer as controller and MCB as processor, covers student, parent, staff, visitor, location, device, photo/video and document data, and permits cross-border transfers subject to stated safeguards. It describes HTTPS, restricted access, monitoring and retention/deletion controls. [15] Its data-privacy commitment says it does not sell customer data and requires TLS 1.2/1.3 for public-network connections. [16]

The official site reports ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and a linked certificate records ISO/IEC 27701:2025 issued 9 November 2026 through 8 November 2029. [17] The available material does not establish SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR or PCI-DSS certification, a named hosting region or DPDP Act readiness beyond general privacy language. No public incident disclosure was found.

### Strengths

- Broad all-in-one coverage for Indian schools: SIS, LMS, admissions, finance, HR/payroll, communications and safety hardware.
- Strong local fit through board-specific gradebooks, NEP-style holistic reporting, WhatsApp/SMS, Tally, Razorpay and Indian school workflows. [5] [10] [11] [12]
- Meaningful scale evidence: 3,200+ schools and 2.1M+ students claimed by the official site as viewed 24 November 2026. [1]
- Higher-education capability is more substantial than a basic K–12 ERP because it includes OBE, CO–PO/PSO mapping, backlogs and NBA/NAAC reporting. [13]
- AI is visible in production-oriented workflows, especially VED AI and Examcell, rather than only in a roadmap. [8] [9]
- Older directory reviews praise the single-platform breadth, ease of use and support; SoftwareSuggest reviewers specifically praised admissions, finance and HR/payroll. [22] [23] [24]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Public pricing is opaque and contradictory: buyers must request a quote, while directory cards show an implausible $3,000 per user per month against a historical Indian per-student range. [22] [23] [25]
- Mobile UX is the clearest weakness. Google Play reviewers report lag, missing or empty notifications, stale calendars and sibling-account problems; teacher-app reviews mention constant hanging and missing class/profile data. [18] [19]
- iOS reviews report timetable loading failures, transport tracking that stays unavailable, awkward attachment handling, app crashes and unread-notification bugs. [20]
- Independent web reviews are positive but extremely thin: Capterra, Software Advice and SoftwareSuggest each expose only two reviews or similarly small samples, so their 4.5–5.0 scores are not robust evidence of broad satisfaction. [22] [23] [24]
- Public documentation is shallow for API schemas, hosting architecture, implementation, statutory payroll, data residency and government identifiers. UDISE+, APAAR, GST, NIRF and AISHE support should be treated as unverified until shown in a live product or contract; no verified OneRoster/LTI/Ed-Fi/SIF certification or marketplace was found.

### Key Milestones

- **2008:** Official journey marks the establishment of MyClassboard Educational Solutions; PitchBook also reports 2008 as the year founded. [2] [27]
- **2009:** Official history records the first client; the private limited company was incorporated on 15 December 2009. [2] [26]
- **2010:** YourStory describes MCB as launched in Hyderabad and says K-12 Techno was its first onboarded school. [25]
- **2011:** Official history records 200+ schools and 1 lakh+ students. [2]
- **2013–2014:** Android parent app launched in 2013 and iOS parent app in 2014. [2]
- **2015:** Smart School mobile app and enhanced gradebook were introduced. [2]
- **2016:** Official history records a new web version plus APIs and third-party integrations. [2]
- **2017:** School Store launched in collaboration with Amazon, according to YourStory. [25]
- **2018–2019:** Official history records visitor-management/discipline modules and growth to 10 lakh students in 2018 and 14 lakh in 2019. [2]
- **2020:** Online classes and online exams were introduced; YourStory reported 2,500 schools and 1.5M students around this period. [2] [25]
- **2021:** Advanced course-management/LMS modules launched; YourStory reported a ₹4.5 crore pre-Series A round from ICICI Bank. [2] [25]
- **2022:** Official history records 20 lakh+ students, student loans and eNACH. [2]
- **2023:** Cambridge, IB and preschool gradebooks and SQAA were introduced. [2]
- **2024–2026:** The current catalogue adds VED AI, Examcell, NEP holistic reporting and higher-ed OBE/NBA/NAAC workflows; the homepage claims 3,200+ schools and 2.1M+ students by 24 November 2026. [1] [2] [8] [9] [13]
- **9 November 2026:** Officially linked certificate records ISO/IEC 27701:2025 for educational SaaS development, expiring 8 November 2029. [17]

Guide discrepancies: The supplied guide says 2009, which is correct for legal incorporation but omits the official 2008 establishment milestone and the independent 2010 launch description. Its 3,200+ schools claim is current and corroborated; its 500+ cities claim is on the official homepage, but its 2.1M+ student figure is also needed for current scale. Its six-suite feature summary is directionally correct, but VED AI is separately presented and several guide details (UPI/Paytm, GST, UDISE+/APAAR, NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE, and broad named integrations) were not all publicly verified: Razorpay, Tally, Zoom, Google Meet, LeadSquared, Meritto, biometrics and RFID were verified, while UPI, Paytm, GST, UDISE+, APAAR, NIRF and AISHE were not. The guide’s 2026 OpenEduCat price bands were not corroborated; official pricing is quote-only, and the only independently opened historical price was ₹300–₹500 per student annually in a 2021 YourStory report. The guide’s app names are broadly right, but public store names are MCB PARENT APP and MCB SMART SCHOOL/SMART MCB. No acquisition was found; the 2021 ICICI Bank funding report is an additional ownership/funding fact not stated in the guide.

## India #9. Entab CampusCare (Entab Infotech Pvt. Ltd.)

No current on-premises offering or native desktop client is publicly documented. [2] [5] [22] |

### Overview

Entab CampusCare is an India-focused school ERP and student information system. Its current product family is branded CampusCare 10X and Entab One. It combines admissions, student records, attendance, assessments, report cards, fees, accounting, transport, library, HR/payroll, communication, portals, mobile applications, dashboards and school operations. Entab positions the system as a single source of truth for the lifecycle from enquiry and admission to alumni. [3] [4] [7]

The company says it was founded in New Delhi in 2000 and has focused on school technology for more than 25 years. Entab’s account of its history says the software moved from on-premises delivery to online/cloud delivery. Its post-NEP work added experiential-learning and competency-oriented assessment; the experiential-learning vertical launched on 24 September 2022. [2]

On 5 October 2026, Nelnet Business Services announced its acquisition of Entab. Entab continues under its own brand and leadership, with its New Delhi offices and approximately 290 associates retained. The acquisition is the only publicly verified ownership change found in this review; financial terms were not disclosed. [29] [30]

### Platform Classification Explained

**Browser/cloud delivery:** Entab describes CampusCare as completely web-based and cloud-facilitated, with access anywhere through an internet connection. Current product pages state that the SIS is hosted on AWS Cloud, uses SSL/encryption, automatic daily backup and a 99.9% uptime claim. These are vendor statements, not an independently verified SLA or audit report. [5] [15]

**Mobile:** The current native product is CampusCare 10x for Android and iPhone/iPad. Google Play identifies the developer as Entab Infotech Pvt. Ltd.; the listing showed 5L+ downloads and 4.0/5 from 3.79K reviews when checked. Apple lists CampusCare 10x as an iPhone/iPad education app, 3.7/5 from 1.1K ratings. [26] [27]

**Role-specific apps and portals:** Entab One claims dedicated parent, staff, principal and management apps, plus parent/student, staff, principal, management, central and utilisation dashboards. Publicly verified store pages clearly establish the CampusCare 10x app and a legacy CampusCare iOS app; separate public store records for every claimed role-specific app were not found. [7] [28]

**Desktop/on-premise:** No current native Windows/macOS client or current on-premise deployment offer is documented. Entab’s history says it evolved from on-premises software to online software, so “on-premise” should be treated as historical rather than a current product classification. [2]

#### Admissions and enrollment

The enquiry and registration modules capture multi-channel leads, generate enquiry IDs, tag lead sources, support custom forms by class/stream/branch, allocate counsellors, configure pipeline stages, log activities and reminders, track response time/conversion KPIs, and provide role-based counsellor dashboards. Registration adds document capture, admission numbers, onboarding and counselling workflows. [14] [4]

#### Student information and records

The SIS maintains a 360-degree student profile from admission through alumni, with automatic admission-number generation, sibling identification by mobile number, student master search, bulk field updates, bulk photo/data import through Excel, class/section lists, parent contacts, dropout details, academic history, certificates, transfer certificates, ID cards and custom reports. [15] [3]

#### Attendance

CampusCare supports bulk daily attendance, daily or period-wise configuration, student leave requests and approvals, configurable publishing cut-offs, holiday calendars, absence lists, class/student reports, percentage views and Excel/CSV/PDF export. Student attendance can notify parents through SMS and app notifications. Staff attendance can be manual, biometric, RFID or geo-tagged and can feed payroll. [16] [11] [19]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

The platform lists timetable management, timetable substitution, teacher workload and instant substitution alerts. The mobile app supports timetable access and staff/admin workflows; the public material does not expose a standalone constraint solver or detailed master-scheduling specification. [4] [7] [11]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Exam management includes subject-wise, student-wise, optional-subject and multiple-subject mark entry; class permissions; exam and report locking; PDF locking; hall-ticket generation; configurable report-card templates; mark-entry defaulter reports; comment conditions; subject-group totals; question-bank integration; offline/written and digital tests; analytics and Excel import. The assessment model includes competency and rubric-based evaluation. [13] [3]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Report cards are automatically generated by class, exam and student configuration, can be customised or uploaded, archived and viewed through parent/student portals. The system supports CBSE-aligned templates and transfer/certificate generation. Entab specifically documents NEP 2020 and NCF 2023-aligned 360-degree Holistic Progress Cards (HPC), covering academic, social, emotional, creative, sports, values and wellbeing dimensions, self-reflection, multi-source feedback and parent suggestions. No public evidence found for named ICSE or every state-board template. [13] [21] [3]

#### Learning management and homework

Current pages list LMS management, online classes, lesson and academic plans, homework/classwork, projects and assignments, school diary, online PTM, digital teaching resources, assessment and an experiential-learning repository. The Apple description adds AR-based interactive assets, hands-on activities, lab experiments, concept maps, practice worksheets, customisable lesson plans, short notes and competency-based question banks. [4] [27]

#### Communication

Communication includes in-app notifications, SMS, email and WhatsApp. The WhatsApp module offers approved templates, department/form-level toggles, attendance and leave alerts, fee reminders and confirmations, online-class links, circulars, event announcements, approval messages and audience targeting for parents, teachers and staff. Entab does not publicly name the underlying WhatsApp provider. [10] [7]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Role-based access separates management, principals, teachers, staff, students, parents, counsellors and administrators. Parents can view attendance, grades, report cards, homework, diary remarks, circulars, fee history/receipts and live bus location. Students access assignments, study materials, timetable and their portal; teachers enter attendance, marks, lesson plans and assignments; management receives branch and school dashboards. [7] [11]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Fee functions include configurable fee structures, instalments, fee cards, concessions and approvals, defaulter management, fines/penalties, transport and hostel fees, full-and-final settlement, demand bills, receipts, cash/cheque/DD/NEFT and digital modes, reconciliation, carry-forward of dues or excess amounts, payment links through email/WhatsApp/SMS, online status, cheque-bounce records and fee analytics. The finance area includes accounts and bill entry, expenses/claims, audit trails, financial accounting and Tally app integration. The fee page says multiple configurable gateways and RBI-approved gateways are supported, and lists UPI integration in the module catalogue; it does not name Razorpay or Paytm. It explicitly claims GST calculation, summaries and GST-return export. [4] [12]

#### HR, staff and payroll

HR covers departments/designations, hiring, shifts, leave, attendance, biometric integration, IDs, training/orientation, holidays, policy, visitors, exit management, staff profiles and performance management. Payroll supports pay structures, earnings/deductions/arrears, payslips, PF, ESI, TDS, gratuity, Form 16, statutory registers, ECR files, loans/advances, bank-disbursement exports, multi-branch processing, appraisal/training links and attendance/leave integration. [4] [19]

#### Transport

Transport provides route and stop management, driver and vehicle records, live GPS, route playback, speed/stoppage data, route optimisation, route-change requests and approvals, transport billing, parent alerts, driver details, vehicle registration/licence information, RFID/biometric bus attendance, delay/deviation alerts and route-capacity, fuel, maintenance, attendance and driver-activity reports. [17]

#### Library

Library features include catalogue/acquisition, bulk book entry, membership, barcode printing, OPAC search, reservation and reservation approval, overdue notifications, stock verification, magazines, requisitions, circulation, digital resources, fines linked to fee ledgers, multi-library support and PDF/Excel/CSV reports. [18]

#### Hostel and boarding

The module catalogue lists hostel management and hostel fee management, but the current public feature pages provide little operational detail about rooms, beds, wardens, mess, boarding attendance or resident welfare. Treat hostel as a listed capability requiring demonstration rather than a fully evidenced current module. [4] [12]

#### Inventory and assets

Inventory tracks consumables and assets across stores/rooms, stock value, low-stock items, sales, orders, goods received, indents, purchase entries, vendors, quotations, purchase orders, issue/return slips, asset lifecycle, maintenance, depreciation, repair and disposal. It supports bulk import, request/approval workflows, finance linkage, GST-ready purchase documentation and audit-ready reports. CampusMart/tuck-shop or bookstore operations are also listed. [20] [4]

#### Health and medical

An infirmary/healthcare module is listed in the enterprise and operations categories. Entab One calls it Healthcare/Hospital Management, but public pages do not detail clinical records, medication, immunisation, consent or emergency workflows. [4] [7]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

The Anecdote module records structured observations about behaviour, discipline, achievements and interventions. The homepage also lists behaviour management, incident reporting and analytics. This is a useful pastoral/whole-child layer alongside HPC, although the public material does not describe a full safeguarding case-management workflow. [4] [1]

#### Special education and safeguarding

No dedicated special-education, IEP/SEN, child-protection or safeguarding module is publicly documented in the reviewed materials. Role-based access, audit logs, encrypted storage, incident/behaviour records and child-privacy language provide relevant controls but should not be represented as a complete safeguarding product. [1] [9]

#### Alumni and fundraising

Alumni management maintains a structured graduate database, academic history, locations and career milestones. Fundraising, donations, campaigns and advancement accounting are not publicly evidenced. [4] [7]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Entab One claims 500+ MIS reports, real-time admissions/attendance/academic/finance dashboards, multi-branch central dashboards, utilisation dashboards, fee and revenue tracking, performance trends, operational bottleneck detection and audit reports. Report exports commonly include Excel, CSV, PDF and other formats. [7] [4]

#### AI features

Current marketing pages claim an AI analytics dashboard, predictive analytics, early risk/trend detection, AI-assisted school planning, chatbot assistants for website/ERP/parent portal, personalised learning paths, auto-grading, content recommendations, plagiarism checking, behaviour analysis, performance forecasting and AI-generated questions/notes. These are vendor claims; no public technical documentation, model governance, accuracy benchmark or named production AI model was found. [1] [7]

#### Government, board and Indian compliance

CampusCare publicly documents CBSE-aligned report-card/question-bank workflows, NEP 2020/NCF 2023 HPC, 5+3+3+4 mapping, vocational/bagless-day tracking and CPD hours. It documents GST-ready billing, PF/ESI/TDS/gratuity payroll, audit trails and SQAAF quality-control support. I found no public product documentation confirming UDISE+ export, APAAR ID lifecycle support, a complete ICSE/state-board library, NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE reporting, or vernacular-language packs. [3] [4] [12] [19]

#### Mobile apps

CampusCare 10x provides mobile attendance, marks, lesson plans, assignments, online classes, library insights, fees, approvals, transport, visitor approvals, diary remarks and notifications. Parents can view results, homework, fees, circulars and transport. The public stores verify iOS/iPadOS and Android availability; the Apple listing says the app language is English. [11] [26] [27]

#### Integrations and APIs

Documented integrations include AWS hosting, GPS devices, RFID/biometric devices, WhatsApp, SMS, email, UPI/payment gateways, Tally app integration, bank-disbursement exports and a generic geo-fencing/API-integration listing. A public developer API, API reference, marketplace or certified OneRoster/LTI/Ed-Fi/SIF/Clever/ClassLink connector is not documented. [4] [12] [19]

#### Security and privacy

Entab claims encryption in transit and at rest, AES-encrypted records on AWS, role-based access, MFA, audit logs, continuous monitoring, automatic backups, restore, regular updates, SSL and a 99.9% uptime target. Its privacy policy covers student, parent, teacher, usage and IP/device data; it describes access/correction/deletion rights, retention, third-party processors and child protections, and says COPPA applies where relevant. App-store disclosures are inconsistent: Google Play displayed “Data isn’t encrypted,” while Apple displayed “Data Not Collected”; these are store disclosures rather than a third-party security audit. No public SOC 2, ISO 27001, FERPA or GDPR certification was found. Entab is publicly engaging with DPDP Act issues through a Delhi NCR school-leader roundtable scheduled for 18 December 2026, but that is awareness/readiness activity, not proof of DPDP certification or completed compliance. [9] [15] [32] [26] [27]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **NEP-native holistic assessment:** 360-degree HPC, competency/rubric assessment, 5+3+3+4 mapping, vocational/bagless-day tracking and teacher CPD are explicitly positioned as core workflows rather than add-ons. [3] [21]
- **AI and predictive layer:** The current site claims predictive analytics, risk detection, forecasting, chatbots, auto-grading and personalised learning recommendations, although technical validation is not public. [1] [7]
- **No-code-style configurability:** Custom enquiry forms, fields, pipeline stages, report-card templates, message toggles, concessions and role permissions let schools adapt workflows without a published coding requirement. [14] [10]
- **Deep Indian finance/payroll localisation:** GST outputs, UPI/gateway flows, Tally linkage, PF/ESI/TDS/gratuity/Form 16/ECR support address India-specific administration. [12] [19]
- **Whole-campus operating depth:** Live GPS, RFID/biometric attendance, library OPAC/barcodes, inventory lifecycle, visitor management, infirmary and alumni extend beyond a basic SIS. [4] [17] [18] [20]
- **Multi-branch leadership visibility:** Central dashboards, branch permissions and cross-campus reporting target school groups such as the 45,000-student Aditya Birla network case study. [1] [7]

### Pricing Details

Entab’s current Entab One/CampusCare 10X page says **custom pricing based on school size**, with “no hidden costs,” one subscription, 35+ modules, unlimited users, mobile apps, WhatsApp/SMS/email, onboarding, migration, 500+ reports and a 99.9% uptime guarantee. It does not publish an INR per-student-per-year or per-school-per-month price, tier names, implementation fee or USD equivalent. The official price-information page likewise explains price factors rather than publishing a price card. [7] [6]

Third-party directories display stale or contradictory metadata. G2 and Capterra both show a nominal “Basic” price of **₹0.45 flat rate per month**, while Capterra records zero reviews and “contact vendor” in its comparison details. This figure is not corroborated by Entab and should not be treated as a credible buying price. GoodFirms says annual subscription, contact-vendor pricing and a 30-day free trial; its page does not state a rupee amount. An older 2014 company announcement described a pay-as-you-go monthly fee based on student/user counts with no upfront licensing fee or extra charges, but no current price was stated. [22] [23] [24] [31]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

The practical integration story is India-specific: Tally app integration; UPI and configurable/RBI-approved payment gateways; WhatsApp, SMS and email; GPS; RFID/biometrics; bank-disbursement exports; AWS hosting; and a generic API/geofencing feature listing. These are meaningful operational integrations for Indian schools. However, no public evidence was found for OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, a documented public API, SSO protocol, or an integration marketplace. The “Microsoft Gold Partner” language is a vendor claim and does not by itself establish Microsoft 365 interoperability. [4] [12] [19]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

CampusCare’s public security posture includes vendor-claimed AWS hosting, encryption, daily backups, role-based permissions, MFA, audit logs, monitoring and restore. The privacy policy describes educational-purpose processing, third-party processors, retention, access/correction/deletion requests and child safeguards, including a statement that student information is not used for advertising or profiling. [9] [15]

There is no public SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certificate, FERPA/COPPA audit report, GDPR certification, penetration-test summary or India data-residency statement. COPPA is mentioned in the privacy policy where applicable; the policy does not specifically name the DPDP Act. The December 2026 DPDP roundtable signals active engagement with consent, children’s data, vendor access, incident readiness and responsible AI, but should be scored as readiness activity rather than demonstrated compliance. [9] [32]

The reviewed sources disclosed no public security incident. App-store self-reports need caution: Google Play showed “Data isn’t encrypted,” whereas Apple showed “Data Not Collected,” and both conflict with Entab’s web privacy/security claims. Schools should request a current DPA, subprocessor list, hosting region, security assessment and incident-response commitments during procurement. [26] [27]

### Strengths

- Broad, integrated Indian-school scope spanning academics, administration, finance, transport, HR, communication and operations. [4] [7]
- Strong localisation for CBSE/NEP workflows, HPC, Indian payroll and GST-oriented finance. [3] [12] [19]
- Cloud/web access plus Android/iOS apps, parent engagement, GPS and WhatsApp/SMS communication. [5] [10] [11]
- Long operating history, New Delhi support footprint and acquisition by Nelnet, which adds international education-technology scale. [2] [29]
- Independent reviews, while few, commonly praise ease of use, comprehensive coverage, online fees, attendance, homework, timetables and responsive support. [23] [24] [25]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Public pricing is quote-only and directory pricing is unreliable; smaller schools may face higher cost or implementation complexity. [6] [7] [22] [23]
- G2’s sole reviewer cites a learning curve, limited customisation, variable support responsiveness and potentially high cost/implementation time for smaller schools. [23]
- Google Play reviews report slowness, crashes, results/assignment loading problems, a weak chatbot and limited support; Apple reviews similarly mention lag, login friction, bugs and inaccessible assignments. These are user reports, not independently measured performance results. [26] [27]
- Review coverage is thin and inconsistent: Capterra has no reviews, G2 has one, GoodFirms has one and SoftwareSuggest has eight, so aggregate satisfaction is not statistically robust. [22] [23] [24] [25]
- Public evidence is weak for UDISE+, APAAR, named Razorpay/Paytm connectors, vernacular languages, higher-education NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE reporting, public APIs, open standards and audited certifications. [4] [12]
- The Google Play “Data isn’t encrypted” disclosure conflicts with Entab’s web claims of encryption, creating a procurement diligence issue. [26] [9]

### Key Milestones

- **2000:** Entab Infotech founded in New Delhi; the company says it began addressing manual school administration and ERP needs. [2] [29]
- **2014:** Entab published a CampusCare “pay as you go” announcement describing a monthly student/user-based plan and a then-claimed 800+ institutions across 26 Indian states and seven countries. [31]
- **2015:** AppBrain records the legacy CampusCare iOS app as available on the App Store from October 2015. [28]
- **2020:** Entab says it began dedicated research into NEP 2020 reforms, competency assessment and experiential learning after the draft policy. [2]
- **2022:** Entab’s experiential-learning vertical launched at the All India Experiential Learning Summit on 24 September 2022. [2]
- **2024:** Freshdesk release notes show CampusCare 10X releases across administration, academics, fees, accounting, transport, payroll, attendance and student information in September–December 2024. [8]
- **2025:** Entab said it turned 25, implying the 2000 founding date, and current pages promoted CampusCare 10X/Entab One. [2] [7]
- **1 October 2026:** Entab’s homepage says it became part of Nelnet Business Services. [1]
- **5 October 2026:** Nelnet formally announced the acquisition; financial terms were undisclosed, founders and roughly 290 associates remained, and the announcement reported 1,000+ schools and 1.5M+ students in 28 states. [29] [30]
- **18 December 2026 (scheduled):** Entab announced a Delhi NCR roundtable on student privacy and India’s DPDP Act; this is a future event as of the 24 November 2026 review date. [32]

### Overview

LEAD School is an integrated school operating and learning system from Mumbai-based Leadership Boulevard Pvt. Ltd. It combines curriculum, pedagogy, teacher training, classroom hardware, student/parent learning, and an academic ERP instead of selling only a back-office SIS. The current product identity is **LEAD Nucleus**, described by LEAD as its Academic ERP and as a hybrid-mode platform. The public workflow covers school-owner visibility, teacher delivery, parent/student progress, admissions, attendance, assessments, homework, reports, fees, and communication [5] [6].

LEAD was founded by Sumeet Mehta and Smita Deorah in 2012. Its first school was Shantiniketan English School, and the founders expanded from operating schools to a partner-school model: teacher-app work began in 2016, the integrated system was offered to partner schools by 2017, and the partnership model scaled nationally. The company raised $28M Series C in 2020, $30M Series D in 2021, and $100M Series E in January 2022 at a $1.1B valuation. In 2023 it completed the acquisition of Pearson India’s K-12 learning business, adding curriculum/content capability [3] [4] [14] [15].

As of November 2026, independent company data still classifies LEAD as a private company. Inc42 reports Leadership Boulevard Private Limited as founded in 2012, with FY25 revenue above ₹367.4 crore and last funding listed as debt financing in 2023; SetterVC records the last disclosed equity round as January 2022 and approximately $166.5M total disclosed funding, subject to its own data caveats [16] [17]. These are business-status indicators, not proof of a public offering or of a current valuation above the 2022 funding mark.

### Platform Classification Explained

**Browser/cloud delivery.** Nucleus is accessed at https://nucleus.leadschool.in/ through a mobile-number/OTP login. LEAD describes it as a cloud-based, remote-access ERP with role-based access and encrypted storage. The teacher service is also browser-accessible at https://teacherapp.leadschool.in/ [5] [7]. No public evidence identifies AWS, Azure, GCP, a data-residency region, a desktop executable, or a self-hosted/on-premise deployment.

**Hybrid academic operation.** “Hybrid” means LEAD’s school workflow can toggle online, offline, or both modes, not that customers receive an on-premise ERP. The teacher app’s Play listing says lesson plans, audiovisual content, assessments, and practice tests can be bundled on an SD card with the teacher tablet for low-connectivity/offline classroom use. Smart TVs, teacher tablets, activity kits, printed books, and digital content are part of the integrated package [5] [12].

**Native mobile apps.** The LEAD Group Student App is listed on both Google Play and Apple’s App Store for iPhone/iPad. It supports parent/student access to unit progress, attendance, assessment scores, homework, practice, and videos. LEAD Teacher App is an Android app tied to a compatible Lenovo teacher tablet, while the School Owner app is an Android app for school metrics, student/parent/teacher reports, announcements, and LEAD support [10] [11] [12] [13]. A separately verified iOS owner or teacher app was not found.

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

LEAD publicly describes online admission forms, collection of student information and admission fees, a school listing page, enquiry generation, a personalised LEAD CRM, follow-up, walk-in conversion, and paper reduction. The ENROL/admissions offering is broader than a simple Nucleus form and is marketed as an admissions and school-visibility service [18].

#### Student information and records

Nucleus maintains a central student and teacher database, class-wise student lists, academic records, attendance, grades, progress data, and parent/teacher-linked information. The ERP’s privacy policy explicitly identifies student and teacher databases, notices to parents, online fee collection, reports, and analytics as platform uses [19].

#### Attendance

Teachers record attendance and parents can view daily attendance. School owners receive attendance and teacher-performance tracking, while the student app exposes attendance history. Public evidence does not establish biometric, RFID, facial-recognition, or gate-attendance support.

#### Timetable and master scheduling

LEAD describes daily timetable scheduling, school-mode configuration, subject/topic additions, and teacher allocation. The current public pages do not document a district-style constraint solver, room scheduling, substitute/cover module, or multi-campus master-scheduling engine [5] [6].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Teachers can access assessments, prior submissions, grades, practice tests, quizzes, and remedial analysis. The current homepage markets **Jasper**, an AI Assessment Builder that lets teachers create assessments by topic and rigour. LEAD’s NEP/NCF material emphasizes competency-based, formative, practical, and 360-degree assessment; public evidence does not show a separate board-exam administration suite [1] [20] [21].

#### Report cards and transcripts

The Academic ERP and Student App generate progress/performance reports, and LEAD says its NCF-aligned system generates holistic report cards covering academic performance, skills, and overall growth. A conventional official-transcript module, transcript exchange, GPA engine, or alumni transcript service is not publicly documented [20].

#### Learning management and homework

The Student App provides live and recorded classes, videos, homework and assignments, practice tests, gamified quizzes, downloadable worksheets, and “Ask Doubts.” Teachers receive lesson plans, audiovisual materials, worksheets, syllabus plans, and assessments. School@Home connects home learning with classroom learning [5] [10] [12].

#### Communication

The verified channels are in-app alerts, school/teacher updates, notices, announcements, parent-teacher interaction, and app-based doubt resolution. The privacy and master-terms documents allow electronic communications and third-party payment processors. A dedicated named WhatsApp connector, SMS gateway, bulk-email engine, or pricing for messages is not publicly documented; therefore the guide’s implied SMS/Email/App bundle is only partly confirmed [19] [22].

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

The Student App serves parents and students; the Teacher App and teacher web login serve classroom staff; Nucleus serves school owners, principals, and academic coordinators; and the Owner App provides school-level metrics and contacts. Features vary by the school’s selected books/offering, so every partner may not see the same app modules [10] [13] [19].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

LEAD confirms fees management, online collection, payment records, collection from parents on behalf of a customer, and use of third-party payment processors/gateways. No current official page names Razorpay, Paytm, UPI, GST invoicing, Tally, QuickBooks, general ledger, reconciliation, payroll accounting, or statutory accounting reports. Treat those as unverified rather than native capabilities [6] [22].

#### HR and staff

Staff-management data, teacher attendance/performance tracking, teacher onboarding, teacher training, LEAD Academy courses, certification, workshops, and support are evidenced. Payroll, leave approval, recruitment, appraisal workflows, and employee self-service are not publicly documented as Nucleus modules [1] [7].

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

School owners can view key metrics and drill into student, parent, and teacher reports. Nucleus produces progress reports, trackers, class analysis, and remedial analysis; LEAD positions these data-driven insights as part of academic planning and learning-outcome monitoring [5] [13].

#### AI features

Jasper is a production-facing AI Assessment Builder for customized assessment creation, and LEAD now describes its broader learning solutions as AI-based. Public sources do not substantiate a general-purpose conversational assistant, predictive early-warning model, natural-language BI, or no-code workflow builder.

#### Government reporting and compliance

LEAD publicly aligns curriculum and assessment with NEP 2020 and NCF 2023, describes 5+3+3+4, competency-based and holistic assessment, and says its systems adapt to CBSE, ICSE, and JEE tracks [2] [21]. No public evidence was found for UDISE+ submission, APAAR ID, state-census exports, CBSE SARAS integration, NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE reporting, or higher-education administration.

#### Mobile apps, integrations and APIs

Verified integrations are the Google for Education ecosystem claim, Google authentication/YouTube connection in Nucleus privacy documentation, app-store distribution, and generic third-party payment processing [1] [19]. SaaSworthy records API support as “NA,” and no public API reference, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever/ClassLink, Microsoft 365, or marketplace directory was found [8].

#### Modules not publicly substantiated

The guide lists library, transport, inventory, hostel, health, behavior, special education, alumni, and fundraising. The current official LEAD pages and legal documents reviewed do not provide enough primary evidence to count these as native Nucleus modules. There is also no public evidence of a dedicated cafeteria, clinic, boarding, asset-depreciation, safeguarding, or fundraising module.

#### Security and privacy

Nucleus uses OTP login and states role-based access, encrypted storage, consent, data-principal access/correction/erasure/withdrawal rights, deletion/anonymisation practices, processor agreements, breach notification obligations, and a grievance officer. The Nucleus privacy policy expressly references India’s DPDP Act 2023 and was last updated June 2, 2026. No SOC 2, ISO 27001, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR certification, hosting region, penetration-test report, or public incident disclosure was found [19].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Integrated system rather than ERP-only:** Curriculum, printed books, classroom hardware, teacher development, apps, assessments, and Nucleus are sold as one school transformation proposition [1] [6].
- **Hybrid-mode continuity:** Online, offline, and combined school modes are supported, including offline teacher-tablet content for low-connectivity classrooms [5] [12].
- **Jasper AI Assessment Builder:** Teachers can customize assessment topic and rigour, with remedial analysis positioned alongside the assessment workflow [1] [12].
- **NEP/NCF-oriented holistic reporting:** LEAD connects academic results with skill development and overall growth rather than only marks [20] [21].
- **Affordable-private-school specialization:** The system targets schools serving moderate-fee families in smaller towns and attempts to lower non-learning operating costs [10].
- **Owner visibility:** School-owner dashboards and a dedicated owner app expose school, parent, student, and teacher metrics remotely [6] [13].

### Pricing Details

LEAD publishes no rate card, per-student INR price, USD price, tier names, setup fee, implementation fee, or free-trial terms for Nucleus or the bundled LEAD Learning System. Official pages use “Enquire Now,” “Book a demo,” or partner onboarding rather than self-serve checkout. The master terms confirm that each customer agreement sets the invoice value for books, onboarding, platform licensing, ancillary products/services, and taxes; the invoice is generally non-refundable [22].

SaaSworthy independently records “custom plan,” “quotation based,” and no free trial, with its pricing information last updated August 29, 2024; it does not supply a reliable INR or USD range [8]. Any guide or directory estimate should therefore be treated as unverified. Pricing is best described as a negotiated annual school/partner agreement, likely bundling software with curriculum, books, training, apps, and hardware rather than a standalone ERP subscription.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

The public evidence supports Google for Education compatibility and Google authentication/YouTube connection. The master terms permit third-party payment processors/gateways, but name no gateway. No verified public API, developer portal, integration marketplace, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Microsoft 365, Tally, GST, UPI, Razorpay, or Paytm integration was found. Interoperability is therefore basic and partner-agreement dependent, not an open standards-led ecosystem [1] [8] [19] [22].

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The June 2, 2026 Nucleus policy says Leadership Boulevard processes data for school customers, collects student/teacher records and location when permitted, requires verifiable parental/guardian consent for minors, provides access/correction/erasure/withdrawal/grievance/nomination rights, uses data-processing agreements, retains data only as necessary, and will notify the Data Protection Board and affected people for qualifying breaches. It expressly claims compliance with the DPDP Act 2023 and rules [19].

LEAD’s general website policy, last reviewed January 19, 2024, is weaker and more generic: it promises reasonable safeguards but no absolute security and allows retention for analytics, records, fraud prevention, and legal reasons [23]. Google Play reports encryption in transit and deletion requests for the Student App, but reports that the Owner App’s data was not encrypted and could not be deleted in its store disclosure at the time viewed [10] [13]. No SOC 2/ISO certificate, FERPA/COPPA/GDPR commitment, data-hosting region, or public breach history was located.

### Strengths

- Strong fit for affordable private Indian schools that need curriculum, teacher enablement, hardware, parent engagement, and academic administration together.
- Large claimed reach: 9,000+ schools and 4.1M+ students on the current homepage, with a 2022 unicorn funding history and 2023 Pearson K-12 acquisition.
- Clear hybrid/offline story for low-connectivity classrooms, with teacher tablets and downloadable or bundled content.
- Native student/parent, teacher, and owner touchpoints, plus useful attendance, homework, assessment, progress, and owner-dashboard workflows.
- NEP/NCF, CBSE/ICSE, holistic-progress, competency, and multilingual-policy positioning is more India-specific than a generic global SIS.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- No public pricing, public API documentation, standards certification, or detailed module catalog makes procurement and interoperability diligence difficult.
- The current website presents conflicting scale figures: 9,000+/4.1M/65,000 on the homepage versus 8,500+/3.8M on several product and history pages.
- Scope is tightly integrated and partner-oriented; schools seeking a modular standalone SIS, higher-education ERP, or on-premise deployment may find it limiting.
- Google Play reviews include a November 2026 complaint that the Student App was slow, sometimes failed to open, and froze; a teacher-app review reported a service issue unresolved for a week. Apple reviews mention book-activation/access-code problems and lack of iPad horizontal mode [10] [11] [12].
- The Owner App’s store disclosure reported no encryption and no deletion option, while the newer Nucleus privacy policy makes stronger DPDP claims; buyers should reconcile app-level disclosures contractually.

### Key Milestones

- **2012:** Sumeet Mehta and Smita Deorah co-founded LEAD School in Mumbai; the first-school story centers on Shantiniketan English School.
- **2013:** LEAD’s newer corporate history describes the founders as starting with one school in this year; this is the first-school operating date, not the legal/company founding date.
- **2014:** ELGA English Language and General Awareness and the initial full curriculum were launched.
- **2016:** LEAD created its first teacher application and transitioned teachers to tablets; the partner-school learning-system expansion followed.
- **2017:** LEAD began presenting an integrated system for teachers, parents, students, and school owners.
- **2020:** Series C funding of $28M led by WestBridge Capital and Elevar Equity; nationwide digital/hybrid learning expanded.
- **2021:** Series D funding of $30M; LEAD’s integrated system was reported at 8,500+ schools and 1.2M students in the milestone history.
- **January 2022:** Series E raised $100M at a $1.1B valuation, making LEAD the first school-edtech unicorn of 2022 [14] [15].
- **January–March 2023:** LEAD raised reported debt financing and completed the acquisition of Pearson India’s K-12 learning business [16] [24].
- **2024:** LEAD’s corporate history says it expanded its product portfolio with tech-first and AI-enabled solutions.
- **2026:** Nucleus privacy policy updated June 2; Student App version 7.2.5 was updated in October; current website claims 9,000+ schools and 4.1M+ students [10] [19].

| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | G2: 4.1/5 from 35 reviews, last updated November 4, 2026; Capterra: 3.5/5 from 22 reviews, page updated January 7, 2026; Apple Aeries Mobile Portal: 1.5/5 from 25K ratings; Apple Aeries Teacher: 1.9/5 from 43 ratings; Apple Aeries EM2: 2.5/5 from 48 ratings; all app ratings viewed November 24, 2026. Google Play Mobile Portal showed 100K+ downloads but no score/review count in the opened localized listing. [10] [11] [12] [13] [14] |

### Overview

Aeries SIS is a K-12 student information system centered on student records, attendance, scheduling, gradebook/grade reporting, portals, state reporting, and district data operations. Its surrounding product family adds Aeries Online Enrollment, Aeries Enroll Path, Aeries Analytics, Aeries Communications powered by ParentSquare, Aeries Payments, JumpRope, and ActivityHero. It is designed for district-wide data governance, school operations, teacher workflows, family access, and state compliance. [4] [5]

Aeries is particularly important in California because its data model and support content track CALPADS, CAASPP, Civil Rights Data Collection, college-readiness indicators, and other state workflows. It also has Texas PEIMS/TSDS and assessment content, with official customer examples including a Texas ISD. [4] [15] The company traces its present identity to 1995 and was formerly associated with Eagle Software. In 2025, Francisco Partners made a growth investment; Aeries stated that it remained family-operated. [1] [2]

### Platform Classification Explained

**Browser and cloud.** Aeries provides a web-based SIS and portals. Its hosted offering runs on Amazon Web Services, with monitoring, encryption, firewalls, secure transfer protocols, backups, redundancy, and rollback recovery described on the SIS page. [5] The API documentation also explicitly distinguishes districts hosted by Aeries from districts that host their own installations, so the most accurate classification is cloud SaaS plus a hybrid/self-hosted option rather than cloud-only. [6]

**Self-hosted and desktop.** The API documentation says self-hosted customers are responsible for some deployment choices, including HTTPS, and that each customer has an independent Aeries website. This confirms a non-hosted/self-hosted deployment path. I found no current evidence of a separate Windows/macOS desktop client; the former Eagle/Aeries CS desktop history is not a current product mode in the reviewed materials. [6]

**Native mobile applications.** The named apps are **Aeries Mobile Portal** for parents and students, **Aeries Teacher** for teacher attendance and gradebook work, and **Aeries EM2** (Emergency Management App Version 2) for school-site personnel and offline emergency access. Apple listings verify all three iOS apps. The official support article and Google Play listing verify Aeries Mobile Portal for iOS and Android. Mobile Portal covers grades, attendance, report cards, contacts, demographics, payments, state test scores, notifications, Communications, and supplemental-attendance check-in; full portal functions can open in the phone browser. [7] [12] [13] [14]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

Aeries Online Enrollment provides a multilingual, survey-style registration flow, configurable questions, editable pages, sibling-based reuse, save-and-return processing, direct synchronization into Aeries, and reduced manual entry. It supports English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Korean, and Farsi. Aeries Enroll Path adds customizable forms, dashboards, role-based access, audit logs, document uploads, and workflow-style enrollment management. [16] The guide’s paperless multi-student-registration lead is directionally correct, but audit-log details are documented for Enroll Path rather than clearly for Online Enrollment itself.

#### Student information and records

The core SIS stores demographics, addresses and address history, contacts, identifiers, languages, enrollment history, programs, activities and awards, student documents, custom fields/tables, student groups, college/career pathway data, work permits, foster-care records, 504 records, and health-related fields. Its REST API exposes student, staff, program, discipline, test, fee, immunization, medical-insurance, and supplemental-data endpoints. [17] [18]

#### Attendance

Attendance includes daily and class/flexible-period attendance, absence codes, attendance history and summaries, tardies, attendance notes, supplemental-attendance sessions, attendance notifications, attendance logs, Texas attendance-reporting data, and teacher attendance submission. Mobile Portal supports attendance viewing and QR-code supplemental-attendance check-in. [7] [17]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

The scheduling model includes courses, sections, course requests and alternate requests, prerequisites, bell schedules, calendars, tracks, master-schedule data, flexible scheduling, class rosters, section staff, and scheduling wait lists. Teacher and student/parent portals expose relevant class and course-request views. [18] [19]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Teacher Gradebook supports gradebooks, assignments, assignment types, grading scales, standards-based scores, gradebook terms, scores, backups, transfer scores, custom marks, dashboards, and parent/student visibility. The API supports gradebook and student-grade endpoints. Aeries also maintains exams, exam sections, questions, versions, response data, scoring rules, test administration, state test scores, college test scores, and assessment imports. [18] [20]

#### Report cards, transcripts and graduation

Grade reporting covers marking periods, report-card marks, GPA calculation, grade-report history, report-card printing, standards-based grades, grade snapshots, transcripts, course history, transcript requests, graduation requirements, graduation status summaries, endorsements, pathways, and college entrance requirements. [18] [21]

#### Learning management and homework

Aeries is not presented as a full native LMS or homework platform. It provides gradebook/class tools and integrates with Google Classroom, Canvas, Schoology, HMH, IXL, Renaissance, and other learning products through the ecosystem. The evidence supports interoperability with LMSs, not a bundled Aeries course-content, assignment-delivery, or homework engine. [20] [22]

#### Communication

Aeries Communications, powered by ParentSquare, supports emergency/general messaging, two-way communication, surveys, polls, forms, permission slips, mass notifications, classroom communication, engagement reporting, and automatic translation. Channels include email, voice, SMS text, social, websites, and in-app notifications. A customer statement cites more than 100 languages. WhatsApp was not verified. [23]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Parent and Student Portals support account creation and management, portal-group permissions, grades, gradebook, attendance, scheduling, contacts, translations, data confirmation/summer re-registration, digital signatures, document requests, alerts, and weekly progress emails. The Teacher Portal includes attendance and gradebook. Portal usage logs and field-level security controls are documented. [19]

#### Fees, billing, payments and fundraising

Aeries Payments (formerly Aeries Financials) processes fees, fines, tuition, debit/credit transactions, monthly payment schedules, online stores, and district-controlled crowdfunding campaigns. It reports transactions, arrears, donor/campaign statistics, and financial statements. The current page names PayPal and Stripe as processors. The guide’s budgeting/accounting wording is broader than the verified emphasis on payments, tuition, stores, and fundraising. [24]

#### Health and medical

The data model includes health problems/notes, immunizations, medical insurance, dental records, health tests, and medical/health/student-wellness support content. EM2 exposes medical information to authorized school personnel and can cache it for offline emergency use. [14] [17]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral/counseling care

Aeries includes discipline and assertive-discipline records, offenses and dispositions, expulsions, behavioral emergency reports, discipline notifications, counselor conferences/notes, at-risk indicators, interventions, student wellbeing fields, and career/academic planning. These are records and intervention-management capabilities, not a marketed standalone pastoral-care suite. [17] [18]

#### Special education, 504 and safeguarding

The data model contains special-education demographics, disability services, infant services, student services, alternate assessments, suspensions, secondary transition, preschool outcomes, 504 plans/accommodations, foster-care legal cases, placements, education rights holders, meetings, goals, hearings, and notes. It also supports data permissions and red-flag indicators. The reviewed sources do not claim a separate child-safeguarding case-management product. [18]

#### Inventory, assets and resource management

Aeries’s data model includes district resource titles, items, course assignments, checkout assignments, documents, and custom tables. The ecosystem integrates with GreenLight Locker and other resource/asset products. This is narrower than a full standalone procurement and asset-management suite. [18] [22]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Aeries Analytics provides ready-to-use and custom dashboards, interactive drill-down charts, dynamic student groups, indicators, permissions, exports to Excel, and early-warning monitoring. Indicators can use grades, discipline, interventions, college-admission requirements, attendance, program participation, and other data. The published LCAP example includes 25+ dashboards, 50+ charts, 100+ indicators, and subgroup analysis. Robust queries, custom reports, ad-hoc reporting, and state/federal extracts are core strengths. [25]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

The product has deep California CALPADS and assessment/reporting support, including CAASPP, CTE, college/career indicators, CRDC, Civil Rights calculations, and physical-fitness extracts. Texas support covers PEIMS/TSDS, Texas attendance reporting, STAAR/TELPAS-related imports and regulatory changes. Documentation is release-driven, with current 2026/27 CALPADS and Texas regulatory notes. [15]

#### Mobile apps

Aeries Mobile Portal is the family/student app; Aeries Teacher is the staff app for attendance, lunch count, assignments, grades, imports/exports, class tools, and Communications; Aeries EM2 is an authorized school-personnel emergency/offline app for student, contact, discipline, medical, class, and attendance information. Ratings indicate that functional breadth does not equal consistent mobile reliability. [12] [13] [14]

#### Integrations and APIs

The Aeries Ecosystem lists Ed-Fi, Clever, ClassLink/OneSync, Google and Google Classroom, Microsoft, Canvas, Schoology, ParentSquare, Follett Destiny, Frontline, Renaissance, MySchoolBucks, SchoolCash, nutrition systems, transportation providers, safety tools, and many other partners. The REST API is version 5, outputs JSON or XML, supports SSO, and exposes student, staff, scheduling, gradebook, attendance, grades, transcripts, fees, medical, discipline, and reporting-related endpoints. Updates are restricted to selected datasets and require district-issued certificates and permissions. [22] [26]

#### Security and privacy

Aeries states that AWS hosting uses encryption, firewalls, secure transfer protocols, monitoring, regular backups, redundancy, and disaster recovery. The June 18, 2026 privacy policy defines Aeries as a school official/service provider under district control, prohibits selling student PII, limits processing to contracted educational purposes, and provides return or secure destruction on termination. [5] [27]

There is no publicly documented native hostel/boarding, transport-management, payroll/HR, alumni-management, or university administration module. Transport, HR, library, nutrition, and LMS functionality is primarily represented by ecosystem integrations, not by Aeries-native modules. No production generative-AI assistant was found in the reviewed materials.

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- California-first compliance depth: current CALPADS, CAASPP, CRDC, and Texas PEIMS/TSDS support is maintained in the public release/support system. [15]
- Early-warning analytics: Aeries Analytics creates indicators, dynamic groups, drill-down dashboards, and intervention/supplemental-attendance records for at-risk students. [25]
- No-code enrollment configuration: Online Enrollment and Enroll Path let districts configure questions, pages, forms, documents, permissions, and audit-oriented workflows without building a separate application. [16]
- Interoperability as a product strategy: Aeries maintains a large integration lineup and a documented REST API rather than forcing every district workflow into a single suite. [22] [26]
- District-controlled family communications: ParentSquare-powered messaging unifies email, voice, SMS, web, social, in-app notifications, translation, surveys, and permission slips. [23]
- Offline emergency access: EM2 caches authorized student, contact, discipline, medical, class, and attendance records for situations without network access. [14]
- California-scale student data operations: the vendor reports more than 2.5 million students managed daily and more than 750 districts/LEAs. [4] [8]

### Pricing Details

Aeries publishes no official prices, tiers, per-student rate, implementation fee, or setup fee. The official pricing URL reviewed did not present a pricing schedule, and both G2 and Capterra direct buyers to contact the vendor; Capterra explicitly says no free trial and no free version are available. [10] [11] The commercial model should therefore be treated as sales-led, district-level quoting for the core SIS and selected add-ons, with hosting, implementation, training, support, and integrations potentially scoped in the contract. No credible public third-party numeric range was found, so no estimate is supplied.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Aeries is a member of the Ed-Fi Alliance and says it adheres to Ed-Fi data standards. It also lists Clever, ClassLink, Google/Google Classroom, Microsoft, Canvas, Schoology, ParentSquare, Follett Destiny, MySchoolBucks, SchoolCash, nutrition, transport, HR, safety, assessment, and analytics partners. The API is REST-based, version 5, with JSON/XML output, SSO support, district-issued certificates, and endpoint-level permissions. OneRoster, LTI, SIF, and a public app marketplace were not verified; the ecosystem page is an integration catalog. [5] [22] [26]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

AWS cloud documentation describes encryption, firewalls, secure transfer protocols, advanced monitoring, automatic backups, redundancy, and rollback recovery. The privacy center states that Aeries does not share student information with advertisers or marketers, does not own district-tracked data, and is compliant with FERPA, COPPA, HIPAA, SOPIPA, and California Education Code 49073.1. The June 18, 2026 policy adds school-official obligations, subprocessor controls, customer audit rights, and data return/destruction terms. [5] [8] [27]

Public materials reviewed did not verify SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, India DPDP Act, or a specific AWS data-hosting region. Self-hosted customers make some security choices themselves, including HTTPS configuration, according to the API documentation. I found no publicly reported Aeries security incident in the reviewed official releases, support pages, or independent listings; that is not evidence that no incident has ever occurred. [6] [26]

### Strengths

- Exceptional California state-reporting and data-model depth, with growing Texas regulatory coverage.
- Broad K-12 operational coverage around student records, attendance, scheduling, gradebook, grade reporting, portals, analytics, enrollment, communications, and payments.
- Large reported installed base: more than 750 districts/LEAs and over 2.5 million students managed daily.
- Strong REST API and integration philosophy, with Ed-Fi, SSO, Clever, ClassLink, Google, Microsoft, LMS, assessment, nutrition, safety, and transportation connections.
- Flexible district configuration through custom fields/tables, dashboards, forms, permissions, portals, and reporting.
- AWS-hosted option plus a documented self-hosted path gives districts deployment flexibility.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Usability is inconsistent. Capterra is 3.5/5 overall, with 3.4/5 ease of use, 3.0/5 value for money, and 2.7/5 customer service as of its January 7, 2026 update. [10]
- Capterra reviews report excessive clicks, clunky navigation, slow or frustrating workflows, difficult training materials, ticket-based support, and separate enrollment/admin portals that can require imports. [10]
- G2’s otherwise stronger 4.1/5 average still identifies gradebook complexity, hard-to-find options, confusing reports, and gaps in parent/teacher grade transfer as recurring issues. [11]
- Mobile experience is a major risk: Apple ratings were 1.5/5 for Mobile Portal, 1.9/5 for Aeries Teacher, and 2.5/5 for EM2, with reviews citing crashes, login failures, loading errors, locked attendance, and limited in-app functionality. [12] [13] [14]
- The product is U.S.-centric and especially California-oriented; there is no verified international-country footprint or higher-education feature set.
- Several enterprise functions are ecosystem integrations rather than native modules, so total cost, implementation effort, and data-governance complexity can rise across partners.
- No public pricing makes competitive budgeting difficult, and no production AI assistant was verified.

### Key Milestones

- **1972:** The guide claims an Aeries founder created an early SIS in this year; I found no primary-source confirmation, so it remains unverified.
- **1995:** Aeries Software’s current site and app materials identify 1995 as the company/copyright origin. [4]
- **2014:** Aeries API documentation records the original public API release and SSO release in its revision history. [26]
- **2015–2017:** API additions expanded student programs, test scores, enrollment history, transcripts, graduation requirements, report cards, fees/fines, discipline, scheduling, and gradebook coverage. [26]
- **2020:** API versions were consolidated toward v5, adding flexible scheduling support and broader endpoint coverage. [26]
- **2025:** Aeries announced a growth investment from Francisco Partners while stating that the company remained family-operated. [1] [2]
- **2026:** Aeries materials show ongoing CALPADS, Texas regulatory, CRDC, mobile, enrollment, API, privacy, and product-release activity; the current privacy policy took effect June 18, 2026. [15] [27]
