### Overview

Gradelink SIS is a school information and administration system built around a single web-based record for students, families, staff, classes, grades, attendance, communication and tuition. Its stated value proposition is operational simplicity for smaller and mid-sized schools: administrators enter information once, teachers manage gradebooks and lesson plans, and families access grades, assignments, attendance, conduct, schedules and billing through portals or the mobile app. [1] [2] [14]

The product is especially relevant to private, parochial, charter and international K–12 schools that want admissions, academics, parent communication and basic billing in one subscription rather than a large district ERP. Gradelink says it has served schools for 24 years and currently claims 2,200+ schools and 400K users, but it does not publish a country-by-country adoption table. The company was founded in 2001 according to LinkedIn and Crunchbase; a separate product launch year, acquisition history, and funding history were not publicly disclosed. [1] [10] [13] [14]

### Platform Classification Explained

Gradelink is browser-first Cloud SaaS. The company says it runs entirely online, works on major browsers and operating systems, requires only an internet connection, and cannot currently be downloaded or used offline. It supports Macs, PCs, tablets and mobile browsers. [4] [13] The security page says customer servers are hosted in a locked data-center facility in Irvine, California, with U.S.-based IT staff; it does not name AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or another public cloud provider. [8]

There is no evidence of a Windows/macOS desktop client, self-hosted package, or customer-managed on-premise edition. Native mobile software is the **Gradelink Student/Parent App** for iPhone/iPad and Android. It exposes grades, assignments, attendance, homework, schedules, news, discipline, report cards, billing and configurable alerts. The product pages do not identify a separate native teacher or administrator app; staff use the responsive browser service. [7] [19] [20]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

The core SIS includes a prospective-student inquiry form and prospect workflow. The paid EnrollMe add-on provides online applications, re-enrollment, custom enrollment forms, document collection and automatic fee collection when paired with Gradelink Payments. Help documentation covers application management, importing applicants, enrollment sessions, reports and setup for a new academic year. [2] [3] [6]

#### Student information and records

Student records cover demographics, status, photos, family and sibling links, campus assignment, tags, emergency-card information, contact details, religious information, languages, government IDs, testing IDs, files and documents. Administrators can withdraw or promote students, lock or reset student/family accounts, view login information and export records. The security model isolates each school in a separate database. [6] [8]

#### Attendance

Attendance includes daily and per-class registers, attendance and conduct reports, holiday scheduling, custom and detailed reports, total-school attendance, extended-care tracking and preschool/child check-in. The 2026 product news documents parent absence reporting through the portal or app, with opt-in email notifications to teachers and administrators, and batch check-in/check-out for groups. [2] [10]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Classes and Scheduling supports block scheduling, concurrent mixed terms such as quarters and trimesters, class calendars, custom class types, custom and managed grade scales, standards per class, simple or advanced teacher schedules, and student scheduling. The evidence supports class scheduling rather than a full transportation-style master-scheduling optimizer. [2] [5]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Teacher Gradebooks provide assignment collections, assignment-type weighting, file attachments, automatic lowest-grade drops, extra credit, curves/grade boosts, custom grade codes and comments, preset comments, low-grade highlighting, projected semester grades, semester/year averages, effort and citizenship, team teaching/grading, and unified multi-class views. Teachers can record homework, tests, projects and quizzes; reports include GPA/scores, honor roll and sports eligibility. Standards-based grading and class/teacher/student standards metrics are included. A separate high-stakes examination-management module was not found. [2] [6]

#### Report cards and transcripts

The platform generates comprehensive, conduct, deficiency, progress and standards-based report cards, with customizable templates and paperless distribution. It produces transcripts and transcript labels, preserves academic history, and supports export of transcript records as PDF. A 2026 Award Certificates tool adds dynamic templates, drag-and-drop design, smart data fields such as name, term, principal and GPA, and batch PDF export. [2] [6] [10]

#### Learning management and homework

This is an SIS with learning-support functions, not a full standalone LMS. Native tools include lesson plans, assignment collection, attachments, homework/test/project/quiz tracking, teacher pages and upcoming-assignment visibility. Google Classroom can synchronize assignment and quiz grades into the Gradelink gradebook. No public evidence was found for SCORM, LTI, course authoring, discussion forums or a full LMS product. [2] [5] [11]

#### Communication

Built-in SmartSend supports email blasts, group building, school calendars, school news, teacher pages and automated parent alerts. SmartSend Pro is an optional add-on for unlimited text and voice messaging, message scheduling and history logs, with automatic synchronization of students, parents, staff and alumni. The 2026 news page reports full STIR/SHAKEN “A” attestation for voice caller-ID trust. WhatsApp and native push broadcast support were not documented. [3] [10]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Separate parent/family and student accounts provide grades, assignment details and teacher comments, attendance and conduct, transcripts, schedules, calendars, news, downloadable attachments, absence reporting and grade/attendance alerts. Teacher functionality is delivered through the web interface and Teacher Pages rather than a separate teacher portal or app. The redesigned Parent and Student Portal launched before the 2026 review period. [2] [6] [10]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Tuition & Billing includes accounts receivable, multiple tuition rates, billing statements, aging reports, convenience fees, automated lunch billing and incidental billing. Gradelink Payments, integrated with PaySimple, accepts ACH and credit cards, supports one-time or recurring donations, AutoPay, AutoPost and multi-month installment plans; families can pay tuition, lunch, sports and other charges. This is school billing and payment collection, not a complete general-ledger, procurement or fund-accounting suite. [3] [5] [11]

#### HR and staff

Staff accounts store credentials, employment status, contact information and pay grade, with configurable access levels and notifications. Staff rosters and staff reports are available. No native payroll, benefits, recruiting, performance-management or employee self-service module was found. [2] [6]

#### Health and medical

Medical records include allergies, immunizations/immune status, insurance information, medical history, medications, physical exams, office/injury visits, vision, hearing and scoliosis exams, plus medical reports. [2] [6]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Discipline tools store incidents, demerits and counseling/discipline entries, support configurable menu choices and discipline email alerts, and expose discipline reports and exports. A broad pastoral-care or safeguarding case-management product was not evidenced. [2] [6]

#### Special education

IEP tracking is an administrative report and student-record feature. Help documentation covers IEP and 504 plans, custom dropdown menus, adding plans and IEP reports. The public materials do not establish a full special-education workflow comparable to a district SpEd case-management suite. [2] [6]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Native reporting includes address labels, birthday lists, classes by attendance or average grade, family directory, IEP tracking, lunch, staff roster, standards-met-by-teacher, volunteer hours, security activity, student rosters, transcripts, attendance and financial reports. District Login adds cross-school demographics, academic performance, attendance, census data, maps, subgroup reports, staff/student details and group email. Predictive analytics, data warehousing and natural-language BI were not found. [2] [12]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Public integration materials identify Ed-Fi certification as a student-information capability and describe Wisconsin WISEdata/Ed-Fi reporting for Choice schools. Other named exports include Indiana DOE Data Exchange and Choice Scholarship reporting, Michigan MSDS Early Roster, Georgia HOPE Scholarship and NCEA reporting. These are targeted state or association workflows, not a universal international statutory-reporting engine. [2] [5] [11]

#### Mobile apps

The native app is the Gradelink Student/Parent App for iOS/iPadOS and Android. It offers grades, assignment and category-weight graphs, report cards, attendance history, discipline, billing statements, school news, schedules, grade alerts, attendance alerts, absence reporting and multi-child switching. The app requires the school to subscribe and some features depend on school settings. [7] [19] [20]

#### Integrations and APIs

Named integrations include Google Classroom, ClassLink, Schoology, Clever, Microsoft School Data Sync, Apple School Manager, Renaissance RDI/Star, FACTS Tuition, PaySimple, Edmentum, Canvas, ClassWallet, Indiana Data Exchange, Michigan MSDS and Wisconsin WISEdata. GetApp’s product FAQ explicitly says no API is available, so these are vendor-supported connectors and exports rather than a documented public developer platform. No public LTI, OneRoster, SIF, marketplace or QuickBooks Online integration was verified. [5] [11] [17]

#### Modules not evidenced as native Gradelink modules

The reviewed primary materials did not substantiate native transport management, library management, hostel/boarding, inventory and asset management, payroll, alumni/fundraising CRM, AI assistant, predictive analytics, WhatsApp messaging, or a dedicated teacher mobile app. Some third-party catalogs list generic category labels, but those listings were not accepted as proof against the vendor’s actual feature pages. [2] [5] [17] [21]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **District/Diocese Login:** Cross-school reports, subgroup filters, census/map views, staff and student detail, and district-wide email give a small-school product a useful multi-school oversight layer. [12]
- **School-isolated databases:** Gradelink states that schools are kept in separate complete databases rather than shared tables, a distinctive privacy boundary for a multi-tenant service. [8]
- **Fast implementation:** The vendor targets a five-to-ten-business-day setup after receiving the roster and report-card information, with standard current-record transfer included. [3] [4]
- **Integrated private-school workflow:** EnrollMe, SIS academics, family communication, billing and PaySimple payments connect the admissions-to-revenue path without a long-term contract. [3]
- **Targeted compliance exports:** Ed-Fi/WISEdata, Indiana, Michigan, Georgia and NCEA connections address specific U.S. state and Catholic-school reporting needs. [5] [11]
- **Configurable family alerts:** Parents can set grade and attendance thresholds in the app, while schools can send scheduled email, SMS and voice notifications. [3] [19]
- **Dynamic award certificates:** The 2026 certificate editor turns report data into branded, batch-printable awards without external design software. [10]

### Pricing Details

The official calculator displayed **US$106 per month plus a one-time US$275 setup fee** when checked on November 24, 2026. Pricing is based on actively enrolled students, billed monthly, with no long-term contract; the calculator does not present a simple public annual per-student rate. The official page lists a free trial and says standard data transfer, staff training, support and updates are included. [3] [4]

Optional published add-ons are **EnrollMe: US$20.83/month plus US$497 setup**; **SmartSend Pro: US$16.67/month**; and **Gradelink Payments: US$0/month software fee plus payment processing**. Clever Sync, Renaissance Learning, transcript import and educational standards are listed as additional options requiring a sales quote. Extended historical-data transfer may also incur a fee. [3]

For comparison, Capterra and GetApp report **US$121/month for up to 50 students, US$164/month for 51–100, and US$210/month for 101–150**; these are third-party displayed tiers, not a replacement for the official calculator. [15] [17]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Gradelink supports Google Classroom grade sync, ClassLink and Clever rostering, Schoology, Microsoft School Data Sync, Apple School Manager, Renaissance RDI/Star, FACTS Tuition, PaySimple, Edmentum and Canvas. State/sector connections include NCEA, Indiana DOE Data Exchange, Michigan MSDS, Georgia HOPE and Wisconsin WISEdata. [5] [11]

The official feature page labels Gradelink “Ed-Fi Certified,” and the Wisconsin integration is described as an Ed-Fi/WISEdata pathway. Google SSO is supported. However, no public API is documented; GetApp explicitly answers “No” to API availability. No verified OneRoster, LTI or SIF certification, public integration marketplace, Microsoft Graph API, accounting-platform connector or QuickBooks Online connector was found. [2] [3] [17]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The security page reports SSL encryption for web and mobile connections, nightly redundant backups using local and remotely encrypted storage, an additional off-site backup, audited device/IP requests, network segregation, firewalls, intrusion detection, log aggregation, VPN access, configurable timeouts, password complexity and lockout rules, teacher-level permissions and separate school databases. The pricing page also advertises MFA, Google SSO, encrypted service, login/IP/DNS tracking, daily backups and student-privacy compliance. [3] [8]

Gradelink says servers are in an Irvine, California data center and IT staff are in the United States. Schools retain ownership of their data and can export Excel-compatible student data, PDF academic records or an encrypted SQL backup. Its privacy/DPA language commits to reasonable industry-standard technical and organizational safeguards, applicable privacy laws, CCPA, school data policies, subcontractor controls, incident notification and deletion/return on request. [8] [9]

No public SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certificate was located. FERPA is referenced contractually, including directory-information language, but a public FERPA certification does not exist in the materials reviewed; COPPA, GDPR and India’s DPDP Act were not publicly claimed as certifications. No publicly reported Gradelink security incident was found in the sources reviewed through November 24, 2026. Schools should obtain the current DPA and security plan directly before procurement. [8] [9]

### Strengths

- Broad, coherent SIS coverage for private and faith-based K–12 schools: records, attendance, gradebook, report cards, transcripts, communication, admissions and tuition.
- Public calculator pricing and a monthly, no-long-term-contract model are unusually transparent for a commercial SIS. [3]
- Very strong support reputation: Capterra shows 4.9/5 for customer service, while GetApp reviewers frequently praise rapid, knowledgeable help. [15] [17]
- High review usability scores, especially Capterra ease of use at 4.6/5 and strong Apple app feedback. [15] [19]
- Practical state/association exports and a district/diocese rollup for organizations that do not need a large district ERP. [5] [12]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Reviewers report occasional freezes, unexplained returns to the home page, glitches/timeouts and limited comment space. [15] [17]
- The interface is considered less modern or less streamlined than larger SIS products, and several reviewers describe report customization or complex reporting as limited. [16] [18]
- The native app is family/student-focused; a Software Advice reviewer said staff sometimes must use a computer because the web software is not usable on mobile, while a Capterra reviewer reported parent complaints about app glitches and bill-pay usability. [16] [17]
- Billing can become confusing when a family pays tuition, lunch and activities in one transaction, and GetApp reviewers complain that PaySimple setup/importing is not sufficiently user-friendly. [15] [17]
- Add-on pricing and sales scope can make total cost harder to predict, and advanced enterprise integrations, API access, predictive analytics and ERP modules are limited or absent. [17] [18]

### Key Milestones

- **2001:** Gradelink is reported as founded by LinkedIn and Crunchbase; the vendor’s separate product-launch date is not publicly disclosed. [13] [14]
- **2024:** The official news archive documents billing arriving in the Student/Parent Mobile App and batch check-in improvements. [10]
- **2025:** Gradelink announced a redesigned Parent and Student Portal, retaining the prior feature set with a more modern interface. [10]
- **2026:** Product updates documented new parent absence reporting, a redesigned District Login, SmartSend Pro caller-ID verification, a certificate designer, improved School News/Teacher Pages/email editing and a refreshed mobile app. [10]
- **2026:** The homepage claimed 2,200+ schools and 400K users, while LinkedIn identified the company as privately held with 29 employees in its public profile. [1] [14]
- **Funding and acquisitions:** No verified funding round, acquisition, parent-company transaction or product acquisition was found in the primary or independent sources reviewed.

## Global #23 (evaluated). ManageBac+ (Faria Education Group)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Faria Education Group Ltd; the service’s legal terms identify ManageBac LLC as the operator and Faria Education Group as the group/trade-name owner. [7] |
| Headquarters | San Francisco, California, United States (ManageBac LLC legal address: 548 Market St. #40438). [7] |
| Company founded (year) | 2006, founded at the University of Pennsylvania by three IB Diploma graduates. [2] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | 2007 as CAS Manager; renamed ManageBac in 2009 as scope expanded beyond CAS. [2] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud SaaS and web-based, with native ManageBac+ iOS and Android apps; no desktop client or on-premise deployment is publicly documented. [6] [10] |
| Primary segments | IB World Schools (PYP, MYP, DP and CP); international schools using Cambridge, IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel, AP or build-your-own curricula; teachers, coordinators, administrators, students and parents. [1] [11] |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | ManageBac states more than 800,000 students, 3,000 schools and 130 countries (claim viewed 24 November 2026). [2] Faria’s wider group claims 10,000+ schools, 4M+ students and 155 countries, which should not be attributed to ManageBac alone. [15] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://www.managebac.com/ |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://www.managebac.com/mb-bundle |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | https://help.managebac.com/hc/en-us |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | No public price list; official billing documentation: https://help.managebac.com/hc/en-us/articles/360031153712-Your-Billing-Subscription |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | Viewed 24 November 2026: G2 4.5/5 from 3 verified reviews; Capterra—no public ManageBac rating/profile located; Apple App Store Norway 3.3/5 from 12 ratings; Google Play 2.5/5 with 1.48K reviews (the ratings panel showed 1.34K). [12] [13] Trustpilot was 2.5/5 from 4 reviews, a small and non-verified sample. [14] |

### Overview

ManageBac+ is Faria’s curriculum-first learning and academic-management platform for international schools. It connects curriculum design, unit and lesson planning, classroom resources, tasks, assessment, gradebooks, portfolios, report cards, transcripts, attendance and school-to-home communication. It supports the IB continuum, Cambridge, IGCSE, Edexcel, AP and custom programmes through more than 600 standards sets. [1] [11]

The product is used by programme coordinators, teachers, students, parents and administrators. ManageBac began in 2006, launched CAS Manager in 2007, and adopted the ManageBac name in 2009. Its history includes automated IBIS registration (2011), OpenApply and iOS (2013), Faria’s reorganisation and LaunchPad SSO (2016), AWS Canada migration (2017), Atlas collaboration (2018) and Curriculum Trak/SchoolsBuddy joining Faria (2019). [2] ManageBac+ is an operating subsidiary of Faria Education Group, not an IB subsidiary or IB-endorsed software company. [2] [9]

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser/cloud:** ManageBac+ is explicitly web-based, requiring an internet connection, modern JavaScript-enabled browser and school-specific domain. The FAQ says it is hosted in Amazon Web Services data centres in Canada, the United States and China, with location dependent on school and local law. [9]
* **Desktop/on-premise:** No native Windows/macOS desktop client or customer-managed on-premise edition was found in the official product, FAQ or terms pages. The deployment model is hosted SaaS.
* **Native mobile:** The native app is named **ManageBac+** in current help documentation and is available for iPhone, iPad and Android. It supports students, parents, teachers, coordinators and administrators, including tasks, portfolios, attendance, messages, CAS and projects. [10] The public store listings still display the shorter app name **ManageBac**. [12] [13]
* **Mobile browser:** The 2026 AI Writing Assistant works in web and mobile browsers but, at the time checked, not inside the native iOS/Android apps. [17]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Curriculum management and academic standards

Collaborative real-time unit planners, curriculum mapping, lesson planning, resources, scope and sequence, learning outcomes, accreditation alignment and whole-school curriculum analytics are native. ManageBac advertises 600+ standards sets; its implementation guide reported 607 sets and more than 1.5 million licensed standards/benchmarks. [11] It supports IB PYP, MYP, DP and CP, British/Cambridge/IGCSE, Edexcel, AP and build-your-own programmes. The 2026 redesign added grid-based unit views, active/archived filters, Quick Add, week view, teacher notes, description/guidance, reusable resources and audience visibility controls. [8]

#### Teaching, learning and classroom/LMS

Classes contain units, lessons, resources, tasks, assignments, announcements, discussions and calendars. Teachers can share files, websites, video, photos, text notes, Google Docs and online lessons; students submit work and receive feedback. Presentation Mode and Zoom support remote lessons, while KeyChat supports school communication and social-emotional check-ins. [11] Portfolios hold files, photos, videos, links, goals, reflections, coursework and awards.

#### Admissions and enrolment

Admissions is not a full native ManageBac module. Faria’s separate OpenApply admissions system integrates with ManageBac for admissions, enrolment, re-enrolment and family information. The 2026 OpenApply Mini Profile can show tags, applicant-history status changes and configured general/custom fields on a synced student profile, including examples such as ESL, SEN and Medical Alert. [8] [15]

#### Student information and records

ManageBac provides student, parent, teacher/advisor, coordinator, administrator and read-only observer accounts; school-specific domains; profiles; year groups; classes; homerooms; programmes; permissions; contacts; academic records; attendance; portfolios and report data. It exports student information as PDF forms and CSV and supports synchronisation with SIS partners such as iSAMS, PowerSchool and Veracross. [9]

#### Attendance

Teachers record class and homeroom attendance by day or period; administrators configure attendance preferences, categories, days off, reminders and daily digests; parents can submit absence excusals. The 2026 release added confirmation per homeroom day and class period, missing-confirmation queues, reminder notifications, CSV import and iOS confirmation. [8] [11]

#### Timetable and scheduling

Users have calendars and timetables showing lessons, events, tasks, deadlines and exams, with student, class, group and year-group views. [10] A full master-scheduling/room-allocation engine is not publicly documented.

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

The gradebook supports points, criteria, comments-only, binary, interdisciplinary and custom assessment models; task and term grades; rubrics; differentiation; annotations; local-grade conversion; hidden results; and administrator tracking of submission progress. The assessment page adds Google Docs coursework, Turnitin plagiarism checking and Vantage Reader collaborative annotations. [4] AssessPrep, available as a Faria-linked online-assessment service/add-on, adds interactive questions, formative and mock exams, lockdown mode, live monitoring, analytics, AI question creation and AI grading, with gradebook sync; the current page advertises 20+ question types and 40,000+ ready-to-use questions. [4]

For IB, ManageBac supports DP plans, CAS, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, Internal Assessments, Group 6 IA, eCoursework, exam calendars, candidate/session data and IBIS exam registration. The 2026 eCoursework dashboard covers IA, EA and Core components, missing submissions and links to IB upload requirements. [8]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Custom report-card templates support term grades, percentage equivalencies, exam scores, 21st-century skills, Cambridge Learner Attributes, service learning, portfolio highlights, advisor/student reflections, attendance, extra-curricular activity, class reports, cover sheets and grade descriptors. Schools can use multilingual UTF-8, right-to-left Arabic/Hebrew, custom layouts, 30+ patterns/wallpapers, error checks, online responsive reports and bulk print-ready PDFs. Transcripts include built-in checks for names, grades, comments and rubrics. [4] [11]

#### Learning management and homework

Tasks may be summative or formative, tied to units, categories, resources and differentiated classes. Students see upcoming/completed work and deadlines, upload coursework and access teacher feedback. Google Docs templates can be assigned in three clicks and saved automatically into portfolios; Zoom and Presentation Mode support synchronous/remote learning. [11]

#### Communication

Native communication includes announcements, class/year-group/group discussions, individual messages, 1-to-1 direct messaging, multi-user chat, notifications, push/mobile notifications, profanity filtering, parent alerts, daily/weekly digests and KeyChat. The evidence reviewed does not show a native SMS or WhatsApp gateway; those should not be assumed from the term “communications.” [1] [11]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

Role-based web and mobile experiences provide separate dashboards, calendars, classes, tasks, grades, attendance, portfolios, report cards, behaviour notes, messages and settings. Parents can switch between children, submit attendance excusals, see progress and join PTA activity; students manage goals, coursework, reflections, CAS and projects; teachers plan, teach, grade, message and record attendance. [10]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

ManageBac’s own subscription billing supports annual invoices, credit cards, purchase orders, cheques and China-only bank transfer, with actual or adjusted student-count billing. It offers 5% off for two years paid upfront and 10% off for three years paid upfront. This is not a school-fee ledger, payroll or general accounting module; SchoolsBuddy is Faria’s separate activities/bookings/payments product. [5] [11]

#### HR, staff and payroll

No native HR, recruitment, staff appraisal, payroll or workforce-payroll module was identified. ManageBac has staff/advisor accounts, roles, permissions and implementation/support workflows, but those are not an HRIS.

#### Transport

No native transport-routing or bus-tracking module was identified. Faria positions Vectare as its separate transport product, so transport should be treated as a suite integration/adjacent product rather than a ManageBac feature. [15]

#### Library, hostel/boarding, inventory/assets

No native library circulation/cataloguing, hostel/boarding, dormitory, inventory, asset-register or procurement modules were found in the reviewed official pages.

#### Health and medical

ManageBac can display configured OpenApply fields such as a Medical Alert tag in a synced Mini Profile, but a native nurse/clinic, immunisation, medication or medical-record workflow was not documented. [8]

#### Behaviour, discipline and pastoral care

Parents can view behaviour notes; teachers record Behaviour & Discipline through the app; KeyChat includes social-emotional support; homeroom/advisor comments and reviews support pastoral workflows. A dedicated safeguarding case-management or restorative-discipline module was not evidenced. [10] [11]

#### Special education and safeguarding

Role permissions, access controls, privacy settings, discussion controls, profanity filtering and configurable OpenApply tags can support SEN/safeguarding practice. ManageBac does not publicly describe a complete IEP/504 workflow, mandated-reporting case system or safeguarding register. [8] [17]

#### Alumni and fundraising

No native alumni-relations, donor, fundraising or advancement module was identified. OpenApply covers admissions/re-enrolment; it should not be counted as an alumni CRM without separate evidence.

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Whole-school curriculum analytics, engagement analytics, academic overview, DP/MYP academic analytics, tagged learning-outcome exports, eCoursework monitoring, submission-progress tracking, report-card error checks and parent/teacher dashboards are documented. The platform reports performance by student, class and group, but no predictive-risk score or publicly documented no-code workflow builder was found. [1] [8] [11]

#### AI features

ManageBac AI Writing Assistant can generate text, revise selected text, simplify, expand, correct grammar/spelling and translate; administrators enable it at school level and control teacher/advisor access. It is not enabled for China, does not pull page context, and the vendor says student/teacher personal information is not used to train models. AssessPrep adds AI question generation and AI grading as an associated assessment service. [4] [17]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

ManageBac provides IBIS integration and curriculum/reporting tools for international-school standards, but the reviewed pages do not document certified Ed-Fi, SIF, state reporting or national-government submissions. GDPR/ePrivacy controls and compliance support are documented; compliance is not the same as a state-reporting module. [8] [9]

#### Mobile apps

The native ManageBac+ app supports iPhone, iPad and Android for all major roles. Current functions include tasks, portfolios, goals, reflections, CAS/community engagement, projects, classes, messages, gradebook, attendance, behaviour and report cards. iOS supports coursework scanning and attendance confirmation; Android 2026 support added project worksheets, proposals, reflections, journals, notes, documents and presentations. [10]

#### Integrations and APIs

The official site advertises 50+ integrations: Google Workspace/Docs/Drive, Microsoft Office 365, Clever, ClassLink, Turnitin, Zoom, IBIS, IB eCoursework, Kognity, Concord Infinity, BridgeU, iSAMS, OpenApply, SchoolsBuddy and AssessPrep. Faria’s public Integrations Portal documents ManageBac+ APIs and an interactive “Test it” endpoint feature, with structured data retrieval/updating but no AI/LLM capability in the API itself. [1] [3] [18]

#### Security, privacy and access control

Faria reports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, encrypted connections and at-rest encryption, restricted production access, malware scanning, security training, 24/7 incident response, warm standby, backups and disaster recovery. ManageBac’s FAQ adds real-time redundant and daily/off-site backups, role permissions and cloud hosting. [9] [16] The reviewed public material does not establish SOC 2, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF certification, or an India DPDP Act claim.

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **IB-native programme workflow:** IBIS registration, eCoursework, CAS, EE, ToK, IA and Core tracking reduce spreadsheet-based IB coordination. [2] [8]
* **Curriculum-first architecture:** More than 600 standards sets and curriculum mapping connect units, learning outcomes, assessment and reporting. [11]
* **Multi-curricula single account:** IB, Cambridge/IGCSE, Edexcel, AP and custom programmes can coexist in one international-school environment. [1] [11]
* **Holistic portfolio and service learning:** Portfolios, goals, reflections, CAS/community engagement and project-based learning capture evidence beyond grades.
* **Configurable international reporting:** Multilingual, right-to-left, branded web/PDF reports with proofing and rubric support are unusually deep for an LMS. [4]
* **Role-complete mobile access:** One native app serves students, parents, teachers, coordinators and administrators, rather than only a student companion app. [10]
* **ManageBac AI and AssessPrep AI:** Writing generation/revision is production functionality, while AssessPrep adds AI question creation and grading as a linked assessment product. [4] [17]
* **Faria family ecosystem:** OpenApply, SchoolsBuddy, Atlas, Vectare and other products can connect around the learning platform, although they are separate products. [15]

### Pricing Details

ManageBac+ has no public price card or currency-denominated tier price. Official documentation says it is an annual subscription priced according to total student numbers, with quotations available from sales; the terms state that recurring-service fees are based on enrolment and individual modules can vary with enrolment. [9] [7] The product page exposes Essential, Standard and Pro bundle names, but not prices or a public per-student/per-school rate. [3]

As of 24 November 2026, the official billing guide documents annual invoicing, net-30 terms, credit card/cheque payments and China-only bank transfer. Two-year prepaid agreements receive 5% off and three-year prepaid agreements 10% off. The guide does not publish setup or implementation prices; ManageBac says an Implementation Manager guides setup and training, and the About page states that it does not add surprise setup, training, maintenance or upgrade fees. [5] [9]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

ManageBac’s strongest interoperability is practical ecosystem connectivity: Google Workspace/Docs/Drive, Microsoft 365, Clever, ClassLink, Turnitin, Zoom, IBIS, eCoursework, Kognity, iSAMS, OpenApply, SchoolsBuddy, BridgeU, Concord Infinity and AssessPrep. [1] Faria maintains a public developer portal with ManageBac+ technical documentation, APIs and browser-based endpoint testing. [18]

The evidence reviewed does not show public certification on OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi or SIF, nor a conventional third-party app marketplace. Google, Microsoft, Faria and partner SSO options are supported in the app guidance, but a detailed public SAML/OIDC matrix was not located. [10]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Faria reports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification under BSI certificate IS 664562, TLS/SSL in transit, encryption at rest, restricted production access, malware scanning, annual security training, 24/7 incident response and disaster recovery. [16] ManageBac reports GDPR compliance, COPPA support, PIPEDA and UK DPA 2018 coverage, plus China Cybersecurity Law controls; its FAQ says hosting is in AWS Canada, the United States and China. Faria’s broader security page also refers to servers in Canada, China and the EU, so exact region is school- and contract-dependent. [9] [16]

Faria says it does not store card data and transmits payment information to Stripe, describing PCI DSS compliance. [16] FERPA and the India DPDP Act were not expressly claimed on the public pages checked, so they should be confirmed contractually. No public security incident disclosure was located in the reviewed official materials; absence of a disclosure is not proof that no incident has occurred.

### Strengths

* Deep, purpose-built IB workflow, including IBIS, CAS, EE, IA, Core and eCoursework.
* Strong curriculum-to-assessment-to-reporting continuity across IB and non-IB international curricula.
* Broad role coverage and unusually capable parent/student/teacher mobile access.
* Flexible multilingual report cards, portfolios, service learning and project-based learning.
* Practical integrations with the productivity, SIS, assessment and admissions tools international schools already use.
* Transparent public documentation for hosting, backups, privacy, billing mechanics and current releases.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* It is not a full SIS/ERP: admissions, transport, fees, HR/payroll, library, boarding, assets, health and alumni functions are absent or delivered by separate Faria products/partners. [11] [15]
* Pricing is quote-only; schools cannot compare a public per-student price or know tier limits without sales engagement. [5] [12]
* G2’s small but verified sample praised integrations and breadth while criticizing navigation/UI, maintenance interruptions and information density. [12]
* Mobile-store feedback is materially harsher: Google Play was 2.5/5, with complaints about unintuitive navigation, a finicky interface and changes to task/deadline organisation. [13]
* Apple reviewers described the app as confusing, difficult to navigate, inconsistent between dashboard and calendar, and reported a login error; the sample was only 12 ratings. [13]
* Trustpilot’s four reviews were all one-star and complained about confusing layout, updates, upload/task workflows and perceived downtime; Trustpilot warns the small unprompted sample may not be representative. [14]
* Advanced AI is constrained: the Writing Assistant is not in native mobile apps, is unavailable in China and only processes text explicitly sent to it rather than platform context. [17]

### Key Milestones

* **2006:** ManageBac founded at the University of Pennsylvania by three IB Diploma graduates. [2]
* **2007:** CAS Manager launched at the IBAP conference.
* **2008:** MYP Community & Service, Extended Essay and ToK functions added.
* **2009:** CAS Manager renamed ManageBac; IB permission to digitise selected handbook forms; Spanish launched. [2]
* **2010:** Curriculum-planning and assessment functions added.
* **2011:** More than 1,000 schools claimed; automated IBIS exam registration; PYP curriculum-planning system launched.
* **2013:** OpenApply launched; ManageBac iOS launched. [2]
* **2015:** Direct ManageBac integration with IB eCoursework launched.
* **2016:** Faria reorganised as an international education services/systems group; LaunchPad SSO launched; ManageBac exceeded 2,000 schools. [2]
* **2017:** Migration to AWS Canada; Curriculum-First support broadened to IGCSE, A Levels and AP.
* **2018:** Responsive ManageBac interface launched; Atlas and ManageBac joined forces on curriculum-first development.
* **2019:** ManageBac mobile redesign; PYP Next launched; Curriculum Trak and SchoolsBuddy joined Faria. [2]
* **2023:** ManageBac Community Ambassador Programme launched.
* **2026:** ManageBac+ re-positioned as a next-generation platform; releases included attendance confirmation/CSV import, unit and lesson redesign, OpenApply Mini Profiles, eCoursework Dashboard, MYP Academic Analytics, report-card enhancements, AI Suite/Writing Assistant, AI translations, mobile project workflows and Google Drive/OneDrive refresh. [8]

## Global #24 (evaluated). Oracle PeopleSoft Campus Solutions and Oracle Student Cloud (Oracle)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Oracle Corporation |
| Headquarters | Redwood Shores, California, United States [1] |
| Company founded (year) | 1977 [1] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | Oracle Student Cloud was announced in 2014, with first-phase release planned for 2015; the original Campus Solutions product-line launch year is not publicly disclosed in the reviewed Oracle material (Campus Solutions 9.0 was reported as released in December 2006) [10] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Hybrid portfolio: PeopleSoft Campus Solutions is a web-based, on-premise or customer-hosted/IaaS deployment; Oracle Student Management and Student Financial Planning are Oracle Fusion Cloud SaaS; responsive browser/mobile access and a legacy Campus Mobile app are available [2] [5] [12] |
| Primary segments | Colleges, universities, community colleges, continuing-education providers, professional/graduate education, and institutions with complex or multi-entity academic models |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | Oracle's cloud-journey blueprint says more than 800 customers have used Campus Solutions over several decades (claim in the undated blueprint, accessed November 24, 2026); Oracle's 2022 release named Bowie State (6,000+ students), Butler Community College (7,000 students), Coppin State, Skidmore, and University of Pittsburgh as higher-education cloud customers [5] [11] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://www.oracle.com/government/education/higher-education/ |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://www.oracle.com/government/education/higher-education/student-cloud/ |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | https://docs.oracle.com/en/applications/peoplesoft/campus-solutions/index.html |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | No public pricing page; Oracle publishes list-price PDFs and sells through enterprise quotation/contracting |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | G2 PeopleSoft Campus Solutions: 3.7/5 from 91 reviews, page updated November 4, 2026; Capterra Oracle PeopleSoft: 4.1/5 from 283 reviews, last updated September 29, 2026; Gartner Peer Insights PeopleSoft Campus Solutions: 3.7/5 from 16 ratings, updated/viewed November 24, 2026; Apple App Store Oracle Fusion Applications: 3.7/5 from 452 ratings, viewed November 24, 2026; no verified Google Play rating for a dedicated Student app found [6] [7] [8] [20] |

### Overview

Oracle's higher-education portfolio deliberately combines two different generations of student technology. PeopleSoft Campus Solutions 9.2 is the mature, deeply configurable student information system (SIS) for recruitment, admissions, academic records, advising, financial aid, student accounts, advancement, and self-service. It can remain on premises or be moved to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) as hosted infrastructure. Oracle Student (also called Oracle Student Cloud or Fusion Cloud Student) is the cloud-native direction: Oracle Student Management for admissions, academics, advising, and student financials, plus Oracle Student Financial Planning (SFP) for financial aid [2] [5].

The distinction matters. Campus Solutions gives institutions direct access to code, database tables, and the PeopleSoft Integration Broker, while Student Management is SaaS with configuration, APIs, and Oracle-managed updates rather than customer-owned code. Oracle's 2026 strategy is coexistence rather than a forced migration: PeopleSoft support is rolling ten years through at least 2037, and Oracle Student is intended to earn adoption over time [2] [9]. Oracle acquired PeopleSoft in 2005 for approximately $10.3 billion, preserving a major enterprise-application installed base [1] [17].

### Platform Classification Explained

**Browser/web:** Campus Solutions is delivered through PeopleSoft's web and Fluid UI. The Student Homepage is a browser self-service hub for academic progress, records, finances, financial aid, classes, profile, and tasks; the same Fluid home appears when users sign in on a mobile device [13].

**Cloud hosting:** PeopleSoft may run on an institution's infrastructure, an Oracle implementation partner's infrastructure, or OCI. Oracle's own positioning says PeopleSoft can run on premises or in the cloud; OCI is an IaaS hosting option, not the same thing as SaaS [2] [5]. Oracle Student Management and SFP are natively hosted Fusion Cloud SaaS services on Oracle infrastructure. The current Fusion service description measures Student Management by Hosted FTE Student, Student Aid Eligibility by Student Aid Applicant, and SFP by Student Aid Recipient [19].

**Desktop client:** No separate end-user desktop application is required or documented. Administration is web-based; legacy implementation tools and local integration infrastructure may still exist in a customer-managed PeopleSoft deployment.

**Native mobile:** Campus Solutions documentation names **Campus Mobile**, built on Oracle ADF Mobile, with deployment to Android APK and iOS IPA. It supports student-facing mobile functions such as enrollment, schedules, grades, notifications, and progress, subject to licensing and configuration [12] [20]. The newer default is responsive Fluid web rather than a dedicated student-store app. Oracle Fusion Applications is a general native iOS/iPadOS app with 3.7/5 from 452 ratings, but the listing is primarily HCM/ERP and says available mobile flows depend on licensed and implemented applications; it is not evidence of a standalone Oracle Student parent/teacher app [20].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Campus Community, identity, and constituent data

The shared person/organization layer stores names, addresses, IDs, demographics, languages, ethnicity, religious preferences, health and identification attributes, participation data, FERPA controls, emergency contacts, and organization data. It includes U.S. SEVIS F/M and J-1 visa processing with DHS submissions/updates, plus the cross-portfolio “3Cs”: Communication Management, Checklist Management, and Comment Management [3] [4].

#### Recruiting, admissions, and enrollment management

Recruiting and Admissions captures requests for information, prospects, recruiters, regions, interests, events, communication plans, test data, transcripts, multiple applications, status history, program-specific requirements, automated evaluation, admission decisions, accept/decline, online deposit payment, Quick Enroll/Admit, and applicant self-service. Enrollment management sets hierarchical targets by institution, career, term, admit type, program, gender, and ethnicity and compares target versus actual enrollment [3] [4].

#### Student information and academic records

Student Records covers academic structure, course catalog, schedule of classes, student programs/plans/subplans, student activation, enrollment, repeat checking, transfer credit, student data tracking, attendance tracking, instructor workload, grades, academic statistics, enrollment verification, transcripts, graduation processing, and LMS integration [3] [4]. Oracle Student Management adds Curriculum Registry, multiple assessment types, credentials, structured learning paths, academic calendars, student results, sponsorships, and dynamic entities for consortia, multi-institution degrees, and exchanges [14].

#### Attendance, timetable, and examination scheduling

Attendance tracking is a delivered Student Records function. Schedule of Classes, meeting patterns, class search, class and exam schedules, enrollment appointments, instructor workload, and faculty schedules are supported. The reviewed documentation does not establish a separate automated master-scheduling engine; institutions can integrate specialist schedulers.

#### Grading, assessment, transcripts, and degree progress

PeopleSoft provides student grading, grade rosters, grade history, academic statistics, unofficial/official transcripts, enrollment verification, graduation application, and degree-progress reporting. Academic Advisement defines course lists, requirement groups, shared courses, exceptions, what-if scenarios, outstanding requirements, and advisement reports. Oracle Student adds configurable result sets and credentials; SFP adds a financial plan alongside academic choices [3] [13] [14] [15].

#### Learning management and homework

Campus Solutions does not present a full native LMS, homework workspace, or content-authoring product. It provides LMS integration and faculty links to LMS sites; homework, lessons, discussion, and content delivery require an external LMS [3] [4].

#### Communications and alerts

The 3Cs support targeted incoming/outgoing communications, checklists, comments, notes, due dates, status tracking, and constituent interactions across prospects, applicants, students, staff, alumni, donors, and organizations. Campus Mobile can reuse SMS or email notification; Oracle Student supports automated emails and alerts triggered by dates, actions, or events, while intelligent alerts surface academic and financial tasks. WhatsApp messaging is not documented as native [3] [14].

#### Student, faculty, applicant, and proxy portals

Campus Self Service provides applicant status and admission response; Student Center; Student Planner; enrollment shopping cart; add/drop/swap; class search; grades; transcripts; enrollment verification; graduation application; transfer-credit modeling; financial-aid award accept/decline; account inquiry; credit-card/eCheck payment profiles and payments; and Faculty Center access to rosters, grades, schedules, advisees, catalog, and LMS links. It also supports Community Directory, personal information, FERPA privacy, holds, checklists, and contributor-relations outreach. Oracle Student's Student Central provides personalized widgets, to-dos, applications, finances, academics, program links, and proxy/delegate access for a parent or other authorized person while preserving FERPA controls [4] [14].

#### Fees, billing, payments, and accounting

Student Financials calculates tuition and fees, maintains customer accounts, creates bills, supports payment plans, refunds, cashiering, collections, tax forms, and general-ledger interfaces. Self-service supports credit card and eCheck payments. Student Management extends this with pay-to-enroll, student accounts/invoicing, receipts, sponsorship credits, bills, invoices, learning packages, refunds, direct-bank payments, and population-based fee assessment; it depends on Oracle Financials for enterprise structures, General Ledger, Receivables, Payables, and Payments [3] [4] [14].

#### Financial aid

Campus Financial Aid processes applications, eligibility, need calculations, budgets, awards, packaging, disbursements, Direct Lending, FFELP, CommonLine/Common Record, Pell and Title IV, work-study, Canadian aid, and FISAP. Oracle SFP adds electronic document requests/submission, signatures, automated verification, C-code clearing, ISIR corrections, tailored cost of attendance, federal and non-federal packaging, configurable disbursement, COD/G5/CommonLine communication, credit-balance splitting, automated 10-step Return of Title IV, post-withdrawal and late disbursement, grant overpayment handling, real-time synchronization, and financial-aid analytics [3] [15].

#### Advancement, alumni, and fundraising

Contributor Relations includes constituent information, gifts and pledges, prospect management, events, campaigns, volunteers, memberships, planned giving, matching gifts, tribute/memorial gifts, acknowledgements, giving clubs, strategies, action plans, to-do lists, and outreach analysis. Alumni-facing self-service is included in the broader Campus Self Service audience, while recruiting/engagement/advancement marketing can be extended with Oracle CX [3] [4] [5].

#### Analytics, dashboards, and reporting

Delivered summary pages, enrollment-target reports, advisement reports, academic statistics, outreach reports, configurable queries, and PeopleSoft Insights/Pivot Grids support operational reporting. Oracle Student adds integrated dashboards and real-time insights for retention, recruitment, academic performance, and financial aid. This is strong enterprise reporting, but not a no-code report builder for nontechnical users [2] [5] [8].

#### AI and intelligent automation

Oracle Student markets proactive alerts, intelligent automation, automated financial-aid intervention, and predictive-style retention insights; SFP is marketed as self-correcting and able to automate up to 90% of the aid lifecycle [2] [15]. The June 2026 Quest roadmap says delivered AI agents will not be retrofitted directly into Campus Solutions; customers can use PeopleTools 8.63 MCP capabilities to build AI experiences. Thus, AI is more mature in the cloud direction than in the legacy SIS [9].

#### Government reporting and compliance workflows

Native compliance includes SEVIS/DHS visa processing, U.S. Department of Education financial-aid regulation updates, Direct Loan/Pell/COD, Title IV, FISAP, Canadian aid, and international legislative updates such as HESA, UCAS, TCSI/HEIMS, and other country-specific requirements in the roadmap [3] [5].

#### Integrations, APIs, and interoperability

PeopleSoft provides Integration Broker, web services, EDI Manager, LMS integration, Oracle Integration Cloud options, and delivered integration to SFP. The 2025 release made Campus Solutions the first SIS certified on 1EdTech Edu-API, initially provisioning persons, classes, programs, academic periods/sessions, organizations, and class enrollments for LMS, parking, housing, and other ecosystem applications [16]. Oracle Student Management has a public REST API with OAuth, JSON, batch actions, CORS, JWT, metadata, SOAP support, and hundreds of documented resource families [18].

#### Security, privacy, and accessibility

PeopleSoft supports role-based security, FERPA privacy controls, data masking/privacy frameworks, configurable security, and mobile service-operation security. Student Management uses abstract/job/data roles, LDAP synchronization, role mappings, access history, and Security Console controls [5] [17]. Oracle's cloud compliance catalogue lists ISO/IEC 27001/27017/27018/27701, SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS and other frameworks, but warns that attestations are service- and region-specific; this should not be read as a product-specific certification without contract evidence [17]. Oracle pages reviewed did not provide a dedicated COPPA, India DPDP, or product-specific FERPA certification claim. No public product security incident was identified in the sources reviewed through November 24, 2026.

#### Modules not native to the reviewed product scope

There is no documented native transport routing, library, hostel/boarding, inventory/asset, behavior/discipline, pastoral-care, or special-education/safeguarding module. Health and medical data can be stored as Campus Community attributes, but this is not a clinical or school-nurse system. HR, staff, and payroll are separate PeopleSoft HCM/Oracle Cloud HCM products, not Campus Solutions modules [2] [3].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Two-speed modernization:** Institutions can retain customized Campus Solutions while adopting Oracle Student Financial Planning or OCI hosting incrementally rather than replacing the SIS in one “big bang” project [5].
- **1EdTech Edu-API certification:** The 2025 certification creates a standards-based path for exchanging person, class, program, term, organization, and enrollment data [16].
- **Dynamic entities:** Oracle Student can model systems, consortia, multi-institution degrees, and exchanges without re-implementing the student system [2] [14].
- **Highly automated financial aid:** SFP combines rule-based packaging, document automation, reconciliation, disbursement, and Return of Title IV workflows [15].
- **Configuration over customization:** Student Cloud's core frameworks let business users maintain rules and workflows; Campus Solutions supplies extensibility through PeopleTools, Fluid, Activity Guides, notification, search, and configuration frameworks [2] [5].
- **Lifelong-learning support:** Oracle Student spans traditional degrees, continuing education, non-credit programs, variable course lengths, credentials, and multiple academic models [2] [14].
- **FERPA-aware proxy access:** Delegates can complete selected transactions for a learner while the institution retains privacy control [2] [14].

### Pricing Details

There is no public Oracle pricing webpage with tiers, implementation bundles, or a standard SaaS quote. The official **PeopleSoft Component Global Price List dated June 11, 2026** lists Campus Solutions at **245** for the component license and **53.90** for software update and support, measured per **FTE Student**; the PDF table does not explicitly label a currency, so these are list-price figures rather than a guaranteed USD contract price. Oracle defines FTE Student as each full-time student plus each part-time student counted as 25% of an FTE [19].

Oracle's current Fusion service description is also unit-based, not a public rate card: Student Management is per Hosted FTE Student, Student Aid Eligibility per Student Aid Applicant, and Student Financial Planning per Student Aid Recipient, with separate test environments and optional services. Implementation, integration, data conversion, training, support level, OCI hosting, Oracle Financials/HCM/CX dependencies, and local tax/contract terms are quote-based [19]. G2 says pricing is unavailable; Gartner reports subscription pricing varies with users, modules, support, customization, integration, training, and implementation but gives no reliable numeric range [6] [8]. Checked November 24, 2026.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Campus Solutions supports PeopleSoft Integration Broker, REST/JSON and SOAP web services, EDI Manager, Oracle Integration Cloud, Oracle Financials/ERP/HCM/CX, Student Financial Planning, payment processing, and LMS links. Edu-API is the clearest verified open standard and was certified in 2025. Oracle Student Management documents public REST resources, OAuth, JWT, JSON, batch actions, CORS, metadata, and SOAP. The reviewed sources do not verify OneRoster, LTI certification, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, or a dedicated marketplace; these should be treated as possible partner integrations rather than native certifications. Payment support is documented for credit cards, eCheck/direct bank payments, and Oracle Payments, but no named third-party gateway was verified [4] [16] [18].

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Role- and data-based security, LDAP synchronization, Security Console, role mappings, access history, FERPA privacy flags, proxy access, and configurable mobile-service security are documented. Oracle's cloud compliance catalogue includes ISO 27001-family controls and SOC reports, but availability depends on service and region. PeopleSoft's strongest compliance coverage is operational: SEVIS/DHS, U.S. Department of Education aid rules, Title IV, Pell/COD, FISAP, Canadian aid, and international reporting. Oracle does not publicly publish a single Student Cloud data-hosting region list or a product-specific COPPA/DPDP certification on the reviewed pages; GDPR/DPDP suitability remains a customer/contract assessment. No publicly reported incident was found in this review set through November 24, 2026 [3] [5] [17].

### Strengths

- Unusually broad higher-education lifecycle coverage, including admissions, records, advising, aid, billing, advancement, and self-service.
- Mature academic and regulatory depth for large universities and multi-campus institutions.
- Extensive configuration/customization, integration, and data-model control in Campus Solutions.
- A credible incremental cloud route: OCI, SFP, Oracle Student, ERP, HCM, CX, and Edu-API can be adopted in stages.
- Strong financial-aid automation and complex-program support in Oracle Student Financial Planning.
- Long support horizon through at least 2037 reduces forced-migration risk [9].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

G2 users praise breadth, reliability, customization, and centralization but report a steep learning curve, outdated-feeling interface, upgrade complexity, and integration difficulty; its overall rating was only 3.7/5 as viewed November 24, 2026 [6]. Capterra reviewers cite unintuitive navigation, slow or peak-load performance, costly/effort-heavy customization, glitches after upgrades, limited mobile ease, and dependence on specialist IT support [7]. Gartner reviewers like the integrated student lifecycle but say reporting is too technical for ordinary users and that navigation/training costs erode value [8]. The biggest strategic weakness is portfolio complexity: institutions must choose between maintaining a heavily customized legacy SIS and adopting a newer SaaS product that is still maturing, while HR, LMS, transport, library, housing, and safeguarding capabilities require separate systems.

### Key Milestones

- **1977:** Larry Ellison, Bob Miner, and Ed Oates found Software Development Laboratories, Oracle's predecessor [1].
- **1989:** Oracle moves headquarters to Redwood Shores, California [1].
- **2004:** Oracle announces a definitive agreement to buy PeopleSoft for approximately $10.3 billion [17].
- **2005:** Oracle completes the PeopleSoft acquisition and adds the PeopleSoft enterprise application portfolio [1] [17].
- **2006:** PeopleSoft Enterprise Campus Solutions 9.0 is reported as released in December 2006; Oracle Student Cloud had not yet been announced [10].
- **2013:** Oracle adds Campus Solutions mobile capabilities for enrollment, schedules, grades, notifications, and academic progress [20].
- **2014:** Oracle announces Oracle Student Cloud; first phase was planned for calendar 2015 with enrollment, payment, and assessment [10].
- **2019:** St. Petersburg College moves Campus Solutions and related PeopleSoft applications from on premises to OCI [4].
- **2022:** Oracle names higher-education cloud customers including Bowie State, Butler Community College, Coppin State, Skidmore, and University of Pittsburgh [11].
- **2025:** Campus Solutions becomes the first SIS announced as certified on the 1EdTech Edu-API standard [16].
- **2026:** Oracle extends rolling PeopleSoft support through at least 2037; the June 2026 roadmap emphasizes security, regulatory updates, Fluid UX, cloud readiness, and configuration [2] [9].
- **2026:** Oracle's current Fusion service description prices Student Management, Student Aid Eligibility, and SFP by hosted student/applicant/recipient units, while the PeopleSoft global list publishes Campus Solutions per FTE Student [19].

| Field | Detail |
