No official Gibbon iOS or Android app was found, so App Store/Play Store ratings are not applicable. [11] [12] |

### Overview

Gibbon is a free, GPL-3.0, teacher-created school information and learning platform. It brings student records, lesson planning, homework, assessment, attendance, timetables, communication, library, activities and school finance into one browser application. Teachers, students, parents and administrators use the same installation, with permissions controlling what each role can see and do. [1] [4] [10]

The project began at International College Hong Kong in October 2010. Ross Parker describes building it after finding existing systems too rigid and poorly suited to international/IB-school workflows; the early project grew from a prior system called Muse. In 2023, copyright moved from Parker to the non-profit Gibbon Foundation. Gibbon Education Limited separately sells support, server management, certification and Catalyst. [2] [3] [13]

Gibbon is a self-hosted alternative to SaaS MIS products, but the school owns the infrastructure and operational responsibility. Official materials provide a global-use map but no independently audited adoption totals. [1] [5]

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser access:** Gibbon is a PHP, CSS and JavaScript web application using MySQL. Users access the installation through a domain or server URL in a browser. [5] [6]
* **Cloud hosting:** Cloud is an infrastructure choice, not a Gibbon SaaS service. Schools may use a VPS, shared host or cloud server; Gibbon Education Limited can provision and maintain virtual servers as a paid service. [5] [9]
* **Desktop client:** None identified. The product is a server-hosted web application, not a Windows/macOS desktop package. [5]
* **On-premise/self-hosted:** Explicitly supported through Apache 2 or Nginx, PHP and MySQL 8 or compatible MariaDB. [5] [6]
* **Native mobile apps:** No official “Gibbon” iOS or Android app is listed; the current approach is responsive web access. [8] [12] [13]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Planner and learning management

Planner supports Smart Blocks, rich multimedia lesson plans, units, curriculum outcomes, homework assignment, online work collection, attendance within a lesson, notes and teacher feedback. It can expose lessons to students, parents and guests. The Resources database catalogs school-wide materials by category, purpose, tags and year group; Departments organize Learning Areas, scope and sequence, and shared documents. [4]

#### Student information and records

Students consolidates profiles, family links, academic, behavioral, medical and SEN alerts, photographs and a Fast Student Finder. User Admin handles families, enrolment, medical data and updates. Form Groups organize tutor/tutee relationships. Data Updater routes staff and parent personal or medical changes into an administrator review queue. [4]

#### Admissions and enrollment

Application Form provides public online applications, priority-based queues, accept/reject decisions, automatic user-account creation and family links for accepted students. Class Enrolment, an extension, lets parents enroll children into classes; Course Selection supports student course choices and can feed a timetable engine. [4] [8]

#### Attendance

Attendance can be taken for form groups or individual students, with recent/full history, future absences, parent visibility and emergency-evacuation absence reports. Lesson Planner attendance can be compared with school attendance. Activities can generate attendee lists and printable registers. [4]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

Timetable displays individual student and teacher schedules, room location and room telephone information. Timetable Admin defines courses, classes and enrolment, while facilities can be booked. Google Calendar events can overlay school and personal calendars. v29/v30 releases added a redesigned timetable and further timetable improvements. [4] [14]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Markbook records continuous academic data across subjects, exposes selected results to students and parents, and links to Planner submissions. Teachers can return marked work, rubrics and voice recordings. Rubrics track outcomes over time. Formal Assessment captures internal/external tests, includes CATS by default, supports additional tests and can calculate value-added scores. Crowd Assessment enables peer review and discussion. There is no documented enterprise examination-office suite. [4]

#### Report cards and transcripts

The current core feature catalog emphasizes Markbook, Tracking and Formal Assessment rather than a separately named report-card/transcript module. Tracking graphs data by student or cohort and exports selected assessment data to a spreadsheet. The open-source Mastery Transcript extension can create, track and issue credits with an evidenced portfolio; it is an extension, not evidence of a universal core transcript engine. [4] [8]

#### Communication

Messenger sends targeted email, SMS or Message Wall communications to flexible groups such as classes, forms and activities. Messages can include links, files or HTML from the Resource Bank; the Message Wall can produce individualized daily bulletins. v28 added a mailing-list feature. No native WhatsApp or push-notification channel is documented. [4] [14]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

There are role-based dashboards for parents, students and staff rather than separate commercial apps. Parents can view attendance, academic progress and calendars; students access lessons, homework, resources and assessment where permissions allow; teachers use planning, profiles, attendance and Markbook. The module framework supports Parent Dashboard, Student Dashboard and Staff Dashboard hooks. [1] [4] [19]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Finance manages fees, billing schedules and invoicees, and generates/emails invoices, receipts and payment reminders. It tracks payments, lists outstanding family balances, and manages expense requests through approval, payment and reimbursement. The official page does not document a general ledger, payroll accounting, card gateway catalogue or native online payment processor. [4] [20]

#### HR, staff and payroll

Staff supports job openings and applications, conversion of applicants into staff accounts, a staff directory, role-based detail visibility and contract tracking. Staff can update their own personal information through Data Updater. No native payroll, benefits, timekeeping or full HRIS module is listed in the current core feature catalog. [4]

#### Transport and trips

There is no native transport fleet, route, GPS or bus-payment module. Trip Planner supports trip planning and approvals; Activities handles applications, participant lists and off-site attendance registers. [4] [8]

#### Library

Library catalogs books, films, computers, cameras and other loanable items; manages loans and inventory; lets students browse items; and can share reading records with teachers. v29 also improved the Library view in Student Profile. [4] [14]

#### Hostel and boarding

No dedicated native hostel/dormitory or boarding module is documented in the current official core or extension catalog. Capterra’s feature summary does not list it; older user feedback mentioned “dorm” as a feature, so schools should verify whether that reflects an older add-on or local customization rather than current core. [8] [12]

#### Inventory and assets

Library can track and loan items such as computers and cameras, and Resources catalogs teaching materials. No organization-wide asset-register, depreciation or procurement module is documented. [4]

#### Health and medical

Medical information and alerts are part of student profiles, with parent/staff updates through Data Updater. Nurse workflows, immunization schedules and medication administration are not advertised. [2] [4]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Behaviour records positive and negative notes, school-defined descriptors and severity, comments, follow-up, form-group summaries and profile alerts. Student Alerts was added as a v30 core module, and v30 introduced a Pastoral heading. House Points is an extension for tracking house awards; Badges supports academic, social and athletic awards. [4] [8] [14]

#### Special education and safeguarding

Individual Needs supports designated learning needs, individual education plans, longitudinal archiving, Planner integration and differentiation indicators. SEN alerts are included in Student Profiles. Gibbon does not publicly claim a dedicated safeguarding case-management, statutory child-protection or formal IEP compliance suite. [4]

#### Alumni and fundraising

The Alumni extension accepts alumni registrations and links them to existing user accounts. There is no native fundraising, donor CRM, campaign, gift-processing or advancement module listed. [8]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Tracking graphs Markbook and Formal Assessment data for individuals and cohorts and exports selected data for offline analysis. Query Builder creates/runs SQL statements and exports results to Excel; the Catalyst license unlocks 151 maintained queries and 31 commands. Role-based dashboards and Fast Finder provide operational views, but there is no advertised warehouse, predictive analytics layer or executive BI product. [4] [8] [9]

#### AI features

No production AI assistant, generative AI, predictive model or AI writing/reporting feature is documented on the official website, documentation, extensions page or current release notes. Schools can build custom modules, but that is development work, not a native AI capability. [4] [8] [19]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

No dedicated state-census, Ed-Fi, SIF, OneRoster or government-reporting package is advertised. Query Builder and exports can support local reporting, but statutory mapping and submission remain a school responsibility unless a partner builds a custom module. [8] [19]

#### Mobile web experience

Recent releases replaced older front-end libraries with HTMX and Alpine.js and describe more app-like page loads; the official Extend page lists a responsive, mobile-friendly theme. [8] [14]

#### Integrations and APIs

Google integration supports OAuth-based single sign-on and Google Calendar API overlays. The Moodle module exposes Gibbon users and courses to Moodle through external-database authentication/enrollment and scheduled synchronization. Module hooks, database access, exports and custom PHP modules provide extensibility, but the public materials do not document a versioned REST API or developer marketplace. [17] [18] [19]

#### Security and privacy controls

Schools control data location because Gibbon is self-hosted. The documentation recommends HTTPS, SSH keys, restricted access and production server hardening. Role/action permissions, module enablement, update notifications, backups and a responsible-disclosure process are documented. Gibbon’s security policy says older versions are not directly supported and advises use of the latest stable release. [5] [7] [15]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **Teacher-designed workflows:** The product originated inside a school and models planning, teaching and assessment. [13]
* **Role/action permission model:** Each module action can be assigned to roles, enabling granular configuration without changing core code. [19]
* **Module and theme extensibility:** Schools can install, update, uninstall or build modules and themes, with hooks into dashboards, Student Profile and Planner. [7] [8] [19]
* **Catalyst Query Builder:** A paid license supplies 151 maintained queries and 31 commands, while the free Query Builder supports SQL execution and Excel export. [8] [9]
* **Internationalization:** The project supports right-to-left text, UTF-8 and a volunteer translation system; the current homepage says 26 actively translated languages. [1] [2]
* **Self-hosted ownership:** Schools choose server, backups and data location. [5]
* **Open-source sustainability model:** The 2023 Foundation transfer separates non-profit core stewardship from optional paid support and hosting. [3]

### Pricing Details

The core Gibbon software is free to download and licensed under GNU GPL-3.0. Schools pay their own server, domain, backup, administration and implementation costs unless they contract for help. [5] [10]

The official Gibbon Education Limited page, checked 24 November 2026, lists a **Gibbon Catalyst License at USD $150 per installation for one year**. Multi-site discounts are automatically applied. Catalyst unlocks the Query Builder library of 151 useful queries and 31 commands. Server provisioning, installation, configuration, maintenance, contract support and ad hoc support are quote-based; no public hosting rate card or implementation fee is shown. [9]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Documented integrations are Google OAuth/SSO and Google Calendar API, and a Moodle module that syncs users and courses through Moodle’s external database authentication and enrollment functions. Gibbon’s module hooks and GPL source support custom connectors, CSV/spreadsheet import/export and local database integration. [17] [18] [19]

No public evidence was found for 1EdTech certification, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Microsoft 365, WhatsApp, payment-gateway certification or an official public REST API; the extension page is a curated catalogue rather than a commercial integration marketplace.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Gibbon publishes no SOC 2, ISO 27001, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR or India DPDP Act certification claim. Self-hosting can help a school meet data-residency and privacy obligations, but compliance depends on configuration, contracts, access controls, backups, subprocessors and local law. [5] [15]

The security policy provides responsible disclosure guidance, supports the current stable version and uses a six-month release cycle, with mid-version patches for high-severity issues. NIST’s NVD lists nine Gibbon CVE records through 27 May 2025, including CSRF, XSS, PHP deserialization, server-side template injection, directory traversal, arbitrary file write and session-fixation issues affecting older versions. [15] [16]

The v30.0.02 and v30.0.03 GitHub releases in November 2026 were explicitly marked essential security updates. The v30.0.03 notice says Gibbon had no known data breach, credits responsible-disclosure researchers and advises PHP 8.2+ preparation for the next patch. [14]

### Strengths

* Free GPL-3.0 core removes license and per-student fees and permits modification and self-hosting. [1] [10]
* Strong teacher-centric breadth across planning, homework, assessment, attendance, communication and timetables. [4] [13]
* Granular permissions, multilingual support and extensible modules suit international and resource-constrained schools. [1] [19]
* Schools retain control of data location, backups and upgrade cadence rather than being locked into a SaaS tenancy. [5]
* A Foundation, active GitHub development and paid support ecosystem support ongoing maintenance. [3] [8] [14]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

* Adoption scale is not publicly quantified; the official map is voluntary. [1]
* Self-hosting transfers installation, hardening, backups, upgrades and monitoring to the school; documentation says an administrator is normally required. [5]
* There is no native iOS/Android app, no documented push or WhatsApp channel, and no public evidence of a full state-reporting or standards-certified interoperability layer. [8] [13]
* Current core documentation does not show payroll, transport fleet, hostel, fundraising, enterprise asset management or dedicated report-card/transcript operations. [4] [8]
* Independent review evidence is thin. G2 has one review (3.5/5), whose reviewer praised usability/UX but reported that the system was slow and “somewhat frozen.” [11]
* Capterra’s two reviews average 4.5/5 for overall value, but the weaker sub-scores are ease of use 3.5/5 and customer service 3.5/5. One reviewer said learning it was somewhat difficult; another said the frontend, finance workflow and mobile experience could be improved. [12]
* Security maintenance requires discipline: NIST records vulnerabilities in older versions, and November 2026 notices called for essential patching. [14] [16]

### Key Milestones

* **2010:** Ross Parker founded Gibbon in October at International College Hong Kong after finding existing school systems too rigid and difficult to use. [2] [13]
* **2013:** The public project history recorded v7.1.00, the seventh version, released in December. [13]
* **2014:** An independent project history described 24 core modules, five free add-ons and active use at Parker’s college and partner school. [13]
* **2023:** The Gibbon Foundation was established; copyright of the codebase transferred from Parker to the Foundation. [3]
* **2024:** v28 refreshed the front end with HTMX and Alpine.js, added Activities registration and mailing lists, and moved core-module ownership visibly to the Foundation. [14]
* **2025:** v29 redesigned the timetable, improved Student Profile library views, added Petty Cash and Behaviour observations, and strengthened CSRF/nonce handling. [14]
* **2025–2026:** Foundation-maintained extensions expanded, including Alumni, Query Builder, Trip Planner, Higher Education and Flexible Learning. [8]
* **20 November 2026:** v30.0.00 marked 15 years of development, added Calendar and Student Alerts as core modules and reported 29 production languages in its release notes. [14]
* **13–18 November 2026:** v30.0.02 and v30.0.03 were released as essential security updates; the latter said v31 work was paused while security work continued. [14]

## India #11 (evaluated). Teachmint (Teachmint Technologies Pvt. Ltd.)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Teachmint Technologies Pvt. Ltd.; founders Mihir Gupta, Payoj Jain, Divyansh Bordia and Anshuman Kumar [1] [2] |
| Headquarters | Bengaluru, Karnataka, India; the company also lists offices in Delaware, Singapore, Manila and Dubai [1] |
| Company founded (year) | 2020; PR Newswire gives May 2020 [2] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | 2020 mobile-first teaching app; exact public launch date is not disclosed. The institutional product Teachmint for Institute launched in July 2021 [3] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud-backed SaaS/web plus native Android and iOS apps; hybrid classroom hardware through Teachmint X. No vendor-documented on-premise deployment or native desktop client found [1] [4] [5] |
| Primary segments | K-12 schools, coaching/tutoring, higher education, individual educators and edtech providers [1] [3] |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | Teachmint’s current Classroom Platform page claims 20M+ users served, 10+ countries and 17 languages; the About page says 10+ countries and 90+ languages. A 2021 company claim reported 10M+ teachers/students in 25 countries and 4,000+ institutes [1] [2] [4] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://www.teachmint.com/en-us |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://www.teachmint.com/en-us/products/classroom-platform |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | https://support.teachmint.com/ (URL verified; no crawlable public article content was returned) |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | https://www.teachmint.com/pricing (current page is a product/demo page, not a software price list) |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | Viewed 24 Nov 2026: G2 seller profile 4.9/5 from 52 reviews; Capterra 4.8/5 from 74; Google Play listing 4.6/5 from 188K reviews (the detailed review widget showed 4.5/5 from 182K); Apple App Store India 4.0/5 from 1.8K ratings [5] [6] [7] [8] |

### Overview

Teachmint began as a pandemic-era, mobile-first, video-first teaching app for tutors and teachers to create virtual classrooms, run live lessons, share notes, assign work, take attendance and collect fees. It then added Teachmint for Institute for schools and colleges, and by late 2026 its public positioning is centered on Teachmint X: an AI-powered interactive flat panel plus connected classroom software, EduAI, VisionX device management and Share X. The platform is relevant to Indian schools because it combines classroom delivery, student engagement and institutional workflows rather than acting only as a video-conferencing tool [3] [4].

The company raised $3.5M/$4M seed funding in October 2020, $16.5M Series A in May 2021, $20M pre-Series B in July 2021 and $78M Series B in October 2021. TechCrunch reported more than $115M raised and a $500M valuation in 2021; an independent funding database totals $118M across four rounds [9] [10]. Teachmint acquired Teachmore in 2021, acqui-hired Teachee’s Indian team in December 2021, and is reported to have acquired MyClassCampus in January 2022; the latter is not confirmed by a current Teachmint release, so it should be treated as a secondary-source claim [2] [11].

### Platform Classification Explained

- **Browser/cloud:** Teachmint provides web access and describes cloud-synchronized whiteboards, cloud storage for teaching materials and recordings, and online dashboards. Its privacy policy says data may be stored in India and transferred abroad subject to applicable law; it does not name a cloud provider [4] [12].
- **Mobile:** The Android app is **Teachmint AI Connected Classes**; it supports live video, chat, screen sharing, recordings, homework, quizzes, materials, attendance and progress reporting. The iOS app is **Teachmint : AI study app**. A separate **Whiteboard by Teachmint** Android listing and **Share X by Teachmint** iOS listing also exist [7] [8] [13].
- **Hardware/hybrid:** Teachmint X panels run Android 16 on current product pages, are Google EDLA-certified, support Google Play apps, NFC/multi-user sign-in, cloud lesson saving and wireless sharing. This is a device-plus-cloud hybrid classroom model, not an on-premise ERP [4] [14].
- **Desktop/on-premise:** Capterra lists web, Android and iPhone/iPad deployment. No current public evidence of a separately installed Windows/macOS desktop client, self-hosted edition or on-premise school server was found [5].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment
The legacy school suite had an Admission Management portal that passed admitted-student information into the SIS, with customizable criteria and a website/CRM lead-management workflow. The current admissions page explicitly says the standalone admission module is no longer available, so this is a historical capability rather than a current purchase assumption [15] [16].

#### Student information and records
The institute product supported a Student Information System, centralized student records, student management, ID cards, certificates and downloadable documents. Current classroom software still advertises student management, learner progress and stakeholder visibility, but a full public SIS schema is not documented [3] [4] [5].

#### Attendance
Current Teachmint X supports digital attendance, and the panel’s AI camera can recognize students from verified profile images, permit corrections before submission and reduce proxy attendance. The mobile app also advertises automatic attendance tracking; staff attendance existed in the older ERP description [4] [7] [14].

#### Timetable and master scheduling
Teachmint supports live-class scheduling and lesson planning. The older commercial package listed automated timetable generation and yearly calendars, but the current product pages do not document a full conflict-aware master-scheduling engine [4] [17].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations
The active classroom product supports tests, quizzes, question banks, assignments, automatic grading/attendance claims, submission tracking and learning-gap analysis. Digital content includes a 20 lakh-plus question bank. The former institute package included assessments and exam management [4] [7] [18].

#### Report cards and transcripts
The Report Card Generation page describes end-to-end exam scheduling, marks updating, customizable titles and signatures, parent/teacher visibility, printable output and bulk downloads. No public evidence of a separately maintained transcript, credit or university academic-record module was found [19].

#### Learning management and homework
The strongest current module is the LMS/classroom workflow: live classes, recordings, notes, PDFs, videos, cloud materials, lesson plans, homework, quizzes, class recaps, sharing and engagement tracking. Teachmint’s content library claims 520+ hours, 9K+ Hindi/English learning modules, NCERT mapping, offline content and 20L+ questions [4] [18].

#### Communication
Current tools include teacher-student chat, notices, announcements, live-class chat and sharing with students and parents. The older ERP page describes broadcasts for annual day, PTA meetings and fee due dates. Public materials do not verify native SMS, email gateway, WhatsApp parent messaging or Paytm/Razorpay messaging integrations; a G2 reviewer’s WhatsApp reference was to customer support, not necessarily a product channel [4] [5] [6].

#### Parent, student and teacher portals
The platform has a shared admin dashboard and a single teacher/student app, with parent visibility described in the legacy school-management page. The current public app is positioned primarily for teachers and students; no separate, role-specific parent app or staff app is publicly identified [4] [7] [16].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting
Historically, Teachmint offered fee collection, online payments, receipts, reminders and 20-plus filtered fee reports. The current official fee page says the standalone fee-management solution is no longer available. No current evidence verifies GST invoicing, UPI, Razorpay, Paytm, Tally or a live accounting ledger, so these India-specific capabilities should not be assumed in 2026 [5] [20].

#### HR, staff and payroll
The older school page describes a staff repository from joining to relieving, credentials/documents, staff attendance, leave tracking and access rights. Payroll processing, statutory payroll, recruiting and appraisal workflows are not publicly documented [16].

#### Transport
Transport management appeared in a third-party description of the former Advanced package, but current official pages do not explain routes, vehicles, GPS, stops or fee linkage. Treat it as legacy/uncorroborated rather than a current native module [17].

#### Library
No current official evidence of cataloging, circulation, barcode/RFID or library fines was found.

#### Hostel and boarding
Hostel management appeared in the former Advanced package reported by SoftwareFinder, but no current official details on rooms, wardens, meals or boarding fees were found [17].

#### Inventory and assets
No current public evidence of procurement, stock, fixed assets, purchase orders or asset depreciation was found.

#### Health and medical
No current public evidence of nurse/clinic, immunization, medical records or incident workflows was found.

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care
An independent listing mentions behavior monitoring, but Teachmint’s public product pages do not detail discipline cases, counseling, safeguarding or pastoral workflows [21].

#### Special education and safeguarding
Teachmint advertises age-appropriate, safe AI answers and Google Play data controls, but no public special-education plan/IEP, child-safeguarding case management or mandated-reporting module was verified [4] [7].

#### Alumni and fundraising
No current public evidence of alumni relations, donations, campaigns or fundraising management was found.

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting
Current analytics cover classroom/student performance, teacher activity, device usage, homework, attendance and quiz insights. Legacy ERP pages described customizable stakeholder reports and 20-plus fee reports; CBSE Result Analyser accepts a board text file and exports performance reports to Excel [4] [16] [22].

#### AI features
EduAI provides AI Studio content, AI whiteboards, Ask Anything, lesson plans, quiz and homework generation, math/equation solving, summaries/class recaps, mindmaps, voice commands, OCR and text-to-speech. The privacy policy also names legacy GYD AI, lecture Q&A, EduBits, AI tutor courses and AI summaries/transcripts; it says AI features are optional, consent-gated and use Google to generate responses without sharing names, marks, attendance or original files [4] [12].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance
Teachmint historically advertised automated government-compliance reports and current content is mapped to NCERT; the site also offers a CBSE Result Analyser. I found no public Teachmint documentation verifying UDISE+, APAAR ID, CBSE/ICSE/state-board report-card templates, NEP 2020 Holistic Progress Cards, or higher-education NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE reporting. CBSE’s own HPC guidance defines a multidimensional, cognitive/affective/socio-emotional/psychomotor card, which is more specific than Teachmint’s generic customizable report-card claim [19] [22] [23].

#### Mobile apps
Native Android and iOS delivery is verified. Android shows 10M+ downloads and a Nov. 5, 2026 update; iOS supports iPhone/iPad and lists in-app GYD and AI-tutor purchases. The current app includes live classes, recordings, notes, assignments, quizzes, chat, announcements, attendance and reports [7] [8].

#### Integrations and APIs
Google EDLA provides Play Store access; Teachmint’s panel FAQ names Google Meet, Zoom, YouTube and other LMS apps as usable third-party apps. The privacy policy documents YouTube Data API scopes. No public REST API, webhook documentation, marketplace, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever or ClassLink certification was found [12] [14].

#### Security and privacy
Teachmint states ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 certification, encryption, firewalls, need-to-know access, India storage with possible international transfers, consent management and deletion/access rights. Google Play reports encryption in transit and deletion requests. No public SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR certification or security-incident disclosure was found; DPDP Act readiness is not expressly claimed, so it remains unverified [1] [7] [12].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **EduAI embedded in the board:** Produces curriculum/grade-aware lessons, quizzes, homework, summaries and explanations without leaving the classroom [4].
- **VisionX device management:** Centrally monitors classroom feeds, audio/screen activity, app access, OTA updates, alerts and device settings [4] [14].
- **Face-recognition attendance:** The panel camera can recognize verified student images and allow teacher corrections before submission [14].
- **Click X response clickers:** Student clickers provide 100% participation claims, live quiz responses and accuracy/attempt insights [14].
- **Google EDLA hardware:** Gives the panel Play Store/Google-services access with enterprise security controls [4] [14].
- **NCERT-mapped bilingual content:** Hindi/English notes, video, practice questions, offline content and topic-level grouping support Indian curricula [18].

### Pricing Details

No current public software price card or per-student/per-school ERP price was found; Teachmint’s pricing page is a demo/product page and the vendor asks buyers to engage sales. SoftwareFinder reports custom pricing, while Capterra displays a third-party $5 per user per year figure that is not confirmed by Teachmint and may reflect legacy software [5] [17].

The current public hardware catalog lists Teachmint X panels at INR 110,000 for 65-inch, INR 130,000 or INR 150,000 for 75-inch variants, and INR 170,000 for 86-inch, viewed 24 Nov 2026; each includes the Teachmint X ecosystem. The iOS app lists GYD Max at INR 259/month or INR 1,599/year, plus AI-tutor purchases of INR 100-199. Installation/training and 365-day support are advertised, but software implementation fees are not published [8] [14] [24].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Teachmint has practical device-level interoperability through Google EDLA, Play Store apps, Google Meet, Zoom and YouTube, plus a documented YouTube Data API use case. It does not publicly claim OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever or ClassLink certification; there is no public API reference, webhook guide, SSO/SCIM guide or marketplace. Legacy payment and accounting integrations such as UPI/Razorpay/Paytm/Tally were not verified in current documentation. This supports a basic-integrations score, not an open-standards score [12] [14] [17].

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The About page claims ISO 27001 and Google EDLA certification. Teachmint’s privacy policy describes encryption, firewalls, restricted access, security monitoring, consent, deletion/access rights and India-based processing with possible cross-border transfers. Google Play states data is encrypted in transit and deletion can be requested [1] [7] [12].

There is no public evidence in the reviewed materials of SOC 2, FERPA, COPPA or GDPR certification, and no public incident disclosure was found. The policy references India’s Information Technology Act and Data Protection Rules but does not expressly say that Teachmint is DPDP Act-ready. Schools should therefore request a current DPA, subprocessor list, retention schedule, breach-notification terms, child-data controls and DPDP contractual commitments before procurement.

### Strengths

- Broad evolution from live teaching and LMS into a hardware-plus-cloud classroom ecosystem.
- Strong Indian-market fit through mobile-first delivery, Hindi/English content, NCERT mapping, CBSE result analysis and vernacular/global-language support.
- Distinctive, production AI features embedded in lesson preparation and classroom hardware.
- Native Android/iOS reach, cloud recordings and live-class continuity.
- Large dated adoption evidence: 4,000+ institutes and 10M+ users in 2021, plus a current 20M+ user claim.
- High independent ratings: G2 4.9/5 and Capterra 4.8/5, with reviewers commonly praising ease of use and breadth [5] [6] [9].

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Product scope is in transition: official pages say standalone admissions and fee management are no longer available, creating migration and procurement risk for schools expecting a classic ERP [15] [20].
- Public pricing is opaque; current software pricing, implementation fees and enterprise limits require a quote.
- Interoperability is weakly documented: no public standards certifications, open API, marketplace or verified Tally/payment-gateway connectors.
- Users report performance/stability problems, delayed or unresolved support, limited customization and constrained integrations; SoftwareFinder summarizes crashes/slow response, while Capterra notes confusing edits, rigid reports and support-ticket friction [5] [17].
- Apple reviewers cite broken UI/layout, test-upload friction and lack of dark mode; Google Play reviews cite AI-tutor limitations, missing library visibility, poll bugs and paid recordings [7] [8].
- Several requested India compliance functions—UDISE+, APAAR, NEP 2020 HPC, GST, state-board templates and NAAC/NBA/NIRF/AISHE—are not publicly verified.

### Key Milestones

- **2020:** Teachmint founded in May by four IIT alumni; pandemic-era mobile teaching app launched; seed funding reported at $3.5M/$4M in October [2] [10].
- **May 2021:** $16.5M Series A led by Learn Capital, with reported rapid tutor/teacher adoption [3] [10].
- **July 2021:** $20M pre-Series B; Teachmint for Institute launched for schools and colleges; TechCrunch reported 1M+ teachers and 25M live classes consumed in the prior month [3].
- **October 2021:** $78M Series B co-led by Rocketship.vc and Vulcan Capital; reported valuation $500M, 10M+ users and 4,000+ institutes [9].
- **2021:** Acquired Teachmore for course selling; acqui-hired Teachee India in December [2].
- **January 2022:** Multiples reports acquisition of MyClassCampus, undisclosed value; not independently confirmed in the reviewed vendor releases [11].
- **2023:** Teachmint’s About page cites EdTech Startup of the Year 2023 and ISO 27001/ISO 9001 certification [1].
- **2025-2026:** Public product repositioned around Teachmint X interactive panels, EduAI, VisionX, Share X and connected classroom software; current site claims 20M+ users served and hardware prices in INR [4] [24].

## India #12 (evaluated). Edunext ERP (Edunext Technologies Pvt. Ltd.)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | Edunext Technologies Pvt. Ltd. |
| Headquarters | Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India. The official contact materials give a Sector 63/68 Noida address; the legal registered address shown by Tracxn is in East Delhi. [1] [13] |
| Company founded (year) | 2012. The incorporation record is 6 June 2012; the company’s own timeline also labels 2012 as its foundation year. [1] [13] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | Not publicly disclosed for the ERP itself. The independently reported Edunext Parent App launched in 2013; the official timeline records Version II in 2015. [1] [15] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud-based, browser/web ERP with native Android and iOS mobile applications. No desktop client or on-premise edition is publicly documented. |
| Primary segments | Indian K–12 schools: primary, middle, secondary and senior secondary; day, residential, international, multi-campus and school-group networks. It also supports schools outside India. |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | 1,400+ schools globally on the current official home/about pages (not clearly dated); the official timeline says 1,000+ clients and Bangladesh presence in 2023, and 800+ clientele across India and international markets in 2022. The admission product page separately claims 1,300+ schools and 800,000 annual admission enquiries. [1] [2] [4] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://edunexttechnologies.com/ |
| Product / features page (full URL) | https://edunexttechnologies.com/academics.php |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | https://edunexttechnologies.com/portal-help.php |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | No public pricing page. Pricing is obtained through a demo/quote. |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | G2: 4.5/5 from 1 verified review (page updated 17 Nov 2026); SoftwareSuggest: 4.7/5 from 24 reviews; Apple App Store Edunext Parent: 4.4/5 from 7.2k ratings; Google Play Edunext Parent: 4.6/5 from 17.9k reviews and 1M+ downloads. Viewed 24 Nov 2026. [11] [12] [14] [16] |

### Overview

Edunext ERP is a broad, India-oriented school-management suite combining admissions, student records, attendance, academics, examinations, report cards, fee collection, finance, HR/payroll, transport, library, inventory, hostel operations, e-learning and parent/teacher/management mobile apps. The vendor positions it for schools that want a single cloud system instead of separate administrative, academic and communication tools. The official site says it serves 1,400+ schools globally; its historical timeline records expansion to Dubai/Sharjah in 2015, Nigeria and Ghana in 2018, Japan in 2022 and Bangladesh in 2023. [1] [2]

The company was incorporated in 2012, but the ERP’s first-launch year is not stated. EducationWorld reports the copyrighted Parent App launched in 2013 and Alexa integration in 2018. The official timeline records Tally (2014), Version II (2015), e-learning (2020), AI proctoring (2021), WhatsApp/admission CRM (2023), and event, cafeteria, safety, task, grievance and appraisal capabilities (2024). Tracxn reports no disclosed funding rounds or acquisitions. [1] [13] [15]

### Platform Classification Explained

Edunext is a cloud/web ERP: the official technical page says there is no client-machine installation, the system is accessible through the internet 24x7, and it is built with Java, React JS, MySQL and Apache. The terms page describes the service as cloud-based and names AWS, SSL and encrypted passwords; the official timeline says the technology shifted to Amazon Web Services in 2017. Browser access is through each school’s Edunext ERP login, with Chrome and Firefox explicitly supported in the parent help page. [1] [7] [17]

There is no public evidence of a Windows/macOS desktop client or an on-premise deployment option. The product has native Android and iOS mobile delivery. The principal parent-facing listing is **Edunext Parent**; Apple also lists **Edunext Teacher**, **Edunext Management**, **Edunext Alumni**, **SecureNext**, and **EdunextCafe** under the developer. The vendor describes role-based student, parent, teacher and management apps, plus separate visitor and transport applications. [8] [9] [10] [12]

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment

The admissions module is a full enquiry-to-enrolment workflow: user-defined enquiry and admission forms, custom fields, mandatory-field sequencing, publish/unpublish controls, class-wise age rules, configurable stages, applicant login, document uploads and stage tracking. It adds lead assignment, follow-ups, reminders, status tracking, counsellor dashboards, interaction and campus-tour scheduling, entrance-test question-paper generation, online evaluation, weighted selection criteria, OTP and document validation, audit trails, online invoicing, multi-bank/gateway settlement and admission conversion reports. The page names CBSE, CISCE, IB, IGCSE, state and national curricula and says age–class checks are aligned with NEP and CBSE guidance. [4]

#### Student information and records

The SIS supports user-defined student profiles, ID-card generation, document-expiry alerts, certificates, birthdays, clubs and houses, status changes for suspension, struck-off, withdrawal and transfer certificates, data mining, dynamic reports, completeness statistics and compliance reports. Historical records, previous-year data and Excel migration are supported. [5] [17] [29]

#### Attendance

Attendance is available for students, staff, online classes, libraries and transport. Teachers can mark students in the app; staff attendance supports department calendars, shifts, leave and late-coming MIS; biometric/face-recognition devices can feed employee attendance; RFID gates and Android bus phones support student movement/attendance. Online-class attendance can be marked automatically when a student joins a scheduled class. [1] [6] [9] [18]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

The public materials document student and teacher timetable access, teacher calendars, lesson-plan schedules, class-wise online-class scheduling, merged sections, remedial classes, observers and period-wise online attendance. A detailed public description of constraint-based master scheduling or room/resource optimization is not available. [3] [8] [9]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Teachers can enter marks, grades and remarks; schools can configure assessment terms, grading structures, weightages and rounding, create subjective or objective papers, run quizzes, annotate checked papers, publish results, and compare performance across years, classmates, classes and subjects. Examination pages explicitly support CBSE, CISCE, IB and IGCSE workflows and CBSE result TXT-file import. [3] [19]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Schools can customize, print and publish report cards online and in the mobile app; the academic page claims 1,100+ report-card formats. The SIS also generates customized certificates and transfer certificates. No separate transcript-credit-management product is publicly described. [3] [5] [19]

#### Learning management and homework

The e-learning layer stores audio, video, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, web links and chapter/topic resources; teachers assign homework, assignments and projects to classes, sections, groups or individuals; students submit attachments; teachers annotate, comment and award marks/credits. Discussion boards, quizzes, online assessments, live classes and automatic results are included. [3] [9] [15]

#### Communication

Communication includes in-app parent–teacher and intra-school messaging, SMS, email, push alerts, circulars, news, calendar, remarks, photo galleries and automated birthday/fee/overdue reminders. Business WhatsApp integration supports broadcast messages, automated replies, PDFs, URLs, audio, video, payment links, read receipts and fee reminders. The admission CRM adds WhatsApp, SMS and email logs and stage notifications. [4] [5] [8] [20]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

The browser portal is school-branded and reached from a school website. The parent app covers profiles, attendance, homework, fees and receipts, communication, circulars, calendar, remarks, achievements, report cards, leave, syllabus, e-content, online classes, quizzes, transport and bus location. A single family login can switch between multiple wards. Teacher app functions include attendance, remarks, homework, syllabus, e-resources, timetable, leave and parent communication; management app functions include fee/admission summaries, attendance, circulars, SMS, library status and staff inspection. [8] [9] [10]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Fee management provides day-wise collection, dues/receipts, projected collection, concessions and waivers, overdue reminders, caution/security-deposit refunds, ECS/NACH, 40+ reports and branded challans/receipts. The current fee page documents cards, net banking and UPI, while the payment page documents web/mobile integration, registration and miscellaneous receipts, transaction synchronization and bank settlement. Finance supports user-defined ledgers, groups, vouchers and schemes, student auto-ledgers, cheque printing, day books, trial balances, income/expenditure, cashbooks, bankbooks, petty cash, balance sheets and drill-down. Tally ERP 9 integration is documented. Razorpay and Paytm are not named in the opened official pages, so provider support should be confirmed in a quote. [1] [6] [17] [18]

#### HR, staff and payroll

HR covers vacancy requisition/approval, online resumes, custom recruitment forms, shortlisting, merit lists, offer letters, joining documents, staff profiles, IDs, qualifications, employment history, subject/class allocation, tasks, leave and biometric attendance. Payroll processes salaries, payslips, TDS, PF/ECR, ESI, savings/investments, loans, advances, increments, arrears and bank-disbursement reports. [17] [21]

#### Transport

Transport includes route/stop and vehicle management, route vacancy/occupancy dashboards, fuel logs, maintenance/document-expiry reminders, online requests to add, withdraw or change transport, transport attendance and Android-based GPS. The transport app uses an Android phone on each bus rather than a dedicated GPS device; the bus in-charge can capture route-wise attendance while parents track the live location. [6] [9] [22]

#### Library

The library module supports DDC book records, OPAC search, acquisitions, barcode issue/return, stock verification, periodicals, library in/out registers, members, fines, employee/student transactions, overdue and circulation history, discrepancy reports and library attendance. [3] [23]

#### Hostel and boarding

The cloud hostel module allocates students to available rooms, supports custom hostel fields, is configurable for institutional requirements and has a mobile interface. Detailed mess, warden, boarding-roll and hostel health workflows are not publicly itemized. [24]

#### Inventory and assets

Inventory covers online requisitions and user-defined approval levels, purchase-order templates, goods-receiving notes, verification, stock entry, invoice processing, payment approval, item/item-kit issue, sale and return to students, staff and departments. Reports cover issue, return, stock, daily sales, item history and employee consumption. [25]

#### Health, medical and cafeteria

A dedicated medical/health-record module is not publicly evidenced in the reviewed materials. The 2024 timeline lists cafeteria management, but no detailed public cafeteria sub-feature page was found. A 2020 independent profile mentions thermal-scanner attendance and temperature alerts, not a clinical health record. [1] [15]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

The SIS exposes remarks, achievements, suspension and struck-off status; the parent app displays teacher observations, and the management app supports staff inspection and observations. A dedicated behavior-point, incident, restorative-discipline or pastoral-care module is not documented. [5] [8] [10]

#### Special education and safeguarding

Edunext has visitor management, contactless check-in, QR appointments, RFID child-safety tooling, SecureNext and bus tracking. No public evidence was found for an IEP/special-education case-management module, safeguarding case workflow or statutory child-protection register. [1] [26]

#### Alumni and fundraising

Dynamic website content can include alumni data and forms, and Apple lists an Edunext Alumni app. No public evidence of donation processing, campaign management or fundraising analytics was found. [10] [27]

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

Dashboards cover fees, admissions, enquiries, follow-ups, conversion, attendance, transport occupancy, library, homework, lesson-plan coverage, staff and student performance. The academic page claims 100+ graphical/analytical reports; EducationWorld reported more than 2,000 structured reports in 2020. Reports are exportable to Excel and can be customized to school formats. [3] [15] [17] [29]

#### AI features

The official timeline says AI-based exam proctoring launched in 2021, and the product includes PowerTEST online proctoring. Alexa voice skills, launched in 2018, answer requests about homework, attendance, news, circulars and fee dues. Public material does not establish a generative AI assistant or predictive-risk model. [1] [18]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

Edunext documents CBSE, CISCE, IB and IGCSE exam/report-card compatibility, CBSE result TXT imports, state/national curriculum support and generic compliance reports. The current llms.txt markets the platform as NEP 2020 compliant, while the admissions page cites NEP/CBSE age eligibility. I found no verified public evidence of direct UDISE+ submission, APAAR ID integration, GST invoicing, or NEP 2020 holistic progress-card templates; schools should validate these in procurement. Higher-education NAAC, NBA, NIRF and AISHE reporting is likewise not documented as a product capability. [4] [5] [19] [28]

#### Mobile apps

Native Android/iOS delivery includes Edunext Parent, teacher and management apps, with additional alumni, SecureNext and cafeteria apps listed on Apple. Parent Android has 1M+ downloads and 4.6/5 from 17.9k reviews; iOS shows 4.4/5 from 7.2k ratings. [11] [12]

#### Integrations and APIs

Named integrations are AWS hosting, Tally ERP 9, Google Meet/Google Drive/G Suite, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Amazon Alexa, WhatsApp Business, biometric/face-recognition devices, RFID, Android GPS tracking and payment gateways. No public developer API, OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever/ClassLink connector, marketplace, Microsoft 365 directory/SSO, or Google Workspace SSO documentation was found; G2’s product FAQ explicitly says Edunext does not offer an open API. [1] [11] [15] [17]

#### Security and privacy

The vendor describes AWS hosting, SSL/TLS, encryption, automatic backups, IP restriction, OTP authentication, role-based access, audit logs, encrypted IDs in admission forms and data export in Excel on termination. Its privacy policy says it follows the IT Act/SPDI rules and claims alignment with India’s DPDP Act 2023, including consent, minimization, access/correction and breach-notification language. Public evidence of SOC 2, ISO 27001, FERPA, COPPA or GDPR certification, regional hosting choices, penetration-test reports or a public incident register was not found. Google Play’s developer-declared data-safety panel says no data is shared/collected but also says data is not encrypted and cannot be deleted, which warrants a school-level privacy and DPA review. [7] [11] [28]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Alexa “talking ERP”:** parents can ask for homework, attendance, circulars, school news and fee dues by voice. [18]
- **AI-based online proctoring:** PowerTEST is positioned for monitored online examinations, although public technical detail is limited. [1] [18]
- **Admission CRM:** lead capture, configurable stage workflows, weighted entrance evaluation, OTP/document validation and payment reconciliation are unusually detailed for a school ERP. [4]
- **No-device bus tracking:** the transport app uses an Android phone on the bus for location and attendance instead of dedicated GPS hardware. [22]
- **High report-card customization:** the vendor claims 1,100+ report-card formats plus board-specific CBSE/CISCE/IB/IGCSE handling. [3] [19]
- **Role-specific mobile ecosystem:** parent, teacher, management, alumni, visitor/safety and transport experiences are separated by role and use case. [9] [10] [12]
- **Task escalation:** overdue tasks trigger alerts to the responsible employee and escalate to higher management, with service-request approval workflow and dashboards. [27]

### Pricing Details

No official price list or public pricing page was found. The terms page says clients pay one-time implementation and training charges and then monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly subscription charges under the final agreement; it does not publish amounts or tier names. [7]

SoftwareSuggest likewise says there is no fixed plan and that price depends on requirements, users and customization. IndiaMART lists the product as a one-year license with online training and PC/mobile compatibility but does not show a price on the opened listing; separate search-result cards for other Edunext listings showed inconsistent figures, so they should not be treated as verified Edunext pricing. No USD price is published. Date checked: 24 Nov 2026. [12] [14]

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

The verified integration set is practical rather than standards-led: Tally ERP 9; Google G Suite/Drive/Meet; Microsoft Teams; Zoom; Amazon Alexa; WhatsApp Business; payment gateways supporting cards, net banking and UPI; biometric/face-recognition devices; RFID; Android GPS and Excel imports/exports. The platform also supports configurable school forms, custom fields and report formats. [1] [3] [17] [20]

There is no public evidence of OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever or ClassLink certification, a developer marketplace, a public API, or documented SSO with Google Workspace/Microsoft 365. G2’s product page says no open API is offered. [11]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Edunext states that it uses AWS, SSL/TLS, encryption, role-based permissions, OTP, IP restrictions, audit logs, automatic cloud backups and encrypted form IDs. It provides data export in Excel at termination and describes access/correction, opt-out and machine-readable-copy requests. Its privacy policy expressly references the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and claims lawful processing, consent, minimization and breach notification. [7] [17] [28]

This is policy-level readiness, not independently verified certification. No SOC 2, ISO 27001, FERPA, COPPA or GDPR certification was found, and no public breach/incident register was located. Google Play’s self-declared data-safety panel says no third-party sharing and no data collected, but simultaneously says data is not encrypted and cannot be deleted; that inconsistency makes contractual data-processing terms and technical due diligence important. [11]

### Strengths

- Broad native coverage across Indian school administration, academics, finance, HR, transport, library, hostel and mobile engagement.
- Strong board-oriented assessment support for CBSE, CISCE, IB and IGCSE, customizable report cards and CBSE result-file import. [3] [19]
- Meaningful India-specific finance workflows: UPI, ECS/NACH, concessions, refunds, Tally integration and statutory payroll calculations. [6] [17] [21]
- Mature role-based mobile experience with high-volume parent-app distribution and dedicated helpdesk. [8] [11] [12]
- AWS cloud deployment, Excel migration, configurable fields/reports and implementation/training services. [15] [17] [29]
- Distinctive Alexa voice, RFID, face recognition, phone-based bus tracking and WhatsApp capabilities.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is quote-only; the vendor publishes no tier, per-student, per-school or implementation price, making comparisons difficult. [7] [12]
- G2 has only one review, so its 4.5 score is not a robust market signal; that reviewer liked stability but reported lag and slow data loading. [11]
- SoftwareSuggest’s review synthesis cites complex module views, slow implementation, limited notifications, server/app instability and transport-management issues; individual reviewers asked for better mess/budget functions, more streamlined finance, faster issue resolution and less manual subject allocation. [14]
- Apple reviews report slow performance, erratic notifications, stale unread status, broken leave date-picker behavior, repeated false update alerts and weak support hand-offs; one reviewer said support redirected them to the school rather than resolving app defects. [12]
- Public interoperability is weak: no open API or 1EdTech/Ed-Fi standards evidence was found. [11]
- UDISE+, APAAR, GST invoicing, Razorpay/Paytm, vernacular language packs, higher-education accreditation reporting and DPDP operational controls are not sufficiently documented publicly.

### Key Milestones

- **2012:** Edunext Technologies founded/incorporated in India. [1] [13]
- **2013:** Edunext Parent App launched, according to EducationWorld; the official timeline describes India’s first school mobile app. [1] [15]
- **2014:** Tally integration recorded in the official technology timeline. [1]
- **2015:** Edunext Version II launched; international reach expanded to Dubai and Sharjah. [1]
- **2016:** Official timeline records India’s first talking school ERP integrated with Alexa as a technology milestone. [1]
- **2017:** Visitor app launched and technology shifted to AWS; Lucknow regional office opened. [1]
- **2018:** RFID gates and the Alexa talking ERP were launched; the Alexa event was held 16 Dec 2018 at the Brainfeed School Excellence Awards. [1] [18]
- **2019:** Edunext participated in the Bett Tech Summit in London. [1]
- **2020:** E-learning launched; EducationWorld’s 2020 profile reported 550+ school clients in India/UAE and more than 20 modules. [1] [15]
- **2021:** AI-based exam proctoring launched; Learn o test Olympiad/Yogshala milestones recorded. [1]
- **2022:** School Shopper launched; the company reported 800+ clientele and reach into Japan. [1]
- **2023:** Official timeline reported 1,000+ clients and Bangladesh presence; WhatsApp integration and admission CRM launched. [1]
- **2024:** Event, cafeteria, SecureNext, task, grievance and employee-appraisal management were added to the official technology timeline. [1]
- **2026:** Current official pages claim 1,400+ schools globally; Google Play lists the parent app as updated 7 Aug 2026, and G2’s product page was updated 17 Nov 2026. [1] [11]

## India #13 (evaluated). OpenEduCat (OpenEduCat Inc.)

| Field | Detail |

| Vendor / owner | OpenEduCat Inc.; official leadership page names Parthiv Patel (Founder & CEO) and Neha Patel (Co-Founder) [2] |

| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Browser/web-based ERP; managed cloud SaaS; self-hosted/on-premise; hybrid; native iOS and Android apps. No separate desktop client was verified [1] [6] [13] |
| Primary segments | K–12 schools, preschools, colleges, universities, vocational/training institutes, boarding schools, and multi-campus education groups [1] [3] [9] |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | Vendor claim: 1,000+ institutions, 3M+ users, 90+ countries; checked 24 November 2026. The figure is not independently audited in the sources reviewed [2] |

| Product / features page (full URL) | https://openeducat.org/features/ |

| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | G2 4.6/5 from 154 reviews (viewed 24 Nov 2026); Capterra 3.8/5 from 4 reviews (page last updated 28 Sep 2026; viewed 24 Nov 2026); GetApp 3.8/5 from 4 reviews (last updated Mar 2026); Software Advice 3.8/5 from 4 reviews; SourceForge 4.8/5 from 37 reviews; Google Play “OpenEduCat - Educational ERP” showed 1K+ downloads but no visible score/review count; Apple App Store “OpenEduCat - Educational ERP” said insufficient ratings/reviews to display an overview [15] [16] [17] [18] [19] [21] [22] |

### Overview

OpenEduCat is an open-source education ERP built on Odoo. It combines a student information system with admissions, academics, fees, accounting, HR, learning, campus operations, communications, and higher-education workflows. The Community Edition is free and self-hostable under LGPL-3; the Enterprise Edition adds commercial modules, managed hosting and vendor support [5] [6] [8].

The company says it was founded in 2014, reached 100 institutions in 2016, launched Enterprise in 2017, added LMS in 2018, released native apps in 2021, introduced AI in 2023, and passed 3M users/1,000+ institutions in 2024 [2]. The repository predates that company milestone, having been created in 2013 [7]. I found no verified acquisition or venture-funding history in the reviewed sources.

### Platform Classification Explained

OpenEduCat is web-first, with browser access, APIs and role-based portals. Managed cloud deployment includes updates, backups, scaling and a stated 99.9% uptime SLA; cloud regions are described in North America, Europe or Asia-Pacific [13].

Self-hosting is a core differentiator. The download page offers Windows, Ubuntu/Debian, Red Hat/CentOS, source ZIP and Docker images, with PostgreSQL, Python and Nginx requirements. On-premise keeps data on institutional servers, while hybrid combines local sensitive data with a cloud portal [6] [13]. No standalone desktop client was verified; the Windows package is for deployment.

The native mobile product is named “OpenEduCat - Educational ERP” on both Google Play and Apple’s App Store. The vendor describes branded iOS and Android apps for parents, students, faculty and staff with grades, attendance, timetables, assignments, fee payments, library access, push notifications, offline caching and role-based permissions [4] [21] [22].

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment
Online application intake, applicant stages, document upload, review, merit-list/selection workflows, conversion from applicant to enrolled student, subject-wise admission, e-signature offer letters, mass applicant email, application tracking and drag-and-drop forms are documented. The richer form-builder and e-signature functions are Enterprise additions [3] [8].

#### Student information and records
The core SIS stores student, parent/contact, demographic, academic-history, health, document, program, course, batch, subject, department and faculty records. It supports portals, student badges, configurable terminology, academic plans, activity logs and multi-campus data [3] [8].

#### Attendance
Basic attendance supports marking and reporting by class/date, with student leave requests, absence alerts and attendance-linked reporting. Enterprise pages add biometric, fingerprint, RFID and face-recognition capture, kiosk check-in, offline mobile marking and parent notifications [3] [4] [8].

#### Timetable and master scheduling
The timetable module creates sessions and conflict-free schedules, allocates rooms and faculty, supports timetable changes, lesson/session planning, study-material allocation and calendar synchronization. Live-class integrations can generate meeting links from scheduled sessions [3] [8] [14].

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations
The Enterprise stack includes a central gradebook, marks and letter grades, GPA/CGPA, CBCS credits, outcome-based education with CO–PO attainment, question banks, auto-graded quizzes, weighted scoring, multiple exam versions, negative marking, OMR scanning and anti-cheating/proctoring. Community has basic exams, configurable letter grades and marksheets, but not the central gradebook or full LMS [3] [8].

#### Report cards and transcripts
OpenEduCat generates marksheets, progress/report cards, result publications and transcripts. Enterprise secure-transcript workflows add QR verification, digital signatures, watermarks, batch processing, self-service ordering, online payment and financial-hold enforcement. AI-generated report-card comments are described as an Enterprise AI use case [3] [8].

#### Learning management and homework
The Enterprise LMS provides course authoring, video/content delivery, quizzes, forums, surveys, gamification, certificates, H5P/SCORM content and learning analytics. Assignments support submission, marks, feedback and gradebook linkage; Enterprise adds inline annotation, rubrics, multiple attempts and late-submission rules [3] [8].

#### Communication (SMS, email, push, WhatsApp)
Communication includes email, notices, news/blog publishing, forums, announcements, surveys, push notifications and in-app messaging. Enterprise integrations send attendance alerts, fee reminders, exam/result notifications and emergency broadcasts through Twilio/Vonage SMS or WhatsApp Business API; WhatsApp supports approved templates, broadcasts, two-way replies and logged responses [3] [11] [12].

#### Parent, student and teacher portals
Student, parent, faculty and staff portals expose role-specific records. The parent portal covers grades, attendance, fee balances, messages and circulars; the student portal covers courses, timetable, assignments, results and documents; faculty views include schedules, attendance, grading, leave and substitutions [3] [4] [8].

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting
Fee structures, tuition/program/hostel/exam/lab charges, discounts, installments, invoices, receipts, scholarships, refunds, online payment, fee reminders and automated reconciliation are supported. The accounting layer provides double-entry books, chart of accounts, journals, AP/AR, bank reconciliation, budgets, cost centers, fund-level tracking and fee-to-ledger posting [3] [8] [10].

#### HR, staff and payroll
Faculty/staff profiles can include qualifications, skills, degrees, prior employment, workload, substitutions, attendance, timesheets, recruitment, appraisals and performance reviews. Payroll covers salary calculations, taxes, benefits and payslips, with attendance and contracts as inputs [3]. Indian PF/ESI is claimed in a comparison page search result but was not substantiated by a page opened for this profile; treat it as unverified.

#### Transport
Enterprise transport manages routes, vehicles, student stops and allocations, driver certifications, tracking/operations and transport-fee billing linked to student records, attendance and parent portals [3] [8].

#### Library
The library module covers catalogs, members, circulation, barcode-enabled lending, fines and collection reports. Enterprise adds barcode-scanner workflows and a digital/e-book library tied to courses and student records [3] [8].

#### Hostel and boarding
Enterprise hostel management handles room/bed allocation, occupancy, check-in/check-out, visitors and IDs, gate passes, facility maintenance, inventories and fee linkage [3] [8].

#### Inventory and assets
Inventory tracks supplies, lab chemicals, IT equipment and campus assets across buildings and stockrooms, with barcode scanning, reorder points, lot/expiry alerts and valuation. Asset requests add budget approvals, acquisition-to-disposal lifecycle, warranties, maintenance and procurement/accounting linkage [3].

#### Health and medical
Health information is a documented SIS field and the Enterprise student-welfare suite adds institutional health records. The reviewed pages do not substantiate a full clinical/medical-records module, electronic medication administration, or a certified school-nurse workflow [3] [8].

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care
Enterprise welfare covers discipline, grievances, leave, mentoring, feedback, achievements, skills assessment, progress, withdrawal and basic pastoral lifecycle records. Community exposes only a basic activity log [8].

#### Special education and safeguarding
Third-party listings tag “Special Education,” but I found no opened official feature or documentation page proving IEP/504-style plans, safeguarding case management, or child-protection workflows. Score this capability as not publicly verified rather than assuming the generic student-welfare tools are special-education functionality [16] [18].

#### Alumni and fundraising
Enterprise alumni management covers graduate records, reunions/events, an alumni job board and alumni blog. Email marketing can target alumni and donors, but a dedicated fundraising, donation ledger or campaign-management module was not clearly documented [3] [8].

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting
KPI dashboards cover enrollment yield, retention, graduation, staffing, attendance, class capacity, fees and budget utilization. Advanced reporting produces academic, financial and compliance reports on demand or on schedule with CSV/Excel export; Microsoft 365 integration advertises Power BI export [3] [14].

#### AI features
Enterprise AI covers essay/assignment grading, rubric and quiz generation, lesson planning, note summarization, report-card comments, at-risk alerts and predictive performance/enrollment insights. The model-agnostic layer supports OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Llama and Mistral, with quotas, guardrails, audit logs and REST APIs. G2 additionally lists an AI chat assistant and AI-enhanced search; those claims are not independently verified [14] [15].

#### Government/state reporting and compliance
The India page explicitly markets CBSE, ICSE/ISC and state-board schools, 22 official Indian languages, Indian fee workflows and school/university reporting [9]. The platform has generic compliance-report and advanced-reporting capabilities, but no reviewed official page confirms ready-made UDISE+, APAAR ID, NEP 2020 holistic progress card, NAAC, NBA, NIRF or AISHE exports. GST-specific invoicing, Tally integration and Paytm as a distinct gateway are also not publicly confirmed; Razorpay supports UPI and Paytm as a wallet/UPI method [10] [11].

#### Mobile apps
The exact app name is “OpenEduCat - Educational ERP.” iOS/iPadOS and Android versions offer role-based access, attendance, grades, schedules, assignments, payments, library, messaging, push notifications and offline synchronization. Google Play showed 1K+ downloads but no visible score; Apple reported insufficient ratings/reviews [4] [21] [22].

#### Integrations and APIs
The integrations directory advertises 29 integrations, including Google Workspace/Classroom/Drive/Calendar/Gmail, Microsoft 365/Teams/OneDrive/Outlook/Azure AD, Zoom, Google Meet, BigBlueButton, WhatsApp, SMS, 19 payment gateways, SAML/LDAP and LTI/SCORM. The platform also advertises REST APIs and webhooks [14].

#### Security and privacy
Security controls described by the vendor include AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, tenant database isolation, encrypted backups, RBAC, record-level rules, MFA, SAML/OIDC, LDAP/AD, Google/Microsoft SSO, API keys/OAuth/JWT, rate limiting, audit trails, anomaly monitoring and configurable retention [13].

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- **Open-source and self-hosted:** LGPL-3 Community source code can be audited, modified and deployed without per-student licensing [5] [6] [7].
- **Odoo data model:** Academic, finance, HR and campus data share one database rather than requiring separate SIS/LMS products [1] [7].
- **No-code customization:** Enterprise No Code Studio provides drag-and-drop apps, forms, workflows and reports [3].
- **AI plus local-model option:** AI tools can use cloud providers or self-hosted Llama/Mistral endpoints, with quotas, guardrails and audit logs [14].
- **Indian fee collection:** Razorpay handles UPI, net banking, cards, wallets, EMI, payment links and student-ledger reconciliation [10].
- **Higher-education depth:** CBCS, OBE, CO–PO attainment, thesis management, convocation and placement are unusual in school-first products [3] [8].

### Pricing Details

The official pricing page, checked 24 November 2026, says Community is free and LGPL v3. Enterprise starts at **$79 per module per year**, uses user packs from 25 to 10,000+ for cloud or unlimited users for an on-premise one-time option, and has no per-student fee. It advertises cloud or on-premise deployment, a 15-day trial, no setup fees, and “buy 2 years + get the 3rd year free.” The live configurator is required for a final quote; the public page does not show INR prices, so an INR equivalent is **not publicly listed** and should not be treated as a fixed rupee price [4].

The TCO calculator gives illustrative group prices from $299/year for Core SIS to $1,999/year for all modules. Its example shows implementation/training of $7,000 for Community and $13,000 for Enterprise, plus Community hosting; these are scenario estimates, not contractual prices [23].

Official mobile pricing on the feature page lists the Android app at **$889/year** and iOS app at **$1,179/year**, unlimited users, licensed separately. Independent directories display inconsistent prices: G2 and Capterra/GetApp/Software Advice show a $59/year starting figure, while SourceForge lists $79/month and much higher plan examples. These should be treated as directory/listing data, not authoritative Enterprise quotes [4] [15] [16] [17] [18] [19].

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

OpenEduCat has a public REST API/webhook story, SSO through SAML 2.0, OIDC/OAuth, LDAP/Active Directory, Azure AD and Google authentication, plus a maintained integrations directory [12] [13] [14]. LTI 1.3, SCORM 1.2/2004 and xAPI are explicitly documented, including grade passback and a learning-record store [25]. Google Workspace syncs Classroom rosters, Drive, Calendar, Gmail and Meet; Microsoft 365 connects Teams, OneDrive, Outlook, Azure AD, SharePoint and Power BI [26] [27].

Razorpay, Stripe, PayPal and other gateways are documented; India-specific payment methods include UPI, net banking, RuPay, cards, EMI and wallets including Paytm [10] [11]. I found no evidence of certification for OneRoster, Ed-Fi or SIF, and no verified Clever or ClassLink connector. Therefore interoperability is strong for an Odoo/API platform but should not be described as standards-certified.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

The vendor claims FERPA, GDPR and COPPA readiness through access controls, audit logging, consent workflows, portability/deletion tools and parental-consent controls [13]. It says SOC 2 reports and DPAs are available on request, but no public SOC 2 report or ISO 27001 certificate was provided on the reviewed page. No explicit India Digital Personal Data Protection Act readiness statement was found. On-premise deployment can keep data in an institution’s network; cloud regions are described as North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific [13].

The product page claims AES-256, TLS 1.3, isolated databases, daily backups, RPO under one hour and RTO under four hours. No public security incident was located in reviewed sources through 24 November 2026; app-store privacy disclosures should still be validated against institution-configured processing [13] [21] [22].

### Strengths

- Broad academic, financial, HR, campus and higher-education coverage in one Odoo-based data model.
- Free LGPL-3 Community Edition and genuine self-hosting reduce lock-in and permit code inspection.
- Strong deployment choice: managed cloud, self-hosted or hybrid.
- Good Indian payment fit through Razorpay, UPI, SMS/WhatsApp links and automatic reconciliation.
- Native mobile apps, LTI/SCORM/xAPI, Google/Microsoft integrations and public API/webhook claims.
- Enterprise differentiators include CBCS/OBE, OMR, AI, no-code workflows, thesis, placement and convocation.

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Setup and configuration can be difficult: G2 users praise centralization but repeatedly mention learning curve, setup difficulty, technical issues and limited customization [15].
- Independent reviews are less enthusiastic than G2: GetApp and Software Advice show 3.8/5; Software Advice gives 3.5 for ease of use and 3.25 for support [17] [18].
- Users report too many menus/icons, language terminology barriers, a dated student profile, and library shortcomings; one review wanted a glossary and fewer menus [18].
- Reviewers say grading-period and multi-teacher workflows can be closed or cumbersome, and support/documentation may be insufficient for non-technical integrations [18] [19].
- SourceForge feedback cites limited out-of-box customization, incomplete documentation, occasional performance slowdowns and weak state-reporting coverage [19].
- India-specific government identifiers/reporting and Tally/GST/DPDP claims are not sufficiently evidenced in public documentation, so local implementation effort may be material.

### Key Milestones

- **2013:** Public OpenEduCat GitHub repository created on 2 May 2013 [7].
- **2014:** Vendor’s stated founding year; began as an open-source education-management project [2].
- **2016:** Vendor says it reached 100 institutions across 20 countries [2].
- **2017:** Enterprise Edition launched with advanced modules and support [2].
- **2018:** Full LMS and online course delivery/grade synchronization added [2].
- **2019:** Vendor says it passed 500 institutions and 1M users [2].
- **2020:** Remote-learning and virtual-classroom support expanded [2].
- **2021:** Native Android and iOS apps released [2].
- **2022:** Vendor says it reached 2M users and added multi-campus/advanced analytics; a contemporaneous press release reported 300k installations and 2M users [2] [20].
- **2023:** Vendor says AI course-generation, quiz-generation and predictive-analytics features were introduced [2].
- **2024:** Vendor says it passed 3M users and 1,000+ institutions in 90+ countries [2].
- **2025:** Platform modernization, UI/security refresh and expanded API capabilities claimed [2].
- **2026:** Current pages emphasize global expansion, 73+ features, 29 integrations, AI, no-code tools and Indian-market workflows [3] [9] [14].
- **Acquisitions/funding:** No verified acquisition or funding event was found in the opened sources.

## India #14 (evaluated). Toddle (Teacher Tools Pvt. Ltd.)

| Field | Detail |

| Vendor / owner | Teacher Tools Pvt. Ltd.; founders listed by Crunchbase are Deepanshu Arora, Gautam Arora, Misbah Jafary, Nikhil Poonawalla and Parita Parekh. [1] |
