| Company founded (year) | 2019. The founders’ school project began earlier; Toddle’s own story dates the external turning point to December 2018. [2] [3] |

| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud SaaS and web-based, with native Toddle Family, Toddle Educator and Toddle Student apps for mobile. No desktop client or on-premise deployment is publicly documented. [4] [5] |
| Primary segments | K–12 schools and districts, especially IB (PYP, MYP, DP, CP), Cambridge/IGCSE, American/AP, English, Australian, CBSE, ICSE, independent, public, charter, faith-based and competency-based schools. [4] |

| Product / features page (full URL) | https://www.toddleapp.com/product/product-overview/ |

Google Play search results did not verify the school Toddle app ratings; a similarly named Belgian daycare app is not counted. [7] [8] [9] [10] |

### Overview

Toddle is an India-founded, cloud-based K–12 teaching-and-learning platform positioned as “more than an LMS.” It connects curriculum mapping, unit and lesson planning, assessment, gradebook, portfolios, progress reports, transcripts, attendance, timetables, communication, behaviour/well-being and accreditation evidence. Its strongest fit is an international or progressive school that wants teaching and reporting workflows to share data rather than operate as disconnected tools. [3] [4]

The founders were educators and school operators who built the first version inside their own school after experiencing fragmented tools. Toddle’s official history records a December 2018 inflection point when visiting educators asked the team to make the tool available more broadly; independent company sources identify 2019 as the founding year. [2] [3] A January 2023 Series A announcement said Toddle raised $17 million led by Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV), with Tenacity Ventures, Trifecta Capital, Matrix Partners, BEENEXT and Better Capital participating. [6] No acquisition was identified in the sources reviewed.

Toddle began with IB schools but now markets to multiple curricula, including CBSE and ICSE. Its current public positioning is much closer to an academic operating layer and curriculum/LMS platform than to a full Indian school ERP: there is no public evidence in the reviewed materials for native fee accounting, payroll, transport, hostel, library, inventory or admissions management.

### Platform Classification Explained

Toddle is a browser-accessed SaaS service at web.toddleapp.com, and its privacy policy explicitly describes both a web end and a mobile end. It names three native mobile products: Toddle Family, Toddle Educator and Toddle Student. The policy describes separate teacher, student, parent and administrator roles; family users can view portfolios, calendars, news, policies and teacher communications. [5]

The platform is cloud-hosted and the integrations page identifies AWS regional hosting choices, including Australia, China, Europe/Ireland, Hong Kong, Singapore, the UAE and the United States, with backup locations. [11] No downloadable desktop client, self-hosted package or on-premise edition is publicly documented. Mobile capability is therefore native-app plus web, not a desktop/on-premise hybrid.

### Complete Feature Inventory

#### Admissions and enrollment
No native admissions funnel, application management, entrance testing, seat allocation or enrollment workflow is publicly documented. SIS integrations can bring rosters into Toddle, but that is not evidence that Toddle replaces an admissions system. [11]

#### Student information and records
Toddle has centralized student profiles and connected evidence across portfolios, assessment, attendance, behaviour and reports. Rosters, term grades, timetables and attendance can synchronize from supported SISs. It is not publicly presented as a complete demographic, birth-record, transfer-certificate or statutory SIS. [4] [11]

#### Attendance
The Class Operations module supports daily, rotation-based and period-wise attendance, configurable codes/categories/reminders, SIS synchronization and attendance visibility in analytics and reports. [4]

#### Timetable and master scheduling
Toddle provides teacher/student schedules, calendars, workload views and cross-subject insights. Schedules can be imported from SISs and tools such as aSc and EdVal; supported SIS sync includes timetable/calendar in several connectors. [4] [11]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations
Assessments can be standards-, competency- or score-based and use rubrics, checklists, varied submission formats and multimodal feedback. The unified gradebook receives internal grades and can display uploaded external results such as NAPLAN, PAT and MAP. Assessment delivery includes timers, extra-time controls, browser focus mode and screen-absence alerts. [4] Toddle markets AI assessment creation, first-pass grading and inline feedback, but independent commentary flags that high-stakes lockdown capabilities may not be as deep as specialist exam systems. [12]

#### Report cards and transcripts
Schools can build customizable, visual, media-rich progress reports and transcripts. Evidence from portfolios, gradebook, behaviour and attendance can feed reports; grades flow into transcripts; reports can be published digitally or printed. AI can draft evidence-linked comments for teacher review. [4]

#### Learning management and homework
The LMS layer covers courses, units, lessons, assignments, worksheets, resource links, student submissions, differentiated tasks, class drives and learning experiences. AI can generate worksheets, questions, rubrics and differentiated activities. [4] [13]

#### Communication (SMS, email, push, WhatsApp)
The Communications Hub offers one-to-one messaging, group channels, announcements and an administrator conversation view. Announcements can be shared in Toddle or by email; AI drafts messages, summarizes threads and flags attention items. Auto-translation supports 100+ languages. Native SMS, WhatsApp Business, push-notification specifications and transactional messaging APIs are not publicly verified. [4] [11]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals
Teachers plan, assess, grade, communicate and curate portfolios; students submit work, set goals, self-evaluate and document learning; families receive portfolios, reports, announcements and messages through Toddle Family; administrators approve plans, manage permissions and view insights. Family invitation management includes bulk email, class invite links, printable PDFs, QR/text codes, approval states and removal. [5] [14]

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting
No native fee ledger, invoicing, GST billing, online fee collection, UPI, Razorpay, Paytm or Tally integration is publicly documented. The integrations directory does list Sponte for fees and student services, but that is a third-party connector, not Toddle accounting. [11]

#### HR, staff and payroll
No public evidence of employee records, recruitment, leave, appraisal, payroll, statutory deductions or teacher payroll export.

#### Transport
No public evidence of bus routes, vehicle tracking, driver/attendant management, pickup permissions or transport fees.

#### Library
No public evidence of cataloguing, circulation, barcodes, acquisitions, fines or library-resources management.

#### Hostel and boarding
No public evidence of dormitory allocation, wardens, boarding attendance, leave permissions or residential pastoral workflows beyond general behaviour/well-being tracking.

#### Inventory and assets
No public evidence of procurement, stock, asset tagging, issue/return or maintenance modules.

#### Health and medical
No public evidence of clinic visits, immunization records, allergies, medication or nurse workflows.

#### Behaviour, discipline and pastoral care
Behaviour Management records and reports behaviour/well-being events, supports school-configurable approaches, uses AI to help write nuanced reports, and surfaces patterns in school culture and well-being. It is a pastoral/behaviour layer, not a documented safeguarding case-management system. [4]

#### Special education and safeguarding
Toddle supports differentiated learning, flexible evidence formats, accessibility and AI Tutors that adapt to pace and needs. It states WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA conformance and support for screen readers, keyboard navigation, VoiceOver, TalkBack and live captions. A dedicated IEP/SEN case-management or safeguarding incident module is not publicly documented. [4]

#### Alumni and fundraising
No public evidence of alumni relations, donations, campaigns, events or fundraising CRM.

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting
Ready-made dashboards cover curriculum coverage, student performance, attendance, behaviour and engagement. Leaders can correlate performance, attendance and behaviour; dashboards can be delivered daily, weekly or monthly. AI Insights accepts natural-language questions and returns charts, tables and suggested actions. [4]

#### AI features
Toddle AI is production-embedded rather than a separate chatbot. Publicly described tools include Curriculum Design Assistant, Assessment Builder, Grading Assistant, Report Writing Assistant, Writing Assistant, AI Tutors and AI Insights. They generate or differentiate plans and assessments, read multiple formats, draft evidence-backed report comments, summarize communications, analyze school data and provide teacher-configured student tutoring. Toddle says teachers remain in control and that AI Tutors are teacher-led, monitored and automatically flagged for unsafe/off-topic content. [13]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance
Toddle’s public FAQ says it supports Indian CBSE and ICSE curricula, but no reviewed page verifies CBSE/ICSE/state-board statutory report-card templates, NEP 2020 Holistic Progress Cards, UDISE+ export, APAAR ID, AISHE, NAAC, NBA or NIRF reporting. These should be treated as unconfirmed rather than assumed from curriculum support. Accreditation Management includes evidence, reviews, feedback and built-in standards for 15+ accrediting bodies including IB and NEASC. [4]

#### Mobile apps
The privacy policy names Toddle Family, Toddle Educator and Toddle Student. The web help center notes that some administrative family-invitation functions are web-only, so mobile parity is not complete. Apple’s public ratings show a significant gap between the well-rated web product and the lower-rated Student and Family apps. [5] [7] [8] [14]

#### Integrations and APIs
Toddle advertises 50+ integrations and two-way SIS synchronization. Named systems include Veracross, PowerSchool, Blackbaud, iSAMS, Compass, TASS, Sentral, Synergetic, Edumate, OpenApply, QuickSchools, SIMS, Skyward, Infinite Campus, Clever, ClassLink, Wonde, Edlink, Google, Microsoft, Teams, Zoom, Turnitin, Edpuzzle, H5P, ClickView, Educaplay, McGraw Hill, OneNote, Wayground and Kognity. The page documents OneRoster and LTI routes and says custom integrations can be evaluated; a fully public developer API specification was not located. [11]

#### Security and privacy
Toddle reports ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2, ISO 42001, 1EdTech Data Privacy, FERPA, COPPA and GDPR-related controls. Its privacy policy says it acts as processor/data fiduciary counterpart to schools and commits to India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDPA). It describes encryption, regional AWS hosting and role-controlled school access. No publicly reported security incident was identified in the reviewed sources. [5] [11]

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

- Curriculum-first design links maps, standards, units, lessons, assessments and evidence rather than treating the LMS as a file repository. [4]
- AI is embedded across planning, assessment, grading, reporting, communication and analytics, with teacher review and school-context grounding. [13]
- AI Tutors provide teacher-configured, immersive student experiences with conversation visibility and safety flags. [4] [13]
- Portfolio evidence flows into reports and transcripts, supporting a longitudinal K–12 learning record.
- Curriculum publishing creates a current public-facing curriculum view for families, boards and accreditation work.
- Accreditation Management centralizes evidence, reviews and feedback with 15+ built-in accrediting frameworks. [4]
- Toddle Buddy implementation support assigns a former educator to migration, onboarding and ongoing adoption. [12]
- Auto-translation supports family/community communication across 100+ languages, while the interface itself is available in nine languages. [4]

### Pricing Details

Toddle publishes no INR, USD or per-student price. The official page presents three plans: Planning Pro (curriculum planning), Advanced (curriculum planning plus assessments/gradebook, portfolios, worksheets, reports/transcripts, communications, attendance/timetable/calendar, analytics and accreditation) and Ultimate (Advanced plus AI Tutors, AI-powered reports, AI grading, AI feedback, conversational analytics and behaviour management). The page also says pricing is tailored to school/user count and requirements, offers a free trial with setup/training, and supports two- or three-year discounts. [15]

The FAQ says trials typically run 2–3 weeks; no setup, implementation, per-student/year, per-school/month, INR or USD amount is stated. G2 likewise records free trial and custom pricing, with final negotiation directly with Toddle. [9] No credible third-party numeric price range was found, so no estimate is supplied.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

Toddle’s strongest interoperability evidence is practical rather than certification-based: SSO through Google, Microsoft, Clever and ClassLink; two-way SIS roster/attendance/timetable/term-grade synchronization; OneRoster and LTI connections; and 50+ named integrations. Google Drive/Meet/Calendar, OneDrive/SharePoint/Teams, Zoom and Turnitin are explicit examples. [11] There is no reviewed evidence of Ed-Fi or SIF certification, a public developer portal/API reference, or a marketplace with independently installable apps. Payment/accounting interoperability for Indian gateways is not publicly verified.

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

Toddle’s public compliance position is comparatively strong for an Indian-founded K–12 SaaS: ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2, ISO 42001, 1EdTech Data Privacy, FERPA, COPPA and GDPR/DPA support are described in its privacy and integrations materials. It also explicitly states DPDPA/DPDP Act 2023 readiness, data minimization, school-directed processing, governance processes and regional hosting choices. [5] [11] This is a vendor assertion; buyers should request current certificates, subprocessor lists, breach-notification terms, retention schedules, AI data-use terms and India-region availability during diligence. No public incident was found in the reviewed sources through November 24, 2026.

### Strengths

- Broad, connected academic workflow for curriculum-led K–12 schools.
- Very strong web-review sentiment: 4.7/5 on both G2 and Capterra as viewed in November 2026. [7] [8]
- Production AI covers several teacher workflows, not only content chat.
- Deep international-school and IB fit, with growing CBSE/ICSE and public/district positioning.
- Strong SIS, SSO, LTI and OneRoster integration story.
- Educator-led onboarding and “Toddle Buddy” support are repeatedly praised by reviewers. [7] [12]
- Clear privacy/compliance documentation, including explicit DPDPA language. [5]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

- Pricing is fully quote-based; no INR/USD benchmark is public, making procurement comparison difficult. [9] [15]
- The platform’s breadth creates a learning curve; G2 users describe it as overwhelming and Capterra users report multiple clicks, slow loading and frequent interface changes. [7] [8]
- Secondary/departmental workflows can feel card-heavy; one Capterra reviewer reported difficulty using the gradebook as a spreadsheet and reliance on Google Classroom/spreadsheets. [8]
- Customization and granular defaults are recurring requests, and some users say AI output needs correction or does not follow instructions exactly. [7] [8]
- Mobile sentiment is much weaker than web sentiment: Apple shows 2.8/5 for Toddle Student and 2.1/5 for Toddle Family, with complaints about lag, crashes, confusing navigation, missing assignments, login/region errors and deleted work. [7] [10]
- The product does not publicly demonstrate the Indian ERP capabilities expected in a full school-management suite: fees, GST/Tally, UPI/Razorpay/Paytm, payroll, transport, hostel, library, inventory, UDISE+, APAAR or higher-education statutory reporting are unverified.

### Key Milestones

- **December 2018:** Educators visiting the founders’ school saw the internal platform and encouraged a broader product. [2]
- **2019:** Teacher Tools/Toddle founded by Deepanshu Arora, Gautam Arora, Misbah Jafary, Nikhil Poonawalla and Parita Parekh. [2] [6]
- **Early years:** Began with IB-focused teaching and learning, planning, portfolios and collaboration; the commercial product’s exact launch year is not publicly disclosed. [2] [6]
- **January 2023:** Announced a $17 million Series A led by Sequoia Capital India, with additional participation from Tenacity Ventures, Trifecta Capital and existing investors; reported 40,000+ educators, 1,500+ schools and 100+ countries. [6]
- **Late 2024:** AI Tutors launched, according to independent product-history coverage. [12]
- **Early 2025:** AI Curriculum Design Assistant, AI-assisted grading and worksheet generation were reported as new capabilities. [12]
- **2026:** Official pages describe 2,500+ schools in 100+ countries, AI across workflows, 50+ integrations, accreditation management and explicit DPDP/DPDPA positioning. [3] [5] [11]

## India #15 (evaluated). MyClassCampus (Teachmint Technologies Pvt. Ltd.)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Vendor / owner | MyClassCampus; acquired by Teachmint Technologies Pvt. Ltd. on 28 January 2022. Transaction terms were not disclosed. [4] |
| Headquarters | Bengaluru, Karnataka, India in current company records; an earlier founder profile identifies Ahmedabad as the operating headquarters. [3] [7] [14] |
| Company founded (year) | 2015 in company and database profiles. Acquisition coverage instead says 2017, so the public record is inconsistent. [3] [4] [7] [14] |
| Product first launched (year or Not publicly disclosed) | MVP launched in March 2016, according to a 2021 founder interview; the product was being built from 2014. [7] |
| Platform classification (Cloud SaaS / Web-based / Desktop / Mobile iOS+Android / On-premise / Hybrid) | Cloud-based, web-based ERP with native iOS and Android applications. A third-party directory also lists a Windows desktop app, but this is not corroborated by primary material. No on-premise deployment is publicly documented. [2] [8] [9] |
| Primary segments | K–12 schools, colleges/universities, coaching centres, private institutes and other educational organisations. [2] [4] [7] |
| Market presence (schools, students, countries, with date of claim) | Claims vary by date: StartupTalky reported 2,000+ registered educational organisations, 300,000+ students and 600,000 parents in 2021; the January 2022 acquisition coverage reported 1,500+ institutes and 2m+ students across 30 countries. LinkedIn described use in India and 20+ countries. These are vendor or press-reported claims, not an independently audited current count. [2] [5] [6] [7] |
| Official website (full URL) | https://www.myclasscampus.com/ (viewed 24 November 2026; now presents Teachmint X rather than a standalone MyClassCampus product site). [1] |
| Product / features page (full URL) | No current standalone product page verified. Historical product description: https://www.linkedin.com/products/myclasscampus/ [2] |
| Documentation / help center (full URL) | No standalone public help centre verified. Historical official how-to and demo material: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCkLUra2-WzmIARXV6YMx8lA/videos [11] |
| Pricing page (full URL or No public pricing page) | No public MyClassCampus pricing page. The domain now redirects to Teachmint-related content; current Teachmint pages do not publish a MyClassCampus price. [1] [15] |
| Review ratings (G2, Capterra, App Store, Play Store with score, review count and date viewed) | Viewed 24 November 2026: SaaSworthy 4.9/5 from 75 ratings, but the listing is unclaimed and its pricing/features disclaimer says the details were last updated 4 December 2019. [9] [10] App Store listing tracked by AppBrain: 3.00/5 from 2 ratings; removed 1 February 2024. [12] No current Google Play rating or G2/Capterra listing was verified. APKPure retains a historical Android package, version 15.6, updated 22 September 2023, but does not provide a comparable verified store rating. [13] |

### Overview

MyClassCampus was positioned as an “operating system” for education: an India-origin, cloud and mobile-first ERP joining administration, academics, finance, communication and campus operations. Its stated users were school administrators, teachers, students, parents and staff. The product was designed for single- and multi-branch institutions, with role-based access and configurable settings. [2] [7]

The product history is a pre-acquisition timeline, not proof of a currently sold standalone product. A founder profile says the MVP launched in March 2016, while company records use 2015 as the founding year and acquisition reporting says 2017. Teachmint acquired MyClassCampus on 28 January 2022, intending to combine its ERP with Teachmint’s LMS. [3] [4] [5] [6] [7]

As of 24 November 2026, myclasscampus.com no longer exposes a current MyClassCampus catalogue, price list or documentation portal. It leads to Teachmint X classroom hardware and AI teaching content. A current independent comparison likewise reports that the old domain redirects and that it is not possible to establish from public primary pages whether the legacy ERP is still sold under its old name, folded into Teachmint, or retired. [1] [15]

### Platform Classification Explained

* **Browser/web access:** Historical descriptions call it a web-based school-management ERP and show web administration workflows for fees, inventory, transport, website building and system logs. [2] [8] [11]
* **Cloud hosting:** MyClassCampus was repeatedly described as cloud-based. No public source verified the cloud provider, hosting region, tenancy model or data-residency commitments. [2] [7] [8]
* **Native mobile applications:** LinkedIn describes advanced native iOS and Android apps. Historical Android package records identify “My Class Campus,” package `com.myclasscampus`, and version 15.6. [2] [13] The iOS app “My Class Campus” was free, version 1.5, and was removed from the App Store in February 2024. [12]
* **Desktop client:** SaaSworthy lists “Desktop App (Windows),” but labels the vendor profile unclaimed and does not supply primary evidence. Treat this as unverified rather than an established deployment mode. [9]
* **On-premise/hybrid:** No public evidence of an on-premise installer, customer-managed database or hybrid deployment was found.

### Complete Feature Inventory

The inventory below relies on historical product material; SaaSworthy describes 40+ modules, while StartupTalky, SoftwareStreets and the official video channel expose concrete sub-features. [7] [8] [9] [11]

#### Admissions, enquiry and enrollment

Online admissions, inquiry management and academic-year enrollment were documented, with inquiry dashboards, forms and Tawk.to chat integration. Certificates and dynamic certificate generation with field logic were shown in the official video archive. [7] [8] [11] Merit lists, OCR, waitlists and application-payment workflows were not publicly verified.

#### Student information and records

The student module stored profiles and records, supported certificates, progress information and QR-code profile scanning. Multi-branch institutions and role-based access were supported. [2] [7] [9]

#### Attendance

Attendance tracking covered students and staff, with attendance reports and advertised wireless biometric support. Hardware brands and offline behaviour were not publicly specified. [7] [8] [9]

#### Timetable and master scheduling

The system included a dynamic calendar, timetable, holiday and year planner, plus scheduling features for classes. Public material does not specify constraint-based scheduling, room/resource optimization, substitution management or timetable imports. [2] [7] [9]

#### Gradebook, assessment and examinations

Documented academic tools include exam scheduling, exams and results, online quizzes, question banks, an offline paper generator, target management with ratings and result generation. The platform could conduct online tests and notify users of result dates. [7] [8] [9]

#### Report cards and transcripts

Result reports, student progress reports and report-card generation were listed. CBSE, ICSE/CISCE, state-board, NIOS, IB, IGCSE, transcript, NEP 2020 or PARAKH templates were not publicly verified. [7] [9]

#### Learning management and homework

The LMS layer included study material, document libraries, quizzes, question banks and homework. “Pocket Study,” introduced in April 2020, was described as an integrated LMS, with Pocket Study and Teachmint Live Class workflows shown in the official video archive. [2] [11]

#### Communication: SMS, email, push and WhatsApp

The historical product advertised bulk SMS gateway support, an SMS panel and app-based communication for management, teachers, students and parents. Native email campaigns, push configuration, WhatsApp Business API, templates and named WhatsApp vendors were not publicly verified. [2] [7] [8] [11]

#### Parent, student and teacher portals

The product had mobile/web access for parents, students and teachers, including fee history, online fee payment, learning material and communication. SaaSworthy lists parent and student portals; LinkedIn calls the product mobile-first so stakeholders do not need a web login for important daily updates. [2] [9] The exact staff-app name and role-by-role permission matrix are not publicly specified.

#### Fees, billing, payments and accounting

Finance and fees were among the strongest documented modules: fee structures and collection, fee reports, passbook, income/expense and summary reports, bank and cash accounts, cheque management, company/accounts management and a student wallet. Online payment gateway support and fee payment through the app were listed, including fee history and settlement reporting. [7] [8] [9] Specific support for UPI, Razorpay, Paytm, GST invoicing, Tally integration, automated reconciliation or India e-invoicing was not publicly verified.

#### HR, staff and payroll

HRMS covered employee, vacancy, leave, loan, promotion/transfer, appraisal, staff attendance, payroll and salary, plus staff/HR reports. EPF/ESI, statutory filings, biometric-to-payroll automation and employee self-service were not specified. [7] [8]

#### Transport

Transport management included GPS-enabled buses, vehicles, routes, waypoints, waypoint-user transfer, a tracking dashboard and reports. The video archive shows an app view and SMS panel; vehicle vendor, hardware, geofencing and route-alert specifications were not published. [7] [9] [11]

#### Library

Library management included library/book reports and was listed as a core module. Barcode/RFID, circulation rules, overdue automation and cataloguing standards were not specified. [7] [8] [14]

#### Hostel and boarding

Hostel management with mess was explicitly listed, and SaaSworthy identifies housing/hostel management. Detailed boarding workflows were not publicly documented. [9]

#### Inventory and assets

Inventory covered requirements, purchase orders, stock, infrastructure/allocation, sales/invoices, item history, item-kit history, approvals and dashboards. [8] [11]

#### Health and medical

SaaSworthy’s generic taxonomy marks “Clinic Management,” but no vendor-specific clinic workflow or medical records, visits, immunization, medication or emergency management was verified. [9]

#### Behavior, discipline and pastoral care

Complaint/grievance, guest-user and gate-pass management were listed. SaaSworthy’s behavior label is generic; detailed discipline, counseling, safeguarding or pastoral workflows were not verified. [9] [11]

#### Special education and safeguarding

No source verified individualized education plans, special-needs accommodation, safeguarding case management or consent workflows; SaaSworthy’s “Special Education” tag is generic. [9]

#### Alumni and fundraising

No public evidence was found for alumni, donor, fundraising or advancement modules.

#### Analytics, dashboards and reporting

The product included analysis and reports, daily summaries, 40+ custom reports, fee reports, exam and attendance reports, inquiry reports, vehicle tracking reports, library/book reports, user-data reports and staff/HR reports. Dashboard videos exist for finance, inquiry, inventory, complaint, target and hostel modules. [7] [8] [9] [11]

#### AI features

No production AI assistant, predictive analytics or generative-AI feature was verified for the legacy ERP. Current Teachmint X EduAI features should not be attributed to MyClassCampus without a continuity statement. [1]

#### Government/state reporting and compliance

No verified public evidence was found for CBSE/ICSE/state-board report-card standards, NEP 2020 Holistic Progress Cards, UDISE+, APAAR ID, GST invoicing, Tally, NAAC, NBA, NIRF or AISHE reporting. These requirements should be treated as quote-stage validation items, not assumed capabilities.

#### Mobile apps

Native iOS and Android apps were a central differentiator. The historical iOS app was “My Class Campus,” while the Android package was “My Class Campus” with package `com.myclasscampus`; the product also had Pocket Study for LMS use. Historical app evidence is stale: the iOS app was removed in 2024 and the Android listing preserved by APKPure was last updated in 2023. [2] [11] [12] [13]

#### Integrations and APIs

Documented integrations include online payment gateway, bulk SMS gateway, Tawk.to for inquiry/admission chat, GPS/transport hardware and wireless biometric devices. A DIY website builder and hosting service was also offered. SaaSworthy says API support is “NA” and answers its FAQ “Does MyClassCampus provide API?” with “No,” so no public API should be assumed. [8] [9] [11]

#### Security and privacy

Role-based access and data backup were documented. A current Teachmint privacy policy, updated 24 August 2026, describes collection of student, parent and teacher personal data, consent, data-subject rights, service providers and deletion within six months after termination for the Teachmint platform. It does not prove that the same terms, controls or retention policy applied to the legacy MyClassCampus ERP. [7] [16] No public MyClassCampus-specific SOC 2, ISO 27001, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR, India DPDP Act readiness statement, hosting region, penetration-test report or incident register was verified.

### Advanced and Distinctive Features

* **40+ configurable modules:** The broad ERP scope covered administration, academics, finance, HR and campus operations in one platform. [2] [7]
* **Mobile-first stakeholder access:** Native iOS and Android apps were designed to surface daily updates without relying on a browser login. [2]
* **Multi-branch administration:** One account could support single- and multi-branch institutions. [7]
* **GPS transport operations:** Vehicles, routes, waypoints, dashboards and reports were tied to GPS-enabled bus tracking. [7] [11]
* **Wireless biometric support:** Historical product listings included wireless biometric attendance integration. [9]
* **Integrated Pocket Study LMS:** The April 2020 LMS connected study material, quizzes and online classes to the ERP user base. [2] [11]
* **Dynamic website and certificate tools:** A DIY website builder/hosting module and field-logic certificate generation extended the ERP beyond back-office administration. [7] [11]
* **QR profile scan and student wallet:** These were distinctive convenience and identity/payment features in the historical premium module list. [9]

### Pricing Details

No current official price was publicly available on 24 November 2026. The standalone site no longer publishes a pricing page, and the current destination does not quote a MyClassCampus rate. [1] [15]

The best dated historical figure is StartupTalky’s 13 April 2021 profile, which reported ₹100–₹150 per student per year, with Basic, Advance and Premium packages. It did not publish a package-by-package feature matrix, minimum enrolment, implementation fee or taxes. [7] SaaSworthy currently labels the product “Premium Plans (Quotation Based)” and a “Custom” plan, but warns that its feature/pricing details were last updated 4 December 2019; it is not a current official quote. [9] [10] No reliable USD price, setup fee, migration fee, support fee or renewal schedule was found.

### Integrations, Standards and Interoperability

The public record supports payment-gateway connectivity, bulk SMS, Tawk.to inquiry chat, GPS/transport hardware, wireless biometrics, app-based fee payments and a hosted website builder. [8] [9] [11] No verified evidence supports OneRoster, LTI, Ed-Fi, SIF, Clever, ClassLink, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Tally, Razorpay, Paytm, WhatsApp Business API or an open public API. SaaSworthy explicitly reports API support as unavailable. [9]

### Security, Privacy and Compliance

MyClassCampus publicly described role-based access and data backup, but did not publish a security certification or compliance matrix. [7] The current Teachmint privacy policy, last updated 24 August 2026, is the closest live parent-company statement and discusses PII, consent, processors, access/correction/deletion rights and retention; it should not be read as a MyClassCampus-specific DPDP Act attestation. [16]

No public evidence was verified for SOC 2, ISO 27001, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR, India DPDP Act readiness, Indian data-hosting region or a public security-incident history. The absence of evidence is not proof that controls do not exist; it means a buyer must request the DPA, subprocessor list, hosting location, incident-notification terms and export/deletion procedure in writing.

### Strengths

* Broad historical ERP coverage across admissions, academics, finance, HR, transport, library, hostel, inventory and communication. [7] [8] [9]
* Strong India-market orientation with mobile apps, fee collection, GPS buses, biometric support, SMS and multi-branch configuration. [2] [7] [9]
* Mobile-first delivery and an integrated LMS/Pocket Study layer made the product more than a back-office database. [2] [11]
* Reported scale was meaningful by 2021–2022: 1,500–2,000+ institutions and 300,000 to 2m+ students depending on the dated claim and definition. [5] [6] [7]
* Acquisition by Teachmint supplied a larger education-technology parent and a potential ERP-plus-LMS route. [4] [5]

### Weaknesses and Common User Complaints

The major current weakness is verifiability: the original site no longer exposes a standalone catalogue, current price, roadmap or data-export documentation. [1] [15] Buyers cannot reliably tell whether the legacy ERP is still sold under the MyClassCampus name or folded into Teachmint. [15]

Public review evidence is thin and not fully current. SaaSworthy shows a high 4.9/5 from 75 ratings, but the profile is unclaimed and carries a 2019 data-freshness warning. [9] [10] AppBrain shows only two iOS ratings averaging 3.0/5 and records that the app was removed in February 2024. [12] I found no dependable review corpus identifying recurring operational complaints; therefore widespread usability or support complaints should not be invented. The most defensible user pain point is the uncertainty created by stale listings, discontinued/removed app evidence and quote-only current access.

### Key Milestones

* **2014:** Founders say they began conceiving the product in response to schools still managing operations, records and communication manually. [7]
* **2015:** Company founding year shown in LinkedIn, CB Insights and StartupTalky records; public acquisition coverage also gives 2017, creating a date conflict. [3] [4] [7] [14]
* **March 2016:** Minimum viable product launched and early sales began with coaching classes and schools. [7]
* **2017:** The acquisition announcement’s company-history version places the founding here; this may reflect incorporation or a later operating milestone rather than the earliest build. [4] [5]
* **2018:** My Class Campus iOS app became available on the App Store, according to AppBrain’s historical record. [12]
* **April 2020:** Pocket Study LMS introduced as an integrated online-teaching layer. [2]
* **2021:** StartupTalky reported 2,000+ registered organisations, 300,000+ students, 600,000 parents, 10 countries and historical pricing of ₹100–₹150 per student per year. [7]
* **28 January 2022:** Teachmint announced acquisition of MyClassCampus; terms were undisclosed. Press coverage cited 1,500+ institutes and 2m+ students across 30 countries. [4] [5] [6]
* **September 2023:** Historical Android package record shows My Class Campus version 15.6 updated 22 September 2023. [13]
* **1 February 2024:** AppBrain records removal of the My Class Campus iOS app from the App Store. [12]
* **24 August 2026:** Teachmint’s current privacy policy was updated, but it does not identify a standalone MyClassCampus ERP policy. [16]
* **24 November 2026:** The MyClassCampus domain was checked and found to lead to Teachmint X; no current MyClassCampus pricing or documentation page was verified. [1] [15]

# Part IV. Backend Teardown of the Top 3 System-of-Record Platforms (REA-assisted): PowerSchool, Infinite Campus, Ellucian

**As-of date: 27 November 2026.** This report uses only lawful public material: vendor documentation and product pages, public GitHub repositories, NIST’s vulnerability database, public breach reporting, HTTP headers, and passive REA observations of public pages. It does not log in, bypass authentication, scan, fuzz, or access a customer system.

The public record is uneven. PowerSchool publishes unusually concrete administrator documentation for plugins, data events, throttling, and mobile server registration. Infinite Campus publishes clear hosting terms and interoperability claims, but much of its direct API documentation is partner/customer gated. Ellucian publishes strong public evidence for Ethos’s application/resource/change-notification model through its official GitHub organization, while detailed tenant-specific API schemas remain behind the customer center. Where the internal implementation is not public, the report says **Inference** rather than presenting a guess as fact.

### Comparative snapshot

| Platform | Publicly evidenced integration center | Hosting posture visible publicly | Event/data movement | Main architectural liability visible from public evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PowerSchool SIS | Plugin packages, PowerQuery, REST data exchange, Universal Rostering, SIF, Data Event API | Cloud product; customer deployments also expose server/node/load-balancer concepts in admin docs | Real-time REST roster/grade exchange and configurable data-change events | Powerful legacy customization surface and plugin credentials create a large blast radius; the December 2024 PowerSource incident shows support-plane compromise can reach SIS data [1] [2] |
| Infinite Campus | 1EdTech OneRoster, LTI, partner APIs, ODBC for a designated customer employee | Hosted production instance plus staging option; documented Windows, SQL Server, Apache Tomcat, Java, SSL middleware [3] | OneRoster rostering, grade passback, secure launch; direct API is commercially gated according to an independent integration guide [4] | Integration fragmentation across OneRoster versions and partnership tiers; documented stack is operationally traditional and customer-specific |
| Ellucian Banner/Colleague/Ethos | Ethos REST proxy APIs, versioned EEDM resources, application/resource ownership, API keys/JWT, change notifications/pub-sub | Ellucian Cloud SaaS is the strategic direction; Banner/Colleague also have installed/legacy and hybrid estates [5] [6] | Resource-level create/update/delete notifications, publish/subscribe, low-code orchestration, real-time sync [7] | Strong abstraction improves interoperability but adds schema/version/entitlement complexity; legacy self-service surfaces still produce conventional web vulnerabilities [8] |

### Evidence quality and public-observation checks

The public material supports interface and operating-model conclusions better than database-engine conclusions. None of the vendors publishes a complete production schema, deployment diagram, or authoritative list of all internal services.

I ran the requested REA CLI against one public page per vendor. The PowerSchool homepage yielded nine observed/analyzed scripts, but no verified application routes or API endpoints; two low-confidence query-string candidates were explicitly marked unverified by REA. The Infinite Campus partner page yielded three observed scripts; the Nuxt bundle at `/_nuxt/O9Ss3k2F.js` was marked unavailable because of an analysis deadline, and no routes or endpoints were established. The public Ellucian Ethos GitHub organization page yielded zero captured scripts, so it provides no frontend inference. These are observations about public marketing/community pages, not evidence about the authenticated SIS front ends. [9] [10] [11]

A passive `curl -I` check found PowerSchool returning `x-frame-options: SAMEORIGIN`, HSTS, and `x-content-type-options: nosniff`; Infinite Campus’s public page returned Netlify headers and a detailed CSP; Ellucian’s product page returned a Cloudflare 403 to the head-request path. These headers are perimeter observations only. They do not reveal the SIS backend or prove that customer tenants share the same edge configuration.

## 1. PowerSchool SIS

### Data model and core entities

**Documented fact.** PowerSchool describes SIS as managing student records, enrollment, attendance, grades, scheduling, family communication, reporting, and special programs. Its public Universal Rostering documentation names student, course, and related enrollment data, while its product page names attendance, behavior, health, graduation progress, assets, and student demographics as reportable domains. [12] [13]

**Inference.** The observable model is a district/school hierarchy with person-centered records, enrollment/roster relationships, academic offerings and sections, attendance, grading/assessment, and extensible program/health/behavior records. The public documents do not prove whether the underlying transactional store is one relational schema, a service decomposition, or a mixture. The plugin and page-customization model strongly suggests a long-lived transactional core with compatibility layers rather than a pure greenfield microservice model.

### API styles and authentication

**Documented fact.** PowerSchool exposes REST data exchange through plugins. Universal Rostering supports REST GET for roster information and REST PUT for course assignments and grades. PowerSchool also documents Data Event API Services for notifications of changes between PowerSchool and third-party applications, plus a SIF Agent option. [2] [14]

The PowerQuery ecosystem is a distinctive extension path: an installed plugin can include a PowerQuery and the plugin itself is packaged as XML or ZIP. The public administrator docs do not present a public, vendor-hosted OpenAPI contract for the whole SIS. [15]

**Documented fact.** Plugin data exchange uses OAuth 2.0. PowerSchool auto-generates a client ID and secret for a plugin, and administrators can regenerate them when compromise is suspected. [1]

**Not publicly verified.** A general PowerSchool GraphQL API, a general public SOAP API, and Ed-Fi as the primary native SIS API were not established in the public sources reviewed. SIF is explicitly documented; it should not be conflated with REST or GraphQL. SAML/OIDC SSO is a product/deployment capability in the broader ecosystem, but the public administrator pages reviewed do not expose enough detail to state which flows are supported by every SIS release or tenant.

### Extensibility and integration/event architecture

PowerSchool’s extension point is unusually administrator-visible. Plugins are installed from XML/ZIP packages, may register with an external registration server, may add links, and can include PowerQueries. The SIS product page claims administrators can modify interface pages, add or adjust SIS pages, and extend existing pages with new tables and fields without custom development. [12] [15]

Data Event API Services provide change notifications. The administrator can enable event generation separately from, or together with, the SIF agent. PowerSchool also exposes a per-plugin minimum interval between API requests, with throttling enforced at the server and requiring restart after a setting change. [14]

**Architecture reading.** This is a “deep plug-in into a transactional application” model, not only an external integration gateway. It is flexible for districts and partners, but it increases the number of code, credential, and compatibility paths that must be governed. Per-plugin throttling is a useful guardrail, but it is a coarse control compared with a centrally managed quota, tenant-aware rate budget, and asynchronous delivery queue.

### Multi-tenancy, hosting, and frontend observations

PowerSchool publicly calls SIS cloud software, but its administrator documentation still refers to a PowerSchool server, node, remote web traffic, Tomcat or load-balancer SSL, and server arrays. [12] [13] **Inference:** the installed/on-premise and hosted estates likely coexist, with a compatibility-oriented deployment abstraction rather than one uniform SaaS runtime.

The public marketing site’s JavaScript is visibly WordPress/theme/plugin oriented in the REA capture. That says nothing reliable about the SIS UI. The public SIS material supports a browser/mobile web-service model, but no authenticated SIS bundle or public login bundle was analyzed. The safe conclusion is that the frontend framework of the SIS is **not publicly established**.

### Reporting, warehouse, and mobile

PowerSchool positions SIS as providing ad hoc and state/provincial reporting across attendance, behavior, health, graduation progress, assets, and demographics. Its separate Analytics & Insights product advertises role-based dashboards, ad hoc reporting, configurable metrics and filters, and cloud hosting with role- and row-based security. [12] [16]

**Inference.** The product boundary implies an operational SIS plus a reporting/analytics plane, with at least some denormalized or derived data used for dashboards. The public pages do not prove the warehouse technology, ETL cadence, or whether analytics is physically isolated from transactional storage.

Mobile is not merely a responsive web claim. The administrator documentation describes registering a district server with PowerSource, a mobile server address and port, SSL status, and a load-balancer/node deployment option. The product page advertises iOS and Android family access for grades, attendance, schedules, notifications, and payments. [13] [17]

### Security incident and architectural lesson

PowerSchool states that on 28 December 2024 it became aware of unauthorized exfiltration from certain SIS environments through the PowerSource customer support portal. It says a single compromised credential was used, that the activity was limited to selected Students and Teachers tables, and that it found no evidence of system-layer access, malware, or compromise of other products. [18]

The lesson is architectural, not merely procedural: support, community, registration, and operational data planes must be treated as separate trust zones. A support credential should not yield a path to bulk SIS-table extraction. A modern design should require phishing-resistant MFA, short-lived scoped credentials, per-tenant and per-resource authorization, just-in-time support access, immutable audit trails, export anomaly detection, and hard separation between support tooling and production data paths. PowerSchool’s documented plugin credential-regeneration control is useful, but rotation after suspected compromise is reactive rather than a substitute for least privilege. [1]

### Specific weaknesses visible from public evidence

* Plugin XML/ZIP installation, page customization, PowerQueries, external registration, and OAuth secrets form a broad compatibility surface. The public record does not show a signed-package policy, sandbox, or capability manifest.
* Data Event API and REST exchange are valuable, but the public docs do not show durable event IDs, replay semantics, dead-letter handling, consumer offsets, or schema evolution rules.
* The coexistence of server/node/load-balancer concepts and cloud marketing suggests migration and deployment variance. That improves compatibility but complicates patch consistency, observability, and incident containment.
* Reporting, mobile, family engagement, and payments are marketed as connected, but public material does not show a canonical identity graph or an explicit consent/purpose ledger for cross-product data movement.

## 2. Infinite Campus

### Data model and core entities

**Documented fact.** Infinite Campus describes Campus SIS as covering enrollment, scheduling, grading, state reporting, and roles for staff, teachers, students, parents, administrators, and technology teams. Its partner program explicitly supports roster movement and score passback. A public integration guide identifies OneRoster services for results, resources, and enrollments; OneRoster 1.2 adds role/org/account mappings, preferred names, master IDs, scoped endpoint access, standards-based grading fields, and localized OpenAPI service discovery. [19] [4]

**Inference.** The core model is an institutional hierarchy with organizations/schools, users and multiple roles, courses/classes/sections, enrollments, results/grades, resources, and sessions. The OneRoster 1.2 shape is an interoperability projection, not proof of the internal Campus schema.

### API styles and authentication

The vendor’s public partner page says it was the first SIS certified for both 1EdTech OneRoster and CASE, and lists OneRoster provisioning, gradebook/score passback, assessments, and LTI secure launch/content selection across partners. [19]

A public integration analysis says Infinite Campus supports multiple OneRoster implementations, including 1.1 and 1.2, and that developers encounter OAuth 1.0, OAuth 2.0, and JSON depending on the implementation. It also says direct API access typically requires a partnership-level commitment, leaving OneRoster as the practical path for many developers. This is an independent integration source, not an Infinite Campus contract; the commercial-gating claim should therefore be treated as **reported external evidence**, not a universal vendor policy. [4]

**Not publicly verified.** The reviewed public sources do not establish a general GraphQL API, public SOAP contract, native Ed-Fi API, or a vendor-published OpenAPI file covering every Campus deployment. SAML/OIDC details are not public enough to characterize by tenant. The clear public interoperability center is OneRoster plus LTI, with partner-specific APIs layered alongside it.

### Extensibility and integration/event architecture

Infinite Campus publicly emphasizes standards-first partner connections: real-time rostering, grade passback, secure launch, and 1EdTech certification. [19] This is a comparatively constrained, contract-driven extension model. It is safer and easier to certify than arbitrary in-process plugins, but less expressive for partners needing non-roster domains.

**Not publicly established.** No public vendor page reviewed documents a general custom-field schema, page/plugin runtime, webhook delivery contract, or durable event bus. The absence may reflect customer-gated documentation rather than product absence. OneRoster’s fixed service model, version variants, and endpoint scoping are the observable integration boundaries.

### Multi-tenancy, hosting, and frontend observations

Infinite Campus’s public Cloud Hosting Services terms are unusually specific. A hosted customer receives a single production instance; computing hardware, system software, database software, and storage are located at Infinite Campus facilities. The documented middleware includes Windows OS, Microsoft SQL Server, Apache Tomcat, Java, drivers, and SSL certificates. Infinite Campus describes backups retrieved each business day, backup servers intended to restore service within 24 hours after catastrophic disruption, and an optional staging environment. [3]

The same terms permit ODBC access to one designated customer employee, subject to approval. That is a powerful operational escape hatch, but it exposes a coupling risk: ODBC can become an unofficial integration surface that bypasses versioned API governance. [3]

The public partner page is a modern Nuxt-rendered site; REA observed the Nuxt bundle URL but could not analyze that particular bundle before its deadline. This is a marketing-site observation only. The Campus SIS frontend framework is not established by public evidence. The product pages do establish a family mobile app for grades, assignments, attendance, food service, announcements, fees, stores, and activity registration. [20]

### Reporting and data products

Infinite Campus markets built-in state reporting and a Campus Analytics Suite that uses attendance, behavior, academic, curriculum, classroom performance, and stability signals. It advertises daily risk predictions, embedded operation without imports/exports, visualizations, and customizable reports. [21]

**Inference.** The analytics product likely consumes derived/feature data within or alongside the SIS rather than relying exclusively on external batch exports. The public record does not establish the warehouse engine, whether the transactional and analytical stores are separate, or the exact retention and lineage model.

### Security incident and architectural lesson

As of the report date, HIBP records a March 2026 incident in which data alleged to be from Infinite Campus was published, describing roughly 137,000 email addresses and names, phone numbers, physical addresses, and support tickets. HIBP says subsequent notifications characterized much of the exposure as staff directory information. [22] UpGuard described the incident as alleged, reported through dark-web monitoring, with PII categories unconfirmed and no formal vendor response available at its publication date. [23]

This is not equivalent to a vendor-confirmed production SIS breach. It is nevertheless an important public security signal: support and corporate-contact datasets can be valuable even when they are not student records. The design lesson is to minimize support-ticket data, separate corporate CRM/support identity from SIS tenant identity, enforce MFA and conditional access, and make incident scope auditable. For customers, ODBC and partner credentials should be treated as privileged data paths, not convenience interfaces.

### Specific weaknesses visible from public evidence

* Multiple OneRoster versions and authentication variants increase connector branching and testing cost. Version negotiation and capability discovery must be first-class.
* A standards-first surface is predictable but narrow. Non-roster domains such as health, behavior, finance, and local custom entities may require partner-specific work.
* ODBC access is useful for controlled reporting but can undermine API governance, auditability, and forward compatibility if used for operational writes or large extracts.
* The hosting terms describe a traditional Windows/SQL/Tomcat/Java stack and customer-specific production instances. That can simplify isolation and change management, but it may constrain elastic scaling and make fleet-wide patch/observability uniformity harder than in a fully multi-tenant SaaS control plane.

## 3. Ellucian Banner/Colleague and Ethos

### Data model and core entities

Ethos publicly exposes a resource-oriented model rather than a table-oriented contract. The official Ellucian Ethos Community repository describes an **application** that owns resources and a subscribing application that consumes resource change notifications. Its example resources include students, courses, grades, parking tickets, and finance objects. The official Java and C# repositories describe invoking Ethos APIs and consuming or publishing change notifications. [7] [24] [25]

**Documented fact.** Ellucian’s public platform positioning covers the full higher-education lifecycle: recruiting, enrollment, retention, finance, HCM, advancement, and alumni engagement. Its public analytics page describes unified SIS, ERP, CRM, and third-party data, with a governed data lake/single data warehouse. [5] [26]

**Inference.** Ethos is a canonical integration/data-contract layer over heterogeneous Banner and Colleague domains. It is not evidence that Banner and Colleague share one physical database or one internal domain model. Versioned resource schemas and tenant-enabled resources are a more defensible design target than direct table replication.

### API styles and authentication

The publicly observable Ethos style is REST/JSON proxy APIs with resource versioning and application/resource authorization. The official Python pub/sub example says Ethos applications obtain API keys, use those keys to obtain JWTs, and that JWTs expire after five minutes; the Java examples explicitly cover getting an access token, invoking the proxy API, and consuming/publishing change notifications. [7] [25]

The public sources reviewed do not prove GraphQL or a general SOAP surface for Ethos. Legacy Banner/Colleague estates have older web/API and transaction integration mechanisms, but the evidence supports Ethos REST as Ellucian’s preferred modern integration boundary. SAML/OIDC may be used for human user SSO in campus deployments, but Ethos machine-to-machine authentication is the API-key-to-short-lived-JWT pattern shown in the public examples.

### Extensibility and integration/event architecture

Ethos’s extensibility model is explicit and useful: an application can own a resource, subscribe to another application’s resource, and publish or consume create/update/delete change notifications. The public Python demo models a parking-ticket authoritative application and a finance subscribing application, and shows polling for notifications in addition to publishing. [7]

Ellucian’s product page adds a low-code data-orchestration capability, pre-built connectors and APIs, serverless scalable APIs, real-time data sync, and custom transformations. These are vendor product claims rather than a public implementation diagram, but they demonstrate a deliberate move from point-to-point integrations toward a governed integration plane. [5]

**Not publicly verified.** The public sources do not show the complete webhook delivery contract, ordering guarantee, replay window, dead-letter policy, schema registry internals, or whether every Banner/Colleague resource is event-enabled. The official examples show change-notification semantics and a polling consumer; do not infer exactly-once delivery from them.

### Multi-tenancy, hosting, and frontend observations

Ellucian’s Trust Center describes SaaS capabilities across the student lifecycle and lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, UK Cyber Essentials Basic, and NIST 800-171, while also publishing links for a Cloud Disaster Recovery Plan and shared-responsibility materials. It says a UK certification covers segregated AWS networks, but that statement should not be generalized to every Ellucian product or tenant. [27]

Ellucian’s public platform pages describe a central workspace that unifies student, finance, and HCM systems with personalized, role-based dashboards and one access point. [28] The marketing/product frontend is publicly visible, but no authenticated Banner/Colleague/Ethos UI bundle was inspected. The safe conclusion is a SaaS, role-based workspace approach around APIs; the exact client framework is not publicly established.

Banner and Colleague remain relevant as installed or hybrid systems. Ethos reduces direct coupling, but an institution migrating from local Banner/Colleague to Ellucian Cloud still has identity, data-quality, version, and operational boundary problems. The public docs’ customer-center gating is itself evidence that the detailed schema/entitlement surface is controlled rather than openly discoverable.

### Reporting, warehouse, and mobile approach

Ellucian Reporting & Analytics claims pre-built dashboards, role-specific analytics, a single data warehouse, a governed data lake, and data orchestration/custom transformations. [26] The platform’s central workspace exposes dashboards, reports, KPIs, and role-based experiences, while Ellucian’s product portfolio includes transcript exchange and process automation. [28]

**Inference.** Ellucian has made the analytical and experience layers explicit platform products, rather than treating reporting as SQL access to the ERP. That is a good separation of operational, integration, and analytical concerns. It also creates governance requirements: lineage, resource-level consent, cross-module identity resolution, and clear freshness indicators.

The public central-workspace material supports responsive, cross-device access, but does not prove a native mobile architecture. Public app-store listings show Ellucian-branded mobile apps, yet the backend contract and offline behavior are not public. Treat mobile as an API consumer of the same role-aware platform unless tenant-specific evidence says otherwise.

### Security incidents and architectural lesson

NIST’s NVD records CVE-2026-47106 for Banner Self-Service before the April T2 release dated 23 April 2025: stored XSS in course search, where authenticated Banner ERP write access could place payloads in faculty/course fields and an unauthenticated API response could serve them to viewers. NVD describes a medium CVSS-B score and identifies the affected Banner Self-Service line. [8]

This is not an Ethos cloud breach, but it demonstrates the risk of legacy/self-service surfaces adjacent to ERP data. A canonical integration API does not remove the need for output encoding, API-specific authorization, content security policy, and security regression tests in every presentation layer. The architectural lesson is to keep untrusted descriptive fields typed and encoded at every render boundary, and to avoid allowing an unauthenticated read endpoint to become a payload delivery path merely because the underlying fields were written by an authenticated user.

### Specific weaknesses visible from public evidence

* Resource abstraction hides legacy complexity, but versioned schemas and entitlement-dependent resources can become a compatibility matrix that is difficult for open-source adopters to test locally.
* API keys that mint short-lived JWTs are better than long-lived bearer secrets, but public examples do not show per-resource scopes, key rotation UX, or workload identity federation.
* Pub/sub examples show polling and notification semantics, but public evidence does not establish ordering, replay, backpressure, or delivery durability. Integrators must assume they need idempotency and reconciliation.
* Low-code transformations and custom resources improve time-to-value but can create opaque data lineage and “integration logic outside version control” unless every mapping is exportable, reviewable, and testable.
* Legacy Banner/Colleague and modern SaaS surfaces coexist. The migration boundary is a product strength but an operational weakness when identity, audit, and data semantics differ between estates.

## Architecture lessons for a new open-source platform

1. **Use a canonical education domain model plus projections.** Define stable entities and relationships for person, organization, campus/school, academic period, course, section, enrollment, attendance, assessment, grade, credential, program, support plan, finance, and consent. Expose standards projections such as OneRoster and Ed-Fi without allowing either projection to become the only internal model. Preserve source IDs, effective dates, and provenance.

2. **Separate operational, integration, and analytical planes.** Keep the transactional system authoritative for writes. Publish an outbox-backed event stream for integrations. Build a governed analytical store with lineage and freshness metadata. Do not grant reporting users arbitrary database access to production; provide read models, SQL views, or a controlled query service.

3. **Make multi-tenancy explicit in every identifier and policy.** Tenant, institution, campus, and organizational scope should be first-class claims and database partition keys. Enforce row-level authorization at the service boundary and again in analytics. Provide an auditable support plane with just-in-time, tenant-scoped access rather than a support credential that can bulk-read unrelated customer data.

4. **Prefer capability-based extensions over arbitrary plugins.** Offer signed, declarative manifests with named capabilities, scopes, event subscriptions, UI slots, custom fields, and rate limits. Run extension code out of process or in a sandbox. Make every extension install, upgrade, credential rotation, and data export observable. This keeps PowerSchool-like flexibility without allowing a plugin to become an implicit database superuser.

5. **Treat events as a durable contract.** Every event needs an immutable event ID, tenant ID, resource type/version, actor, occurred-at and observed-at timestamps, causation/correlation IDs, before/after or patch semantics where permitted, and a schema URL. Provide replay from a documented retention window, consumer offsets, idempotency keys, dead-letter queues, backoff, reconciliation endpoints, and an explicit ordering guarantee per aggregate.

6. **Support standards with version negotiation and conformance tests.** Implement OneRoster 1.2 and Ed-Fi/other required standards as adapters over the canonical model. Publish OpenAPI documents, JSON Schemas, examples, capability discovery, and a local conformance test suite. Accept that districts will expose multiple versions and make the connector choose capabilities rather than branching on undocumented behavior.

7. **Use modern workload identity and least privilege.** For machine integrations, support OAuth 2.0 client credentials with private-key JWT or mTLS, short-lived access tokens, narrow resource scopes, rotation without downtime, and secretless workload identity where possible. For people, support OIDC and SAML federation, phishing-resistant MFA, SCIM or equivalent lifecycle provisioning, and explicit separation of support/admin identities from customer users.

8. **Design reconciliation as a first-class operation.** Real-time events fail, tenants pause integrations, and standards versions drift. Every connector needs a bounded full sync, delta sync, cursor recovery, conflict policy, dry run, and human-readable error report. Track per-field provenance and never silently overwrite a more authoritative value.

9. **Make custom fields safe and portable.** Store custom definitions as typed, versioned metadata with validation, access policy, retention, export/import, and migration hooks. Do not allow arbitrary SQL or unescaped HTML into core UI paths. Encode at output, sanitize rich text, and maintain security tests for every custom page, report, import, and API projection.

10. **Build mobile and frontend on the same policy-aware API.** A web app, native mobile app, partner integration, and reporting job should receive the same authorization decisions and consistent resource representations. Add offline-safe sync tokens only for data that has an explicit mobile policy. Do not create a second “mobile API” with weaker authorization or untracked fields.

11. **Ship tenant-visible security and operations evidence.** Provide audit logs, export logs, API token inventory, event delivery health, dependency/version inventory, backup-restore tests, and a public status page. Publish security advisories and a supported-version matrix. The PowerSchool and Infinite Campus incidents show why support data, credentials, and operational metadata deserve the same controls as student records.

12. **Keep the open-source boundary honest.** Document what is core, what is an adapter, and what is an optional hosted service. Provide a reference single-node deployment, a horizontally scalable deployment, and migration tooling. An open platform wins not by pretending every institution has one schema, but by making variation explicit, testable, observable, and reversible.

# Part V. Blueprint: "OpenCampus One", an Open-Source Platform Designed to Beat Every Platform in This Report

> **Status:** blueprint only. No development has been started. "OpenCampus One" is a working name; check trademarks and domains before public launch.
> **Design rule:** every feature in this blueprint traces back to a documented competitor gap (gap codes C1–C12 below) found in the 40 dossiers and Appendices A–C.

## V.1 Strategic Thesis: Why a New Platform Can Win

The incumbents are strong on breadth and installed base but weak on the things buyers now care about most. The evidence across the 40 dossiers shows the same pattern:

- **Pricing is opaque.** Almost every enterprise vendor is quote-only (PowerSchool, Ellucian, Workday, Infinite Campus, Skyward, Blackbaud, Jenzabar), and implementations run three to seven months (G2 reviewer averages for PowerSchool and Blackbaud).
- **Satisfaction is mediocre.** The Key's 2025 survey of 961 UK MIS users found an average satisfaction of 6.6/10. Only 47% found their system intuitive for new users, only 54% were satisfied with support, and 21% were considering a switch within a year (35% among SIMS users).
- **Mobile is the weakest layer.** Arbor's parent app scored 1.9/5 and PowerSchool Mobile 2.5/5 on Google Play when checked, even though both cores are highly ranked.
- **Trust has been damaged.** PowerSchool (2024–2025), Blackbaud (2020), Illuminate (2021, with FTC action in 2025) and Frontline (2026) all showed that a school system's support or credential plane can expose millions of student records.
- **Segments are split.** K-12 runs on one vendor class (PowerSchool, Arbor, Fedena) and higher education on another (Ellucian, Workday, Jenzabar, MasterSoft). Groups that own both schools and colleges, which are very common in India, the Gulf and Africa, must buy and integrate two systems.
- **India is underserved on compliance.** Few vendors document UDISE+, APAAR, ABC, DigiLocker, PARAKH HPC or DPDP Act 2023 / Rules 2025 workflows end to end.
- **Open source exists but is stale or narrow.** Fedena's public repository was last pushed in May 2020. openSIS and Gibbon are PHP/MySQL single-tenant designs. OpenEduCat depends on the Odoo stack. None is multi-tenant, RLS-secured, offline-first and multi-segment.

**The thesis.** Build one open-source, cloud-native, offline-capable platform that serves a nursery, a K-12 school, a college and a multi-campus university group from the same core. Then win on four promises that no incumbent can easily copy:

1. **"Switch in a weekend, leave in a click."** Migration tooling for every major competitor, plus a contractual one-click full-data exit.
2. **"Published price, or free forever."** The AGPL core is free to self-host. Hosted plans have public per-student prices with no implementation fee for standard migrations.
3. **"Works on a ₹8,000 phone with no signal."** Offline-first teacher and parent apps, low-bandwidth mode, WhatsApp/SMS fallback and 22 Indian languages plus global languages.
4. **"Security you can audit."** Open code, database-enforced tenant isolation, a public security model, immutable audit logs, just-in-time support access and published penetration-test summaries.

## V.3 Target Markets, Institutions and Beachhead Sequence

**Primary beachhead: India private K-12 schools and affiliated colleges (years 1–2).** India has 1,471,473 schools and 246.9M enrolments (UDISE+ 2024–25), plus 45,473 colleges and 1,168 universities (AISHE 2021–22). Private unaided schools alone number 339,583. Indian buyers are price-sensitive, mobile-first and under new compliance pressure (DPDP Rules 2025, APAAR, NEP 2020 HPC). The ranked Indian vendors are fragmented, mostly closed and mostly quote-only. This is the largest addressable base where a free, compliant, offline-first platform has an immediate edge.

**Second wave: UK and international schools (years 2–3).** The UK market switched more than 4,000 schools in 2025 and is in a retention phase. Arbor's app ratings and Bromcom's support scores leave room for a better parent and teacher experience. International and IB schools (iSAMS, ManageBac, Toddle, Veracross territory) need curriculum mapping, multi-language families and multi-country groups.

**Third wave: emerging markets (years 2–4).** The Gulf (GCC private school groups), Southeast Asia, Africa (Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa) and Latin America have strong private-school growth, limited budgets and connectivity constraints, and few modern open options.

**Fourth wave: US private, charter and small public districts (years 3–5).** These buyers need OneRoster 1.2, Ed-Fi, FERPA/COPPA/state-privacy tooling and the published price advantage, positioned against FACTS, Gradelink, Alma and openSIS.

**Higher education throughout.** Small and mid-size colleges and private universities that cannot afford Ellucian, Workday or Jenzabar can adopt the Higher-Ed Pack (CBCS/credits, OBE, NAAC/NBA, examinations, hostels, placements).

**Institution types served from one core:** pre-schools and nurseries; K-12 schools (government, aided, private, charter, independent); international and IB/Cambridge schools; coaching and tuition centres; vocational and ITI/polytechnic institutes; colleges (affiliated and autonomous); universities (state, private, deemed); multi-campus groups, trusts and MATs; government departments and education ministries (state dashboards).

## V.4 One Core, Configurable Segment Packs

The core holds the canonical model: people, organizations, campuses, academic periods, programmes, courses, sections, enrolments, attendance, assessments, results, credentials, finance, consent and audit. Packs add terminology, workflows, rules and compliance outputs without forking the code.
